Question: What did your pastor say or do that made you quit his church?
Answer: In 1997 the old Catholic priest of our neighborhood was a few months short of retiring. We saw a sudden radical change in his style. We were surprised when our old priest made a claim that those weeping statues of Mary reported around the world were actually true and that it was a sign of the coming apocalypse. He lamented that people were dropping out of church and parents were not forcing their children to attend with them and yadee ya. My brother and I laughed to ourselves and wondered who were the lucky children whose parents made church an option for them rather than force them to attend like our mother did. Some weeks later my mother began having trouble sleeping at nights. Rather than attribute this to our newborn baby sister who kept her up she said that she felt an evil force in the house. One night the electricity went for the entire night. Already scared and exhausted out of her wits she slept with a candle burning nearby and in the morning she explained that she had awaken to see a demonic shadow glide across the room and towards our baby sister that night. My mother made the accusation that this was all the work of our neighbor Vanessa, who used to be her friend but was now an enemy. Vanessa was praying to Satan and conjuring up demons to attack us. She immediately sought the old priest the following day. My brother and I found the ordeal amusing. We both knew that the problem was my mother was stressed out from being kept up at night and from our stepfather not providing the money he was supposed to towards the baby and the household in general. Also my mother wanted to taint Vanessa’s name and have her seen as a witch after an anonymous lady sent our stepfather a hoax love letter in the mail box, claiming him to be her lover and encouraging him to elope with her. My mother believed it was all Vanessa’s doing. She knew Vanessa’s handwriting and bad spelling. My brother and I were certain that the priest would say some words of comfort and send her off. To our surprise we saw the priest come by the following day, dressed in his official garments and enter our humble abode. He went into the bedroom and said several prayers. My mother, just as surprised as we were that he actually came, then asked the priest to cast out the evil prayers of Vanessa and to pray that any further evil she sends be directed back to her. The priest gave a wry smile and said that he prayed that all those wrapped in Satan’s grip be released. He then left. Christmas was approaching and at church this would be the final week of the old priest. Inspired by the priest’s dedication to his service our mother made us attend every week. For his final sermon he decided to drop a bomb on us. Lamenting again the amount of people dropping out of church and denying Christ. He explained to us that the day of reckoning was near. He asked us how many times did Peter deny Christ. ‘Three,’ the congregation murmured. ‘What number represents the mark of the Beast?’ ‘666’ ‘Every time you deny Christ you invoke the mark of the Beast. What is the mark of the Beast x 3?’ There was a murmuring among the congregation. ‘1998’ the old priest cried. Everyone shuddered in fear including myself. We were just a few moths shy of the year 1998. The old priest then became enraptured in his own sermon and declared ways for us to stave off this year of reckoning. We needed to repent. We needed to fast. We needed to stop speaking filth. We needed to keep our children away from cable TV and that awful rap and heavy metal music. Most of all we needed to congregate in church as often as possible. When we left I asked my brother why wasn’t he afraid. He said that that old priest was full of shit. He assured me that nothing was going to happen and when 1998 came around, indeed nothing did happen. My mother didn’t like the new priest and stopped us from coming to church altogether, my brother and I still watched cable with its rap and heavy metal and we still cursed like sailors, church numbers dwindled like never before but the day of reckoning never happened in 1998. As we grew older my brother and I were completely disenchanted with the Catholic Church. Whenever I’m asked to attend church with someone I think back to the old priest who sat in his room. The old priest who toyed with his calculator and the multiples of the number 666 and stood aghast at a revelation. A gimmicky, meaningless revelation but a revelation nonetheless.

Question: What is your most interesting encounter with the police?
Answer: I was working pizza delivery some years ago. I had a delivery to make at what is called ‘the old airport.’ It is a collection of buildings located at what used to be the official airport of the country some decades ago but has long since been discontinued since a more modern airport has been built nearby. As such the ‘old airport’ is now used to house a few airport related businesses and airport administration. It is rather a quiet, relatively vacant area in comparison to the actual airport and no one pays it any mind except for the people who wait for the bus there. One afternoon I dropped off a pizza to a lady who worked at the local Swissport that was located there. While riding the motorcycle out I was stopped by a police vehicle. The driver beckoned me to come over. The glass of his vehicle went down revealing a middle aged male officer behind the wheel and an attractive young female officer at the passenger’s side. The male pointed to some arrows on the surface of the road. Apparently I had entered along the exit arrow and was leaving along the entrance arrow. It was a really petty issue. Nobody cared about those arrows since the old airport was no longer in use and hardly any vehicle ever came there to begin with. Regardless I apologized to the officer and explained to him that I never noticed those arrows until now. Expecting him to let me off the hook and return to my duty I stood in silence waiting. ‘License and insurance,’ he then says in a stoic tone. ‘Is this guy for real?’ I thought to myself. I went to my wallet for my license and while searching I heard the guy explain haughtily to his female sidekick how he busted a pizza delivery man who didn’t even have a driver’s license but was working delivery and how he believes that regular check ups like this reduces the amount of accidents that occur on the road. From the tone of his voice I could sense that the man was trying to make some kind of impression on his female partner and that she was on some kind of training with him. Looking at her face I could sense that she was quite fed up the partner she had been assigned to for the day but was trying to be patient with him. I showed the officer my license. ‘And the insurance?’ Never in my years of working delivery had an officer ever asked me for insurance. The restaurant I worked for was a major chain and police generally knew that this franchise did not make joke with their insurances. Regardless I showed him the insurance title taped inside the back of the delivery box. ‘What’s this? What’s this?’ the officer bellows. ‘All insurances must be presentable for officers to inspect.’ The officer demands that I yank it off from the back and hand it to him. Another petty call. I pulled it off from the box and handed it to him. Meanwhile he barely looks at it but begins to chastise me about how dirty my bike looked and that I should be more prideful of my duty when delivering people’s food and how people die from food poisoning every day. He saw that I had another order to deliver. I was expecting him to send me on my way. This had gone on long enough. ‘What’s in that bag there?’ ‘It’s another order.’ ‘I know!’ he bellowed, ‘What is it?’ Did this man really want me to call out the order that someone made for a pizza? I explained to him it was a pepperoni and pine pizza. ‘Are you sure?’ ‘Yes,’ I replied and I was about to show him the customer’s bill when he said, ‘Take it out the bag and open the box.’ At that point his partner had had enough and she cried loudly, ‘Curtis are you some kind of ass?’ She folded her arms in defiance and shook her head. There was a silence and Curtis the officer proceeded to awkwardly laugh off the situation. ‘Pizza man,’ the officer said in a tone that showed a measure of humility, ‘Pay attention to the road. Don’t let us have this conversation again.’ With that said Curtis the officer returned to his vehicle. His female sidekick gave me an apologetic look with eyes that seemed to say ‘Believe me, you don’t want to be in my shoes right now’ and with that they were gone. I drove off myself, wondering where exactly Curtis was going when he asked me to open the pizza box. Did he expect me to have a stash of cocaine hidden there? Did he want me to try and bribe him by offering the pizza? God alone knows.

Question: In Saving Private Ryan, is Upham the biggest scumbag in movie history?
Answer: It’s funny how the human psyche works. In that famous scene where the German (Steamboat Willie) that Upham saved from execution is struggling with Private Mellish on the ground, about to drive a knife into him, our hatred is directed to Upham who stands at the stairs, armed to the teeth with ammo and a rifle, but does nothing. Upham knows what is happening but is undergoing some state of shock and paralysis. As the knife is driven into Mellish and Upham remains cowering at the spot it creates one of the most sad and frustrating scenes in cinema history and renders Upham one of the most detested film characters ever to grace the screen. Funny how no one directs a quarter of that hate to the real scumbag Steamboat Willie. Our psyche works in a way in that we accept killing and violence as part of our human condition. However the thing we collectively and subconsciously detest the most as humans is disloyalty and selfishness, especially in times when camaraderie is crucial to the survival of all. The group all had differing values and opinions but they sacrificed their dislikes and disagreements for the sake of completing the mission or at least survival. They were all forced to find some stupid kid named Ryan who got caught/lost and his mama wanted him home. This was just fresh after the horror and trauma of D-Day Normandy. By this point in the Ryan mission most of the group had been killed and remaining few relied heavily on each other’s loyalty and camaraderie to defend one another. Upham, from the very beginning, stuck out like a crusty old sore thumb. Upham demonstrated a more pacifist intellectual side. He did not have a kill count and hoped to avoid bloodshed as much as possible and hopefully stave off some needless killing. His lack of combat experience combined with his unrealistic ideals irritated his fellow men but at the end of the day he provided a valuable service in regards to being a solid translator. Love him or hate him, he did his primary job and he did somewhat redeem himself of the burden of Mellish’s death by killing Steamboat Willie the second time he was captured, finally understanding that you can’t always play by the rules when it comes to war. He is the one of the most frustrating characters but he’s not the biggest scumbag. That award goes to the Ukrainian collaborators particularly the one nicknamed Little Policeman in the Russian WWII film Come and See. Little Policeman is a dwarfish, hideous man that has led the Nazis to several Belarusian villages and jeers at countless throngs of women, children and elderly people being shot and burned alive. Little Policeman has no allegiance with anyone. He is concerned with saving his own skin and as such he relishes in whatever happens at the moment as long as it favors him. The Nazis see him as a clown and as such he portrays himself as a grotesque caricature of one for their delight, with his shrill, unsettling voice, sporting a wooden ‘gun’ and helmet with a crude swastika self painted on its surface. Never before have I witnessed such a scumbag that I felt like destroying my TV in anger whenever he came onto the screen. Even more disgusting is how he and the other collaborators plead for their lives when they are caught by the resistance. They claim to be victims and beg to be allowed to kill the Nazi captives to show their new loyalty. Little Policeman did not kill or hurt or single person in the film but he was detested far more than the actual Nazis themselves because of his sickening treachery and selfishness. Question: What single moment in a film was an example of some of the greatest acting you've ever seen from an individual or ensemble cast?
Answer: The Last Picture Show (1971) is, in my honest opinion, the greatest piece of ensemble acting I've ever seen. I would go as far and say that this is one of the rare moments in cinema where a certain magic takes over and the movie takes unexplainable life of its own. It is one of the few movies that can move me to tears even if I were to watch it reading captions on mute. The acting, both vocal and non-vocal, is that good. But before I go on a rant, for those who don't know about the film, it revolves around various characters living in a dusty, dying small town in Texas. Life for practically everyone is uneventful and everyone shares a certain yearning; for the older generation it is of good times gone by and things that could've been, for the younger generation, a deep desire to escape the monotony and perpetual routine of the life of their parents and forefathers. Every major character wants to make some kind of difference in their lives and escape the stagnancy that surrounds them; some in constructive and helpful ways and some through seeking attention and infamy. The rest of the characters just seem to accept their fate and live for the rare special moments of feeling some sort of fleeting joy, a connection or purpose in life. The titular ‘Last Picture Show’ symbolises the only escape for most of these individuals in the form of a crumbling local cinema that is about to be closed down by its benevolent but sickly owner who himself represents the life of the town. As such the film is a meditation on loneliness, yearning, alienation and the desperate desire human beings have to connect with others by whatever means possible, a desire that becomes more intense the more isolated society is from the outside world. I would safely assume that all the actors read either the script (and/or the magnificent book by Larry McMurtry) understood the themes, did the assignment and delivered. Practically every scene is like a masterclass in acting. My personal favourite being the final scene where the teenaged protagonist Sonny returns, dejected and alienated, to the middle aged Ruth Popper. She herself has long suffered such feelings and they both share a moment, finally understanding one another; older and younger generation, with the gentle touch of hands. Around them the wind howls non stop in the background while the strain of the same old country songs, same old ads and same outdated radio shows play on the transistor behind them. This serves to remind them that this is their lives and there is little to nothing they can do to change it. This is a film that I believe anyone who lives (or has lived) in a location forgotten by the rest of the general population can relate to, regardless what part of world it is.

Question: Did gamers in the 90s think that the game graphics at the time were super realistic?
Answer: 90s gamer here. It was rare to find a realistic game in the 90s so ‘super realistic’ was never a phrase 90s gamers would use when describing the graphics. Mortal Kombat (1992) was probably the first game whereby its realism was remarked upon by society to the point where it became infamous for its violence and gratuitous gore captured with real life human models. It’s almost laughable now that such stiff characters executing caveman like fight moves with dubious physics and anatomy created such a moral outcry back in 90s. Technology was limited back in the day that whenever game developers tried their hardest at realistic graphics great sacrifices had to be made. Gran Turismo (1997) had the most graphically precise 3D cars (for its time) but the graphics for practically everything else in the game was shite. The Virtua Fighter, Tekken and Dead or Alive franchises created awesome human\humanoid characters that looked somewhat realistic (especially in cut scenes) but looked clunky and zombie like while fighting. It was the norm for laughable physics such as characters seemingly floating in the air while jumping/falling or a mere kick to the shin making an opponent’s entire body contort as though struck with a sledgehammer. Don’t even mention the bland, lifeless backgrounds with beaches, canyons, temples and bridges as wide as a football field. No one I knew ever sat and praised the realism of graphics of such games. Graphics were usually referred to as good or bad in the 90s. It was in the late 90s was when gamers really began to praise realistic graphics. Metal Gear Solid (1998) is the PlayStation title that held unanimous praise for solid graphics (as well as sound, physics, perspective etc) throughout. There was hardly a sour note in its execution and most gamers I know had that ‘felt as if I was there’ feeling while playing the game. The limitation with Metal Gear was that practically every level looked like a replica of the last with snowy blue/green military compounds/laboratories being the general motif. The Sega Dreamcast arrived in 1998 and rather than good or bad, realistic graphics became a major talking point. Soul Calibur (1998) erased all the clunky eeriness of its 3D beat ‘em up predecessors. However the game that took realism as close to super realism graphically and gameplay-wise was Shenmue (1999). As laughable and meme worthy Shenmue has become now, it was seen as the beacon for games of the future. Controlling every action and decision of the protagonist in a sprawling, well rendered Yokosuka Japan, full of interactive and dynamic human characters, it was as close as one could get to virtual reality at the time. The graphics were gorgeous for its time; seeing old women dusting shop fronts, falling rain, men puttering about on mopeds and petals floating about in the wind made it one of the first games to embrace cinematography. Were it not for the gratuitous cut scenes/camera angles, uncanny valley faces and goofy dubbing Shenmue would’ve been the closest thing to a real life simulation. So as an old fart former 90s gamer I know these games are as ancient to young gamers as PacMan was back in my time. Technology has gotten so that no one seems to be bothered by bad game graphics anymore but do I hope this answer sheds some light on the question.

Question: Were you popular in high school?
Answer: Yes and no. In my early years I was just this odd kid with beaten up glasses who smiled a lot, was respectable to my elders but easily manipulated by my peers. Awww that's so sweet Elijah. Who's the lucky girl you going to give this to? Elijah: I'm giving it to you. I meant all that I wrote in it. Melanie: (blushes) But Elijah you know I have a boyfriend now. Elijah: What? I thought that was just a joke. How can he be your boyfriend? You only started taking to him a week or two ago. I've been friends with you since we started school. Melanie: Don't take it the wrong way. I like you too but he's older and more mature. Elijah: Yeah he looks old as hell. Melanie: Don't talk like that. Listen I just hope we can still be friends. Elijah: Friends! I'll show you friends. (Proceeds to tear up the poem in anger and walks away) I would then hang out with my group of loyal friends and we'd laugh manically at anything with an inkling of potential humour to stave off the pain and humiliation that we each got from our endeavours towards the opposite sex. From 15 and upwards I became a bit less awkward and a bit more refined. I discovered my tastes in music and while everyone grooved to Usher and Sean Paul I was becoming a self proclaimed hippie as I indulged in music from the 60s and 70s. Even though I stuck with my loyal, good-natured friends I began to learn and explore the different niches of kids my age. The popularity hierarchy went a bit like this. Top tier These were generally kids who had some measure of fame or infamy ; promiscuous kids, missing from school for long periods kids, the gang affiliated, football stars, the rich and not bashful about it, dating the hottest girl/boy in school and showing a lot of PDA kids, the consistently fashionable, defiant and challenging to authority kids etc etc. Middle tier Natural comedians, zany characters, stoners (high men as we called them), outspoken future politicians, natural businessmen, confident kids, gearheads, wildboys, good looking kids, athletic but not gifted kids, go-getters, nice guys and girls etc etc. Lower tier Shy kids, poverty stricken kids, teacher's pets, snitches, neurotics, overweight, ‘ugly’ kids, geeks, trying too hard kids etc etc. It's sad but that's how unwritten hierarchies was developed and it's still pretty much the same. School can be cruel. To be fair and honest, no one was guaranteed to remain in any one tier indefinitely. Shane, the most infamous bully of my class missed so much school that he was kept back a year and was sent to his younger brother's class under us. Shane went from top of the top tier to the absolute bottom in an instant. Siddhartha, was a unknown geek but went straight to the top when everyone found out he was the richest boy in school and he began flaunting it. I myself juggled between lower and middle throughout my high school tenure. Whenever I hung around the so-called top tier kids I honestly often felt something akin to sad desperation. They just seemed like miserable people who could never be themselves or had some serious hang ups in life. I didnt stick around them for long. Only when I came into adulthood doing my A’Levels did I become somewhat popular. I started to gain some measure of looks and an endless reserve of wit and confidence albeit with a significant lack of self discipline. I started mingling with everyone and in my cocky, self assurance I broke a few hearts and ended up having my own broken coming towards the end of high school. I think I was generally well liked and accepted amongst 80% of my peers and though I might have been a douche half the time, I was an entertaining, well-meaning and loyal douche throughout.

Question: What are some examples of excellent scenes in generally terrible movies?
Answer: Joe Dirt (2001) has been savaged by critics for over two decades but in my honest opinion some of the most wittiest and well written comedic scenes can be found in this movie alongside some of its more gross and low brow. Two scenes from this movie are continuously etched in my memory. Joe Dirt (David Spade) is an atypical, Southern rock loving, beaten up car driving, mulleted redneck. He is trying to find his parents who misplaced him as a child. On his journey he travels to Indiana and encounters a creepy man who agrees he saw them at the Grand Canyon and Joe is invited inside the man's house. The scene then cuts to Joe (possibly) naked in a deep pit whilst the other man is now in drag and lingerie commanding him to put lotion on his skin whilst sitting with his little dog at the top of the pit. Joe sees nothing strange about the whole ordeal and simply asks periodically for automotive trading magazines for the past two weeks imprisonment. Joe manages to escape by police intervening at the last minute. The man is revealed to be notorious serial killer Buffalo Bob and that he was intent on flaying Joe alive to make a skin coat. None of this seems to be of any major concern for Joe except that idea was ‘gross’ and that Buffalo Bob came across ‘a little fruity.’ I honestly think this is one of the best parodies ever done so much that I've watched it on Youtube more than the actual Buffalo Bill ‘It puts the lotion on the skin’ scene from Silence of the Lambs. All props goes to actor Brian Thompson whose rendition of Buffalo Bill gives the original a run for his money. Further into the movie Joe is employed as a local school janitor in Louisiana. He befriends another janitor Clem (Christopher Walker) who is clearly an Italian American former gangster hiding from the mob under a pseudonym. Being slow witted, Joe accidentally gets Clem to be put on local television which alerts Clem's former mob associates to his whereabouts whereby they arrive the very night and shoot him up inside his house. Joe, visits the house the next day and and learns that Clem was actually Anthony Benedetti. He feels that he was indirectly responsible for Clem's death. In grief he goes to Clem's body at the scene of the crime whilst covered on a stretcher. He then begins describing how Clem would be rejoining his wife in heaven and erotically describes her body. This causes an erection to show on the corpse, revealing that Clem is actually alive. Clem reveals that he managed to kill his assailants in a shoot out and that he's faked his death to thwart the mob once again, going under the new alias of Gert. B. Frobe. It's a scene that just so outrageously silly yet believable that it sounds like one of those really good pub stories we hear that's actually based on a true story. It's also the scene that made me a fan of Christopher Walken. It's a pity that Walken hasn't been involved in more comedy films like this as I consider this his greatest role since The Deer Hunter.

Question: Why do some people not like Coldplay?
Answer: As probably the only guy answering this question who actually likes Coldplay I’d like to put forward my theory. There are actually two Coldplays. Old Coldplay Modern Coldplay What is the first thing you noticed about the photos? Old Coldplay shows a young band full of awkward post A-Level graduates who don’t care how geeky they look but seem to enjoy each other’s company and being themselves. Modern Coldplay shows an intensely edited photo of four men who are trying their utmost best to look cool and serious. Everything about the photo screams over saturated, highly commercial and bloated. I sincerely doubt the guys even posed together for the photo but rather had separate photos, photoshopped together. Old Coldplay is alternative rock. Yes they wrote a fair share of ballads. Yes they could be whiny, moody and (as another Quora writer has so artfully suggested) ‘sangfroid’ but there was a meticulous attention to instrumentation and songwriting that you can’t listen to songs like Trouble, Clocks and Shiver and call it pop music. They were definitely popular but they weren’t pop. They wrote intelligent songs but with a fair share of technical bravado on their instruments and innovative yet tasteful sound engineering in the same vein of bands like Radiohead and Doves at the time. All old school Coldplay fans would probably share similar sentiments. Us Coldplay fans looked a lot similar to this when we were growing up. Modern Coldplay is an example of commercial pop music at its worst. Take away the sonic instrumental experimentation and instead put in electronic computer programmer loops and samples. Focus more on marketing, publicity and touring rather than on songwriting, innovation and simple band practicing. Throw in a bunch of cringey, force fed collaborations. Envision a basic formula for their craft and then multiply that formula by 300%. (Studio execs: ‘They’re a bit whiny. Let’s make that lead singer go Ohhh ohh ooo every five seconds. That's what the fans seem to like. And let ‘em write a a shitload of slow piano driven ballads. I think they're a woman's rock band. Let them have that guitar player repeating the same derivative chiming hook. In fact toss one of his hooks into the looping software and we'll rework it for an entire album. How about we let each one of them wear a different color? You know like the Spice Girls. Make it seem like they care about stuff around the world like climate change and fair trade and all that crap.’) This is what a modern day Coldplay fan kinda looks like. And that’s why some people don’t like Coldplay. In my humble opinion.

I'm open minded about it and welcome all opinions.

Question: Was there something you were repeatedly told as a child that made no sense?
Answer: My mother employed a lot of fantasy to keep my brother and I in check when we were young boys. Some of it was harmless. In an effort to keep us safe from getting struck by a car my mother claimed that there was a man who followed us around when we went to school. She said that he reported to her daily whether we asked for someone's help to cross the road or not. I was scared stiff of this mysterious spy who followed me on my way to school. This man who would ring my mother to inform if ever I crossed the road without asking for help. I wondered what he looked like. I wondered how it is I never saw anyone following me. I made sure to ask adults in the area to help me cross the road for fear that spy would ring my mother and I would get the belt later on at home. A question suddenly sprang to mind. I went to my mother and asked, ‘So why doesn't the man just help me cross the road himself?’ She couldn't answer the question and as such the mysterious road crossing spy became a discarded myth. One of the things that she told me as a child that really bothers me to this day was that my father was a dangerous man, a mad monster even. My father suffered from bipolar disorder and as such life with him was somewhat traumatic for her. She was a child of 18 herself when she had my older brother. Around the time my father was untreated in his mental health, his mood swings and uncontrollable behaviour landed him a few times in prison and finally at the mental asylum where he spent 5 years before being treated and released. It was at this time that my mother would tell my brother and I that my father was a horrible individual: that he was mad, bloodthirsty, that he wanted us both dead and if ever we were to see him on the streets that we should run to the nearest police station and hide. My brother and I were legitimately terrified of this man and such a situation. When we heard our friends talk about their loving fathers and all the things they did together we felt hurt and shame. Our father was our dark secret. We remembered little and knew nothing about him except that he was a monster, that he ruined our lives, wrecked our home and that he wanted to harm us, according to our mother of course. This was the mindset for much of my preteens. Then one day, at the age of 11 I was walking home after school and saw from afar a tall man leave my home and enter a taxi. My mother was standing there waving goodbye to him. I asked her who that was. She said in a jolly voice that I had just missed getting to see my father. She spoke about all the things that he had been through and that he was now a taxi driver and was living at a friend's house for the time being until he got his life in order. She said that he would come the following weekend to carry my brother and I out. To carry us out? But he's a mad monster? I couldn't speak the words in my mind. Apparently my mother had completely forgotten all the stuff that she said about him. She had forgotten that she had conditioned us to fear and hate him. In just one sentence she demonstrated that she lied to me all my life and that all the shame, anxiety and neuroses that I felt towards my father was not a big deal, just the words of a scorned, overprotective mother. My father re-entered our lives around that time but through years of conditioning I have never been able to see him as ‘father’ or ‘daddy’ but as some guy named Trevor. As a father myself I would urge all parents to never try to condition your children to hate/fear the other parent for such a situation. Tell your children the truth and let them develop their own conclusion in time. Your children hang on to your words as the ultimate truth and when they get older and they realize that they've been lied to all their lives, you will be seen as the mad monster from that moment on.

Question: What did you find out about your teacher that shocked you?
Answer: It's not so much what I found out. It's how he reacted to something. My primary school teacher, Mr. Young, was the most exemplary educator I've ever encountered. My entire class at St. Joseph Boys Roman Catholic loved him. He didn't just teach. He conversed with us. His words went directly into our hearts as all his lessons seemed inspired and were riveting. He would also speak to us on our level, whether formal or informal. We could have a conversation, or even make joke with him and not fear being judged or offending him, as long as we spoke with respect. He was open to discuss any thing we found confusing with the Bible during religious instruction periods. We would even laugh at some of the silliness. ‘How did Adam and Eve populate the whole world? Wouldn't incest have to occur?’ ‘If Judas was meant to betray Jesus then why is he a bad person if it was all God's plan?’ ‘How did all those animals fit on Noah's Ark?’ Mr. Young loved to address these questions and would explain that they were all allegories. He even encouraged us to question each Old Testament story scientifically. He liked when we found humour in them as long as we didn't mock them. Periodically we went to the nearby Roman Catholic church for Communion. I was not yet confirmed as a Catholic but was to be confirmed soon in a special ceremony. I watched as all the boys lined up to recieve the blood and body of Christ. It always fascinated me as to what that was like. What did that little white flake l taste like and what about that wine in that cool chalice? Would I get drunk after drinking it? To the other boys it was not a big deal. A few of them even stated that they wished they didn't have to eat and drink that stuff. I was curious for the experience. My friend Kevin asked me why I wasn't going up for Communion. Wasn't I confirmed already? I told him I wasn't confirmed yet, that the confirmation ceremony was a few weeks away. Kevin was also a transfer student and was one of the ‘slower’ students in class. ‘Then you're practically confirmed already. Just go and get it.’ I took what he said into consideration. ‘But what do I say?’ ‘The priest will mumble some stuff. Just say Amen to everything he says.’ It sounded simple enough. I did as was told. The old priest looked bored and ready to sleep when I came up to him. He mumbled something about body and blood of Christ. I muttered Amen a few times and avoided his eyes. He put the chalice to my mouth and I could barely get a sip before he pulled away. He then gave me the wafer that tasted rather stale and with that the experience was over in an anticlimactic manner. That is until after a few hours while in lunch period I heard Mr. Young was furious and wanted to speak to me immediately. I went into the classroom and saw him with a grim look on his face that was very unlike him. He told me that he saw me taking Communion even though we both knew that I wasn't yet confirmed. He demanded to know why I went for Communion. I blabbered something about Kevin telling me it's alright. ‘You’re listening to Kevin!’ Mr Young roared. He then gave me a look that implied that I ought to now better than to listen to one of the slowest students in class. I almost fell backwards. He was bristling with rage. He had never yelled before. This was serious. ‘Do you think it is right for you to come and mock God like this?’ I shook my head no. I could feel tears welling up in my eyes. ‘Would you like you be transferred back to your old school? I can call your mother right now and tell her the news.’ ‘No,’ I cried, ‘Please I'm sorry.’ He watched the tears streaming down my face and dismissed me. Outside a group of boys from my class waited to see what was the matter. None of them had seen Mr. Young behave like that before. They asked whether I was getting kicked out of the school. I tried to make a joke out of it and said that Mr. Young was angry because I farted when I went for up to the priest but it was sorted out now. All went back to normal. Years later I think about it and I'm shocked. I am still very much a Christian but I don't maintain the strict orthodox beliefs that I was raised in. It bothered me that an inspiring and intelligent man like Mr. Young could transform into such a thick headed zealot over something so trivial Iike a common Communion ceremony. Mr. Young who laughed with us at some of the ridiculous stories of the Old Testament and advised us to use science as well as well as faith to solve problems could never be such a mean and spiteful person. I hypothesised a solution to this almost 30 years later. I believe that Mr. Young couldn't have given a fart about what I had done that day or Holy Communion or quite possibly even the Catholic church for that matter. The problem was his job would've been on the line if his boys were seen to be making public mockery of Roman Catholic ceremony. It was simply another ‘read between the lines’ situation with Mr. Young and I. Whatever Mr. Young and the class said or did in our classroom was confidential among ourselves but when we went to church we were to be good and saintly little boys who adhered to strict Catholic customs regardless how senseless and pedantic. I can sympathise with Mr. Young's dilemma and forgive how he behaved but I would say without a doubt if I were in his shoes I would not have reacted the way he did or make such a big deal about it.

Question: What do Hollywood movies get wrong about your country?
Answer: Trinidad doesn't have a major presence in Hollywood films so I base this answer on ‘The Caribbean’ as a whole. According to Hollywood. The Caribbean: Is just one big major tourist destination. Things like factories, refineries, shipping companies etc just do not exist. People don't work. They just laze about in the porch of their brightly coloured, near collapsing, one bedroom hut and watch the goats chewing grass. Every adult male knows how to swim, fish, hunt and traverse for days through the coasts and mountains with nothing but a cutlass (machete) a spliff in their mouth and an old hand radio playing ‘Jamming’ by Bob Marley on repeat. Only black people live in the Caribbean. Any Indian, Chinese or middle eastern person is just a passing merchant. The entire Caribbean is English speaking. Haiti does not count. Haiti is not the Caribbean. Haiti is Haiti. The same goes for Cuba. Cuba is not the Caribbean. Cuba is Castro-land. Everybody here is happy and smiling with nothing to do but entertain tourists all day without expecting anything in return. The Caribbean is paradise. We suck up a lot and we tend to cut corners and scheme if unsupervised. Oddly enough at the same time we are astoundingly loyal. (This stereotype is actually quite true). Besides nice beaches and hotels we don't have any other resources besides bananas, coconuts and Rastafarian merch and music. It's always sunny in the Caribbean. The hurricane season simply does not exist.

Question: What is the "honeymoon phase" in a relationship and why do some couples maintain it while others do not?
Answer: Something called a ‘phase’ cannot be maintained. The honeymoon phase is that brief period in many (if not most) relationships whereby both persons are driven purely by blissful attraction to the extent of which either party can see little to no wrong with their significant other and feel emotionally inclined to spend as much time as possible with that person. It is that so-called feeling of love that songs and poems are written about in regards to hearts racing, breaths being taken away, will die for that person etc. etc. After a while the feeling dissipates and each person recognizes the other for all their flaws and weaknesses rather than see them on a pedestal they now see them for who they really are rather than who they would've liked them to be. Prince Charming suddenly reveals himself to be a regular guy who likes to sit around and drink beers with his buddies and is a bit of a mama’s boy and the woman of your dreams can’t stop complaining about the speck of dust you keep bringing into her house. When the honeymoon phase is over in many cases the relationship begins to crumble as well. Some people look beyond the faults and try to keep the relationship going by focusing on all the positive aspects of the significant other but I am yet to hear of any long-term couple who claim that they have never come out of the honeymoon phase. The honeymoon phase is driven purely be emotions. True love is governed by dedication and loyalty and as such there are many couples out there who have been happily married for decades and never even had a ‘honeymoon phase’ to begin with.

Question: What is the common parenting mistake and how can they rectify that?
Answer: The worst parenting mistake is not showing any genuine love to your children. The most common parenting mistake ironically is to constantly be selflessly giving to them. I see it more as a source of vanity and pride rather than of genuine love. I have three relatives who are from such a household. Their parents are well-off and stable with the mother supplying them an abundance of love and the father an abundance of money whenever the time calls. All three of them are in their 40s and do not live in the same country as their parents. They come to see their parents every Christmas as a tradition. This sounds nice of them, for all three of them to arrange a date to arrive and stay at the family home, plane tickets etc. In reality their parents are the ones who see to that. The parents have been paying for their children to come see them for Christmas for over twenty years. The parents arrange the date, the tickets and additional expenses that their 40 something year old children may accrue during their stay. Some readers may not see a problem with this. If you can afford it, why not treat your kids, especially during the Christmas? My answer to them is that it has nothing to do with money. It has to do with principle. No one should have to pay to see their grown children once a year. If your kids really cared about you they would come on their own volition and expense, not wait for daddy to purchase highly inflated Christmas flights. Not only this but the parents (both in their 70s) are the one to pick them up upon arrival and drop them off for departure. The parents also provide them with a New Year's vacation to a hotel every year and pay all expenses associated with it. The parents cook meals, carry them out for lunch/dinner and arrange all forms of planning and entertainment. To say that their kids are somewhat spoiled would be quite an understatement. To say that their kids were concerned about their parents descent into old age, loss of movement/stamina and increasing loneliness would be a great exaggeration. This arrangement is likely to continue until one of their parents die of which I'm certain the other parent would have to buy their tickets so they can attend the funeral. When you train your kids that they can receive a constant supply of love without them having to reciprocate you are training them to expect love without having to reciprocate. This is almost as damaging as showing no love at all.

Question: What is the best case of “You just picked a fight with the wrong person” that you've witnessed?
Answer: Some years ago I worked in a pretty rough school in a pretty rough neighborhood. I worked in the school library which wasn’t really a popular hangout for the dangerous kids. At least that's what I thought. There were these two boys, Jesse and Adrian who would usually remain in the library well after school hours. Jesse (16) came from a nearby projects. He was athletic and strong. He worked construction on weekends to help his family. He was around 6’2 and sinewy. Just imagine a younger Deontay Wilder without the facial hair and you had Jesse. Adrian was 16 also. He was 5’9, stocky and a video game enthusiast. He wore glasses, had a silly smile with a chipped front tooth and a prominent paunch, quite unusual for a boy his age. Just imagine Emmitt Smith with glasses and you had Adrian. Both of them couldn’t be more opposite. Jesse was thoughtful and polite. He didn’t talk much but when he did it was usually of a philosophical nature. He had a lot of ambition and was determined to make it in life. Adrian was aloof and untethered. He talked a lot and when he did it was always a lot of shit. It seemed all he knew in life were action movies, anime and video games. He had zero ambition. He cared nothing for his future, let alone his school work. Jesse came after school to the library to spend quality time with his girlfriend every once in a while. Adrian came to the library every day to play Halo and Quake III on the library computers with his gamer buddies or by himself. Jesse would come and chat with his girl in private. He never bothered anyone and if we saw any handsy-pansy going on we spoke to him about it and he would obey. Adrian would sometimes be a nuisance. Video games were not allowed but we would give the boys a chance after school hours if they behaved themselves and obeyed us. Adrian would usually overdo it and have us shut off the computers and send him home. One particular evening Jesse was alone in the library studying for the upcoming end of term exams. His girlfriend and him were going through some problems that day so he was alone and not in the best of moods. Adrian came solo as well to play video games. We told him no. He then told us he wanted to finish his assignment on the computer. We allowed him but every few minutes we took our eyes off him he would put on his video games. We could not allow this especially as exams drew near. We told him if we caught him one more time he would not only have to leave but be banned for the rest of the term. All of this childishness from Adrian was starting to get on Jesse's nerves. Some minutes after our final warning Jesse observed that Adrian was playing a juvenile video game from a web browser. He had the web page minimized at a corner of the screen to hide it from being seen. Jesse took it upon himself to deal with Adrian. Before we could say anything Jesse grabbed the mouse from Adrian’s hand and flung it aside. He then rolled Adrian and his chair away from the computer and spun it around to face him. Jesse looked as though he was going to pull Adrian off the chair by the collar. It was Jesse's biggest mistake. He severely underestimated how strong Adrian was. Adrian rose from his seat and fired two tremendous hooks, left and right, onto Jesse’s cheek and head. I could feel the power from those punches by just looking at them and I knew that the fight was over before it even began. Jesse struggled to keep to his feet and attempted to wrestle Adrian to the ground. It was no good. The punches had him dazed. Adrian easily shook him off and was about to land some more until he saw myself and my coworker coming to subdue him. Adrian had momentarily transformed from a goofy nerd into Mike Tyson for a few seconds. He left the scene immediately. We had to subdue Jesse who claimed that he was going after Adrian to teach him a lesson for the ‘sucker punch.’ We all knew that was just talk. Jesse didn't want to face that beast again. No one in their right mind would. Jesse didn't report the matter and requested the same of us, clearly due to embarrassment. With his naturally forgiving nature Jesse had no hard feelings and the boys developed a mutual respect after. Jesse graduated from the school with some decent grades and works as a successful salesman and party promoter. Adrian graduated from the school with nothing but a superb left and right hook. I truly hope he used his power to good use.

Question: What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"?
Answer: I worked with a lady in her early 40s at a pizza restaurant. She was just a ordinary grunt like the rest of us. She aspired to be a supervisor but what held her back was that she had 6 kids, three, in their late teens/early adulthood for one father, another two of toddler age for another father and a baby for her recent boyfriend. This domestic situation made it hard for her punctuality and regularity at work as there was always a babysitting issue or child maintenance issue that needed resolving with her two exes. Her current boyfriend was no supportive stalwart himself as practically once every week she would stop her duties to go outside the restaurant to have long and intense arguments with him on the phone in regards to his inability to come pick her up that evening or various other disagreements that they had. In person the boyfriend had a nasty, arrogant attitude and seemed to care only for casual sex, his car and for her to keep his baby away from her older kids whom they all shared a mutual dislike with one another. She lived with her two toddlers and her baby at her father's house which was shared with several other siblings of similar circumstance. With that there was a lot of family fighting in regards to space and ownership. To put it bluntly she lived in a world of shit. Given the circumstances it seemed unlikely that she would be unable break free from the poverty and drudgery any time soon. I would feel the greatest sympathy for her and try my best to help her at work in any regards. That is until that fateful day when I saw her rubbing her stomach and smiling to herself. ‘Looks like you're ready for another one (baby)’ I said jokingly. She smiled and said that she and her current boyfriend (the arrogant dickhead) was trying for another baby. They had a girl and now he wanted a boy. ‘Are you serious?’ I said. I was flabbergasted that she was saying this so casually. It was as if she suddenly reverted back to a naive 16 yr old who found her first love and was no longer a middle aged woman with 6 children and a truckload of problems. One of my biggest flaws is that sometimes I can't keep my opinions to myself. ‘But you have 6 kids already!’ For a second she came out of her dream and reverted back to reality. She glared at me angrily for a split second .Then she returned to her child like persona and replied, ‘Children are a blessing.’ ‘Children are a blessing when you can afford to raise them right and give them the love and attention they need.’ Those words just came out of me in very emphatic tone. As a father of one (I worked part time at the restaurant) I was struggling to survive, working two jobs to ensure that my daughter had a future and to ensure all of my free time was dedicated to her. This lady worked one job and was dependent on family, friends and the Government to assist with any shortcomings she encountered, which seemed to be every day. I could not relate at all to what she was saying. She glared at me again and the conversation ended. An hour later I'm called into the manager's office. Apparently she got so angry she complained to the manager that I was being emotionally abusive, chauvinistic (the restaurant was 90% female staff) and stuck my nose in other people's business. She even told the manager that my words were so hurtful she felt overcome with hurt that she was considering taking a sick day and leaving. I sat and nodded in silence. I was the given a warning and sent out of the office. I learned a sad but valuable lesson that day: Some people are simply destined for a life of hardship and misery through their own stubborn mentality and poor choices. So to answer the question What screams "I make terrible financial decisions!"?: People who get offended by the truth.

Question: What is the lowest probability event you have personally witnessed?
Answer: I did a degree in Agribusiness when I attended University. Nutrition and Dietetics students shared the Faculty with us and among the students of N&D was a guy named Gandhi. Gandhi was a short, portly and ambiguously gay chatterbox. He was exceptionally kind and friendly but he loved to have long frivolous conversations that ranged from anything from popular soap operas to university gossip. As an evening student most of my classmates were, oddly enough, middle-aged working women, many of them single mothers and a few of them were grandmothers. Gandhi would come over to our area and chat with us and many of these ladies took an instant liking to him. I, on the other hand, found him a bit too loud, clingy and as mentioned earlier frivolous. One day, my fellow Agribusiness students and I were waiting for a bus. We were to go on a cross country field trip. Gandhi was hanging out with us while we waited and being his usual loud and silly self. One of the students didn't show up so there was room for one on the bus. Gandhi speculated whether the lecturer would allow him to come on the trip even though he wasn't an Agribusiness student. When the bus arrived with the lecturer, Gandhi’s lady friends immediately begged for him to be allowed on the trip. Kind and affable, the lecturer said that since he was in the same faculty he couldn't see it being a problem since there was room for one more. We all boarded the bus. Through chance Gandhi got a seat next to me and from the moment the bus took off and the 6 hrs that followed Gandhi yapped his mouth non-stop. I could not enjoy a single moment of silence to enjoy the sights and sounds with this silly, little man next to me going off on every irrelevant topic that a human could think of during a cross country road trip. To say that my experience was somewhat diminished would be an understatement. Two years after graduating from university my aunt invites me to a trip to Dominica organized by a forestry conservation group. The conservation group was, oddly enough, comprised mostly of middle-aged women and a few grandmothers. On the first day we were to go to a cross country trip on a bus around the little island. Some of the group had opted out of the trip in favour of doing some shopping in the capital Roseau or just relaxing in the hotel. As such I had a seat free to myself next to me. While the bus was driving I was reminded of the cross country trip with Gandhi. The bus driver first took us to the the nearest shops for those who still needed to purchase drinks or snacks. We all went into a little grocery. While browsing the shelves I almost froze when I heard a familiar voice. ‘Elijah?’ it said, ‘What are you doing in Dominica?’ I turned around to see none other than Gandhi himself, like a portly imp-genie who manifests himself whenever one thought about him. Surprised to chance another Trinidadian in the country the group asked me if this was my friend. ‘Uh….’ I said not knowing how to answer that question and feeling a sense of dread, ‘Yeah?’ Gandhi filled them in with the details. I had only just thought about him a few minutes ago and here he was in front of me, in a different country. What were the chances? Here's where it gets even more interesting. Gandhi queried as to what we were doing and they told him of the cross country trip. ‘Oh my God’ I thought. ‘You think maybe I could come?’ Gandhi asked, ‘If it's a matter of money I could pay.’ ‘I don't see why not,’ said our group leader who had taken an instant liking of him. ‘Dont worry,’ she continued, ‘The bus has been already paid for. We have room.’ ‘No f**king way,’ I told myself. Filing back into the bus I hoped to God one of the group members would decide to sit next to me this time. I eyed them all down as they entered, with warm looks, in the vain hope that they change their previous seat and sit to my side, preventing Gandhi from sitting next to me once again. As per fate, that was not to be. Gandhi was the last to enter the bus. He saw my empty seat and immediately sat next to me. I stared at him in a state of wonder and disbelief. I was expecting him to feel the same way. What were the odds of him getting on board a bus that he wasn't meant to be on, with a similar demographic of people, on a similar cross country trip and seated next to the same person on an entirely different country? It was mind-blowing to me. Unfortunately none of this registered in Gandhi's mind. None of this seemed in the least bit strange or fantastic. He simply resumed his barrage of idle banter and irrelevancy for the next four hours.

Question: What screams "I'm rich, but I have no class"?
Answer: Some years ago I was at a supermarket looking to pick up a drink. Strangely enough the clothes I wore was similar to the uniform that the workers wore. After I cashed I stood looking at some snacks near a cashier. A lady who looked well-to-do had finished cashing for a heaping trolley of goods and was making ‘Psst, Psst’ noises in my direction. I looked at her. She motioned with her head that her trolley was ready to be carted out. ‘It’s the white X-Trail on the right,’ she said nonchalantly. She apparently thought I was a worker-boy and wanted me to carry her stuff out for her and help her load it into her vehicle. I eyed the cashier who gave me faint, knowing smile. I decided to play along. I took her trolley and rolled off with it. The lady walked a few paces behind me staring at me with more solemnity than a prison guard. It was as if she didn't want to be near me and at the same time wanted to make sure I didn't steal any of her stuff To complete the disguise of a lowly grocery-boy I attempted to make friendly small talk. ‘Looks like it's gonna have some serious rain later.’ She didn't answer. She just kept staring at me and keeping a few feet behind me. The probability that she was just a mean, old rich twat was getting higher and higher. I decided to administer one more test. All of a sudden I stopped the cart, looked at my watch and said, ‘Hey it's time for my lunch date. Later.’ I then walked a few paces away from her and her trolley and pretended to make a phone call. ‘Excuse me!’ she said with venom on her tongue. ‘Hey I'm on the phone,’ I said with gusto at her and gestured a finger to my mouth. I tried my best not to burst out in laughter. One of the workers who kept guard near the entrance door saw all this. He himself tried not to laugh. She went up to him. ‘What’s that boy's name?’ ‘I dunno’ the man replied, stifling a chuckle. ‘Is he stupid or something?’ she spat, ‘Tell him to come back and get my stuff.’ It was so beautiful to watch. I couldn't have responded better than how that guy did. ‘I think you may have to tell him yourself. He doesn't work here.’ There was a silence and a moment of comprehension then bitter acceptance. With a haughty face she proceeded to silently carry her trolley by herself pretending as though nothing happened. To add salt to the wound as she passed me I yelled, ‘Hey, you need any help with that?’ She passed me without a word or a glance.

Question: What do you think of the album Titanic Rising by Weyes Blood?
Answer: I think it's one of the best albums of the 21st century thus far. Titanic Rising has singlehandedly restored my faith in the music industry's ability to still churn out works of art. I've literally spent the entire month of October trying to get ‘Andromeda’ out of my head (in a good way). Titanic Rising is a well-crafted song cycle album consisting of 10 songs that explores topics ranging from heartache to the decline of modern civilization. Her songwriting is poetic and the combination of her smooth, elegaic voice with that of her operatic back up singer creates a warm tone throughout the album. Natalie Mering aka Weyes Blood looks and sounds like she teleported right out of the Golden Age of singer-songwriters of the 70s but with a style of her own. One can't fail to notice the influence of artists such as Joni Mitchell, Moby Grape, George Harrison and even more contemporary artists like Enya and Aimee Mann in her songs. Highlights for me include A Lot's Gonna Change, Andromeda, Wild Time and Picture Me Better which is a sweet country tinged prayer that closes the album to a classically rendered reprise of A Lot's Gonna Changed called Nearer to Thee. I was highly impressed listening to this album from the very first listen (which is rare for me). I truly love this album and I wish more people would see the talent of this truly under appreciated young lady. My rating: 8.5 out of 10.

Question: What are some plot holes in some of famous movies?
Answer: Recently rewatched the 2009 Star Trek film. Don't get me wrong I absolutely love this movie. I think by a long shot it is the greatest reimagining of a popular series and one of the greatest sci-fi adventures of the 21st century. However this part of the plot sticks out like a sore thumb for me. Nero, an angry and embittered Romulan from the future enacts revenge on Spock and his Vulcan race for not being able to save his planet Romulus. With his massive ship he drills a hole into the core of planet Vulcan and inserts ‘red matter’ into the core. This creates a black hole that absorbs the planet committing genocide upon the 6 billion inhabitant Vulcan race (apart from Spock, his father and a few ‘elders’). This grim aspect of the plot takes the normally light-hearted Star Trek to a whole new level of ‘shit just got serious’ seriousness. However, something about these Vulcans just don't add up. The Planet Vulcan Spock and the Vulcan race are supposed to be one of the most intelligent race of beings in the galaxy. One of their biggest traits is to maintain logic over emotion at all times. They store and process information at a volume and speed exponentially greater than humans, they are adept at learning and transmitting knowledge and their analytical skills and foresight would make living Chess legend Magnus Carlsen look like a baboon playing with his toy. Yet look at where they live. This shithole is planet Vulcan. As you can see it is a wasteland full of rocks and sand. As brilliant as these Vulcans are, their architecture looks like a bombed out Cairo at best. Vulcans are humanoid. They need food, water and sex to procreate. They admire beauty, they fall in love and they have something of a sense of humour. Their planet looks to be 20% water within a huge, dry continent devoid of vegetation of any sort. How did their population manage to reach six billion living on a hot, arid and infertile planet? Why did they never decided to colonize a more agreeable and unoccupied planet? I'm pretty sure the Federation would allow it. If they are so advanced in technology why can't they properly develop their planet and find means of increasing and distributing their water supply or getting some trees to grow? Are the Vulcan's really that smart? The Vulcans have the ability to create black holes at an instant yet they have zero defense against Romulan ships blasting holes deep into the core of their planet. They have no planetary shield, no defense satellite, no space army, they don't even have ships to escort their people off the planet. They depend entirely on Starfleet to repel the enemy and evacuate the people. Yet we're supposed to believe them to be creatures of the highest logic. The Vulcans have sent a distress call to Starfleet about their planet being attacked. I'm guessing the distress call was a bit like this: ‘Hey bros send help. Some idiot is drilling a hole into our crappy planet. It's making a lot of noise and really annoying.’ ‘Hey sorry. Forgot to warn you that they have a massive ship, 50 times bigger than the biggest Starfleet warship and using technology and weaponry that is so powerful that it most likely comes from the future. ‘Hope you sent warships and the Starfleet army and not just your student trainees and scout ships…..you did! Crap.’ ‘We’ll just go offer our prayers to our giant stone idols in our primitive church cave where you can't get a signal to beam us to safety.’ ‘If anything just send Spock to come get us.’ That aspect of the film is so utterly ludicrous that it takes me out of the movie a tad bit. Question: What did the "weird" kid in your high school do that made them considered weird?
Answer: When I did my A Levels the first person I sat down next to and made conversation with was a guy everyone called Choke-O-Lingo. For the sake of privacy and convenience I'll refer to him as Jim I thought it was the weirdest name ever and when I heard all the kids in class call him by that name at first I laughed and thought it was some sort of nerdy nickname like ‘Screech’ or ‘Booger.’ He did strike me as a nerd in the classic sense. I looked at his notebook and saw that that was his actual surname (spelled Chookolingo). Before that day I had never heard of such a funny sounding name. He also had a sister who was in the same class with us. They weren't twins so I assumed that Jim must have been kept down a year or more. This was the early 00s when baggy jeans, sneakers, chain wallets, spiky hair with dyed tips were the thing for boys. Handkerchief tops, denim skirts and shiny leatherette pants were the thing for girls. Jim and his sister always looked as though a wormhole opened up in front of them as they were on their way to church in the early 60s and transported them 40 years into the future. . Jim was short, wiry and quite hairy. At 18 he had more chest hair than the rest of boys in class put together. He wore glasses, washed out clothes and usually wore a look in his face that reminded me of hens when they find a comfortable nook to sit and lay. He spoke affably but in a rushed, breathless manner that was like a cross between Barney Rubble of The Flintsones and Jeff Daniel's character Harry from the film Dumb and Dumber. Now all of this isn't weird per se. It just makes him a bit of a character. What made him weird was whenever someone tried to have a conversation with him. Jim either had severe anxiety as well as respiratory problems or he was just a weird guy to talk to because whenever one approached him to chat he would give a terrified look. Within a few minutes of awkward conversation he would make noise that sounded as though he was gasping for breath yet he didn't suffer from any sort of asthma. If you got distracted by someone else while talking to him he would run off. Mind you, he was not anti-social. He enjoyed playing games of chess, Pokémon and Yu-Gi-Oh with the other boys. He was a film buff and anime lover and he would join others when having group conversations even though he had practically nothing to contribute to the conversation. However while doing the above if one attempted to talk to him he would seem to panic like a hunted animal, start making his gasping noises and evade if given the chance. His sister never demonstrated any these habits. She was the dictionary definition of the smiling go-getter. She was very popular with the teachers, a straight-A student and in any academic group/club in the school she was certain to be a member if not the President. Whenever anyone asked her why her brother acted so weird and timid with the gasping noises and running off she would simply smile even broader but would never give an explanation. Poor Jim. For the entire duration of our A Levels he became something of a non-entity. No matter how everyone tried to get him out of his shell he just couldn't find it in him to conquer whatever fear and anxiety he had about the humans around him. Many times we would hear his name mention during roll call and it would sometimes be a startling reminder that he existed. He spent the entire duration of his school years tagging behind his sister and her friends of whom he served as a convenient lunch getter/bag carrier. He seems to be happy and doing well regardless. Question: What is the strangest thing a truck driver has seen while driving?
Answer: I'm cheating a bit. It was a pickup truck but I was hauling a long distance furniture delivery so technically it still counts. My loader Chris and I were on the highway when suddenly a spooked chicken ran across the road in front of us. I'm a soft hearted person by nature so my first instinct was to try and avoid it. As if reading my mind, Chris sternly told me to hit it. He had always advised me that, while driving full speed on the highway, never try to avoid hitting animals that step in front of you, be it a cat, dog or bird. He knew of people who got killed in smash ups trying to avoid hitting the random stray dog on the highway. I did as he advised and the chicken collided with the pick up at a velocity that surely killed it. ‘Pull to the side’ said Chris. He wanted to collect the dead bird to clean and cook when he got home later. I did as told, parked on the shoulder and reversed closer to where the dead bird lay. Chris got out to retrieve his spoils but after a minute he came back with an odd look on his face. ‘What?’ I said. He told me that I needed to see it for myself. I went with him to the bird and looked at it. Everything looked alright. Except for the fact that the bird was in a state whereby it had to have been dead for several hours. Its face and skin had that grey look of being long dead and there were ants coming out of its beak and an eyeless socket. ‘This can't be the chicken that we hit!’ I said. ‘It has to be another chicken that we hit! This one's already dead.’ Chris demonstrated to me that this was the exact location where we struck the chicken. There were feathers that got dislodged from the impact nearby that matched with our speckled bird. It was indeed our chicken. ‘This doesn't make any sense.’ I said stupified. Chris didn't think much about it. He was more focused on the disappointment that his roadkill was inedible. Zombie chickens crossing the road didn't seem to be of any concern to him. To this day I have no idea as to what could poossibly explain that supernatural event.

Question: What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class"?
Answer: My cousin David lived for two years in Trinidad after his upper-middle class parents decided to return to their homeland to retire. David did his SATs at ISPS (International School of Port of Spain), a school which caters to mostly foreign upper-middle/upper class students. It was there that he befriended Carlos. Carlos was a Venezuelan who had an immense stroke of luck. Carlos came from a very poor family in Venezuela and was said to be adopted on a charitable impulse by a rich Texas oil man. Carlos’ foster father didn't intend to have much of a relationship with him but rather wanted to make a point of turning Carlos' life around. He shipped Carlos off to Trinidad and ISPS and left with him a sizable monthly allowance to finish his SATs and pursue a college degree. It was there that Carlos met my cousin David. David did not like Carlos in the least bit. Carlos was the biggest show-off/braggart at ISPS. His first action upon being set to his own devices was to rent a furnished luxury apartment in Goodwood Park (the Beverly Hills of Trinidad). With this apartment he gained fame for hosting weekly parties for his fellow schoolmates laden with weed and alcohol. Like most of Carlos' ‘friends’ David befriended Carlos solely for the opportunity to be invited to these parties. Carlos' attendance at school and his grades soured but he didn't care. He took out a Range Rover and after a drunken night racing along the North Coast he crashed the vehicle and had it wrote off. It was a miracle that he survived and ought to have been an epiphany to change his ways. He didn't. His two years in ISPS were spent indulging, fraternising, boasting, drinking, smoking, chasing girls and maintaining the image of being the most popular student at ISPS. He wasn't the most popular. He was the most infamous. It was hard to find someone who truly liked him. I would include myself in that category. Once when I was in a restaurant with David, Carlos and a few of David's friends, I realized that I had no money for a meal. I made a joke about it. I told everyone that I would be taxing everyone 5% of their meal for charity as I was broke at the moment. Everyone laughed except Carlos who stared at me in horror as though I cursed God and my mother in one sentence. ‘Don’t go anywhere if you don't have any mah-nee!’ Carlos admonished towards me in a stern Venezuelan accent. It was strange how he was so deeply offended by someone near him making a joke about not having money and begging. Everyone stopped laughing. David paid for my meal making sure Carlos didn't notice. Carlos graduated with failing grades and soon found that his funds were depleted. He would guilt trip several of his ‘friends’ for lodging, reminding them of all that he lavished upon them. He reassured them that his foster father was going to send for him to return to the US. This of course was discovered to be a lie, his foster father had washed his hand of an adult Carlos. He found himself broke and homeless. Carlos still lives in Trinidad. He works an ordinary job and rents an unimpressive furniture-less apartment that is above his means. To this day he still brags about his brief period of wealth. His former colleagues take great pains avoiding him whenever they are aware he is around. Otherwise he would stop them in their tracks to entertain lengthy one-sided discussions about the good old days and would inveigle them to grab some drinks in a fancy pub in which they would listen to his ridiculous plans to score big, be constantly reminded of how much he did for their enjoyment at ISPS and then be forced to pay for the bill that he ran up but can't afford with the promise that ‘Drinks are on me next time amigo.’ Such is the life of Carlos. So to answer the question ‘What screams "I'm pretending to be upper class?”’ People like Carlos.

Question: What is the luckiest thing that happened to you?
Answer: Over twenty years ago I was a mere lad of 17 and staying at a cousin's house for the holidays. My aunt was fed up of us staying in the living room all day playing video games and sent us to walk the dogs. The area was a very safe upper middle class location fringed by mountains and a picturesque golf course nearby. My brother, myself and our cousin walked the quiet road calmly discussing our victories in the gaming world when suddenly we heard the ferocious growling and snapping of a giant pitbull which had broken off its owner’s iron chain and was heading towards us in a mad fury, saliva dripping from its mouth. We stood frozen, all three of us knowing fully well that we were going to get mauled. The minute the dog's feet touched the road a speeding pickup came out of nowhere knocked it on the head. The sound of the hit was loud and blood curdling. It literally sounded like a car crash. The force was enough to give instant death to a human yet the dog managed to run back to its house. The driver sped off without even a moment's thought as to what just happened. It was almost as though Jesus Himself was driving that pickup that saved us from getting severely mauled. We stood there petrified, not knowing what to do or say. Should we quickly head back home? Should we query with the owner as to whether the dog was alive? Should we make a report to the police? None of these logical things we did. Instead we had an argument as to whether the dog was alive or not, if it was, whether it was severely concussed or just fine and whether the skull of a pitbull was tougher than that of a human. My cousin, a lover of physics, then made an argument as to whether a pitbull as such, running at 130km an hour could ram into and overturn a small car. I opted out of this argument and took some time reflecting on the poor dog. I'm glad to be unscarred but to this day I hope the bugger didnt suffer too much.

Question: What is the lamest “benefit” you’ve been offered by an employer?
Answer: At Papa John’s Pizza (Trinidad) I was getting fed up that they weren't hiring the sufficient amount of staff to properly run the store. Along with doing bike deliveries I also cashed, took phone calls, entered orders, swept, mopped and emptied garbage. They kept a skeleton staff of 3 workers per shift and whenever they had to pay overtime they grumbled and wanted explanations as to why. Frustrated and fatigued I applied for Domino’s (Trinidad) Pizza delivery. This is how snippets of the conversation went during the interview. Interview Lady: We pay the highest hourly rate of all pizza restaurants. $21(TTD) per hour. Me: Papa John's paid $20 an hour. This is just a dollar more. Lady: Yes! The highest rate for delivery riders in the country! Lady: When you come to the restaurant you’ll be happy to see that you'll be getting so much deliveries. Endless deliveries! Me: How much do I get paid per delivery? Lady: $7 per delivery! Me: That's the lowest delivery payment of all the pizza restaurants. Lady: Yes but you'll be doing so many deliveries, getting so much tips that it wouldn't matter. (I later found out that Domino's charged customers $20 for delivery, the highest delivery charge of all fast food restaurants in the country. They paid the driver $7 out of the $20 charge and the restaurant pocketed the remaining $13 for themselves.) Me: What are the closing hours? Lady: 10:30pm. Me: You mean like only on Fridays and Saturdays? Lady: No every day. Me: Thats a bit late and taxis round here stop working around 8pm. Any transport provided for me to get home? Lady: No. Me: Will I be able to use the Domino's motorcycle to get home? (I was allowed this benefit in a previous restaurant I worked that had this same issue) Lady: No. Me: Can I leave earlier then? Lady: Of course. Due to your transport situation we’ll allow you to leave 10 minutes earlier! Lady: We are a very flexible organization. Me: How so? (inwardly groaning, expecting more bullshit) Lady: We give you the choice to work either as contracted or non-contracted. Me: What does that mean? Lady: Contracted means that you work somewhat as a permanent staff. You can work all the overtime hours you want. However overtime would be paid at the usual rate of $21 an hour. No time and a half. The same applies for public holidays. Non contracted is like temporary staff. We pay the usual time and a half for overtime but as you are non contracted you don't get overtime hours as we send you home after you've made your 40hrs a week. We don't allow you to work on holidays so you basically get your flat salary every week whereas with a contract you are allowed more hours. Me: More hours at the same rate? Lady: Yes. Me: Wouldn't that be a lose-lose situation? Lady: No. It's a win-win! Me: Am I entitled to a free meal? Lady: No. Me: And the uniform? Lady: We are the only pizza restaurant that provides free uniforms for staff? Me: How many uniforms? Lady: Two free Domino's shirts and a cap. We are having them laundered after being returned by a delivery driver who recently left. Me: You're giving me a guy's used clothes? No: No. She only used them for two days. They're practically new. Me: You're giving me used female clothing? Lady: It's a free uniform! Suffice to say I instantly and humbly returned to Papa John's and their skeleton staff. Edit: So as not to confuse anyone else, all rates here are in Trinidad dollars and not US. Approx 7TT = 1US. Edit: Not the first time a fast food restaurant tried to pull a fast one on its workers. Read here how one restaurant tried to borrow money from its workers in disguise.
