They bought a large house together in a picturesque neighborhood called Cascade. Things were definitely not as happy as it appears in the above photos. Grandfather was abusive with untreated manic depression/bipolar symtoms. It was said by my family that he never truly loved my grandmother. His original goal was to find a white wife (as was the norm during colonial times) and she was the closest thing he could get towards that goal. It was also said that he gave preferable treatment to his more Caucasoid children and was particularly unloving to the others who weren't (my father [center of the above photo] being a prime target due to his being the darkest of the lot). In just a few years within the marriage he lost his job at Shell Oil as being seen as unfit. Despite being given a severance payout he depended on his wife's teaching salary to provide for him and the children. Jobless and prone to depressive episodes he would make every attempt to find merriment outside of his home and when he did come home his frustrations over his incapacities and failures were taken out on his wife and children. My aunt would tell me that they would hear him singing drunken songs as he came up the hill towards the house and according to what song he sang, they would know whether he was ready to give everyone a whupping or if he would go shut himself in his bedroom for several hours. They prayed that it would be the latter. He depended on his wife's salary and her kind nature to hold the family together, pay the bills and take care of the house. Meanwhile he repaid her kindness by being more physically and emotionally abusive. Grandma was stricken with motor neuron disease in her early 40s and wasted away wheelchair bound for the last years of her life, passing away at the relatively young age of 48. All this tragedy and abuse contributed to their children suffering from various neuroses and mental illnesses. Only two managed to have some measure of success in their personal lives while the rest succumbed to directionless lives of struggle and financial and mental hardships, the youngest committing suicide at age 40 and two recently passing away alone and in squalor. But rather than delve into personal history (and there's a lot), let me answer the original question. Are there parents who regret having mixed-raced children? It is possible that my grandfather regretted his mixed raced children and harbored deep prejudices. It is also possible that he loved his mixed race children but his untreated mental illness brought out the worst in him. The answer in regards to my grandfather is probably. He showed no remorse when his wife died, relieved himself of any further fatherly duties and made no attempt to establish communication with his children. He sold the house and remarried (his long sought after white bride) a few years after his first wife's death. He died a lonely divorcée in 1994. Would he have made a greater effort to be a better father if he had found his white bride and had a flock of children, all the same complexion as him? No one knows.

Question: What are some of the biggest casting blunders in Hollywood movies?
Answer: I know I may be in the minority with this opinion but when I saw that this guy would be cast as Peter Parker in the first major studio Spiderman movie, disappointment is not strong enough of a word to describe how I felt. Tobey Maguire does not have the wit, charisma and charm of a traditional Peter Parker. Not only that, Maguire was too old for the role from the very first movie. When I saw 27 year old Maguire walking about high school with a jacket, book bag and a distinct 5 o’clock shadow on his face I was immediately taken out of the movie. (Yeah that's definitely a teenaged schoolboy boarding a bus and not a smirking, semi-creepy man pushing 30) Peter Parker is a charming and witty young man, loyal to friends and family, a great problem solver and a smartass with a touch of geekiness. The only characteristic Tobey Maguire demonstrated from the above was the geekiness, of which he laid on as thick as cheesecake. Maguire’s Spiderman was this awkward, pitiable schmuck who had as much charisma and charm as a mild-mannered peeping tom. The whole shtick the producers seemed to go with was to make Peter Parker nothing but a sad, bullied nerd because I guess maybe they arrogantly believed Spiderman fans are nothing but a bunch of nerds who love the comic book not because of its quality story and characters but because it supports a geek fantasy of getting fantastic superpowers through simple means, getting to beat up thugs and bullies and winning chicks. Sam Raimi’s Spiderman targeted that niche when they gave us the whimpering, sensitive, thin-lipped Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker in my honest opinion. Maybe that's my personal opinion but personality aside, Maguire doesn't even have the physical attributes. Spiderman/Parker is 5′10, late teens-early 20s, lean, long-limbed, sinewy and with a head of thick brunette hair. He basically has to have the physique of a well experienced trapeze artist due to all the climbing and swinging Spiderman does. At his best in the film Tobey Maguire was a short limbed and somewhat stocky man measuring somewhere between 5′7 and 5′8 with a crop of thin hair above his smirking, punchable face. I grew up watching Spiderman cartoons and gaining a familiarity with Parker's smart, resonating and confident tone. Maguire's whiny, eerily pubescent voice gave a measure of cringe and creepiness. I am not a fan of Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker and will hold that view for the rest of my life. Andrew Garfield and Tom Holland may not be the gold standard either but they are a lot more closer to the mark. Here's hoping that they get it right the next movie.

Question: Who is the most underestimated horror movie villain?
Answer: Practically every boy who grew up in the 90s watching horror movies on SyFy (then Sci-Fi) knew of this guy. I'm pretty certain he's responsible for a lot of nightmares we had back then. Revok from David Cronenberg’s sci-fi/body-horror cult classic Scanners (1981) puts a capital V in Villain. He's a powerful, ruthless and deranged psychic (scanner) bent on taking over the world with powers that can control minds and inflict severe physical damage on others. Michael Ironside who portrays Revok is nothing short of excellence. He makes Jack Nicholson’s Joker look like Mr. Rogers with his intense facial expressions, sinister grimacing and lip curling as well as his menacingly emotionless voice. No one can forget the famous scene at the beginning of the movie where Revok calmly and sarcastically pretends to be ‘scanned’ by a weaker fellow scanner only to casually cause the man's head to explode within seconds. Few actors can put such a stamp on a performance like Ironside did as he did with Revok. Scanners may be a bit of a forgotten movie by now but no one can ever forget the character Revok and Ironside's performance.

Question: What movie felt like you were right there with the actors?
Answer: United 93 Didn't have the opportunity to see this on the big screen when it premiered back in ‘06. Really wish I did. However I'm certain I would've been emotionally drained afterwards. The film deals with the September 11th terrorist attacks and chronicles the last few hours of the only flight of the four hijacked planes in which the passengers managed to fight off the terrorists and prevent the plane from crashing into its intended target. The film employs the use of shaky, handheld camera which has become the signature style of its director Paul Greengrass (of whom I am of the opinion that he now overdoes this style in practically every movie he makes). The frenzied handheld style coupled with the use of real time, unknown actors, strategic camera positioning and lack of a protagonist makes the viewer feel like a random passenger aboard the flight. All of this is done intentionally by the director of course. It is one of the few movies in which, even though I knew what would be the eventual outcome, I was glued to the screen in nervous anticipation as to what was going to happen next. A very underrated movie in my honest opinion.

Question: What screams "I'm low class"?
Answer: A girl, no older than 20 comes into Papa John's a busy Friday evening. I'm helping out at the cash register. It's near the end of the month (pay day for most people) and this is when we get our bulk of orders. The phone is ringing off the hook. I'm really just a delivery guy but the store is short staffed so I help cash. The girl, her cellphone tucked at her groin area in her trousers comes up to me at the register. Totally ignoring the fact that I'm taking an order on the phone she proceeds to talk about what she wants. I paused from the phone call to tell her, ‘One minute please miss I'm on the phone with a customer.’ I look as her eyebrows slant further downwards in anger and she puts her arms on her hips, staring at me in a show of impatience. When I finished with the call I apologized and asked what would she like. ‘Gimme one of the chicken pizzas.’ The phone started ringing again. I sighed inwardly. All the time she spent staring at me in anger she didn't even make up her mind as to what she wanted. ‘Which one of the chicken pizzas?’ I don't know if by asking a simple question like that she found some measure of offense but she replied in a belligerent tone, ‘How am I supposed to know what chicken pizzas you have?’ The phone continued ringing. I sighed again. I pointed to the display above her head and told her I have to take the call, choose a pizza by the time. Instead she frowns at me while I take another phone order, she refusing to look at the menu board herself. When I was done she glared at me and said, ‘Chicken and pine….the largest size you have.’ ‘That would be an extra large’ I said. ‘I know!’ she spat. She then proceeds to take out of her purse a brown envelope which contained the salary she just received from whatever job she worked. She proudly counts her 100s in front of me and gave me $200 without waiting for me to tell her the price of her order. I gave her her change and receipt and told her the waiting time (15–20 mins). She proceeded to stare at me whilst I take other orders, helped cut pizzas from off the oven and organized my deliveries at the same time. With her seeing me doing all these things at once I thought she would have generated some sympathy for me seeing that I wasn't really the cashier but just a delivery guy helping out the situation. While heading towards the exit with my deliveries I passed near her and she beckons me. I thought it was to apologize for her attitude. Instead she tells me something that makes my blood boil instantly. ‘Ummm. How much longer for my order?’ She just placed her order 5 minutes ago! I gritted me teeth and replied, ‘It’s not in the oven yet. 10 to 15 minutes.’ She rolled her eyes and looked away. I then realize what her game was. She didn't really care about the pizza. Her fetish was to feel some sort of superiority over someone else and the only place she could achieve that was in a fast food restaurant. We get customers like that regularly, especially around month's end (pay day). They get some kind of sick thrill out of pissing people off and flaunting what (little) money they have. So to answer the question above, nothing screams 'I’m low class’ more than people who buy fast food for the sake of showing off/putting on airs.

Question: What was your first clue you were no longer as young as you thought you were?
Answer: While working in a school library I was at the computers assisting some students in finishing their assignments to submit to their teachers. Most students would email their assignments to their teacher, others (who didn't have/couldn't remember their email address) would save it on a USB flash drive . This one student who had neither an email address or a flash drive raised his hand for assistance and told me of his situation. I went into our storage cupboard and brought out an old rewritable CD-RW; the kind I used back in school to copy (‘burn’ as we used to call it) data onto. I gave him the shiny disc and walked off assuming that he knew what to do with it. ‘Sir!’ I heard his voice call after me. ‘Yeah?’ ‘What am I supposed to do with this?’ ‘Burn it,’ I said and looked at him stoically. His friends started laughing believing that I was teasing. ‘Sir stop joking. I need to save my work.’ ‘Burn the work onto the CD’ I said and he started to look at me irritated. ‘Sir help him out. Stop joking’ one of the friends said. It then dawned on me that they had no idea what ‘burning a CD’ was. This was before their time. I proceeded to demonstrate to them how to copy data onto a CD-RW, feeling like a crusty old man giving them a tour on a private railroad. The sad thing was they were all 16–17 and I wasn't much older at 24.

Question: Which boxer’s style do you find the most aesthetically pleasing?
Answer: Definitely The Lion Lennox Lewis. ‘The Lion’ is such an apt name because he does have a fighting style similar to a large cat. Lennox is a great tactician who uses his left jab to feint, taunt, displace and sometimes to smother and confuse. His left jab is like a diagnostic tool where he feels for the condition of the opponent and when the timing is right he unleashes powerful combinations. When facing shorter opponents he squats in a crab like posture and and uses his long arms and height advantage to monitor his opponents’ status, peering at them like a feline playing with its meal. If his opponent has some fight left in him and attacks, Lewis retreats in his crab like manner, smothering their offense with his own punches or jabbing them into a clinch. However he does not stick to this style. This style works for his shorter, less rangy opponents. When faced with opponents his own size and strength he's can successfully change styles from outboxer/boxer -puncher to brawler/pressure fighter. This is most evident in his fight with Vitali Klitschko where the bigger brawler’s (Klitschko) style was all wrong for Lewis’ clinical style. What I personally find pleasing about Lewis’ style is that you see the punches when they land, you see the frustration in his opponents face and the calmness in his. What I like about Lewis himself is that his boxing comes from a place of emotional maturity and self control. You see his method and you eventually see the results. His style is effective and shows a peek of the sportsmanship that lies in a sport that has its foundation in crude barbarity. Edit: If I could add the fact that Lewis is a seasoned chess player. I don't want to assume that this is a factor contributing to his typically calm and stoic demeanor, his emotional and ring intelligence. If I could dab in his personal life a bit, the fact that he is one of the few boxers to have relative success in his personal/family life, his ability to hang up his gloves and avoid any possible brain damage (as per his wife's plea) the avoidance of drug abuse, party lifestyle, scandal and controversy makes him (to me) an underrated role model in the world of sports on par with the likes of George Foreman. Just my 2¢.

Question: Have you ever walked out of a movie theater early over a feature movie that you simply could not continue to sit through? If so, what was the movie?
Answer: To this day there is only one movie that was so detestable that I couldn't even sit through it halfway. This movie took all the absolute worst aspects of popular 2010s rom-coms and sex-coms and moulded it into one smelly ball and held it under my my nose for a gruelling 40 minutes. Honestly I've seen many rom-coms and sex-coms that I know to be silly and over-the-top but they manage to provide a level of entertainment. Good writers manage to insert a few relatable scenes and characters that keep it from straying into a fairytale. Also a good writer would understand that good-humour and charm is necessary for a rom-coms and sex-coms to be enjoyable. There is nothing remotely good-humoured about Love and Other Drugs (2010). No one is charming. Everyone is a foulmouth, nihilist/narcissist. The very premise of the story is dark and ugly. A rising pharmaceutical salesman gets romantically involved with one of his customers whose health deteriorates whilst his sales increase. Will he learn the value of love can't bought with all the cash in the world? Will he learn that pharmaceuticals are to help people and not to get rich off of? Will he manage to enjoy a whole bunch of sex with various women while thinking of the above? The movie is infuriating because it seems to be written by three completely different writers who battled as towards the direction of the movie and time ran out on them. Hate is not a word that I use a lot but this is a movie that I honestly hate. It's a cynical, tasteless movie devoid of any charm that becomes shallower the more it tries to look deep.

Question: What was a red flag that made you stop talking to a person immediately?
Answer: My brother had a relative staying over at his apartment and she brought along a friend. They both had just turned 18 and had recently run off from home (Red Flag #1) and were crashing at my brother's place basically sleeping all day and partying all night to their teenaged wont. I struck up a conversation with the friend (let's just call her Alice for simplicity's sake) and found her quite intelligent and charming despite her lifestyle. Went with Alice to hang out one night and we ended up in a club. We began dancing but I was quite surprised how physically close she positioned herself while we danced as we had only just met a week ago (Red Flag #2). I then asked her about how it was staying with my brother and she began a slew of insults as towards my brother's manners and housekeeping standards (Red Flag #3) despite the fact that she didn't help with his bills or rent. We exchanged numbers and I dropped her off home. She laid on her charm quite thick the entire journey and spoke of how great of a guy I was and that she couldn't wait for us to chat again. We exchanged numbers and the following morning I called her to see how she was doing. In a groggy voice she said ‘Who is this?’ I told her my name and to my surprise she said in a irritated tone, ‘Who? How did you get my number?’ (Red Flag #4) I reminded her that she gave me her number willingly the night before. She tried to laugh it off as being hung over. I reminded her that she only had one drink last night (Red Flag #5). There was an awkward silence and she tried to coo about how great of a guy I was but I cut her short and said that I was getting another call. Three years later Alice got pregnant for her boyfriend's married boss.

Question: Which TV shows were popular when you were younger that would flop today? Why?
Answer: Oh man. There are so many shows from the 90s that would flop hard had they been released (as they were) today. These two shows ruled daytime television for a long time in the mid 90s. I think one of the reasons for the success of the two interrelated shows is the fact that they were different and there was nothing else on. These weren't the days of Netflix, streaming, 4K/HD, watch at your own pace, high production value but limited seasons/episodes, hundreds of options to choose from high speed internet TV. These were the days of ‘Damn I missed my show’ cable television, paper TV guides, one new show every few months, low budget production with endless episodes and seasons etc. These were the days of ‘take what you can get’ on TV. HERCULES: THE LEGENDARY JOURNEYS Hercules is this chill, alpha-jock type guy who roams around New Zealand (wearing the same Super V-neck goatskin vest and tight leather pants every day) meeting nice quirky villagers of whom he saves from various villains ranging from petty con-men to full blown freakish monsters. At his side is a short, blond, surfer-dude like Iolaus who is the comic relief character. This is the premise for practically every episode. The show is supposedly set in ancient Greece yet don't be surprised to find English knights, Chinese peasants, Japanese ninjas, Nordic Vikings, Mongolian warlords, Egyptian Pharaohs or any cool and exciting historical anachronism discovered randomly during Hercules’ wanderings. The always well-shaved Kevin Sorbo would never break a sweat or mess up his lovely long hair in fights. Everything always worked out well in the end for Hercules, Iolaus and the villagers and if things got truly icky then you know it would take a second or third episode for the villain to be destroyed or for Iolaus/a love interest/a child to recover from near death. XENA: WARRIOR PRINCESS It’s pretty much the same thing except the leads are women. Xena (previously a minor Hercules villain on the show) atones for her past by going around saving helpless villagers with the aid of her short, blond quirky bard Gabrielle and the village idiot Joxer. Unlike Hercules, Xena had more personality and a rather interesting ‘Ay ya ya ya ya’ war cry accompanied with more of a focus on action scenes rather than Hercules’ constant spew of Dad jokes. The show became far more popular than its predecessor and ran from 1995 - 2001 whereas Hercules began in 1995 as well and ended 1999. Comparing these two shows with the crop of fantasy shows that are available now is definitely a chalk and cheese comparison. Take a look at the following screenshots. Now take a look at various people doing Hercules and Xena cosplay: You can barely tell the difference! Historically inaccurate clothing, easily accessible and cheap to film ‘forest’ backgrounds, pampered hairstyles, anachronisms galore, Hercules: The Legendary Journeys and Xena: Warrior Princess were nothing more than glorified cosplay. If either show were released today, as they were, they would be a source for ridicule and memes. However if I can give one positive comment for the show I would have to say that it doesn’t try to secretly force any message down my throat. Xena is a woman who kicks ass. She is not a feminist and definitely not a lesbian as that lame rumour suggests. Hercules doesn’t spout any subtle parables promoting socialism or taxing the wealthy. There is no powerful and evil villain that looks and acts like Trump (or Bob Dole to be more precise with the time). The show is silly and stupid and doesn’t promote any type of political activism. So I’d definitely watch Xena or Hercules over Rings of Power and She-Hulk any time, any day.

Question: What happened in your school bus on your way to school that you still remember?
Answer: In Trinidad we don't have school buses like they do in the US but we have public transportation buses that (during my childhood) were composed of 90% school children passengers in the mornings before school There was the front of the bus where elderly citizens, parents who accompanied their kids and well-behaved kids would occupy. The middle of the bus was occupied by kids who were not so well behaved (sometimes loud and obnoxious) but relatively harmless. This is where I would usually occupy. The dreaded back of the bus consisted of the really troubled crop of kids who ditched school, smoked, fornicated with other boys/girls, got into fights etc. My older brother was going through a delinquent phase in his late teens and hung around some boys who frequented the back of the bus, ditched school etc etc. One day while we both took the bus he came to the middle section to bring me to the back. Seeing the worried look on my face he explained that no one would hurt me knowing that I am ‘Reuben’s brother.’ We sat alongside each other on a pair of seats and in front of us were a pair of seats facing our direction in which sat a pair of slovenly, oily skinned girls with defiant looks on their faces. The minute we sat a bunch of my brother's friends who were standing closed in on us and surrounded the four seats, blocking the view of us four from the rest of the bus. I wondered what all this meant but then looked in amazement as my brother commanded one of the girls to come sit on his lap and like a loyal servant she did and they proceeded to make out for a few seconds. There was something a tad disgusting about the way they did it. They were both inexperienced and I could see that my brother was trying to emulate what he saw in the movies. Regardless it was something impressive among boys so I was expecting his friends around us to start hollering and hooting but none of them looked as surprised as I was. My brother then gave me a gesturing hard glance for me to sit with the other girl. I did as such and sat there feeling awkward, not knowing what to say. My whole mindset with female intimacy was that I was supposed to be respectful and get to know a girl through long conversations and going on dates etc, so to see my brother just start making out with a random girl he probably didn't even know the name of was quite shocking to me. The girl I sat next to grew angry and said to my brother, ‘Waz de problem with your brother? He retarded o’ sometin?’ My brother explained that I was just a little shy and not used to girls. Feeling irritated by his comment I immediately jumped to my own defense by telling the girl that I danced with much more girls than him and he was the shy one. This piqued her interest and I proceeded to tell her a bunch of bogus stories of fights that I got in on a weekly basis and how I drank a lot of alcohol. After a few minutes I saw that she was giving me a look. The look showed that the time for talk was over and she wanted some action like how my brother and her friend were slobbering lips and touching every few minutes. I put a cold, nervous hand on her leg and she immediately leaned towards me. This was my cue to start slobbering lips. However I was not in the least bit attracted to her so I felt frozen in making the next move. To make matters worse I caught a glimpse of a chunk of wet booger in the corner of her left nostril. The girl caught sight of the disgusted look on my face and retaliated. ‘I doh have time fuh little boys’ she said in an angry but mostly hurt tone. She then turned her face the other direction, folded her leg and crossed her arms. Looking at my brother's face I could see that he himself was fairly disgusted with his ordeal as well but played along to look cool in front of the boys. ‘Go back to your friends,’ he said haughtily and without another word I leapt off the seat and back to the middle section. I never went to the back of the bus again until I got into my late teens and could handle myself against peer pressure. That incident was over twenty years ago but whenever I take the bus and go to the back where the troubled kids still love to hang out, I always picture that girl with the huge wet booger hanging on her nostril positioning herself for a slobbering kiss.

Question: Have you ever been on a date that was going so badly you walked out and left?
Answer: When I was 18, an A-Level student in school, I took the bus and made friends with a quiet and pretty 12 year old girl. Nothing romantic happened. I acted like an older brother to her as I had sisters around that age. I made some silly jokes played some of my awful harmonica music and carried her to the public library for an hour or so and watched magazines. We didn't exchange numbers. It was just a harmless, spontaneous thing. Fast forward seven years later. I bump into her near the University. I'm 25 and she's 19. She gained a few pounds and is a bit more loud and outspoken than I remembered. However the flash back of our good time motivates me to ask her out to a movie the upcoming Saturday night. She agrees. On that day while waiting for her near the cinema I get a call. ‘We’re on our way.’ I wondered what she meant by ‘we’re.’ We agreed it was just her and I. I queried what she meant but she began to burst out in laughter to something somebody was saying. ‘Don’t worry it's another girl,’ she continued, ‘You’re getting to carry out two girls!’ I could hear the friend feeding her every word to say to me. She would then break out in laughter. I got highly irritated with their school girl shenanigans. Something told me to just hang up the phone and head back home. Another part of me said that that would be really bad of me to to do that. She is still just a teenager after all and who could blame her if maybe she felt more comfortable bringing a friend on a date with a guy she doesn't really know that well. I chose to go along with it. Wrong choice. When she and her friend came they came they acted like a pair of spoilt teenaged twats, mentally stuck at age 13. There was no proper introduction to one another. Everything was a joke and a giggle and the only time I seemed to exist was when we passed a fancy restaurant/bar and they wanted get some food and drinks (but couldn't afford it of course). Mentally I agreed to ditch them at the restaurant. I was not going to shell out a bunch of money for these clowns. I bought them their drinks and said I had to to go the washroom. While heading towards the restroom I was having second thoughts about whether this was the right thing to do. I was a wild and careless teenager once. I felt as though it was bad manners and etiquette to ditch my friend who was such a nice girl seven years ago. However I overhead them trying to get people's attention by practically shouting ‘You’re a bitch.’ ‘Oh my gosh no you're a bitch.’ ‘You're the biggest bitch on the planet.’ Etc etc and then bursting out in laughter. I told myself that they clearly didn't give a crap about manners and etiquette themselves. Returning from the washroom I slipped past them and out the building into the streets. I sent a hastily written text message saying that I had an emergency and needed to leave as soon as possible. I then jumped into a taxi and made my way home. I felt a pang of grief for my friend and how she changed for the worse but there was no way I was paying over $300 of my hard earned money to carry two rude and inconsiderate teenaged girls to go see a movie. At least they both got a drink out of it.

Question: I have a fiance who is living in Portugal. I met him in a dating site, and we communicate in my WhatsApp. I want to video call him, but he said Portugal is banned in video calls. Is that true?
Answer: My 66 year old Aunt had similar circumstances. Recently divorced and living alone far from any family in Ontario she was befriended online by a guy claiming to be working in the US Army. For months they have a back and forth on WhatsApp. She constantly asking for him to take some time to visit her, he constantly reminding her that his army duties don't all for him to vacation as often as he'd like. He also refused all WhatsApp audio and video calls because, according to him, it would compromise the US Army. However he did send her a photo of himself. Coincidentally if you search ‘US Army Officer Facebook’ on Google you can easily come across his photo. He assured her that when he does come and see her he would do so while flying through the skies in the Army helicopter and he would most definitely land in her apartment parking lot and take her up for a ride. She became smitten by him and he asked for her hand in marriage. She agreed but not long after he explained that he was tied up in a court battle over unpaid child support. According to him he had a mission in Somalia and had a rendezvous with one of the local women who eventually got pregnant for him and gave birth to son. My aunt, being as scrupulous as she is, asked for photo evidence of this child. He sent her this thumbnail. Coincidentally his son's photo could be found by simply searching ‘cute Somalian boy’ on Google. Nevertheless my aunt was convinced by his evidence and impressed by the cuteness of his son. Her Army boyfriend persuaded her to send $5000 CAD to the child's mother's Somalian bank account. After she did as such (and after being a bit wary as to why he was so adamant to remind her to send it on a daily basis) she stopped recieving messages from him. She came to the conclusion that she was scammed. It deeply hurt her and embarassed her and caused her sons and ex husband to stop sending her any large sums of money. However luck would have it that she befriended through Facebook a Swedish doctor of Indian descent. While discovering that he came into inheritance of a large sum of money he asked for her hand in marriage. Unfortunately, while on his way to see her he was held by Belgian authorities in regards to his large stash of gold in his suitcase in which he's now asking my aunt for help with his legal fees. Because of this unique situation he is unable to send or receive WhatsApp video calls. No matter how much we've tried to convince my aunt to drop this obvious scam she wouldn't listen. Anyway my point being is that whenever you meet some exotic character online who tells you some wacky story with claims that can be disproved with a simple Google search, it is with 100% certainty that person is trying to scam you.

Question: What's the dumbest thing you've gotten in trouble for at school?
Answer: Back in Form 2 (7th Grade) I fancied myself a comic book artist. To entertain myself and my friends I would draw these crude, intentionally homoerotic drawings of over muscled male wrestlers engaged in poses and grapples. My sense of anatomy and perspective was nothing short of abysmal so many of my drawings (at best) looked a lot like this. One of my friends asked that I draw our class teacher Mr. Din Chong. I made an atrocious rendering of him, exaggerating his physical features to a ludicrous degree and as an added touch I drew him shirtless and chicken Chester and pencil necked. The drawing looked nothing like him but my friends loved it and asked for more. I went home and drew the social studies teacher Ms. Moore (Big Shirley) as we called her, who was quite large and overweight. There was a running joke in the school that short, skinny big eared Din Chong and massive Big Shirley were a couple. I drew a comic showing Din Chong and Big Shirley going on a date and even had the nerve to draw explicit images of the two trying (unsuccessfully) to engage in sex. This comic was passed around the class with great fervor. Most of the class enjoyed my tasteless humour and even some of the bad boys were shocked that I went so far. Practically everyone told me to destroy the comic afterwards because something like that could get me in serious trouble if not suspended from school. However I had tasted some fame and was hungry for more. I started rendering practically all of the teachers in school in my dirty comic. I would include a lot of sex, a lot of violence (teachers we didn’t like being shot to pieces/decapitated by rasta gangsters. I would include the male teachers who we suspected to be gay trying to coerce muscle bound male wrestlers into sex and end up being beaten violently. I became so obsessed with my comics that I derived stories with no moral or meaning that ended in the most ludicrous manner of either sex, violence, extraterrestrials, superheroes, urban legends, getting high/drunk or a combination of all six. From just a few pages in my scrap book my comics grew to take up an entire note book. My comic book would be passed along in class whenever someone was bored and there would be a constant snorting and giggling and a declaration of shock from the reader. ‘You’re mad!’ one of the boys in class once told me, ‘One of the teachers are gonna find out about this.’ He then handed me back my notebook. I heard the warning so many times but I couldn’t care less. I had so many fans looking forward to a new panel of comics on a daily basis. However, one fateful day, during recess my best friend Davan was asking me to read some of my comics for him. The ones with Din Chong and Big Shirley. I pulled out my notebook and proceeded to read some of the vulgar dialogue with an emphasis on the obscenity and gross sexual noises. Davan began to giggle like a 5 year old and I proceeded to continue onto my newest comic that involved a superhero with a massive dildo strapped to his head and his interaction with Big Shirley (much to Din Chong’s distress). This I considered my magnum opus and I found myself reading at the top of my voice and laughing at my own creation with great joy. My eyes didnt leave the pages as I turned. After a minute or so I noticed there was no laughter coming from Davan. In fact, the class had grown eerily silent. Stupid me never considered the fact that my seat was next to a window and outside the window stood none other than the Principal peering down at me and my comic and listening rather broodingly, waiting for the moment when I realized that the shit had just hit the fan. I quickly closed the notebook and shoved it under my desk. ‘Let me see that’ she said. ‘It’s nothing’ I said ready to have a panic attack. ‘Boy. I said give me that book’ With a sense of impending doom I handed over the book to her. She flipped through the pages nonchalantly. I saw her eyes widen at some of the pages. ‘You are a very perverted young man’ she said stoically, ‘Follow me.’ Everyone stared as I followed the Principal to her office. It was rumored that she herself had a bit of a lewd sense of humour. Many of the boys on the football team would claim that she would drop a flirt or semi-sexual innuendo at their direction during after-school football practice. However, this comic involved practically every single teacher in the compound in a sexual and/or violent manner. This was nothing for her to joke about. I thanked the heavens that I never thought to include her in any of my comics. However, I was still deep in the shit and I could only imagine the look my mother would give me if she got to see these drawings. She told me to wait outside her office as she spoke to a teacher who had some sort of complaint. I was thinking she would say, ‘Hey, look at what this child did’ and hand him my drawings and pretty soon the whole staff room would come and see themselves rendered in the most atrocious manner and a big ruckus would start. Fortunately the teacher left unaware of the situation and the Principal then beckoned me in. The book was laid closed shut in her book shelf, looking innocent and inoffensive. ‘You have a great talent Mr. Williamson’ she said and stared at me. I didn’t know if to say thanks or smile so I remained silent. ‘You are also quite a disturbed boy and its very sad that you use your talents for such a negative purpose.’ Silence. She continued, ‘Let me catch you drawing more of these and I will make sure your parents are aware of what you do in your spare time. Is that understood?’ I nodded. I thought I was off the hook. I even thought that she would’ve given me my comics back but they remained on her bookshelf. She then reached for her stick and told me to open my palms. Nope. I wasn’t quite off the hook. She gave the the usual 5 lashes on each hand and five lashes on my butt. With tears welling in my eyes she told me to apologize for my language which I did. She then sent me out the office, I did my best to hide my tears as I went back to face my classroom. I was expecting everyone to be waiting with bated breath for me, to find out what trouble I was in and what became of the book. To my surprise no one really cared except my close friends. I explained to them what happened and how she kept the book. Davan looked disappointed. He wanted to know what happened in the end with Din Chong, Big Shirley and the dildo headed superhero. Fighting back tears I explained how Big Shirley had a night of great sex with the superhero and couldn't decide whether to stay with Din Chong or the superhero, in the end all three were run over by a rasta gangster driving a Hummer. We all laughed it off. That chapter in my life was over and it was an interesting experience. I laughed even as the tears streamed down my face. Salvaged drawings from old scrap books: Din Chong The androgynous PE teacher. Math teacher getting head ‘shot’ off by Rasta gangster. Muscled alien grappling with (presumably) Rasta gangster.

Question: Do you think Europe is more racist than the USA?
Answer: I haven't been to the whole of Europe and I haven't travelled all the States of the USA. However I've been to Wales and Kentucky recently and I've had two encounters that I think could be used as data towards answering the above question. Aberystwyth, Wales. I was a student on a scholar for a Masters degree along with a few fellow Trinidadians. When we went out shopping, our favourite store by far was Poundland. We patronized Poundland almost on a daily basis buying chocolates, sweets and various goodies for a pound each to our hearts’ delight. Despite the noticeable frigidity of many people in the area we saw, most were helpful and polite. One day at Poundland I was informed that there were rewards to anyone with purchases of over £25 pounds and up. The more you spent the better the reward. After shopping I checked my receipt and saw that I qualified to redeem a cool digital sports watch. I went over to the guy at customer service and showed my receipt. People from Aberystwyth tend to wear a constant smile that fluctuates from smile to smirk according to the mood/situation. This guy's smile changed to a definite smirk when he saw me waving my receipt. ‘What’s that you say?’ he said as though I were speaking Swahili. ‘I want to get the watch.’ I repeated for the third time, ‘I spent over thirty pounds.’ He watched me waving my receipt with a confused expression on his face as though I were a lunatic waving a bill of rights. ‘Come again?’ he said and I knew he was playing stupid and I started to get annoyed. I notice that he's glancing towards the back of the store as if to communicate to the others that he wanted someone else to come over. Suddenly an older man came towards us and asked what was the problem. I explained that I wanted to redeem my points for the sports watch. I showed him the receipt but he stares at me up and down instead. ‘You’re not from the UK I would guess,’ he says. I said no, that I was here on studies. He hemmed and hawed and then said that the prizes are meant for UK citizens. I told him that there was no mention of that in the advertisement hanging on the wall next to him. He hemmed and hawed again and said that it may not be written in the ad but the promotion is to encourage locals to shop at Poundland more. I asked to speak to the manager and with a smirk he said, ‘Nice to meet you. I'm the manager Steve.’ Him and the other worker then proceeded to stare at me, brandishing their wide smile-smirks. Deciding not to make a ruckus I left the matter at that. Georgetown, Kentucky I visited my girlfriend and we stopped at the police station at the above location for her to deal with a matter. While I was waiting for her in the car I grew bored after 30 minutes. There was a swarm of bees that surrounded the area and as they left I went out to take a video of them as the swarmed off. A police car rolls up about 20 feet away from me and the driver's window rolls down. A latino officer then smiles at me and says ‘Hey.’ I said Hi. He says something else but I couldn't hear him so I went closer to his vehicle. He asks me what I was doing there in the car park and I explained that I was waiting for a friend inside the station. He asked me where I was from and I explained that I was from the Caribbean. Suddenly another police car comes speedily from the opposite direction and parks in an aggressive manner as if to cut me off from running away. A tall stocky Caucasian officer exits the vehicle and comes towards me and demands that I keep my hands away from my pockets. He proceeds to search me and discovers me unarmed. He explains that someone reported me as a suspicious individual hanging around the police station parking lot. I explained that I was just a tourist from the Caribbean. They explained that loitering about a police station is seen as suspicious in the State of Kentucky and that I should remain in my vehicle if I waited on my friend here. Tall stocky guy stares at me and asks if I have any questions myself. I said no but I said I appreciated how alert they were and if only Trinidad had such dedicated officers we would have less crime. They both laugh awkwardly and stocky guy pats me on my shoulder like a schoolkid. They both leave without another word. In conclusion I would honestly say that my experience in Wales seemed to border more on seething racism rather my experience in Kentucky. I believe the officers in Georgetown were doing their job whilst the staff at Poundland at Aberystwyth were discriminating in a subtle manner. There was a certain deep seated resentment I felt in Wales whilst in Kentucky it was more of a passive wariness. I felt as though I could've communicated to the officers and reach a certain compromise whilst with the Poundland staff I felt like a brick wall was between us. I also felt like that with the locals of Kentucky, a friendly warmth while in Aberystwyth it was an air of cold professionalism for the most part. In rural Kentucky, places like Kuttawa and Paducah I got no strange looks and witnessed black people working alongside whites in seeming normalcy whereas in Aberystwyth the one black person I witnessed was a homeless man and the one mixed race person was young man working in a thrift shop. So in my honest and ignorant opinion I would think that racism would be more prevalent in a subtle, passive aggressive manner in Europe whilst in the US it can happen due to wariness of strangers rather than due to race. Edit: There is one commenter who continuously alleges that I’ve fabricated my story about my visit to Wales and Aberystwyth. Every time I reply with evidence to him it somehow disappears so I’ve decided to put the evidence where it can’t be removed here in the answer.

Question: Can you name an actor who was never a good actor but became one?
Answer: Sterling Hayden never wanted to be an actor. He was coaxed into the profession as a young, handsome sailor whose photogenic good looks appealed to a post WWII audience who were just begging for actors who were the image of tall and rugged manliness. The 6′5 blonde, athletic young shipmate got into the industry after a 1938 photo gained popularity in a fisherman's magazine. Dubbed by Paramount as 'The Beautiful Blond Viking God’ he got into the industry as a means to purchase his own ship but grew to resent Hollywood. His early roles were a slew of rather forgettable Westerns and film noirs. After his role in the classic Western Johnny Guitar starring Joan Crawford he became a bonafide star. However around this time his personal life got more attention as he was reported to have communist sympathies during the McCarthy/Red Scare era and during a vicious custody battle for his children he took his four children on a self manned trip aboard his ship Wanderer from San Francisco Bay to Tahiti despite the legal implications that awaited him at home. His impulsive nature, hatred of Hollywood,anti- capitalism sentiments and sometimes reckless behaviour gave him the image of an eccentric, of which is well documented in his autobiography Wanderer (1963). However upon working with Stanley Kubrick in The Killing he found his niche playing manic and impulsive characters, not far removed from his actual personality. His best role arguably being that of the insane American General Jack D. Ripper in Kubrick's classic black political comedy Dr. Strangelove. His final great role was that of corrupt Irish police Captain Mark McCluskey in The Godfather (1972). Despite the critical and commercial resurgence his roles and his writings were used solely to fund his travels of which (along with legal expenses and taxes) he continuously saw his money decrease. He died of prostate cancer at the of 70 in 1986, leaving behind six children.

Question: What is the most badass thing your parent has ever done?
Answer: Martin was a guy who lived a few houses away from us. Outside of his fence was a coconut tree that grew on an empty lot of land. When the tree finally bore coconuts, myself, my brother and some of the boys of the neighborhood went and attempted to climb and get some. Martin, the middle aged perpetual bachelor of the street, came out in his underwear (he was always parading around his yard in his underwear) and cursed at us to leave ‘his tree’ alone. We went home downtrodden. When my mother asked us what the problem was and we explained she suddenly took on a serious countenance. She said the tree did not belong to him. She then tells us to follow her. She went to each of the boys homes, spoke to all the mothers and before we knew it there was a gang of all us boys and our mothers marching to the coconut tree. Our mothers commanded each of us to climb and pick a coconut each. They made sure to be loud to get the attention of the neighborhood. ‘Go ahead,’ my mother said loudly ‘Nobody owns this tree.’ Martin came out to see the ruckus and immediately he had four mothers on his case. They gave him an earful about the coconut tree and cussing out us boys. My mother even tosses in a zinger saying that no one likes to see him in his jockeys, that he doesn't impress any of the ladies living here and if she sees him one more time undressed she would report him to the police. Martin slunk back indoors. After a few laughs our mothers carried us back home. I never thought my mother had it in her to organize an angry mob so quickly and over something so ridiculous.

Question: What is an example of someone who underestimated the wrong individual?
Answer: In my first year of secondary (high) school, taunting and chest-beating was a norm amongst the more silly and immature boys like myself. Balram was an Indian boy who came from rural poverty. He wore worn clothes, kept an outdated hairstyle and mostly kept to himself to avoid the others making fun of him (which they constantly did). They would call him bush-coolie, Mowgli, Balram of the Jungle and various other insulting names. Balram would sit and deflect their insults with the stoic calmness of a Navajo chief. He was an acquaintance of mine but we were not close. However a group of boys looking to make a ruckus started taunting me that I was so weak, even bush boy Balram could beat me up, I quickly took to the offence. I rushed up to Balram who anticipated that I would fall for the bait and before I could say 'Bal’ he pinned me against the wall with two sinewy hands against my shoulders and told me to behave myself. Everyone was astonished at Balram's strength. After struggling to escape his grip for a several seconds he saw I was worn out and released me. That day forward I never messed with Balram and even became his good friend. The class still teased him, but this time they made sure they were at a safe distance when doing so.

Question: What has an employee said that immediately caused you to fire them?
Answer: Jerome (not real name) was a new worker with a big mouth. He was 28 years old at the time, quite older than most of the guys he worked with like myself yet he acted, at best, like a spoilt 15 year old. He was always talking. He always had an opinion about something. He always had to question even the most simple orders and instructions. He believed himself to be the most intelligent person to ever walk the floor of the warehouse and always spoke at length of all the flaws he saw in our system and what he would do to fix the business if he were in charge. Our job was simple: a retail store wants products that we have, we go out with our grocery carts, pallet jacks, forklifts etc, get the products and have them packaged and ready for delivery in the morning. Not Jerome. Jerome's job was to distact you from what you were doing to talk shit about the company and how the money wasn't worth it. He would quote some nonexisting OSHA law that the company wasn't complying with and how he could sue the company if he wanted to. He would discuss his harebrained, get rich quick schemes that he never had to guts to actually attempt. He bragged about his family in the US waiting for him and how he didn't need to work himself like a slave for chump change like we did. At any given day he probably put out 20% of the output of the average worker. He was on a six month probationary period of which it would be decided whether he would be contracted as a permanent worker, given extended probation or let go. No one expected him to be permanently hired. Everyone basically tried to tolerate him for the six month probationary period as best as they could. However he started taking his shenanigans to the next level. He started making the (typically secluded) shampoos lane in the back warehouse his secret hideout. The lane was quiet, had no cameras and far away from our superiors’ field of vision. He decided to set up a makeshift man-cave behind a pallet of Tresemmé 2 in 1 Shampoo and Conditioner. There he would smoke, talk shit with the rare, harmless worker who came by for shampoos and he would watch rap music videos on his cell phone. At the month's end all warehouse workers were allowed to take from the damaged products. We had our own system of fairness whereby we rotated each worker to get a chance to get first pick among the damages. Jerome couldn't give a rat's ass about the system. During the third month of his employ it was observed that practically all of the best damaged goods had gone missing. A co-worker and myself smelt a rat in Jerome and we went to his man cave while he was on lunch and saw the damages were there hidden in boxes. We reported it to the supervisor who came and saw it. He held an emergency meeting and asked for the person who put those damaged goods in the back to come forward. Everyone eyed Jerome angrily but he remained silent. The supervisor reported the matter to the manager who reported it to the company owner and she immediately put a stop to the free damages giveaway. Now the anger towards Jerome had turned into a bloodlust. However the more angry everyone got the more lazy and defiant Jerome became. He was smart enough to abandon his man-cave after his attempted theft but he still spent more than half his working day loitering and talking shit. Every year the company paid for the company staff to have a party, usually at a classy sports bar or a nightclub. We all looked forward to it including Jerome who discussed at length his intention to get drunk off of free premium drinks and score with one of the pretty head office girls. However, one fateful afternoon the owner of the store had an impromptu meeting with everyone in the warehouse. She explained that the company decided to change the format of the staff party. She explained that it was expensive and inefficient having this party every year when too many employees ran up a bill drinking premium drinks all night and then not being able to come to work the following day. She gave the disappointing news that this time the party would be held at 12pm — 7pm the upcoming Sunday. Jerome released a snorting laugh while she spoke. Everyone in the warehouse went dead silent. No one had ever dared interrupt the owner, far less mock her. 'Excuse me,' she said, 'Is there something amusing?’ 'Nobody ever heard of a party 12 o clock in the afternoon,' Jerome said in his spoilt 15 year old voice. 'I've been to many parties 12 o clock in the afternoon' she replied. 'Yeah, birthday parties for kids' Jerome said smugly and looked about for someone to laugh but found only silence. The owner asked Jerome his name and how long he worked in the warehouse. Afterwards she continued her talk uninterrupted but after the meeting was dismissed she, the manager and Jerome went into an office for a talk. Some minutes later Jerome was seen leaving the compound, he was terminated from the job. Sad thing for Jerome was the owner apparently thought over what he said about the party and changed her mind about it. We were allowed to have our traditional, late into the night, party albeit minus the free premium drinks. We had a great time dancing the night away and toasting Jerome whose big mouth finally done some good for a change. Footnote 6/6/2023: There are a few commenters who seem to doubt the validity of my story on the grounds that 'so how come they didn't just fire Jerome as he's on probation?’ Probation is a process of testing and observing a new worker for short period. We signed a contract that we would be terminated on the grounds of serious offences like drug use, sexual harassment, assault, excessive absenteeism etc. Being a crappy worker and talking shit all day wouldn't get you terminated instantly but would definitely make you fail your probation and would have you under their radar for possible termination, which is exactly what happened in Jerome's case. Please. If you find all of this fantastic and unbelievable you are free to shake your head and scroll down.

Question: What are some examples of style without substance in writers?
Answer: I know I may be critized for some of my choices but these are some of the works I've read that I deeply consider to be style heavy but severely lacking in substance imho. Fight Club — Chuck Palahniuk The cult status of this novel has become almost legendary after the film debut in 1999. Back then I thoroughly enjoyed the film for its defiantly anarchist undertones and its twist ending. As I've grown older the film now seems a tad ridiculous and childish and the so-called twist ending makes absolutely no sense in retrospect. Our of curiosity I read the book and it further confirmed my sentiments that the book/movie was written solely for an audience of angst-ridden males between the ages of 16 — 25. Palahniuk's style is some sort of mish-mash stream of consciousness dialogue combined with frenetic pacing, little concern for character development, cliffhangers around every corner and throws in a random fact few pages (gasoline and orange juice can be used to make napalm……oooh {angst filled teen wets himself}. The Beach — Alex Garland Another 90s, stream of consciousness, style heavy writer who's found enormous success with the titular novel which found its way to the big screen back in 2000. Like Fight Club this novel was aimed at disenchanted 16 — 25 year olds tired of the rat race, capitalism etc. More meaningless pretentious philosophizing, even less character development, throw in a dash of romance, a pinch of melodrama, a teaspoon of surrealism and you have a style heavy book that (just like Fight Club) leans on a great idea rather than on good writing. The Short-Timers — Gustav Hasford Another style heavy novel that coulda been. This Vietnam war account is the basis for the famous film Full Metal Jacket (1987) by Stanley Kubrick. Kudos to Kubrick who did away with Hasford's overbearing stoner prose and stuck to the meat of the novel which was the clever boot camp dialogue and harrowing recruit training. The book is semi autobiographical. It seems as though the moment Hasford is free to roam the streets of Vietnam his writing became almost unreadable in a drug induced haze of (again) stream of consciousness babble. Black Spring — Henry Miller One may be surprised to find an established writer like the controversial Henry Miller on this list but after turning the obscene into an art form with Tropic of Cancer he wrote Black Spring which becomes rather unreadable and unintelligible after the first few pages. Miller's gift is to seize your attention within the first few lines in his writing. He shocks you with his unwholesome combination of literary mastery combined with smut and depravity. He explodes within the first few pages with prose so electric that even George Orwell dedicated an essay in praise of him. However his flaw is his inability to sustain this style at length as he goes from captivating to dull and rambling. Black Spring is a perfect example of that flaw. And last but not least The Trial — Franz Kafka Yes. One of the world's greatest writers is also guilty of style over substance, most noticeably in the above stated novel. If there is one author who has cemented a style for himself it has to be Kafka as kafkaesque is now an accepted English word for anything related to paranoia and fantastic surrealism inspired through stifling bureaucracy. The Trial is not a bad book imho. In fact it is the most representative of his style. However one cannot help but lean towards believing whether the work is a testament to his genius or the whimsical ramblings of lonely, neurotic mild-mannered man. I tend to lean towards the latter as halfway through the novel it seems as though his unique style can't help but disguise the fact that there is no real story of substance happening. But these are all my honest opinions. Love em or hate em.

Question: Why do people think Midsommar is a good horror movie? When I'm watching the movie, I didn't think it's scared even a bit.
Answer: If you go to watch Midsommar simply to get 'scared’ then you are in for a disappointment. It may not scare you in the sense that a knife wielding, mask wearing stalker/killer may or an evil, spectral entity that comes after you through your television but it may build feelings ranging from discomfort to dread to shock. It does not rely on fantastic and nightmarish tropes: ghouls, monsters and masked murderers etc. It doesn't condescend to our primitive childhood fears of a single creature/person out to get us (typically in the darkness of night). Most generic horrors play to our primitive childish fears: unwholesome locations, darkness, ugliness, being alone, unexplainable phenomena, pain, danger, the unknown etc. Midsommar does the opposite we are treated to a sunny, picturesque location full of wide open fields, brightly painted buildings and smiling beautiful people. Midsommar is not traditionally ‘scary’ because none of the characters are villains/monsters. None of the acts commited are evil when viewed in a purely cultural context. The film allows you to ponder on the cruelty and barbarism of several centuries past and at the same time offers a critique as to whether the self-centred, indifference that is characteric of our modern times is any better. Midsommar is a slow burning, psychological horror. It is one of the most disturbing movies I've seen in a long time, let alone one of the best. Ari Aster's directing style had been compared to Stanley Kubrick and I can really see the influence from The Shining, another slow burn, psychological horror. The story involves a young woman who recently suffers from a personal tragedy going to rural Sweden with her boyfriend and his college friends and witness/partake in the pagan Midsommar festival held once every 90 years. Little to their knowledge the participants take the festival a little more seriously than to their liking. I consider Midsommar more resonating and effective than 99% of the horror movies out there. If it doesn't scare you then too bad. There's a whole bunch ghouls and psycho killer movies out there for your liking.

Question: Why do movies try to make female characters look strong by making male characters look stupid and weak?
Answer: Hollywood needs to take a course in studying James Cameron. He is without a doubt one of the greatest character writers of the 20th century. This is especially in regards to women. Every female lead he has written has become iconic. They are neither strong nor weak. What they are good at is adapting to their environment/circumstances, using their wits and keeping focus on goals rather than trying to prove how much stronger they are than the opposite sex. Examples include: Ellen Ripley - Aliens Lindsey Brigman - The Abyss Sarah Connor - Terminator/Terminator 2 Helen Tasker - True Lies Rose DeWitt Bukater - Titanic Take a look at all the photos. Tell me what is common among all the women. If you answered fear, uncertainty, anxiety, instability or anything hinting at crippling emotions you are correct. None of these women were stronger or more brave than their male counterparts in these films. However all of them were loyal, intelligent and selfless. They were multifaceted characters, displaying weaknesses in many scenarios and great strength and determination in others. They were all emotional. They all depended on the men around them and in various instances the men depended on them. The relationship between male and female was symbiotic Ellen Ripley offered her experience and intelligence to a group of macho, shoot first, ask questions later, marines to survive an alien invasion. Lindsey Brigman kept the SEAL team from turning into savages, kept the ego of her ex-husband/team leader in check and demonstrated love and humanity to the alien life-forces they encountered. Sarah Connor went from being a relatively weak and mild mannered waitress fighting to survive to an obsessive, violent mercenary and then to a more stable and grounded maternal figure after reuniting with her long lost son. Helen Tasker transformed from a mousy, timid housewife to the world's sexiest woman in a mission to save her marriage, in doing so she saves her husband's life as well and Rose went from being a passive, poor little rich girl to a tragic romantic figure that extended beyond class and wealth. All of these women had their weaknesses. None of them dared to think about defeating/overcoming an obstacle without male help. They were women and they were proud of what they were. Many times they screwed up and many times they made foolish decisions/actions but they always saw the bigger picture. They always knew when it was time to lead and when it was time to serve. They were all globally cherished and were well written female characters. Unlike the ones below.

Question: Is it morally wrong to want to read Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf?
Answer: I’ve no desire to read it but if someone suggested that by reading it, it would prove that I’m secretly a neo-Nazi then I would have a hearty laugh. I’ve read Venus is Furs. I’m not a masochist or into any form of BDSM. I’ve read The Doors of Perception. I haven’t ingested LSD nor have I been tempted. I’ve read Trainspotting. I’m not in the least bit curious to try heroin or any drug 1000 times more powerful than my greatest orgasm. Read The Stranger and Crime and Punishment. I was never tempted to kill someone for the heck of it. Read The Sun Also Rises and I still hate bullfighting to this day. Read all the Harry Potter novels and I'm still not inspired or influenced by witchcraft. I've read Lolita. I don't sympathise with pedophiles and hebephiles. I've read 1984. I think my Government is way too stupid to suppress my thoughts and actions. My point is I've read these books because I enjoy reading. If I don't enjoy the story, find it uninteresting or dislike the author's writing I simply put the book down. The only people who will get influenced by Mein Kampf or any of the books I've listed above are people who already believe the values and ideas they think the book suggests. The book is simply greater affirmation (or for some people, a good excuse) for enacting on these desires.

Question: As a teacher, have you ever been accused of something?
Answer: I'm not a teacher but as a librarian we operate in the role of a teacher sometimes. A student by the name of Keston was in the back of the library, headphones on, singing loudly an explicit rap song complete with excessive use of the n-word, obscene language and misogynistic lyrics. This created a ruckus in the library with some students laughing and others disturbed by his singing. Keston pretended that he was doing schoolwork and not noticing a thing. This grinded my gears. Keston was usually a well-behaved young man but lately he was starting to act up as though desperation for attention. He was of African descent and quite dark skinned. I went over to him and tapped on the table and warned him to stop with the singing. He nodded and I left but the moment I went back to my desk he started singing again, even more loudly, causing the class clowns to bellow in laughter. I went over to him and touched his shoulder. 'Nigger don't touch me' he said and he continued his singing, his clowns rolling in laughter. 'Can you please get out of the library!’ I said calmly and he proceeded to laugh at me and continue singing his vile verses. I asked him one more time to get out of the library otherwise he'd be banned. He proceeded to sing gangster rap lyrics of shooting my bitch-ass full of holes while gesturing pointing a gun at me with his fingers. I then got an idea. 'Keston!’ I said loudly, 'Can you please get your disrespectful black ass out of this library.’ He immediately stopped. His clowns fell silent. I watched as he got worked up called me racist several times and threatened that I would lose my job. In his mind it was okay to call me nigger and gesture shooting me but it was not okay for someone to tell him to get his black ass out. Keston didn't realise that this was Trinidad not the US. Keston then left the library and a few minutes later returned with the School Safety Officer (SSO) Mr. Aigle, a man as dark as himself . Unaware that Aigle and I had a good working relationship, Keston proceeded to recount a story minimizing his actions and emphasising that I shouted violent and racist slogans at him. When I told my side of the story several students confirmed what I had said. I apologized for my choice of words but Aigle told me not to, citing the Golden Rule. He then told Keston to bring his black ass into his office immediately. Aigle was the most un-PC, un-subjective person on the school compound and Keston thought by having the same skin colour, Aigle would have the same mindset as him. Boy was he wrong. He got suspended for a week. I've long since transferred out of that school but if I see old Aigle again I'll get him that beer I promised him.

Question: What was your worst experience while living with roommates?
Answer: Some years ago my father was having trouble with his landlord and was given an eviction notice. Seeing that I had separated from my ex and remained for the time being in our spacious two bedroom apartment he asked to move in with me and split the rent. I agreed, but on the condition that he doesn't bring my brother with him. My brother has been suffering possible untreated manic depression/schizophrenia for years. He refuses to get help and for this has been a strain on everyone around him. My father had been looking after him for the past six years after my brother abandoned his job and stopped looking after himself. This is quite a feat considering my father himself suffers from (treated) bipolar disorder. Long story short within a week of my father moving in I arrive home to see my brother sitting there with all his belongings with him. My father claims that he had nowhere to go and it would be just for a week, after which he'll help him move back in to our mother's house. This ‘week’ lasted an entire year. My father and brother are two of the worst roomates I've ever had and ever will have. In the end our spats became so vicious that I was overjoyed to hear that my father was invited by my uncle to rent a room in his house in Tobago. My uncle didn't know what he had in store for him. The moment they left I changed the lock to the apartment. I've recently built a home and moved in. The house is near completion. My father's stay in Tobago did not last long (unsurprisingly) and he and my brother have been moving around constantly. They are my family and I feel sad that they were unfortunate to suffer such a handicap. I feel sorry that my father in coming down in age (64). Part of me wants to give them lodging when the house is complete but part of me screams in my ear that it will be a big mistake. C'est la vie.

Question: What is wrong with parents these days that they don’t teach their kids manners & respect?
Answer: About a year ago a teacher brought a parent to me. The parent was a mother of two of the most atrocious girls in the school. These were girls who got into fights, provoked others into fighting through taunting and accusing on social media, disrespected everyone in positions of authority and had a nasty, defiant attitude in general. The teacher wanted the parent to get an overall view of all the trouble these girls caused and how desperately they were in need of an intervention. As a librarian for the school library I had had a few bad encounters with the girls so seeing that the mother was there waiting patiently for my story (and wearing a T-shirt that showed that she worked for the police service) I was only too glad to give her the details of my experience and my hope for these girls and their future. After about 2 minutes of recounting my experience with them and making impassioned pleas I glanced at the mother's face and noticed that there was not a trace of emotion. There was an awkward silence as I waited for her to say something. 'Is that all?’ she said with an irritated tone. 'Yes' I replied. 'Did they do anything to you personally?’ she added. 'No. It's not about me. It's about the library…..it's about the school.’ There was another pause. 'So are you banning them from your library?’ she said. 'No I never said I was banning them from the library.’ With that said she remained silent and stared at me, waiting for me to dismiss the conversation of which I did. She then left with the teacher to talk to another teacher who had had encounters with them. Later that day I heard that that was the formula she applied in all the conversations. She listened to every teacher's complaint and simply waited to hear if any action was going to be taken against her girls. She was pumped and ready to fight anyone who was going to take action against her girls or deny them their ‘rights.’ She had no solutions in her mind as to the problems the girls caused because in her mind there were no problems. The girls were defiant against the school system because the mother was defiant against the system. The mom's attitude was that the school system and its rules were a big joke; that all kids behaved like her daughters behaved and she was not having her daughters victimised. So my answer to all this is parents don't teach manners and respect to their kids because they don't believe in the system and they think they are entitled to their own set of rules to live by.

Question: What is the dumbest thing your teacher has said to you, and what did you say back?
Answer: My family was on state welfare for a while. When I was 12 and attending my first year of Secondary (High) school my mom gave me this letter from the Welfare Department for my teacher to sign. The Government had it that every year or so children who are recipients of welfare must have the letter signed by their teacher so as to prove that the child does indeed go to school consistently and the parents/guardians aren't using the money for the wrong reasons. It was usually an awkward, shameful experience for me, having the teacher sign for my family to continue collecting welfare cheques. Most teachers would do me the honours of signing it quickly, getting it over with and sparing me the embarrassment and the risk of other classmates seeing the letter. However this teacher had to be the exception. Mr. Din Chong was our music teacher. He was an eccentric, middle aged bachelor who kept to himself in his cavernous music room and rarely ever associated with his fellow teachers. If one came to school early in the morning, you could hear in the emptiness of the building, him playing sombre classics on his piano like a modern day Phantom of the Opera. When I approached him I expected him to simply read the heading of the letter and the first paragraph, sign his name and return it to me quickly. Unfortunately for me, Din Chong had little experience in such delicate affairs. I nervously handed him the letter and he stared at me. 'What's this?’ he said warily and staring as though I just gave him cease and desist warning. Two girls who sat at the front stared curiously at us. 'It's for you to sign,' I said nervously, 'My mother said to give it to you. It's from the Government.’ Din Chong got fidgety as he opened the letter bearing the coat of arms of the country. He seemed more nervous than me. He read the the first line of the letter. 'Welfare cheque?’ he said aloud, 'What's that about?’ Going red in the face I muttered that it's for my mother to get some cheques. Din Chong stared at me as though I spoke in Latin. He wanted to know if it had anything to do with deductions in his salary. I kept telling him no. The two girls at the front gave me pitiable looks, feeling my pain. Din Chong then takes the letter and leaves to go to his Head of Department to find out what all of this meant. When he came back he looked embarassed. He scribbled his signature at the back of the letter and returned it to me. When I gave my mother the signed letter and explained what took place she got visibly angry? 'Is that teacher an idiot?’ she said. 'Why?’ I asked. 'He wrote his signature in the wrong place and he didn't put a school stamp.’ All of that for nothing. My brother had a welfare letter to get signed as well. Knowing my brother's teacher to be a bit more worldly she took both letters to him, explained the situation and got him to sign and stamp them both. To this day my mother could never forget my teacher who didn't know what a welfare cheque was.
