Question: When have you refused to lend money to someone?
Answer: A few days ago, while working in Papa John's there was a new employee called Stefan. He was 30 and had a soft spoken demeanour about him. He worked pretty well at the restaurant but we all unanimously considered him to be a pest. If there was an award for beggar of the year he would comfortably win it. If one of us headed out to go buy lunch Stefan would beg that he/she buy him a snack. If one of us came back with groceries Stefan would eye our bags so intently so as to determine if there was something edible in it he could beg for. Every day he asked a co-worker for money borrowed on a rotation basis. One of the delivery drivers loaned him $100 after hearing a multitude of sad stories. Big mistake. I would go to the nearby grocery and the lady in charge there would tell me that there is a Papa John's worker who comes in daily and begs for credit, that we ought to do something about it. He would lament about how much he has to pay to travel home at nights and beg for fare money yet we would spot him hanging around bars with his friend late at night after work. He was not functionally literate but would spend most of his free time voice messaging random women on Facebook and incessantly asking us co workers to read the messages they sent for him. Many times we urged him that a lot of these women seemed catfishy and scheming but he would stubbornly ignore us. Whenever he got his salary he would disappear for a day or two and return with another humdrum sad story about how he lost his money. Last week after getting paid he disappeared for three days and the manager listed him as having abandoned the job. The following day a police officer came to us to explain that the night before Stefan made a report to the police station that he was hanging out with a friend at a bar and was robbed. The police added that Stefan would like his job back, that the police felt sorry for him seeing that he couldn't read and write and had to give him a ride home that night. The manager lauded the officer for his consideration but refused Stefan's request to get his job back. He added that most likely Stefan's story was a fabrication and that he lost his money chasing down women again, that he had a bad reputation for begging not just in the restaurant but in the entire district. To answer the above question, one night he claimed he had a $20 in his hand and a strong wind blew and it ended up in the fire in the pizza oven. He asked me if I could lend him $20 to reach home. I explained to him that wind doesn't blow inside of enclosed restaurants and politely declined to lend him the money.

Question: Have you ever come back to your vehicle only to find something quite unexpected?
Answer: I worked pizza delivery some years ago at a branch that was located in a rather iffy town. I used to park my vehicle at the tiny parking lot in the back. There was a dumpster that was located in the parking lot that attracted a lot of drug addicted homeless men who would scour the garbage for some odds and ends of food. One night we worked late and I stayed back after the store closed to give a ride to three ladies who would've been stranded waiting for taxis that late hour. I waited as they swept, mopped and balanced the cash register. An hour later they are finally done and we head to the back to the parking lot. Something looked odd about my pickup and upon closer inspection I saw that one of the glass windows at the door had been smashed with several tiny fragments of glass scattered in the back seat and floor. There was a gaping hole near the dashboard where my deck had once been located. The culprit had smashed a $600 glass window to get in and steal a beaten up, old car deck that probably had a $100 value at best. Having your car deck stolen is pretty commonplace around the world. However what was really unexpected was the reaction of the ladies with me. One of them chastised me for being such a fool for not parking my vehicle to the front of the store. The other found the ordeal somewhat amusing and told me that I should be happy that they didn't hotwire and steal the pickup. The third simply walked off and took a taxi without any comment. These were older women whom I had consistently remained after work to offer a ride being concerned for their safety. None of them even pretended to show any sympathy for what had happened to me. While I swept out the broken glass off the seats and floor, the remaining two stood there trading insider work-gossip and never made an attempt to assist me. I wanted nothing more than get in my vehicle and leave them there but I told myself that I would be the bigger person and go through with what I promised. I drove them homewards in silence. After that experience I stopped offering rides to stranded co-workers unless they were good friends. I used to feel so sorry for many of these ladies working fast food but I later realized that many of them are there not because of circumstances but because of their own ignorance and selfish attitudes. It took me a broken window and stolen deck to learn that lesson.

Question: At what age did you stop enjoying YA fiction?
Answer: I'm not hating on YA authors but I never saw the appeal. As a child Roald Dahl was my favorite author. I also read abridged and illustrated editions of the popular classics from Mark Twain, H.G. Wells, Arthur Conan Doyle, Dickens etc. As I entered my teens I attempted unabridged editions of the classics and voraciously read through my mother's bookshelf of adult novels. In my late teens I fell in love with The Good Earth by Pearl S. Buck and Angela's Ashes by Frank McCourt. I discovered early that I had a passion for historical stories of persistence through hardship, survival etc. YA books, to me, were for the kids who didn't really have a passion for reading and were off to a late start. YA books never had the charisma and imagination of children's books nor did they have the depth and seriousness of adult novels. They were just generic books written for overly self aware kids imho. I know I may sound pompous but I really didn't want to read about rich kids in school, girls dating the bad boy, broken friendships, parents divorcing or a boy and his dog surviving in some post apocalyptic future. I know there are good YA books out there but I really haven't come across one that appealed to me nor am I interested in looking for one at this stage in my life.

Question: What is the best comeback you used on someone?
Answer: When I was much younger my first job was at a warehouse that distributed cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and a host of other things. I was an entry level grunt (or 'picker’ as we called it) along with many other young men like myself. This one guy named Dwayne who came from the hood and spoke as though he had a real tough life in the streets (he didn't) became friends with the supervisor and in little time he got promoted to a 'checker’ which gave him authority over me Dwayne and I didn't have the warmest relationship. He would constantly speak condescendingly of me and my 'book sense' and how I was gullible and naive and 'didn't know the life.’ In reality he was simply envious that I got better grades than him in school. This envy became apparent when I registered for college and got accepted as an evening student. I gave Dwayne my timetable for him to acknowledge that I could no longer work overtime on certain days because of my classes. I didn't need his approval I just had to inform him of it. Dwayne eyed my timetable scornfully and replied that he couldn't approve this because it was unfair to the rest of the staff including himself who had to work overtime even harder now with one man down. I replied that I didn't need his approval. It was already approved by the supervisor. Dwayne snarled and said, ‘Maybe I should go and pursue a degree too? Maybe everyone should go and pursue classes and better themselves?…' 'And that's a problem because?’ I replied. Dwayne then adopted a disappointed look. It was the look he gave whenever he had something condescending to say about me. He said solemnly to himself, 'Some people have book sense but no common sense.’ I replied, 'And you have neither.’ I then walked off. With all his supposed loyalty, less than a year later he left the warehouse after getting accepted to a higher paying job.

Question: Have you ever walked out of an interview?
Answer: I didn’t walk out but I sure pissed the hell out of them and made it as awkward as possible. A cable company was looking for part time sales reps for their dishes. I already had a full time job but was looking for a sideline. They arranged for the interview to be at 9am. I came an hour early to their main office. The security had a sour look in his face and asked me what it is I wanted. I told him my name and that I had an interview for 9am. He looked at me as though I was talking jibberish and simply muttered that he didn’t know anything about that and directed me to the payments/customer service area to ask one of the people there where to go. I ignored the queue and walked directly towards the agents and the guard comes frantically running to me like a mama bird protecting its nest. ‘Follow instructions,’ he grunted loudly, ‘I told you to join the line.’ I wanted to bark at him that he never told me that and that he had to be the worse security guard I’ve ever encountered in my life, but of course that wouldn’t bear well for my interview. Suddenly a short pretty young lady passing by looked at me and said, ‘You’re Mr. Williamson?’ I said yes and she told me to follow her to the waiting area. She was professional but I found her a tad too detached. She didn’t ask me about my trip here or apologize for the confusion or anything. She led me to a corridor and and told me to sit by a row of chairs and that the sales supervisor would see me in a moment. She went into a room and came out with a tall, attractive lady with curly hair who looked no older than 24. They passed me without a glance and I assumed that they were both sales people. While sitting there a bunch of people kept passing and no one seemed to recognize my existence. They were all salespeople and mostly men. They came in to use the company phones to try and close sales and make a bunch of noise laughing and hooting afterwards with one another. Something about the vibe of the place just didn’t sit well with me. Around 9:45am the two young ladies passed by me again and without a word went back into the room they had left prior. A few minutes later the shorter one came out and called me in. She said the supervisor was ready to see me. I came in and saw a simple table in front of me where the tall girl sat with her fingers clasped staring at me. The shorter one sat to the side of her and they beckoned me to sit. Just looking at them I could sense that they were ladies who treated themselves well. Their clothes looked expensive, hair, nails and skin well treated, designer handbags etc. They were both very attractive and they knew it. The taller one proceeded to talk about sales and asked what the word ‘sale’ means to me. I kept mentioning how I prefer customer satisfaction rather than soliciting a sale and each time I did that she paused and reverted back to talking about how this job is concerned with hard selling and customer satisfaction can’t come if you don’t have customers. ‘We focus on sales only’ the shorter one chimed in. In my mind I sarcastically said to myself, ‘That’s a shocker.’ They then started discussing targets. They showed me a list of all the packages they were selling. They wanted to get the most expensive packages sold because they believe that people weren’t aware of how much better these were. They wanted to know if I had a problem focusing on selling only the expensive packages this month. They wanted me to lie and say basic packages were unavailable at the moment and that the next month I can sell basic like normal. I was starting to find them and this whole place tiresome. They clearly had values different from mine and I could see myself having spats with them in no time. I decided that I wanted out. However I wasn’t one to walk out on interviews as word gets around in this tiny country. I started asking about pay. ‘Commissions’ the taller one said. ‘Aren’t there any paying jobs,’ I replied, ‘With like a salary.’ They both looked at each other and the taller one replied that there were but that was a different division. I started telling them how I bought a dish from this company some years ago and how I thought it was garbage. I then said that my skills were so good that I could sell thousands of those garbage dishes to people who didn’t even have televisions. They both remained silent. I then said that I only worked on weekends and I don’t answer calls between 8 - 4 pm. They both looked at each other. ‘So Mr. Williamson’ the taller one said with a smile, ‘That’s the end of our interview. Thank you for your time and we’ll be contacting you before the end of the week.’ Without bothering to shake hands I headed out of the room like a man with a bladder control problem. Regardless to say I got a formal email from them a week later civilly explaining that I was unsuccessful with the interview.

Question: Did you ever stop caring about how old you are?
Answer: I remember when I was 17 and the anxiety I felt knowing that in a few months I would be a full fledged adult with responsibilities. Ripe for work life, going steady and potential marriage. Reality: I was just a kid still going to school and nothing remotely resembling a girlfriend. I remember when I was 19 how much the prospect of turning 20 meant. The big 2–0 meant that I was a ‘hardback’ man planning his career, house and family. No time for shits and giggles. Reality: This was the most immature period of my life and I was far from any kind of career, house or family. I had more time than ever for shits and giggles. I remember at 25 I observed my hairline beginning to recede. I was paranoid that I was going bald. I felt like I would be seen as a balding old perv if I chatted up 18 yo girls in the mall. I thought I was no longer a youth. Reality: I was not a balding old perv but a young man with self esteem issues. At 30 I was working two jobs trying to make ends meet. I had a daughter and was in a troubled relationship with her mother. The last thing I cared about was how old I was and I haven’t put much thought to it since almost seven years later. The moral of my story is I would’ve enjoyed my life much better if I didn’t worry about age and age expectations the way I did as a youth. I am much less bothered about turning 40 than when I was about to turn 20. When the time comes I’ll be proud to know that I was lucky to live so long.

Question: Who are the most uncomfortable movie characters depicting the UK that you’ve ever seen?
Answer: Gotta go with three films and I'm listing the characters based on the level of discomfort (low to high). *** Spoilers ahead *** Movie: Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (1960) Character(s): Arthur Location: Nottingham The late, great Albert Finney gives a magnificent performance as Arthur, a rebellious, young, working class man who has somewhat of a fetish for stirring up trouble and going beyond the limit. The title refers to the fact that Arthur begins his trouble immediately after his work ends on Saturday. He dedicates his Saturday nights to going out pubs and drinking himself beyond consciousness, stirring up trouble in the streets, fighting etc. His Sundays are spent engaging in a sexual affair with the equally defiant wife of his mild-mannered co-worker. He eventually gets her pregnant while hiding his deeds from his own morally virtuous girlfriend. In the final scene Arthur confesses his actions to his girlfriend who forgives him and gets him to agree to marry her and settle down. Arthur agrees but angrily throws a stone at a nearby building. His girlfriend asks 'What did you do that for?’ He replies, 'Just felt like it I suppose.’ I don't live in the UK but I know and have befriended many Arthurs throughout my life here in Trinidad. Arthurs can never find inner peace and unknowingly to themselves, foster a subconscious hatred towards structure, routine and normalcy. They believe that a stone must be thrown into the rolling cogs every so often otherwise life would just be uneventful and monotonous. At their best Arthurs can be just angry, resentful troublemakers but at their worst they can be psychopathic narcissists who cause harm and destruction to all those who engage with them. Arthur in this film was a downright bastard in this kitchen-sink classic and anyone not interested in him as a character study would simply find him mildly repugnant. Movie: Kill List (2011) Character(s): Jay Location: Sheffield Kill List is something of a psychological/supernatural horror inspired by the fiction of HP Lovecraft. However there's nothing fictional about the character Jay. He's a menacing, angry and uncouth ex-soldier turned contract killer, quite possibly suffering from PTSD from a botched mission. He has a son and a wife who urges him to take a normal job as they are in financial distress but Jay prefers to wait for that one big contract job that would provide for him for years to come. His 'luck’ arrives as a friend of his wife hires him to eliminate various unnamed people in a mysterious Kill List. Jay and his friend are given locations of the targets The Priest, The Librarian and The MP. Each kill becomes more mysterious than the last with both of the first two victims softly thanking Jay before being killed. The 2nd kill unearths video evidence of an underground society involved in the most, depraved and disturbing acts imaginable causing Jay to become even more unsettled. Jay's final kill leads him to a mansion where a some sort of pagan cult is taking place with several figures hidden in white robes are having a ceremony. Believing these to be the people involved in the depraved videos he starts shooting them, killing some and manages to kill the leader. However he is captured and forced to a knife-fight with a robed hunchback figure. Viciously stabbing the hunchback all over its body, it is revealed afterwards to be his wife with their son strapped to her back. His final kill was his own family. I believe Kill List to be a portrayal of a man with psychosis and schizophrenia brought on by severe PTSD. Neil Maskell gives a phenomenal performance as Jay. His consistently scowling face and venemous tone make him such an unsettling character that I fear ever running into such a person on a lonely side street at night. I may be wrong but I interpret a lot of the happenings to be solely in Jay's imagination. Jay saw his own killings as something as a grand mission against evil so as to erase guilt from a botched mission in Kyiv where he, quite possibly, had to do heinous acts to survive. Kill List, to me, is a heightened portrayal of a mentally unstable man. Movie: Eden Lake (2008) Character(s): The parents Location: London Condemned by critics for stereotyping and exaggerating the 'Broken Britain’ underclass this film is relentless in its portrayal of savagery. Jenny and Steve are a couple vacationing and decide a visit a lake near a working class community. Steve is highly critical of the behaviour of the children of the area and the parents' role in their poor upbringing. Even though the lake is condemned to become a quarry Steve and Jenny sneak in for a final visit but become targets of a gang of local delinquent 'Chavs’ driven by a maniacal leader Brett. After constantly being harassed by the youths, a fight ensues in which Brett's dog is killed. Enraged he eventually raises the stakes by capturing Steve and having members of the group stab him to death while being filmed. Jenny is then captured and with botched attempts to kill her as well, Brett murders two of his own gang members while the rest look on silently. In the ensuing chase two other members of the gang are killed. Bleeding to near death and dirty, Jenny manages to run to a nearby house where a house party involving several middle aged locals are taking place. There is copious drug, alcohol and sex among the members and even though it is certain that these people are not her cup of tea she seeks help from one of the more sympathetic women. However she soon realises that many of them are parents of the gang and when one of the women get a police call informing of her murdered son, the parents suspect her and suddenly transform into 'we look after our own’ monsters. As far fetched as Brett and the gang is portrayed, I believe a good job was done portraying the parents. There are so many communities of families out there who have vague morals in regards to greater society but a strict code of secrecy and loyalty for themselves. Despite many of the horrific scenes in the movie, nothing was more uncomfortable and disturbing than this final scene. There is no major onscreen violence during the last five minutes but just looking at Jenny hiding in the bathroom as she hears the voices of the parents of these monsters (learning of their dead kids) screaming in trauma and yelling in rage as she acknowledges the fact that they will soon kill her makes it the most uncomfortable scene I've ever witnessed in a film set in the UK.

Question: What's something on an employee's first day that sets off red flags?
Answer: In my second year at my current job, a lady was hired to replace my senior who had resigned. The job was in a public office and for the most part was quite easy going. Somebody off the streets could learn the essentials in just a few hours. The lady who came had seniority and several years more experience than me working at a different branch. I therefore expected her to have a wealth of knowledge and experience to share with me. 'How does this work again?’ 'Did I do this right?’ 'How about you be the one to do that? You're so good at it.’ 'Can you show me how to do (such-and-such) again?’ The lady transferred from a location that had the exact same type of system and technology as mine yet she had not a clue how to do anything! How was this woman in a senior position? She didn't know anything about the job. Was she dumb? A week of 'training’ had passed and she didn't really learn anything and had to be supervised at all times. Before I could find out how it was that she was so slow she suddenly vanished. She stopped turning up at work and calls to her phone went unanswered. I sent an email to HR explaining that she had gone AWOL. They gave some half-assed reply. A few months later, after she had long been forgotten, I get a frantic letter from HR saying that they have been paying her salary and they've just become aware that she has not been turning up to work. ‘No shit,' I say in my mind. HR investigates and finds out that she had accepted another job elsewhere the entire time and was gladly accepting two salaries. HR demanded that she return the unearned salary. She said she would but she was going through financial distress at the moment. She never returned a cent. HR washed their hands of the matter and kept it hush hush. Turns out she wasn't dumb at all. So my answer to the question 'what sets off red flags on an employee's first day?’ Playing dumb.

Question: What are some classic movies with surprisingly conservative themes and agendas?
Answer: Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory (1971) One of my favourite movies as a child and as an adult I still adore it. However as I've grown older I've noticed, what I believe to be, certain pro conservative aesthetics throughout the movie. Casual acceptance of poverty. In the beginning of the film we observe that Charlie is poor and resides in a one room shack with his mother and four bedridden grandparents. Every day he is given ‘cabbage soup' and though little mention of it is made in the movie, Charlie's father in fact died from a work related incident at a toothpaste factory. Despite this, in no instance does the family complain about their lot in life nor the lack of government assistance. They don't even speak about the toothpaste factory's responsibility towards the father's death. They seem to accept their poverty as no fault of the system but simply bad luck and their current lot in life. The Candyman can… In one scene the owner of a popular candy store serenades a bunch of kids with the now-classic The Candy Man song. We see him liberally tossing various candies and chocolates towards the kids without account or interest in his inventory or cash. One gets the perception that this is some sort of communal children's paradise where all these delightful goodies are given for free by a mystical Candy Man figure only for the camera to pan towards Charlie sadly staring in through the window, out in the cold. We then realize that this is not a child's paradise. The kids are indeed charged for the sweets (and quite possibly the Candyman makes a killing when he sends the bill to the parents). This then reinforces the idea that nothing in this world is free. One thing the Candyman can't do is give free candy. Wonka himself Willy Wonka is portrayed as the quintessential 20th century, eccentric man of wealth and power type persona in the vein of Henry Ford and Thomas Edison. He is extremely private and enshrouds his ‘trade secrets' with fanatical obsession. He is portrayed as friendly, giving and charismatic yet mechanical and indifferent to an almost sociopathic level. Only as I grew older did I notice how much the town looked like a ghetto whilst Wonka himself enjoyed a secret, near magical lifestyle that 99.9% of the population could only dream of. The entire competition was revealed to be simply a ploy to find an innocent and faithful child for Wonka to adopt to continue his legacy. Wonka couldn't care less if the children all died as seen in his reactions to their unfortunate accidents. He hires a man who pretends to be his main competitor to try a staged attempt to find out which of the children were susceptible to bribery. He gets the parents to unwittingly sign contracts to the child's disadvantage without giving them time to read. Who could forget the scene where he yells and berates Charlie and grandpa Joe? This is near the end where they come to claim their lifetime supply of chocolate only to find Wonka fiendishly harping on about their signed contract and ranting about how they voided it by dirtying his ceiling through horseplay. Wonka represents a figure of conservative success at its very worst (or best, according to how you look at it). The Slav…..I mean the Oompa Loompas And of course the controversial Oompa Loompas. Represented as pygmy Africans in the book they are portrayed as singing dwarf like men with flaming orange skin, green hair and silly costumes. So many parodies have been created in regards to the Oompa Loompas actually being a colourful representation of slavery. They aren't allowed outside of the building nor any communication with the outside world and it is negligible if they are given a wage or even enjoy the benefit of basic human rights. The movie posits that Wonka once employed ordinary salaried human workers but had to close the factory for 3 years due to spying and sale of his secret recipes, etc by human employees. If I could dare to be a bit tongue in cheek I'm certain Wonka has a team of armed Oompa Loompa sentries who supervise the others and anyone trying to escape is shot on sight. In conclusion Wonka and his ideals are well suited towards a conservative climate. It is clear that he believes in an hierarchy and that his little world must be governed by a select few of which authority must be transferred to those whom are carefully chosen to be the best to rule and uphold order. He is a staunch capitalist and believes that rules and laws should exist but a few eggs must be broken for progress to continue. On a personal level he is charitable but wary of the majority and he places his own self interest and ambitions above that of the collective problems of the common people of whom he believes create their own problems for themselves whenever given an opportunity. So Willy Wonka is my choice for the greatest movie with hidden conservative themes and agendas, good and bad.

Question: What's the stupidest thing you've done for love?
Answer: This wasn't a falling head over heels with the wrong person type of stupid (although that definitely was the case). This was stupid as in a Mr. Bean or Inspector Clouseau level of dimwit. I was an A level student and infatuated with one of my classmates. She didnt have the exact same feelings for me unfortunately. We both were coming to the end of our schooling. We were sent home a couple weeks before our final exams. I would literally beg her to come study with me in the National Library. The library was a brand new building with 3 floors available for the public. I went there a Saturday and was in the adult floor. I called her phone to ask her to come but she never picked up. I told her voice mail that I was in the library if she was interested in meeting me to study. A few moments later I got a voice message from her saying that she's getting ready to leave the house and might meet me. I became totally ecstatic. These were the days before WhatsApp and SMS was the chief source of texting. I sent her a text message 'What time you coming?’ I didn't notice that in my excitement I texted the above message to my own phone number rather than hers. Some seconds later I felt my phone vibrate and saw a message: 'What time you coming?’ This was the message that I accidentally sent to myself. I immediately assumed it was her and hastily replied to message (aka myself) 'I'm already here!’ I was so excited for our potential study date. I envisioned us going out for lunch and planned how it is I would ask her to go visit the zoo with me. I then felt my phone vibrate and saw a message in my inbox, 'I'm already here!’ I almost jumped out of my chair. Wow. That was quick! How did she get here so fast? I called her phone but it went straight to voicemail. I hastily sent her (aka myself) a message 'I’m up on the 2nd floor.' I then quickly went to the entrance of the building to see if I saw her. I looked around like a wild animal but didn't see her. Where was she? Why can't she ever answer her phone? I pulled out my phone to call her when I saw that I received another message: 'I'm up on the 2nd floor.’ What the hell!? I ran back to the second floor and went to the security at the entrance and asked him if he saw such and such girl and gave him her description. He stared at me in a mocking way and replied 'No.’ I went inside and searched through the entire second floor and couldn't find her. I panicked, wondering if she didn't see me and thought I was playing games and left. I replied to her (aka myself) a message, 'I'm not seeing you!!!’ I then called her phone. I was determined that she answered the call. I told myself that I wouldn't stop until she answered. During the second ring I heard a notification sound. I got another message from ‘her’ : 'I'm not seeing you!!!’ Aaargh. 'Well maybe if you pickup the goddamn phone we wouldn't have this problem!' I thought to myself. Part of me felt as though so she was toying with me while another part felt as though this was just a case of bad communication. I rang her phone nonstop until she finally answered in great annoyance. 'What!’ she almost yelled. 'Where are you?’ I almost yelled in return. 'Why is that any of your business?’ she replied in irritation. 'Because I'm looking for you. If you stopped texting me and maybe answered your phone we wouldn't have this communication problem.’ 'What are you talking about I never texted you!’ she replied. 'Come off with the games,' I said in exasperation, 'Which part of the library are you at?’ She then hung up the phone. I grew angry and decided to send her an angry message. I looked at my SMS chat history with her and was confused. Where did all her messages disappear to? I then looked at my sent messages and saw that I had been sending messages to myself all morning. There's never a moment in my life I felt more stupid than that very moment.

Question: What was your scariest reason for an "I think we should leave" moment?
Answer: Turure Falls is one of the best hiking trails in Trinidad and Tobago. It is nestled in the mountainous Northern Range and consists of several gorgeous and pristine waterfalls, each one bigger than the last. It was favoured location for my ex and I and one day we made an impulse decision to take a day off from work and visit. We guessed that it would be nice and secluded if we visited on a Tuesday afternoon. To get there one had to drive for 30 minutes on a difficult and bumpy dirt road and then hike for 30 — 45 minutes on a trail alongside a mountain river. It was a most pleasing and refreshing journey, particularly feeling the cold clean water run on our face and backs. While we were drying off I could smell marijuana burning. A few seconds later we hear the sound of laughter. There was something unpleasant about the laughter, it seemed almost hateful. We immediately decided to leave. There are two trails to get to and from the Falls: follow the man made trail or simply walk the river. We observed two scruffy barechested men staring at us from a distance. From the position they stood at it was obvious they did not come from the trail but from some unknown path. It dawned on me what a dangerous situation we put ourselves in. We were completely alone for a 10 km radius. An idea popped into my head. I pretended to be on a video chat with someone, showing the imaginary person the beautiful scenery. I spoke loudly and with confidence so the men could hear and I made the conversation seem as though my friend was driving into the dirt road and on his way to the hike trail. Then we both got dressed and made our way back towards my vehicle. The two men had suddenly decided to head back as well, despite the fact that we never saw them get into the water. Knowing the two interconnecting trails very well we alternated between the man made trail and the river. We were both terrified out of our minds but tried our best not to show it. Everything about them seemed incongruent with the typical nature loving hiker. They carried nothing with them and nothing in the scenery seemed to be of interest to them. They just kept on following us. We were at the section where the trees were at its densest and we're about to decide to make a run for it when the sound of good-humoured laughter could be heard. It was the most beautiful sight we could behold. It was a large extended family coming to the Falls. There were several men in the family. We passed them by and waved at them. Strangely enough after they passed we could no longer hear the men behind us. It seemed as though they took off through some alternate path that they alone knew of. We came out of the trail and entered the vehicle and drove off, eternally grateful for the stroke of luck we had. We learned a valuable lesson that day. Never go on a hike alone.

Question: When did you think, "this can only be a fake"?
Answer: While employed as a pizza delivery rider, after the lifting of the COVID lock-down, our company decided to pull a fast one. A memo from the head office was circulated among all restaurant staff at all branches. It basically said that the company was so concerned about our welfare in these trying times that they were willing to keep a percentage of our weekly salary for us as a form of savings. The memo also mentioned that if we agreed to this ‘Pizza Savings’ (my term, not theirs) that we will be getting 0% interest. My delivery co-worker and I had a field day with that memo. I explained to her it is a good thing but it makes no sense to save your money with someone giving you 0%. I tried explaining how banks work, about buying shares etc and getting the best rates for your money. Both women looked at me in silence. In the end they both decided to ‘try it out.’ I didn't know what shocked me more. The fact that the restaurant attempted that stunt or the fact that it actually worked on two employees. Question: What is your review of The Banshees of Inisherin?
Answer: Watched this last Saturday with my girlfriend who thought it looked fascinating. Reading the two other reviews I agree with both as they mention that as a film it remains with you. To this hour it is still slowly digesting into my subconscious. I must stress on the word slow though. That is one of the biggest issues I had with the film. There's slow burner, where something is supposed to happen to connect the dots and then there's just slow, where there is little to no point. It's just slow for being slow's sake. That's the case with Banshees imho. The film posits the reason for the slowness being that Inisherin is a remote isle off Ireland and it's the 1920s. There is no electricity and the isle is so dull best friends no longer speaking could make front page news. This is actually the basis of the plot. Colin Farrel's Pádraic and Brendon Gleeson's Colm are no longer on speaking terms. Pádraic wants to continue idle chatting over beers in the pub while Colm wants more in life. This sets the stage for a series of surreal events that's supposed to be a mataphor for Irish Republicanism or something or the other. It is at that point where the film started losing me slowly. The cast is great, particularly Colin Farrell's slow-witted but good natured character who reminds me of George W Bush at times. He hits the nail on the head as a middle-aged, needy, ineffectual drunk. The cinematography is pretty and it does give a genuine sense of a place lost in time exactly one century ago. However both my girlfriend and I felt as though there was really no point. In beating on the head its symbolism and satire the movie missed out on what could've been a truly good period piece. My rating ** out of 4.

Answer: Some years ago, when I was hunting for a house I found a property that seemingly had my name stamped on it. It was a neat little hillside property with two bedrooms that was built sturdily and with class. It was one of those good old-fashioned houses that was built in the 70s/80s with a cute porch and terrazzo flooring. The best part was it was within the mortgage the bank offered me. I called the owner and arranged for a proper tour. I brought my ex with me (who like most women, observed things men wouldn't notice) and we climbed the hill and waited in the yard for the owner to arrive. She then motioned to me that in the yard (just a few feet from one of the bedrooms) was this awful looking makeshift shack that looked to be someone's home. What we in Trinidad refer to as a 'Piper Shack.’ She told me that somebody was squatting on the property. I was really looking forward to getting the house and said the shack was probably just a storage shed. She then pointed to a DirectTV satellite on the roof and some crude plumbing that sent filthy water towards the main house. While contemplating all of this, a wild-looking man appeared out of nowhere and loudly greeted us. He told us the house we were interested is a great house and that so many people are interested in it. We then watched him as he entered the shack. I was completely disheartened but I said that this must be some guy hired to maintain the house temporarily. My ex called me a fool. That he was most obviously a squatter. Two men arrived and introduced themselves as the owners. They were pleasant and they spoke with warm conviction of how great the house was and how it was a shame that they were selling it for so low a price. They explained that they were cousins and the house was willed to them by their uncle who died recently. The uncle had no children of his own and left everything to his closest kin. The cousins, who had homes of their own decided to sell the house and split the money. The younger cousin then went on a tangent reminiscing about how nice their old uncle was and how much work he did on the house. 'And who's that man living in the back there,' my ex bluntly interjected. I could see disappointment swell up on the man's face. He obviously wanted to avoid the subject. He explained that his uncle had no one in his old age. He was unmarried and the nephews were grown and living their lives with their families. The uncle befriended a wandering drug addict (‘piper’ in Trinidad terms) and allowed for the man to build his shack in the yard, use his electricity and water and even included in the will that the man have rights to live there as long as he wants. 'But he's a real nice man when you get to know him!' the other cousin chimed in, 'He's very helpful with manual labor. He could watch after your house for you when you're away!’ It was such a sad sight to see them trying to pitch the idea that having a drug addicted, mentally unstable man living in your yard and with legal rights could actually be a good thing. They said that once we saw inside the house we'd see how great of a deal we were getting. In the end we decided that it wasn't worth our while and politely declined.

Question: Have you ever met a dangerous person and not known it at the time?
Answer: Maurice was a soft-spoken and mild mannered boy in my class. He was friendly and pleasant to all. I cannot think of a single moment where he said or did something that angered or offended anyone while in school. He lived further up the hill from where my school was; practically walking distance from the school. Girls confided in him due to his reserved nature and boys respected his kindness. Once he invited a few of us guys to his house for food and to watch SpiderMan (the very first movie) on his PC, after school. Maurice was the last boy one would think of when the word ‘dangerous’ was mentioned. When we entered Form 5, a boy named Kevin entered the school and stoke fear upon many of us. I say ‘boy’ but he was already an 18yo adult when he came. He had transferred from a really rough school and practically every week he was involved in vicious fights or would be seen breaking class to smoke behind the labs. He would harass random boys, threaten them for their money and if they didn't cough up he'd shove, slap or thrash them, according to his mood. Maurice happened to pass by him one day and judging Maurice to be harmless he tackled Maurice for some money. Maurice ignored him but Kevin grabbed him by the shirt and slapped him on both cheeks, warning him that next time things will be worse. Maurice's shirt was dirty and his face red from the fracas but he remained silent and walked away. After school ended I was walking with my friends out the compound and down the hill when we saw trouble was brewing. We saw a gang of no less than twenty young men from the area had accosted Kevin. Kevin's face was bruised and swollen, eyes red and most of his shirt buttons were ripped out from a prior struggle. They dragged Kevin to Maurice and asked what to do with him. Maurice, in his soft voice told them that that was enough. The men shoved Kevin off and fired kicks behind him as he ran down the hill, thoroughly learning his lesson. The hill where the school lay was Maurice's turf. Kevin learned a lesson that day. The most dangerous people are sometimes the ones you least suspect.

Question: What's the most ruthless thing a new boss has done to show he/she is in charge?
Answer: My very first job was doing construction labor for my stepfather when I was 17. He was a foreman and a downright bastard of a foreman. The guys on the site would refer to him as Pharaoh. When I told him about that nickname he laughed heartily and seemed proud of himself. He worked everyone to the bone. He pretended he had the highest standards when he looked at the work his men did. He boasted that he helped construct mega projects in Brooklyn and Vermont and that the house that we were building must 'shine like his mansion' (even though in reality he lived in a wooden shack with no electricity as my mother had recently kicked him out. The men all respected him though. There wasn't a job that he cussed out a laborer or mason for that he couldn't do himself. For a thin, wiry 5′9 guy he was full of strength and energy. He loved to display this whenever he claimed we were taking too long and would grab someone's shovel and mix mortar or concrete effortlessly as though he was whipping up mashed potatoes. He once gave me the duty of tearing down a large 10ft mound of earth and then transporting the dirt to fill behind a retaining wall. All day I spent labouring and when the sun began to set, barely half of the mound was done. It was too solid for me to break. He dropped some F and C bombs at me, grabbed my pickaxe and with a few solid strikes the mound was no more. I was utterly stunned. However he was utterly provocative, insensitive and and sometimes seemed borderline insane. He would get into these mood swings and yell at us to get off our lazy c**ts and work even if a heavy shower of rain was falling. He wanted to pick a fight with a mason when none of the bricks were laid, not realising that the bricks weren't delivered to the site yet. He would stamp around ceaselessly yelling the F word whenever there was a setback, even if it was no fault of the workers. Sometimes we wondered if he was on drugs. He seemed to have an intense hatred of seeing his workers do nothing and in his tantrums he would flings brooms and buckets our way commanding us to ‘dont sit and gape, clean the f**king place or something.' But all of this were just gimmicks to stoke fear and intimidate everyone. He believed that in his field that was the only way to get the job done. However, the worst thing he ever did to instill fear and show power was when he forced the laborers (mostly young, naive men like myself) to climb planks of wood to get to the foundation floor. He thought it was better than spending money renting some scaffolding. One of the new laborers (a young man who seemed mentally slow) fell off the planks while carrying bricks and received an awful bleeding gash on his elbow, rendering him unable to work hard. Pharoah inspects the wound and gets angry. 'No, no no,' he said solemnly, “Just go. Get out of here.’ The young man pleaded that he could work but my stepfather fired him on the spot, without as much care as to offering a bandaid. Looking at the guy I could see that he came from poverty and probably had little to no education, let alone the fact that he was mentally slow. I thought the rest of the labourers would revolt against him for their friend but Pharoah knew how to please his peons. Beers. Every Friday he treated the boys to drinks on his bill after work at a bar in the closest town. The men would get stone drunk and cheer to their master. They never realised that some of the money he used to buy these drinks was the money he made off cutting costs and overworking them.

Question: What is the biggest culture shock you have ever faced?
Answer: In Aberystwyth, Wales, a group of us Trinidadians went to town for shopping. Trinis are notorious jaywalkers and back home, in most instances, we pay little attention to traffic lights as pedestrians. We were at a traffic light at a rather low-traffic road. One of us observed a store that she wanted to check out. In typical Trini fashion she looked left and right and saw that incoming traffic was several yards away and quickly dashed across the road. She then waited for us to come after her on the other side. An older Welsh man looked at us and said solemnly, ‘You can’t cross until you see the little green man!’ We looked at each other wondering if this was some kind of Welsh humour. I pretended to chuckle at the joke. We then looked left and right and dashed across the road as well. Looking behind us we could see the old man and a group of other pedestrians staring at us in anger and disbelief, murmuring among themselves. I wondered what was up with these people. Why didn’t they cross? The road was clear. What was up with the old guy talking about the ‘little green man?’ It was when I glanced at the traffic light it dawned on me. The ‘WALK’ light had finally come on. Edit: This is not an effort to make fun of UK and/or Welsh culture but rather demonstrate my appreciation for the respect for order and rule-abiding that my friends and I witnessed. However, for all the commenters claiming that the author is lying and then saying 'I'm from the UK and we don't care about/have jaywalking rules’ or 'I visited Aberystwyth and I never saw anyone get upset over jaywalkers’ Please keep your scepticism to yourself. Just because you are from the UK (four distinctly different countries with a combined population of 67 million) doesn't mean you can speak for the population of Aberystwyth. Just because you visited Aberystwyth doesn't mean your experience would be the same as mine. I, myself referred to the act as jaywalking (for simplicity's sake) not the elder Welsh gentleman. Trinidad does not use the term jaywalking either. Below is a photo of where the incident occured and after that is a photo of the Trinis involved in the story.

Question: What did someone do to their home that you just can't understand?
Answer: My stepfather's parents owned a home that was a source of pride for the family. It was a rather large and stately hillside home that possessed several apartments on the bottom floor. The top floor was designed with several balconies that it could be used to host parties and events. The parents themselves had a good reputation with the neighborhood and kept the house in fine shape. They had three sons (one of which was my stepfather of course) all of whom couldn't be any more different than their parents in terms of reputation. When the parents died, they didn't make a will but rather implied to their sons that the oldest would be in charge while the younger ones would have living rights. At the times of their deaths the oldest was homeless and mentally unstable in Brooklyn after a long stint as a crack addict. The middle son (my stepfather), then used this opportunity to take reign, much to the displeasure of the youngest. He commanded the massive top floor to himself and rented the bottom floor apartments. At this time the area had become infused with drugs and crime and the house was starting to show signs of age. Deciding not to renovate it, (even though he's a skilled builder by trade) my stepfather decided to rent it to any old riffraff that comes by. In less than a year the house is infested with drug pushers, addicts, thugs and various people of ill repute whilst my stepfather sat like a Shantytown King overlooking everything from his balcony. The house started to become plagued with issues. Several of the toilets stopped working, many tenants had electrical issues, the front entrance was unusable as a a tree fell onto the front gate and destroyed it but was never removed, the cesspit was in dire need of flushing out so the entire house stank of this deep ghastly scent. The tenants decided to stop paying their rent. My stepfather, always a provocative individual, continuously hurled curses and threats towards his tenants for his rent money until one of them got fed up and assaulted him, threatening to kill him. My stepfather fled the house, never to return. The youngest son took this opportunity to have his daughter, a police woman, gather up her police friends and get rid of all the tenants. He took ownership of the house but by this time the house was so run down that he had no inspiration to do anything but reside on the top floor. He fell victim to lethargy and stopped paying bills and pretty soon the electricity was cut. He abandoned the house and lives with his daughter. The oldest son, deported and homeless, finally took residence in the dilapidated house. To answer the question as to what someone can do to their house that I just can't understand: I can't understand why parents would ever leave behind their house to be shared amongst the children.

Question: What is the most pathetic thing you have witnessed in your life? Share?
Answer: I worked pizza delivery while the State oil refinery PETROTRIN went bust. 5000+ workers were sent home. This may seem sad but bear in mind the State owned refinery was rife with corruption, wastage, poor governance and terrible decision making, accruing a staggering debt that increased each year to the height of 12 Billion TT (1.7 Billion US) before it closed for good. Regardless of its obvious problems the company, the management and its union didn't stop to consider this but went ahead paying exorbitant salaries. The average worker got $45,000 a month. Temporary workers got $21,000 a month. Cleaners got $10,000 a month. When they went on strike they were paid while striking and the company brought in temporary workers who were paid close to the amount of permanent workers. This went on until the strikers decided to stop. A carpenter made $70,000 in overtime in just one month. All of this for a company that didn't see a profit for several years. The last thought that seemed to register on these workers' minds was whether something had to be done to address this wanton wastage. In fact the last unified effort they made before closure was a fight for an increase in wages. I worked two jobs at the time. I worked in a public office by day and did pizza delivery by night. Even with two jobs, with maximum overtime and tips, I wouldn't make a quarter of what the average PETROTRIN worker made each month. But here is the most pathetic encounter ever witnessed by myself and the fine staff at the pizza restaurant I worked: A guy came in with his family on a busy Saturday. In his hand was a thick wad of papers. They were meal vouchers from PETROTRIN. PETROTRIN, in another of its wanton carefree spending measures, allowed for workers to get a voucher for a meal valued approx $40 for each time someone worked overtime. This guy apparently never redeemed his vouchers and came with a year's worth to our restaurant. He knew that in time our restaurant would ban those vouchers as all the other popular food places had done so he decided to cash in all, right then and there, to anyone who was stupid enough to accept these worthless pieces of paper. The combined vouchers had a value of over $2000. The guy wanted to redeem them all. He had a smug look of bitter resolve on his face. His wife looked embarrassed and apologetic towards us while the 10yo son looked confused. The man spoke in raised tones to the cashier when she said she would have to speak to the manager. The manager came and explained that in the history of our restaurant we never had a situation like this. We were all aware that PETROTRIN went bust and there was no chance of the company redeeming us for these vouchers. The man barked at the manager that the vouchers were valid and he was ready to take legal action if we refused them (I rolled my eyes). The wife kept trying to calm the husband down. She seemed exceedingly humiliated by the whole affair but the man persisted. In the end the manager acquiesced. The man ordered something like 8 pizzas, 6 salads and 5 artisan sandwiches. The hubbub caused a queue to form and when they got wind of what was happening, they started angrily protesting for the man to hurry up. However, instead of being thankful that we obliged his worthless vouchers, the guy stubbornly and defiantly decides to pull out his calculator and check his order against his voucher total. He sees that he has $7 remaining. 'How much for one of those donuts?’ he looks at me and asks. 'Six dollars,' I reply stoically. 'And gimme one of those donuts,' he said, 'Any one of them.’ The manager meanwhile was reading the vouchers and then saw something suspicious. She noticed that they were supposed to be signed off by a supervisor. None of them were signed off. Also, they were all consecutively numbered (as in 10,020 straight up to 10,050 with no missing vouchers in between). Also, for supposedly old vouchers they all had that neat, uncreased look. It was obvious that the guy ripped them all out from a voucher booklet and stole them when nobody was looking. However, the manager simply mentioned that the vouchers are irredeemable because they were not signed off. The man throws a tantrum and storms off to his vehicle. Five minutes later he comes back with them all signed. He lies and says that his supervisor was in the area. Practically everyone in the restaurant stares at the man in disgust, even his wife. He folds his arms defiantly. The manager acquiesces again and within thirty minutes he leaves with his massive order. Obviously he and his family would not be able to eat all but wastage is something that he is accustomed to. I look at the guy leaving and feel disgusted. Rather than accept his position with grace he instead choses to become even more bitter, corrupt and deceitful. I felt sorry for the the guy's son who is being taught to milk everything for what it's worth and feel entitled to take advantage of everyone around you, especially when the milk and honey stops flowing

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Which incident offended you badly?
Answer: While attending university I was enrolled in a Human Resource Management course. There was this guy who was also a student but he was doing research for a separate Occupational Safety/Labour Law course or something of that nature. During the break period he would hand us questionnaires for us to kindly respond to for his research. The questions he asked were basic Labour related questions in regards to where we worked, if we understood the meaning of workplace safety, witnessed preventable workplace accidents etc. Of course there were the typical age, gender, ethnicity type questions at the beginning of the questionnaire. When he approached me to answer one he said the usual disclaimer of 'the information will be strictly confidential and used only for research purposes' and yadee yadee ya. However when I finished the questionnaire and handed it to him I was shocked to see him open my questionnaire and begin reading it. I took slight offense to that. Him reading, right in front of me, my personal questionnaire that was supposed to be confidential information used for data collection was very unprofessional. I told myself maybe he's just making sure I didn't leave out a question. He then looked at me and said something that I would never expect a university level student to say 'You really consider yourself mixed race?’ I automatically responded 'Yeah’ and we both stared at each other awkwardly. I tried to figure out what he meant by that. I wasn't African. I wasn't Indian. I wasn't European and I wasnt Other. I was a mixture of all the above. He himself was mixed race. He was of Portuguese-Indian descent with freckles and a pony tail. He saw that I was getting offended so he tried to say something that he believed wouldve defused the situation. Instead what he said after was far more heinous. 'It's just that I'm getting too much respondents ticking ‘Mixed Race.’ I'm trying to show through my research that it's mainly black people who are victims of unfair labour laws and workplace conditions.’ I stared at him. He basically nonchalantly admitted to me his desire to skewer, corrupt and sensationalise his own research along racial lines. The way he casually said it gave me the impression that this was the norm for his department. He gave a brief, nervous laugh and walked away. Thinking to himself that I was the weird one. I learned something unintentionally from my university studies that day.

Question: What was the kindest thing someone did for you when you were young?
Answer: I was a bit of a scatterbrain as a 10 year old. I used to have after-school lessons that would last until 4pm. One evening, after lessons, I checked my wallet and noticed that my traveling money was missing. Being the bright young lad that I was I calculated that since my home was an hour's drive away, I could walk home and it would only take me 2–3 hours at most. I didn't factor in my calculations that my home was an hour's drive away on the highway. I used to watch a lot of adventure cartoons where the hero treks through forests and vast plains for days on end. I told myself that it would be an adventure just like the cartoons. Fast forward three hours later and I'm only a little after the halfway mark. The sun had long set and I'm about to enter the infamous Cleaver Woods (which was, back then, used by murderers to dump bodies). I'm completely exhausted to the point of laying on the ground crying. Suddenly a tall man in his mid to late 20s calls over to me in a voice in which I immediately sense that belonged to a friendly, humourous type person. 'I was liming (hanging out) with my friends in Curepe and I saw you walking. I went to Arouca and I saw you walking. Now I'm home and I see you're still walking...’ I explained the situation and he began to laugh. 'You're mad,' he said, 'Why didn't you take the bus? It's free for school children.’ I felt like a dope. Indeed I had some bus tickets remaining in my wallet and several buses did pass while I was walking. He went to a shop and returned with a snack and a drink for me. While I ate and drank he told me about the dangers of Cleaver Woods and how I could get killed walking through there at night. He then gave me $10 to get a taxi home. He stayed with me until I was put in a taxi and when I was seated and secured he waved goodbye and left. I was so exhausted I don't believe I even told him thank you or asked his name. He didn't seem to care. It looked like what he just did was something normal for him on a day to day basis. At the time the only thing I thought was nice what he did was how he spent money on me. As I grew older I realized that it was much more than that. He looked out for me. Instead of focusing on his own affairs he narrowed his concentration on me and pondered to my ordeal and my safety and made it his duty to help this random boy who had nothing to do with him. At the time my father was absent from my life. This was my first father figure encounter and I could never forget him and what he did.

Question: What's the dumbest thing your boss has gotten mad at you for?
Answer: I worked in a public library that was situated in a high risk location. When I assumed duty the library was rather run down. However, when national elections were near the library got funded by the Government for major renovations. The library was to have a grand reopening, with food, entertainment, a speech and ribbon cutting by the head honcho, the Minister of Communication. Our boss, the head librarian was an older lady. Ms. J was one of those finicky old fashioned women who prided herself on her Victorian etiquette i.e. the kind of person who actually knows about and uses egg spoons and cheese slicers etc. Ms. J wanted to make a grand gesture to the Minister. Her desire to impress him bordered on ludicrous. She wanted us to dress akin to butlers, bellboys, ushers and servants. Even though the library was smaller than a gas station she had us stick arrows all over the ground and wall to show the location of the bathroom, dining quarters etc and prepared these ridiculously overwrought welcoming and closing remark speeches as if by allocating public spending towards our library, the Minister had saved the future of mankind. We were all getting rather irritated with her. We told ourselves she was just a few months shy of retirement but as the days wore on she became overbearingly fussy. We did all the bullwork: moving furniture and getting the entertainment put together. The PR department of the library organized the food and refreshments. Meanwhile, Ms. J stood in the background nagging about the colour of the table cloths and how the utensils weren't of the best quality. Everyone did their best to ignore her. Even the most slow-witted person in the neighborhood could see that this was just another election gimmick. Everyone knew that the Minister would come, pose for photos for the newspaper while cutting the ribbon, chat a bit and quickly make his leave. It was all just PR. This was evident as the renovations were done very slipshod, beyond the deadline and overbudget. By the time the grand opening began, workmen were still on the compound trying to resolve a bad leak in the northern section of the building and the new toilets were not yet installed. However none of this seemed to register to Ms. J. She arrived on the scene dressed like Queen Elizabeth and berated all of those who didn't dress like butlers and maids. The minister arrived an hour after looking rather tired and bored but with a pleasant smile on his face. The ceremony began with a welcome address, a speech from the minister and a live performance. The ribbon was cut, photos were taken and finally food was to be served. My coworkers and I ushered the guests to the tents where the caterers waited amongst dining chairs and tables. We tried to bring the Minister but he was chatting with people from the community. Feeling tired and hungry, we decided to grab something to eat before all the food finished. While we sat eating and chatting, Ms. J stormed towards us and spat, 'You cannot eat until ALL the guests have been served!’ We all looked at one another. We had had enough of her. We continued eating and talking as though she didn't exist. She went to usher the Minister herself and threatened to write bad appraisals for us all. She couldn't find him. To her embarrassment his assistant had left a message that the minister needed to leave and wished to leave us his thanks. Ms. J looked like the biggest idiot in existence. She thought he was going to spend the afternoon chatting with her and praising her for her taste and etiquette. We all shook our heads whenever we passed her. Months later her retirement was near. On her final day we were told that PR wanted have a surprise party for her forty plus years of service. They wanted us each to contribute $100TT ($17US) towards this party and stay back for an additional hour or two on a Friday evening to partake in it. It was all optional of course. They literally begged us. You could guess what our response was.

Question: Who is the best classic rock drummer?
Answer: I tire of reading the same responses. Neil Peart John Bonham Keith Moon I love them all and they all have their own flavour but in terms of consistency of quality I'd go with this kraut. Jaki Liebezeit of CAN Tribal Pulsating Rolling Cerebral Motorik These are some of the adjectives used to describe his primordial style of playing. His style ranges from hypnotic (Oh Yeah) to furiously tribal (Mother Sky) to funky (Vitamin C) to airy and sophisticated (Future Days) and in many instances he incorporates all the above mentioned styles in just one epic song (Bel Air). He is the most idiosyncratic of all the classic rock drummers which isn't surprising coming from the most original band in rock history. A German artrock band with a Japanese lead singer whose freeform nonsensical lyrics are sometimes sung in his own coded language. I love CAN. For the period 1970 — 1975 they released six stunning albums (one each consecutive year) Soundtracks (1970) Tago Mago (1971) Ege Bamyasi (1972) Future Days (1973) Soon Over Babaluma (1974) Landed (1975) To this day I'm yet to see a rock band as consistent as CAN. There's a phrase for that: German precision.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What's the rudest thing someone has said when you were doing them a favor?
Answer: There was a girl named Salsha in a school I once worked. She was quite attractive but had a nasty attitude. When she finished school I heard that she got pregnant. Unfortunately the father broke up with her and she was then forced to raise the child as a teenaged mother with help from her own mom. Now an adult, she came into the school one day all dressed up in office wear as she was job hunting. I was assisting some young students with photocopies. She came to me with the brightest of smiles and asked for a favour. She said she didn't have any money to pay for copies but if I could help her copy her resume a few times. 'How much is a few?’ I said. 'About fifty,’ she replied and smiled even wider. That was asking for too much. We usually did a page or two free for past students in need but fifty was an exorbitant amount. However, I remembered that she was going through a difficult time in her life and told her I'd do it after I see about the kids' copies first. She said ok and folded her arms standing and glaring at the kids, as though doing that would magically speed up the process. Literally less than a minute later she interjected while I was talking to one of them. 'Um,' she said irritably, 'Could you do mine first? I'm really busy right now.’ I took a good look at her. Apparently her attitude still hadn't changed despite her circumstances. There was a sign next to the copier that read 'Students First.’ I pointed to the sign to her and continued photocopying for the kids who were there first. Without a word she stormed out the office. Her attitude was that not only should she get stuff free, she must get far beyond the allowable limit and she must get it at once regardless of who came before her. I really do hope our interaction gave her the large slice of humble pie that she needed.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Have you actually ever heard someone say 'Do you know who I am?' indignantly?
Answer: I was working pizza delivery when I took a call for an order. The person on the other end of the line was a guy called Kerron. He was a local media personality/comedian who went by the name Sunny Bling. He had ordered once before and that time he was quite pleasant and unassuming. Back then, he had referred to himself by his actual name Kerron and had no airs about himself. This time however he was Sunny Bling. He had just gotten his own evening talk show (Sunny @ Sundown) and his ego was now working overtime. 'You know who I am right?’ I said yes. He said that he didn't like how long his pizza took the last time he ordered and if he gets bad service he'd 'light us up’ on his show. I went to the manager and told her about his threat. She made me ignore several other customers who placed their orders before him so he could get a speedy delivery. When I reached his house, he was happy to get his order quickly and acted as though nothing happened. He didn't realize I was the guy who took the phone call as he probably assumed delivery guys didn't answer the phone. 'So are you still gonna “light us up" on your show?’ I said sombrely. He gave an awkward laugh and said no. His show has long been taken off the air. I honestly never met anyone who actually watched it.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What's the most dishonest thing you've experienced in your working life?
Answer: In a school I once worked there was on old curmudgeon who worked as a handyman. For simplicity’s sake I'll refer to him as Levi. Everything about him was dishonest. He was employed as a handyman but could barely repair anything. Any minor problem brought to him, he make it seem as though it were was a huge issue. We had a toilet that gave problems to flush. We told him about it and without flushing and inspecting it, he claimed that the entire toilet was broken and needed to be replaced. He actually managed to get the Principal to sign off on this and any other 'replace’ verdicts he claimed as he knew how to charm women in high positions. He would then 'discard’ of the old toilet or any other item that was replaced. He was a talker and a social butterfly. He would always rant about how hard his life was. He lived to blow smoke up people's asses. Whenever you saw him he always 'just came back from a smoke...' I interpreted this by mentally adding '…up someone's ass’ to his statement. Whenever anyone discussed work with him he would always say his mantra, 'There's no incentive here for me.’ Everyone knew he was corrupt and took advantage of the job and the Principal. Because he was a character with personality and didn't rip-off his fellow workers with his incentives, everyone still liked him. However his desire for more incentives was to get the better of us. The school had a hill of old, beaten up iron and aluminium student chairs. They were stored outside the building in the back. They were an eyesore for the school and especially for the Principal. The Principal wanted to get rid of them but because of auditing purposes she couldn't simply discard them without approval from her district supervisor and a whole bunch of red tape. Levi saw the hill of chairs as a goldmine. He would tell everyone how much it would be worth as scrap iron and made his ultimate incentive to be to get the permission to discard of those chairs. One day he came to me with a proposal. I had a pickup. He told me that the principal gave him permission to discard of the chairs. He wanted me to take them to the scrapyard and we'd split the money 50:50. Knowing that he was a con-artist I went to the Principal and asked if she indeed gave him permission. She confirmed it was true and if I could assist with the transport. I agreed to the proposal. Levi also hired one of the junior handymen for a flat rate. Myself and the junior handyman worked ourselves to the core stacking those chairs to the van and securing. Levi didn't lift a finger as he complained about his old age and his back. It took three trips with my pickup to carry all the chairs to the scrapyard. By the time we were done, the junior handyman and I were dripping in sweat. We waited outside the building to get our cut from Levi. When Levi finally came out he was shouting racial obscenities against the entire Chinese population. We asked him what happened. He said that the owner, a native of China, could barely speak English and inspected the entire haul with the conclusion of 'Iron no good. We want aluminium.’ Levi said that the Chinese owner didn't want the iron chairs, practically 95% of the the haul, but only the aluminium ones which had a higher market value. He said the owner wanted us to carry the iron ones back. Levi said he begged the man to take the iron chairs for whatever price he was willing to offer. We asked Levi how much money he got for the entire haul. Levi showed us $75TT from his wallet. We were stunned. I for one didn't believe Levi's story in the least. I went inside to talk to the owner. Unfortunately it was true that he barely spoke English. We couldn't understand each other and he simply said to me, 'Iron no good. Next time bring aluminium.’ Levi acted the most heartbroken of all. All that work for nothing. We split the money in three. The junior handyman lamented that he never worked so hard in his life for enough money to buy a pack of cigarettes. A few weeks later Levi stopped coming to work. When the school rang him he announced that he was taking early retirement. The principal called me into her office all of a sudden. 'Where are the chairs?’ she cried, 'The supervisor is coming tomorrow.’ I told her I didn't understand what she meant. She explained to me that she gave Levi permission to salvage whatever chairs he could from the pile, have them repaired and painted and in exchange he could 'discard’ the rest. I told her the arrangement Levi had with us and how we carried all the chairs to the scrapyard. She stared at me with fury. She asked me if I knew where Levi lived. I said no. She said her calls to him went straight to voice message. She cried that Levi was supposed to bring 23 refurbished chairs for her since last week. She even had the figure listed in the school inventory. I didn't know what to tell her. I said I would try to find out any information I could. I called the scrapyard to find out if they had any information on him: a second phone number, an address etc. Thankfully the Chinese owner had a English speaking person employed as a CSR. I asked the CSR about Levi and whether she has any information on him. She looked up our sale in the computer. She said Levi made the transaction under the school's name and phone number but left no personal information on himself other than his first name. I then found out that the sale of the chairs as scrap amounted to almost $3000TT. Levi had ripped everyone off, myself, the junior handyman, the Principal and the school. Big time. Looks like he had finally gotten his incentive.
