Question: What one thing did your father do that left your mother sobbing?
Answer: Wasn't my biological father but my stepfather. Calling him 'stepfather’ is a bit of a compliment. He basically lived off my mom, was unemployed more often than not and barely provided anything for the rent free roof that lay above his head. Yet my mother persevered. She got involved with my biological father at a tender age and that relationship was traumatic due to his bipolar disorder. She was intent on having a proper family with my stepfather, especially after she bore him two daughters. As mentioned before he was more often unemployed and when when he did find a job it was temporary as he worked in construction. However, in the early 2000s he found some measure of success in the field and started getting established as a professional foreman. He got high paying, big contract jobs and had the power to hire and fire. Soon most of the guys in the street were given jobs by my stepfather and some of the neighborhood women sent love letters in the mailbox to my mother's ire. My stepfather would laugh it off. However as the months turned into years my mother calculated that with the amount of money my stepfather made, it wasn't reflected in the household. We were still broke, had almost no furniture, bills still piled up and the money he gave her was not any significant improvement to when he was roughing it. Things got worse when my stepfather would constantly disappear for the fortnight weekend, especially when he got his salary. When he gave my mother what scanty money remained in his wallet it led to ugly arguments. Everyone told my mother that my stepfather had to be seeing another woman. My mother refused to believe it. Instead she tried to nag, quarrel and harrass him into doing what was right and it just created more nasty arguments. She then resolved that he could no longer live with us but could see his daughters on the weekend. She believed this would change his ways. He readily agreed to this. One fateful Friday evening I was home and the phone rang. I answered it. I heard my stepfather's voice asking for 'Tracey.’ Tracey was the name of our neighbor's daughter. She was 24 years old and had a reputation. I said Tracey didn't live here. When my stepfather recognized my voice he immediately hung up the phone. My mother came and asked me who called. 'It's just S****n.’ 'What does he want?’ my mother said irritably. 'I dunno,' I replied, 'He just asked to talk to Tracey….I think he dialled the wrong number.’ At 16 years old I was a bit naive to comprehend what all this meant. However I'd never forget seeing my mother's face drop like she saw death materialize in front of her and later tears formed in her eyes. My stepfather was getting involved with our neighbor's daughter right across the street. That's where his money went. That meant everyone knew about it except her. That meant she was a fool. They parted ways permanently afterwards. My stepfather would demand that I say that I was mistaken. That it wasn't him who called. He's 68 now and his daughters want nothing to do with him. It really affected my mother as she became more withdrawn and a bit of a recluse and a hoarder. They both are barely on speaking terms. Sometimes I feel as though I should've had more common sense and just kept my mouth shut.

Question: What guitarists do you think have the most emotionally moving solos?
Answer: I love this question because it's entirely subjective and for someone who has zero technical guitar knowledge and even less skills, I can answer it. It's rare that I sense a feeling of emotion in a guitar solo. Most solos to me just sound like cool improvisations that take you away from the rigidity of the melody and repetition of verse-chorus, verse-chorus. There are only a handful of songs that I've actually felt the emotion behind the playing. It's like the guitarist is talking to you with his guitar and you sense the emotions behind the words. Such are the best examples I can think of: Carlos Santana — Samba Pa Ti. This is possible the best example I can think of in regards to emotional solos. The entire song is basically an extended guitar solo. Wrought with the feelings of longing, regret and desire this song is one of the artist's most impressive contribution. I can hear a man at his wit's end wailing to lost love from the very first few notes. Buck Dharma — Don't Fear The Reaper Nothing is more terrifying than the ominous solo in this pre-heavy metal classic. I get visions of demonic creatures rising from beneath when this manic, blistering guitar starts going off after a creepy rhythm guitar intro. Buck Dharma wrote the song after envisioning death for himself and it shows in his playing. Jimi Hendrix — Little Wing Funny how this original composition grew from obscurity to one of his most covered songs. 'Fly on, Little Wing' Hendrix indeed takes us to soaring heights with this solo full of wonder, hope and optimism. I consider the solo an extension of the themes explored in another Hendrix classic The Wind Cries Mary. Play both solos one after the the other and you'll see what I mean. John Frusciante — Scar Tissue In the land of weeping guitars Scar Tissue reigns King. The greatest achievement of the Red Hot Chili Peppers in regards to their sombre, non funky output. Frusciante's guitar sounds like a broken down and dying animal. Figures that it is shown to be literally broken in the music video. Jonny Greenwood — Paranoid Android + There There Couldn't choose between the two Radiohead classics but they both explore the emotions of fear, paranoia and anxiety. Paranoid Android's solo is fractured yet blistering. It is cold and unconventional yet wrought with feelings, like an android having a physical and emotional breakdown. There There’s rhythm and solo combined instills a deeply fearful feeling of slowly incurring the wrath of some powerful unseen entity. And lastly Duane Allman — Melissa The slide guitar to end all slide guitar. A grandeur solo like no other is encapsulates themes of freedom, love and innocence. Duane's guitar makes its presence from the very beginning and soars to the heavens in its solo. Given the fact that Duane Allman died not long after creating this marvellous piece of work does one sense an almost spiritual connection with Duane's playing on this a masterpiece.

Question: Which movie character do you feel sorry for?
Answer: Miles Dyson: Terminator 2 Judgement Day If there is one casualty from a movie that literally brought tears to my eyes it had to be him. Just imagine that you're a mild mannered microprocessor expert employed for a big-tech company. You are passionate about your job and firmly believe that what you are doing will change the world for the better. While working at home with your wife and preteen son, a woman who just had a violent escape from a mental asylum carelessly empties several clips from a high powered machine gun into your house destroying your workstation and narrowly killing you and potentially causing fatal harm to your family. Then imagine being shot in the arm by the crazed gunwoman and looking on helplessly as she points a gun to you and your family while shouting obscenities and claiming 'It's all your fault.’ She doesn't kill you but she shows you a man wanted for a shootout in a mall who possesses a robotic arm. She tells you that you are the cause of the end of the world. She relates to you a fantastic story of time travel, having sex and producing a child with a man from the future. That her son eventually will become the saviour of the human race and a leader in an epic battle between humans and robots. You are forced to believe her because she has many guns, an emotionally overwhelmed mind and the assistance of a bodybuider with a robotic arm. She then forces you to break into the worklab and destroy all traces of your work and its related developments. In the process you are shot several times by inept police and your body is exploded into several pieces due to holding the detonator the bodybuilder makes you, a 100 pound pencil-necked geek, hold (even though he claims to be a near indestructable cyborg). Sarcasm aside, Dyson's death was sad because he was truly a nice guy with a conscience and a trusting and faithful nature. Kudos to the actor Joe Morton who provides a heartfelt performance full of pathos and leaves an impression on many of the fans of the movie. A pity his career didn't take off after this role. However, it was not Dyson's fault. Sarah's obsession with killing him as the cure for Judgement Day is one of the reasons I have ambiguous feelings towards her as a hero. It was very ignorant and immature of her to foster such primitive cause and effect type logic. It's very much like believing that by killing the guy who created gunpowder you can stop World War I and II from happening. It's also very cowardly of her to bully and assault the harmless and defenceless guy rather than take up her beef with the powerful Cyberdyne corporation, the real villains. No. Assault nerdy Dyson and his family, wrack his mind full of guilt and have him needlessly killed thanks to your crackpot plan. Poor Dyson.

Question: Have you ever had a co-worker who you worked closely with get fired for something truly shocking that you never saw coming?
Answer: He was fired. It was shocking. But I personally saw it coming a mile away. So I'm cheating a bit. Sean was a fellow delivery driver at a pizza restaurant. He was the epitome of the go-getting, happy-go-lucky type of guy who always saw the best in everyone around him. In our restaurant (and most fast food restaurants in the country) the staff is overwhelmingly women. As a male employed in a fast-paced female environment, us male delivery drivers knew that you had to be firm and assertive with the female coworkers otherwise they'd take advantage of you. Sean didn't seem to get the cue. He would mop the floors, refill ice bins, sweep, go out and pickup lunch, lift heavy boxes of meat etc for any female who had the ability to remember his name. He loved to make people happy. Us drivers would warn him to stick with his job specs otherwise he'd be doing favours all day and not get any deliveries done. He paid us no heed. One fateful day, the Assistant Manager held a meeting. She noticed for the past few weeks the meat stocks were going missing. Every week she did a quick audit of the remaining stocks and usually the figure would be off by a package or two. However her audit revealed entire cases of meat were vanishing with no possible explanation other than in-house theft. After viewing the security cameras for a lengthy period she finally discovered the culprit. Sean was fired promptly. Everyone was shocked. Nobody expected Sean, with his heart of gold, to be a petty meat thief. Sean passionately declared his innocence. However the camera footage revealed that he kept entering the chiller where meat and other food ingredients were kept. Delivery drivers had no reason to go in the chiller unless it was busy and they were asked to help bring out stock. The footage also revealed Sean exiting the chiller several times with a mysterious bag just before his shift ended. Sean passionately declared his innocence but management would hear nothing of it. He was fired and blacklisted from ever working at any of the branches again. However meat still continued to go missing at an alarming rate. The assistant manager was at her wits end trying to solve the mystery. The head office warned that any further loss of meat stocks would be deducted from everyone's salary. These were the magic words that made everyone on the alert for the thief. In a few days a breakthrough came when one of the workers confided to the manager that one of the newer workers (I'll refer to her as Janet) kept bringing lunch and putting it in the chiller. However Janet would never be seen eating the lunch that she brought. Instead she would always return the bag home. This was indeed suspicious. Upon inspecting Janet's lunch bag they found a pack of ham. Janet was the culprit all along. She admitted to her crime and with the threat of criminal proceedings, management got her to confess that Sean was innocent. She admitted that Sean had a crush on her and would give her a ride home when both of their shifts ended the same time. Before they left she would ask that he retrieve her 'lunch’ from the chiller for her. Sean never suspected a thing and innocently and unwittingly assisted in her theft. Feeling guilty the assistant manager called Sean to ask if he wanted his job back. Sean declined the offer. He had gotten a much more lucrative position working for a cable company as a technician. Had he still been working at the restaurant he wouldn't have known that they were hiring. Some things happen for the best. I was very happy for Sean. Unfortunately for us we were no longer allowed to keep our lunches in the chiller from the that moment on.

Question: Why is Eric Clapton such a highly rated guitarist when he's very average?
Answer: Average you say? Clapton is in my personal top five of greatest guitarists. I'd even rank him higher than Hendrix and just a smidgen below Duane Allman. I dont know anything technical about guitars, I can't play and I definitely can't determine prowess. However I've listened to hundreds of guitar oriented albums and only a handful of guitarists stick out in terms of consistency of quality. Clapton is definitely one of them. For someone to listen to Disraeli Gears and call the stunning solos on that album average would be the rantings of a madman or the simply just a common troll. From his work with The Yardbirds, John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, Cream, Blind Faith, Derek and the Dominos and his solo work (my least favourite, but heck he wrote Tears in Heaven) he has proven to be more than just average. I think the best performance depicting Clapton's talent is his guitar duel with The Band's Robbie Robertson for the The Last Waltz concert. Here one can see two immensely talented guitarists politely trying to upstage one another in a mastery of improvisation. The fans who wrote 'Clapton Is God’ on a London wall were not paid to do so. They did it because something about his guitar work touched them deeply inside that they felt him to be on a higher realm than ordinary people. Definitely doesn't fit the description of someone with average talent.

Question: What was incredibly expensive twenty years ago, and is completely worthless today?
Answer: Several years ago my brother brought one of these babies home. A friend of his had taken several days off work and needed money to pay for a doctors visit for a sick leave. So the friend asked my brother to try and sell it to me seeing that I had a fascination with film. This entire set up with a bunch of unused VHS tapes would be all mine for the cost of $100 TT ( roughly $15 US). My brother tried hard to pitch the sale to me. Question: What is the worst excuse you've heard someone give for not having money?
Answer: Many moons ago I encountered a guy named Moses. Moses was short, squat and effeminate. He declared himself a staunch Catholic and whenever conversation among his male co workers included discussing even the most minor of obscenities, Moses would take offense and leave. He also was also the most despised among all of us guys working at the warehouse. Not because of his above mentioned traits but because of his notoriety of being a cheapskate. 'Hey Moses we're collecting $20 from everyone to buy Erica a gift for her birthday this Friday.’ Moses: 'Sorry but I already bought tickets for a cruise my church is having on Saturday.’ 'Hey Moses Petra is trying to raise funds for her mother's operation by selling BBQ tickets. It's $50 a ticket.’ Moses: 'Tell Petra I'm sorry but I already ate BBQ twice this month but I'll tell everyone at church to pray for her mother.’ These were the typical type of responses you'd get from Moses whenever money was involved. However the worst excuse he ever gave happened when a bunch of us went to a bar to hang out. We had just gotten paid. It was a gruelling month where we worked overtime every day and on the weekends. We all had some extra money and wanted to unwind with some beers, food and pool. We would all take turns and buy rounds of beers and after some time someone would offer to buy food. Everything was going fine and dandy. Practically the whole warehouse staff was there with the exception of older workers, those with family commitments etc and Moses. However, somewhere between the 3rd and 5th round Moses suddenly appeared in the bar and took a seat among us. By then we were all quite intoxicated and in great spirits. We cheered his arrival and patted him on the back. 'What do you want to drink Moses?’ Moses: 'I'm not a big drinker so a Carib Pilsner (Lite) beer is good for me.’ We all cheered Moses for not being such a tightwad and hanging out with us. A few rounds passed and food was bought and shared among us. Moses made himself at home with food, drink and hospitality. While eating we began to sober up and we became less vocal. Moses decided to use this opportunity to discuss his views on the Bible, his contributions to his church and the events it had in store for the weekend. This sobered us up even more. We then realized that the bastard never bought a single round for us. All he did was eat, drink, brag and preach to our credit. One of us diplomatically asked him when it is he was going to contribute to us by paying for a round of drinks. It was then that Moses uttered the most disgusting excuse for not spending money that I have ever heard: Moses: 'I try not to encourage anyone into a life of vice (alcoholism).’ There was a silence and chuckles from the few who thought Moses was making a joke.’ He had to be making a joke. He just sat and happily drank three beers with us. This fact was mentioned to him and he had an immediate response: Moses: 'I never asked for the beers. I came here to save souls.’ The little bugger wasn't joking. He said that he came with the intention to invite us to a shindig his church was having and only accepted the beers and food from us as a nice gesture. He honestly believed the bullshit that was coming out of his mouth. Before anyone could say anything else, Moses rose majestically from the centre of table like it was the Last Supper. He stoically announced that he had to leave and he hoped that we understood his message clear. He then walked unsteadily towards the exit; possibly a bit intoxicated but undoubtedly cheap, conceited and hypocritical. Needless to say the irritation we had for Moses developed into an intense dislike. He didn't last long in the warehouse though. Some time later he had missed several days of work. When he returned he had the excuse that he developed a hernia and had an operation. This was said with no medical records to his claim. Had he not been such a conniving, cheap bastard, our supervisor would've fought for him to keep his job. But in the end everyone was happy to see him go. Last I saw him, he worked as a merchandiser for an instant coffee distributor. I asked about his hernia. Moses: 'What hernia?’ Edit: Moses was a cheap bastard. There was a time when I tried to be the cheap in the bar with my friends and it led to painful results. Literally. Read it here.

Question: What is a slap-in-the-face job offer?
Answer: More like a splat in the face… I used to cut grass as a sideline. I would drive around in my pickup and stop by houses with unkempt and overgrown yards and call out to whomever was inside to offer my services. Here's the thing any lawn maintenance man would tell you: women are much more likely to hire you than men. Men have this awful macho ego where it is we believe 'why pay a guy when I can do it myself.’ Anytime I called at a house and an able bodied man answers, I know that there's a 90% he's gonna refuse my service because he’s 'gonna do it when he gets the time.’ You can imagine my surprise when, while I was cutting grass at a lady's house, the man who lived across from her came over to hire me. He said that I could start right after I was finished with the lady's yard. I walked over with him to see his lawn and to haggle a price with him. Strangely enough it was a small patch of yard that measured 10*20ft at most. Most men would proudly assert 'I can do it myself' for such a small patch. The grass was fairly high, I set a price of $200 TT ($28 USD) to cut, rake and bag up the grass for him. I was even more surprised that he readily accepted the price without haggle. It was getting stranger by the minute but say what, a job like that would take me 45 minutes at max. Easy money. When I finished the lady's yard I went over to work on his lawn. I started at the back and observed two kennels with four large pitbull dogs staring at me. As I yanked my cord and started, within ten minutes I had to stop. There was a small pile of dog poop hidden in the grass. My string had flicked it and it spattered crap at the front of my boot. 'Ok,' I told myself, 'I'll just cut around it.’ Five minutes later: SPLAT Another pile of dog shit. This one was fresh, wet and pasty. Some of it splattered on my shirt. 'Ok,' ’l told myself, 'This guy did me a bit of a dirty here. If he knew there was dog poop he could've warned me and I would charged him for the inconvenience.’ I told myself I would request an additional $50 for cleaning the two piles of poop for him. Ten minutes later: SPLAT. Another larger pile of shit. It was as though two dogs shat in the same area. This time the situation was critical. Flecks of dog shit had hit my face and neck and was all over my clothes. The poop itself was so disgusting that horseflies were setting up camp on it. I took a good look around. The entire patch was covered in dog shit. It seemed as though the guy didn't clean the yard for months. He didn't hire me to cut grass. He hired me to get rid of his shit and then cut the grass because it was impossible for anyone to cut the grass like that. I washed my face and neck and I knocked on his door calmly. 'I'm sorry I can't cut this yard. There's too much dog mess around. I even got some of it on my face.’ 'I'll give you an extra hundred,' he replied weasily. I wanted very badly to punch him. I said sorry and left without a word. No apology from him whatsoever. Looking back I saw a lot of the dog poop I hit had splattered all over his car. Served him right. But knowing the kind of character he was he would probably take it to a small car wash and not explain to the people there that the muddy stains were actually dog poop. The bastard.

Question: Whom did you feel bad for in high school?
Answer: Balram. There was a boy who came from the depths of poverty named Balram. He was sinewy and had coarse skin and features that made him look like he jumped out of the pages of our history books as an indentured laborer from colonial times. Everything about him was out of sync with the rest of the class. This was the late 90s and baggy pants were the thing, Balram wore his khaki trousers wrapped tight around his skinny legs. Perms from excessive hair gel (my specialty at the time), corn-rows, Caesar styled and spiky hair was the rage amongst teenage boys back then. Balram wore something that looked straight out of a an old Amitabh Bachchan movie from the 70s. Balram's school uniforms always looked faded and threadbare. Never once did anyone see him wearing new items of clothing. This led to many of the kids in class poking fun at the possibility that Balram's family got used clothes for him. Balram didn't have cable. It was possible he didn't have a TV. Balram didn't care for the music everyone else listened to. He didn't go to the arcade and play video games. He didn't get excited hearing about Stone Cold Steve Austin. He was odd in that he only enjoyed games that demonstrated his eerie strength and his skills in survival. This included holding breath competitions, arm wrestling, 'mercy’ and 'bokee' (hitting an opponents fist by flicking a finger against it until someone gives up in pain). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He would sit in class like an old Native American chief, peering knowingly at the world through his squinted, Charles Bronson-esque eyes while everyone else made jokes and acted like morons who needed attention. My friends and I would hang out with him but for some reason he never was an official member of our group. He preferred to roam alone. Once, I was tricked by some boys into pretending to want to beat him up, all for kicks. Before I could say 'Hey' Balram lifted me into the air by the shoulders and against the wall until I yielded. It was an impressive display of brute strength that I could never forget. In moments of boredom Balram was usually an easy target for jokes and insults. Some of the girls were particularly mean to him. One would say to that she would never be with a boy like him who looks dirty and always smells like old curry. The boys would always joke around that he came from 'the bush’ and came to school swinging on vines like Tarzan. One of the boys even managed to create a comic depicting Balram's life in the bush, fighting snakes and tigers on a daily basis etc. Balram learned to laugh with everyone and not let it get to him. In Form 3 Balram vanished. Always a recluse he never communicated to anyone what were his plans/intentions. Some months later he visited the school wearing a new uniform and with a friend at his side. He got transferred to a school closer to home where more rural kids like him were around. He looked much happier and was far more social than he was before. That day, most of the class ignored him but my friends and I held a reception to commemorate the good times we had with him. He said his new school was the best; teachers were hardly there and the kids did what they wanted. He showed me a tattoo that he got on his arm of a dragon. Even though the tattoo looked ridiculously amateurish and his clothes were still faded and threadbare and his hair still outdated my friends and I sang his praises and gave him his day. He really was a great guy. He had no fear of trying to fit in and had an infinite amount of patience for those around him. I wouldn't be surprised to find out that he made a huge success out if his life as an adult. But alas that day was the last time I saw him/heard anything about him.

Question: What does a $1,500,000 house look like where you live?
Answer: Like the house the average lower-middle class bloke lives in. In Trinidad house prices are notoriously inflated. Real estate agents will tell you it's all about supply and demand but in reality it is because there are no checks and balances to the real estate sector. The above image is of a house built and sold by a private developer. Nothing looks outstanding about it. Heck, the owner didn't even bother to take a good photo of the house when the grass develops nicely and in nice weather to show off its mustard paint job. This house looks like how most Government commissioned, detached, single family housing units look like. A 5000 sq ft, 2–3 bedroom cookie cutter nestled amongst a swarm of others like it as far as the eyes can see. It's not unlikely that the guys who built the privately sold house are the same ones awarded the contracts to build the Government properties. Conflict of interest? Maybe. Will the private developer extend a lot of effort to his private development which is monitored by public opinion, customer satisfaction and subject to legal recourse? Yes. Will the private developer extend the same effort to a big fat Government contract whereby he's unsupervised in the making of hundreds of matchbox style cookie cutters, can bribe public officials to cut corners and is shrouded from public opinion as all fault is levied towards 'the corrupt government?’ Not so much. In essence, $1.5 mil in TT dollars can get you a generic matchbox style house with a tiny piece of yard to plant some flowers/herbs. You can apply through the Government if you have chronic problems in regards to finances and all it takes is just bending over backwards to show political allegiance and screaming to the heavens how hard your life in a gross public display. You can do that or be put on a waiting list and expect to be responded to in at least 25–30 years. When you do get your $1.5 mil Government house don't be so quick to celebrate. Crime, shoddy infrastructure and utilities and poor environmental planning are rampant in Government housing projects. So maybe a privately developed $1.5 mil house is the better option? With the private housing developments, there has been a growth in unapproved or downright illegal developments by unscrupulous developers. The house in the very first photo could seem like a pretty decent option but bear in mind these three possibilities. So in conclusion, in Trinidad $1.5 million can allow you to pick your own poison when it comes to housing.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Have you ever lost any respect for someone instantly?
Answer: I once had a supervisor who I had absolutely no respect for. No matter how much my more coolheaded coworkers advised me to just let him ramble on and just nod my head in silence I couldn't help but say what was on my mind to him. You see, his approach to the supervisory role was sleazy at best. He basically implied to us all that he was our boss. According to him: 'There's my work and there's your work.’ ‘His work' entailed: Funny enough when I heard that he would be appointed my supervisor I was happy to hear the news. Only a few years ago I hung out with him as he was a friend of my brother. We knocked back a few beers and discussed the organisation and the amount of favoritism, bloated and unnecessary hierarchy and the gross amount of people who get paid for doing practically nothing. He mentioned then that if he ever rose in the ranks he'd change that. Six years later he's comfortably become exactly what he preached against. I got into so many vicious arguments with him that it led to physical threats on both sides that in the end I was transferred to another branch. Unfortunately for him he suffered from severe psoriasis which worsened as time progresses. I remember seeing him at the head office, a year after our meltdown and my transfer and he looked at me as though wanting to say something. I couldn't bring myself to talk to him. A month later I heard he was in the intensive care unit at the hospital in regards to a heart condition. A week later I heard that he died. I felt awful that I didn't reach out to him that moment. Made me wonder if I was aware that there was a strong chance I would be dead soon, would I act in the careless manner in which he did at work. I forgive him of course but I can't deny the fact, at the time, he had lost every ounce of respect I had for him.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What is the cruelest way to find out someone doesn’t like you?
Answer: SHOWING OFF As a teenager I was sometimes a bit of a dirtbag. One day after school I was hanging out with the boys and we were trading girl conquest stories, most of them fake of course. I bragged to them that there was this pretty girl named Nicole who was obsessed with me. I showed them a picture of her and they fawned over it. I then laughed and told them that I had higher standards and they could have her if they wanted. To add more relish to the dirtbag weiner that I was I pulled out my flip phone for a prank. I called her and put the call on speaker. They listened as she kept saying 'Hello, hello?’ I then replied, 'I can't hear you…….bad signal……..go somewhere different.’ I could hear her moving about.I had to hold my laughter in. Nicole: 'Elijah? Are you hearing me now?’ Me: 'Kinda. You need to talk louder.’ Nicole: 'YOU HEARING ME?’ Me: 'Ahh…..You're shouting in my ears. A little softer.’ Nicole: 'I'm sorry. Is everything ok?’ I hung up the phone. Most of the boys were impressed and found it funny but one boy stared at me angrily but didn't say a word. My phone then started ringing. Nicole was calling me back. 'You see,' I said to the boys while showing them she was calling back, 'She's obsessed.’ I pressed END CALL. Why was I such a dirtbag? The girl whom I was infatuated with didn’t show the same kind of sentiments for me, no matter how hard I tried. Maybe I used Nicole as a vessel to unleash the anger and hurt that I had pent up over my unrequited puppy love? Maybe I was just an insensitive bastard? Regardless Karma came like a you-know-what more than a decade later when I saw Nicole enter my workplace looking ravishing. I engaged her in conversation and she seemed friendly enough. We both were single at the moment. I told myself that the incident was so long ago, so most likely she forgave me and got over it. I ventured to ask her out for lunch. Without sparing a second’s thought she replied, ‘Sorry, I’m busy.’ I ventured to ask for her number. She pretended she didn’t hear me and started wrapping up the conversation. She then politely took her leave. I felt like a massive fool. Serves me right I guess.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What harsh truth did you learn as a teenager?
Answer: There was a boy named Sid in my class in Secondary (High) school. He was an odd boy and a bit of a loner. He was the guy who'd always 'kill the joke’ in class i.e. when everyone in class starts making funny comments about someone or something, he was the one that would make an awkward, completely unrelated comment that killed and buried the laughter. He was one of the few boys to have a full moustache at the age of 12 and the one day he shaved it off he looked like he came from another planet and was the laughing stock of the week. I used to feel sorry for him but sometimes he'd say the darndest things that were so bizarre and unfunny that I couldn't help but shake my head and sigh. Even some of the teachers would groan at some of the unfunny attention seeking statements that Sid would make. Biology teacher: So that's why female dogs produce multiple babies whereas female humans usually produce one. Sid: So why didn't God give female dogs multiple vaginas to make it easy on them. These kind of statements, along with a collective sigh from the class would be the routine for years to come. This was until suddenly I witnessed Sid make an unfunny joke and all of a sudden most of the kids in class started laughing. Then I noticed the teachers started behaving favorably towards him; feigning laughter at his silliness and giving him special attention and help in class Then I noticed two of the most desired girls in school were fighting over him, both of them vociferously declaring to be his true girlfriend. Nobody made fun of him and even the worst bullies and class clowns made sure not to mess with him. I wondered if the world had gone mad. I discussed it with my friends and they explained it to me. 'Didn't you hear? Sid's rich.’ As it turned out Sid's father was a prominent lawyer in the country. Nobody realized this until he visited the school for a parent's day. Having connections to a rich and powerful lawyer was something our dilapidated and poorly funded school coveted and as such Sid was now treated like royalty. For his 16th birthday he was given a new car and he proudly drove it into the compound with his two girlfriends inside; the only boy in the school's history to have that luxury. However he was still as corny and awkward as ever but no one seemed to pay that any mind. So the harsh truth I learned as a teenager was: Money and power can make any donkey look like a stallion. Not Sid. Definitely not as rich. But a striking resemblance.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What is one thing that all men hate?
Answer: Yesterday I was at home. I couldn't attend work because my area had been flooded for the third time in a month. It was both nerve-wracking and boring being stuck in a house surrounded by water and fearful that the rain falls and the water gets higher and enters inside. I get a missed call. It's from a lady at work who is notorious for always wanting something. Practically every encounter I've had with her usually ends up with her saying 'I wanted to ask you about…… ’ Or 'Would it be alright if I…..’ Or 'Next Monday I wanted to……' In other words she wanted a favour from me. This is all fine and dandy but truly I only like to perform favours to people I consider friends. By no stretch of the imagination do I consider her a friend and the sheer volume of favours she's asked me over the years is exponentially greater than the favours every friend of mine has ever asked me combined. I decided to not take the call. Moments later I see that she sends a voice message. I call my girlfriend and discuss whether I should ignore it and she tells me. 'What if the lady just wants to know if you're alright?’ I then feel guilty. Maybe I am being a bit cynical. I decide to listen to the voice message. I play it; 'Hi. Didn't see you in work today. Hope everything is ok….’ In my mind I said my girlfriend was right and I shouldn't be so presumptuous. However, I then hear a sentence that makes me recoil. 'Since you're not here I was wondering if I could use your office to….’ I stopped listening. I didn't reply. I think every single man would agree that we hate when people only seek after us to get favours done.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: Have you ever witnessed an office prank that cost someone their job?
Answer: I may be cheating a bit but I can't help to answer such a burning question. I performed a prank that could've cost me my job. In my late teens I worked in a warehouse doing manual labor which mostly included picking up boxes of products, placing them on a trolley and bringing them to the front to be delivered. It could sometimes be rather monotonous especially when the huge orders came in and you spent all day rolling about the massive double warehouse in your creaky trolley that always had one bad wheel. Jason (or J as he preferred to be called) was our supervisor. He was a muscular guy with a deadpan face and shiny bald head. He was the butt of many of our jokes because he spoke in this forced, psudo-sexy whisper and constantly licked his lips while giving his daily inspirational morning speeches (we would call him LL Cool J in secret). He didn't have much of a sense of humour. He barely ever smiled and no one saw him laugh, although one of my friends claimed to have seen him laughing at an episode of Rugrats while behind his office computer. Anyways. As I mentioned the job could be monotonous. One evening I saw that one of the older female workers, Erica, had written on the bulletin board. 'I love my fellow workers.’ This irritated me because it was not a bulletin and it had an air of Soviet Communism about it. I wanted to change it to 'I love my fellow COMRADES' and draw a hammer and sickle but I knew that most of my coworkers wouldn't get the joke and it would be ignored. In the end I decided to change it to 'I love my fellow SLAVES.’ That would catch their attention and provide a good laugh and then it would be erased and teach Erica to stop using the bulletin board to write her insipid, brown-nosed statements. Unbeknownst to me J, who was of African descent, was in the process of watching all the episodes of Roots on DVD. He was emotionally charged about African history and slavery in particular. It didn't even occur to me that he was wearing a lot of African themed clothing also. The next morning I arrived just in time for the morning prayer and J's speech. The atmosphere was like a funeral as I entered the warehouse and saw everyone staring at me. J, in a low growl, asked me if I was the one who wrote the slave comment on the board. I replied yes. J licked his lips and made a long, impassioned plea about slavery and black pride. Every time I tried to explain to him that I didn't mean it in a context of race he would say, 'Shut up Jumbo (my nickname).’ He then ended by saying in his low psudo-sexy LL Cool J voice, 'Don't you ever………..ever, ever………let me see you write anything racist on this board again.’ Had I not been of African descent myself I'm certain I would've been put on extended probation, let go or at least spoken to by HR. My friends enjoyed the whole ordeal and it made good scuttlebutt for a few days. I never touched the bulletin board again but being the best impersonator of J, I was sought after by my friends and coworkers to re-enact J's racism speech. I would do a perfect impersonation with exaggerated licking lips and have them howling with laughter. Unfortunately I was called into Js office some time later. I was in trouble. Someone snitched to J that I was mocking how he spoke. I was certain now I would get the boot. Instead I saw J with a big smile on his face watching on his phone a video of me impersonating him. 'Jumbo,' he said and then licked his lips, 'Let me see you talk like me.’ I looked at him and repeated what he just said, licked lips and all. To my surprise he simply smiled and gave a soft 'he he he’ laugh and told me to go back to work and stop fooling around. He did have a sense of humour after all. Myself with some friends at the warehouse. J wasn't present unfortunately.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What is the shortest amount of time that you spent at a job? How old were you? Why did you quit?
Answer: 8 hours. I worked for one of the most prestigious cinema multiplexes in Trinidad and Tobago. I had quit my job at the warehouse in an attempt to enter the world of selling life insurance. That didn't work out and pretty soon I desperately needed a job as I was flat broke. I applied to work as a cashier in the multiplex cinema. I always loved their aesthetics and felt as though they really cared about what they did and the people they hired. That couldn't be further from the truth. I was young, a few months shy of 23, but still most of my coworkers were several years younger than me, typically the teenager fresh out of high school looking for their first job. Practically all my co-workers were males and our supervisor was an attractive girl in her mid 20s who had a talent for making us guys feel as though we were scoring points with her and that it was only a matter of time before she would agree to a date. In retrospect I believe this was a tactic she used to keep us from leaving prematurely. With me she directly assisted in dressing me in my uniform and when my trousers was missing a zip, she made flirtatious comments while helping me apply double sided tape on my crotch. I sincerely thought we were going to hit it off until I saw that she responded positively to all the other guys flirtations. This one stocky guy, not very bright, made subtle threats to me that I stay away from her; that he had it in the bag and I'd best go and mind my own business. I was put to train under this kid who couldn't be older than 17. He was openly gay and had an aptitude for being quite helpful. He explained to me that in the cash booth there were no stools for us to sit on. We had to stand the entire 6 — 10 hrs because the company believed that sitting causes idleness which in turn causes mistakes to be made. I told him that that was a shitty arrangement for us cashiers. He agreed but explained to me that he was here just for the summer so it didn't bother him. To this day I've never seen a more effective cashier than that 17 year old boy I met briefly at MovieTowne. He treated the cash he recieved lovingly and would go as far as putting the dirty bills at the back of the pile so that his drawer would look full of crisp new bills. I don't know if that gave him some sense of satisfaction in life but it was quite interesting to watch him. Pretty soon I realized that the cinema was flooded with managers. They seemed to come out of the woodwork. Every shift had a different manager who periodically came and collected the cash whenever it reached a certain amount. While doing this they kept making these ambiguous statements that basically said, 'If even a dime is short we're gonna have your ass for breakfast.’ When it was lunch break I headed over to the concessions booth and to the ushers to make friends. A manager leaped out of nowhere in front of me and told me that I'm not allowed to mingle with other departments. I managed to evade him and strike a conversation with a young female usher. I asked what was the problem with this place and she explained that she felt sorry for cashiers. Managers didn't trust them and always felt as though the new cashiers were trying to find ways to rob the cinema. They basically wanted cashiers isolated from everyone to prevent any kind of 'cahoots’ situation. I was given 15 minutes for my lunch break and within 10 minutes this burly, bald guy was on the hunt for me to be getting back to my post. He was the head honcho manager of that branch of the cinema. Something about him irked me greatly and I could see he had similar sentiments every time our eyes met. That evening was very busy. Terminator: Salvation had had its premier and long lines of patrons came to see it. The cinema had a long list of random discounts and promotions; senior citizens discount, student discounts, free birthday specials, discounts for members of the defense force, discounts for friends of animal shelters, radio promotion discounts etc etc. Even though it was my first day I was expected to learn how to cash all these discounts properly. At the end of my shift, Mr. Baldy came with a smug look on his face explaining to me that I didn't collect two coupons for senior citizens and as such my cash register was short by $80. He explained that this would be deducted from my salary which meant that I worked for $50 that day ($25 of which was spent on getting taxis to and from there and the remainder was spent on lunch). In other words I stood all day on my feet cashing so I could buy myself some lunch. Mr. Baldy then has the audacity to tell me that I'll be working a double tomorrow of which he asserts that it would be good for me to recuperate the money I lost today. I went home a heavy heart. I only spent 8 hrs at the job but already I despised it. However, good fortune was directed my way. My mother gave me a letter that explained that I had an interview for a much more comfortable job with a better salary. I had the choice of going back to Baldy and Madame Psudo-Flirty or going for the job interview. You could guess which option I chose. Edit: This is one of three working-in-a-cinema related stories I have thus far. The other two are much more funny and inspirational and can be read here and here

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What is the worst experience you had during your college life?
Answer: Gotta crack my fingers because I have so many. But I'll stick to two rather sordid experiences that still rock my world anytime I think about it. In the University of the West Indies (Caribbean) there was a period (late 00s to mid 2010s) where college tuition for locals was completely free and paid off for by the Trinidad Government without discretion. Now you'd think that most people would be satisfied with this arrangement as all that matters is personal effort and maybe a few hundred dollars to purchase the required text books and whatnot, but as Trinis are versed in screwing up stuff for everybody there was a growing population of people who believed that despite the free tuition, they should not have to pay for text books or anything at all and they should not have to do any work either. Here are two stories that highlight this freeloading mindset that we have: Marketing was a relatively easy course, especially when given during the short summer period. Most of us enlisted in summer courses were evening students like myself who had a full/part time job and a handful of full time students who failed the course during the prior semester. There was a full time girl, whom I shall refer to as Janet who had a skin condition, bad eyesight and poor posture with coke bottle glasses. Despite being only 20 years old her physical characteristics made her look like a female Mr. Mole Man from The Simpsons. She would sit at the back of the class by herself as she apparently didn't like the attention her skin condition drew. Being something of an outcast myself I felt it my duty to reach out to her and let her feel welcomed among my gang of older evening students as she probably got awkward treatment from the younger full time students. When I first spoke to her I observed that she was somewhat defensive and high strung, seemingly enjoying having an argument about any topic you brought to her. However I reminded myself that anyone with such a lamentable physical condition would be difficult to communicate to considering the pain she endured in life. We were given a group assignment. Her fellow full time students avoided her so I asked her if she was willing to join our group. She hastily agreed and from then on I observed a sudden ego trip on her part as she started to make herself leader of the group and delegated who was doing what and what each person's role for the project was. She didn't assign any task for herself but seemed happy assigning tasks to everyone and making it clear that she had a certain standard for whatever project she was given. Most of us immediately became annoyed with her. All of us had years experience in the world of work and to hear this 20 year old delegate work for us was a bit excessive. We decided to just ignore her demands and explain to her what we democratically decided to do. This was not to happen as she suddenly vanished from class. All calls to her cell went unanswered and we all assumed that she probably transferred to another course, which would've been quite rude seeing that she never communicated with us but whatever. We continued with our group project and during the final week for submission we explained to our lecturer that she had gone AWOL but if she were to return, we would have no issue allowing her to be awarded a grade for an assignment she had literally no input towards. The lecturer said that was very kind of us and when we submitted the assignment, she suddenly appeared out of nowhere. She seemed exceedingly exasperated that no one communicated with her and followed her directions. She wanted the assignment a certain way and when she saw what was submitted she made a motion with the head of department to have the the group declared exploitative and unfair. She wanted the assignment cast aside and for the two days that remained she wanted an emergency meeting to discuss a new assignment, according to her standards and decisions. One could imagine the amount of hatred that was generated towards her. Even the lecturer was most disgusted and tried to appeal to her to simply let it be. Our mistake was that we did not make an official complaint about her and announce that she had abandon the group. She went to the Student Guild and found out that by some obscure policy she had the power to dismiss our assignment as she was an affirmed member of the group. I went to the head of department and explained what had happened and was shocked to hear that she had given a report that we were intolerant towards her medical condition, racist, sexist and the like. Having a good relationship with the department I explained the truth and they found an loophole whereby I simply change a few diagrams and wording, allow her to see the changes and if she refuses to communicate we can have her kicked out the group. Thankfully she didn't catch on to the plan and when I offered her to see the changes we made, like an idiot she outright refused. Her goose was cooked. The department removed her from the group assignment and our project was submitted. She found out what was happening and begged that we include her name on the assignment. Not being idiots we refused and she was forced to create a project from scratch in a matter of a few hours. If she passed or failed the course I do not know. However we all realized that we had just danced with the Devil and were lucky to come out unscathed. From then on I was completely wary of anyone I asked to join any group project, regardless of how sad and lamentable their position in life was. 2. Ruthless Ruth. After that experience I became wary of full time students. I assumed that it was less than likely that an older Evening student would do anything to saboage her compatriots or take advantage of their kindness. That was until I met Ruth. She was a single mother in her mid-late 30s. She was a teacher in a primary (elementary) school and most of us found her to be well adjusted, responsible and mature. No one thought she was capable of doing harm. I had started an endeavour of purchasing used text books online and selling them to students at a reasonable price. Textbooks were insanely expensive and while most would source a new text book at $100 US I would source a new copy only at a quarter of the price and pocket a small profit. I proudly explained to Ruth my successful endeavour and she complimented me on how ambitious and clever I was. We shared a Management Accounting course (of which she had failed prior) and I proudly explained to her that I managed to secure the used text book online for less than a quarter of the price in great condition. 'I want to buy it from you,' she said rather determinedly. As I was good in Accounting I didn't need the textbook and as she was 'one of us’ I offered to sell it at a tiny markup. She agreed to the terms but mentioned that she was in dire straits financially and would only be able to pay after the final exam. Final exam came and went and I passed but Ruth, despite having the text, failed again. She was most angry because now she would have to pay to repeat the course. This course was only available a full year into the future. I expressed my sorrow that she failed and asked her to return the text. I was getting offers from others to buy it at a large markup. 'No.’ She said and looked me dead in the eye. 'Excuse me?’ I replied and she simply laughed off the matter and said that she just needed it for one more semester, that she would (illegally) photocopy the text. She told me to tell my prospect to wait, that the course wasn't due until a year anyhow. I protested but she simply laughed. I didn't know what to do. I went to the Student Guild (a bunch of twenty somethings playing video games in a little office) and explained my situation. They said that it was out of their jurisdiction and that I should've been a little more prudent. My client sourced the book somewhere else and after a year passed I got wind that Ruth failed the subject once again. She had the audacity to tell me that according to law she had preference to pay for the book when she felt like it. I was astonished. This supposed mature lady was nothing but a conniving scoundrel who took advantage of the niceness of others. I spread the word about what she had done to my fellow Eevining students and they looked at me shocked but explained that they always detected a nasty side of her when it came to getting what she wanted. In the end I never got back my book. Years later I'm doing pizza delivery part time and non other than Ruth enters the building. She's wearing a large wig and excessive makeup and she comes to me with a big shit eating grin on her face talking about how she finally got her degree and had secured a house from the Government as well as a promotion from her school. She makes no apology about my text and proceeds to order an expensive pizza, mentioning that it's her son's birthday and didn't like food that came in late. I'm not a violent person but watching her smiling in her hairpiece gave me the most evil of thoughts. I took a breath and let it slide. I delivered her pizza and imagined what a pathetic person she was and that in the end she was probably hurting inside at the direction of her life. I forgave what she did but I could not forget. The second time she called for delivery I immediately hung up the phone on her and explained to my supervisor that she was a difficult customer who couldn't decide what she wanted. That was the last time I heard from her.

Name: Elijah Williamson
Question: What type of women should you never date?
Answer: An acquaintance of an acquaintance of mine was a moderately attractive girl. We all attended the University of the West Indies as Evening students and shared the same course in Management Accounting. I'll refer to her as Sarah. Sarah wasn't the brightest bulb but she had a seemingly friendly disposition and was good with people….well, she was good with just males to be honest. Because she enjoyed a lifestyle of getting into the best parties as a 'promo girl’ (attractive girls dressed in skimpy clothing hired to sell/give away alcoholic beverages) her studies suffered. The night before the final exam she approached me in desperation explaining that she did poorly in her midterm and wasn't ready for this exam. She asked that I come over to her place and we both do an 'all-nighter.’ Being as clever as she was with the opposite sex, she made sure to sumptuously stress on and repeat the word 'all-nighter’ as she was aware it sent erotic images into my mind. Despite originally planning to get some good sleep that night I went over to her apartment. She then served me hot chocolate and cookies whilst moving around in a rather eye popping nightgown. I sat and calmly explained accounting stuff but when 3am reached and I realized that she couldn't get the grasp of the first two chapters, I knew this was going to be a lost cause. I was ready to go home and sleep. However, she rubbed my legs tenderly and gave me puppy dog eyes, explaining how desperate she was to pass this exam. I've always been something of a nice-guy and taking advantage of women in desperation has never been my thing. I asked that she buy lunch after the exam in exchange for staying up all night. We continued and as the wee hours of morning started to break the stillness of the dark, she started getting rather irritable and I condescended to teaching her how to do up legit looking accounting tables and fill them with stuff that's supposed to be there. In my heart I knew she was going to fail. When 8am arrived we were both exhausted. I went home to have a bath and change clothes to ready myself for the exam at 11am. I sat the exam and found it a tad challenging but manageable. However when I glanced back at Sarah her face looked as though she was trying to solve the meaning of life. After the exam ended and everyone filed out the building I headed towards Sarah who bore a disturbed countenance and seemed to be trying to avoid me. I inquired as to her exam experience and she said that it was very difficult and that she didn't even finish half the paper and was certain to fail. I pretended that this wasn't the case. Pondering about the lunch she promised I asked, 'So what's for lunch?’ 'I'm so tired,' she said, 'I need some sleep. See you later.’ She then pulled out her phone as though she just got a phone call and walks the opposite direction from me. Instinctively I know that she is pretending to talk on the phone as a means to get away from me and the topic of her promise to by me lunch. I realize I've been shafted but I tell myself that failing an exam after staying up all night can bring the worst out in anybody. The following semester I'm in the library doing an assignment for marks towards my Statistics midterm. I get a call. I answer it and it's Sarah. I had never even given her my number before. In her typical sugary tones she questions as to how I'm doing and how she doesn't see me around anymore and how I'm so smart she thought I had already finished University with first class honours and yadee yadee yaa. I listen with patience to her insincere flattery knowing fully well that she's looking for some kind of favour. 'Are you doing the Stats course this semester?’ 'Yes,' I stoically replied. I listen as she pretends that this is news to her. She gushes about how it is such a wonderful coincidence and that she is also doing the same course. I already knew this because in the class I had already seen her name signed in the role even though I never witnessed her attending a single class. Clearly she got some naive manchild to sign for her attendance. 'I'm having problems with the stats assignment….you know the one that is due tomorrow. Can I meet you somewhere? Question: How did your boss respond when you told him/her you quit?
Answer: I worked evenings doing pizza delivery some years ago. I performed well and had a good reputation by my coworkers and customers. However I suffered when it came time to head home after work. The taxi situation was dire and I would be stranded in the streets desperately trying to hitch a ride home. 'Can I use my delivery scooter to go home with?’ I begged the delivery manager over the phone an evening. 'It's very difficult for me to get home at nights.’ 'Sorry,' he replied, 'Company policy….’ The company apparently had great fears that I would steal their beaten up, little scooter that bore a fat, moustachioed Italian on the surface of its storage box. And this is after 5 years of service to them. I even offered to buy the scooter on a payment plan but he still refused. I then asked for a transfer to a branch closer to home. He agreed to that idea and seemed to have actually been making some phone calls to get the transfer done when suddenly he called to give me some bad news. 'The position has been taken.’ 'What?’ I said, 'By who?’ 'Ms. Nelson's (a restaurant manager) daughter applied to work delivery. She wanted a location close to home. They gave her the location you wanted.’ He seemed genuinely sorry for me and explained to me that he was delivery manager and not human resource, thus he had no power in regards to staff allocation. It hit like a ton of bricks. Five years I had dedicated to the company and all I asked for was a transfer close to home and they gave it to some girl fresh out of high school who kinda wanted to try deliveries and had connections. The delivery manager begged that I stay stating that most likely the girl wouldn't last and then I could get the position. He was right. The girl didn't last, but still the position was given to someone else. When I got the news again, I immediately sent in my resignation. However my delivery manager was in the process of retiring. After I resigned I heard that the new manager allowed all delivery riders to go home with their scooters/motorcycles if they wanted. It was like three consecutive slaps in the face.

Question: What is your scariest driving on a dark and lonely road at night story?
Answer: A few years ago I had just finished shift doing pizza delivery. It was 11:30 pm at night. I hopped into my pickup and was heading my usual route home. The road I took was a sort of backroad that skirted several impoverished areas, hood, drug blocks and the like. As I made a bend at an area called Enterprise, infamous for an ongoing turf war between rival gangs I heard a frantic female voice screaming and yelling help. She was coming out of this track that led to a cluster of ugly, I'll kept shantytown houses. She looked between 25 — 32 and wore a nightgown. She deliriously ran towards me yelling in our local patios , 'Help, he go kill meh!’ There wasn't anyone behind her but I immediately stopped and beckoned for her to come into my vehicle. She stood there frozen for a moment. Suddenly this unnerving feeling that something was wrong had come over me and I realized that I had made a big mistake. I couldn't understand it but my instinct told me that I should drive off immediately. I saw a big burly man walking calmly towards her. 'Get in,' I shouted. However she just stood there paralyzed. Her fear was indeed real. She was not acting. I beckoned her inside again, all the while the burly man calmly walked towards her. She then gave me a look that I can never forget. She looked me in my eyes as though telling me that she didn't want to get me involved. That her fate was sealed. The man put his arm around her shoulder as though he were a husband comforting a delirious wife and walked her back into the track. I drove off. To this day I can't figure out what exactly happened that night. To this day I don't know what would've happened if she had indeed entered my vehicle but my instinct is grateful that she didn't. I would advise no one to stop and rescue screaming nightgowned women running out of dark, seedy tracks in the middle of the night.

Question: What 1980s movies were huge at the time but are now almost forgotten?
Answer: The Abyss (1989) As a child of the 90s this movie was THE epic sci-fi fantasy movie while growing up in that era. It would show practically every summer on our local TV and even with a runtime of three hours long (with advertisements) my brother and I devoured it with a passion that we were never to experience again. I read critics joke that director James Cameron was: Therefore The Abyss was the product of those desires as it is sometimes condescendingly referred to as Close Encounters of the Third Kind…….Underwater. Regardless of the comparison after recently rewatching both movies I consider, by a thin margin, The Abyss to be the superior movie (because Richard Dreyfuss' character in Encounters is an annoying twat.) In the film, a team of divers, scientists, Navy SEALS and the like is sent to recover a sunken submarine and in the process encounter some strange activity. Unlike Encounters I love all the characters in The Abyss and find them all believable and likable. There are so many plotholes in Encounters that anybody with at least a high school education would find several scenes questionable. (So the Government has made so much effort to hide a top secret alien meeting mission from the public yet some crazy, deadbeat dad manages to evade helicopters, highly trained defense force operatives and scale a mountain with a grieving, frantic mom on tow so he could jump aboard a spacecraft of intergalactic kidnappers whose sole intention are to breed hideous human-alien hybrid children…….all so he doesn't have to pay child support.) Jokes aside, I think in retrospect Spielberg bit off far too much than he could chew. He never worked in top secret Government operatives so the story is a bit far fetched. Cameron on the other hand is a professional deep sea explorer so the movie doesn't go too far off the suspension of disbelief scale into ludicrousness. Both movies have stunning finales but I would personally go with The Abyss in terms of scale and wonder whereas Encounters is more impressive in terms of special effects. Sadly The Abyss is hardly ever mentioned and is on the road to becoming a lost classic. At least in my book.

Question: What disappointed you today?

I tried to empathize with the situation and understand that such were the cards she were dealt in life. She claimed her parents did not help her and she had no one else to turn to. However, some days afterwards I was confronted by the boyfriend on a Friday night whilst about to head out on a delivery. He was alone this time but twice as drunk. He was a tiny guy himself with a scar on his face and tried to put on a mean disposition while shit-faced that made him look as threatening as a battered lawn gnome come to life . He pointed at her through the glass panes and mumbled, 'You see Shorty across there……..she's mine…….. Remember………I live walking distance from here.’ I smiled at his vague threat. I wanted to badly tell him that I was aware 'Shorty’ was his girlfriend and that I was fully aware that awful apartment in that dangerous street that they lived in across the road was a result of him being such a lowlife scrub and drunkard. However I just ignored him and went on my delivery. When I returned, I approached 'Shorty' about the subtle threat her boyfriend just gave me, she again laughed it off and mentioned that he was just ignorant but that she will speak to him. I didn't like how she brushed off such a serious matter but again I reminded myself that she had a bad hand of cards in life. Weeks after I begin my evening shift and encounter her in tears. I asked her what was the matter and she said that the manager was forcing her to work another double. She explained further that the babysitter was not waiting any longer and was going to leave the kids at the apartment unattended. I asked where the boyfriend was in all of this and she muttered something about him out job hunting. She then mentioned that the manager told her that if she left the compound she would be terminated with immediate effect. That part sent me through the roof. The manager was one to take advantage of the ignorance of workers like her. I explained to Shorty that the manager did not have the power to fire her and that the company would dare not fire her under such circumstances because that could be tantamount to the ugliest of lawsuits and a complete stain on the company's image. By saying this she felt the confidence to stand up for herself and without a further word she left the restaurant to see about her kids. A few minutes after I am called to the manager's office to explain to her why it is I encouraged insubordination amongst the employees. That discussion led to a literal shouting match between the manager and I. We did not get along well and this matter escalated the growing rift between us (of which several months later I would eventually be terminated from the company.) After some weeks passed Shorty proudly bragged to everyone that she was quitting her job. Her sister was making a fortune selling face masks on the street and she decided to join her and become an entrepreneur. I tried to warn Shorty that this whole face mask business was good but it didn't seem like something that would last well into the future, that maybe she should do it on the side part time. She ignored me. She was on her own Cloud 9 and wanted to celebrate her pending wealth and financial independence. She left the company the following Friday and from that day forward she came to dine at the restaurant every Saturday, with her boyfriend and kids to show off that she was no longer an employee but now a customer with money to spend. While ordering she started speaking to us in arrogance, telling the cashier how well done she wanted her pizza and not to skimp on the toppings and to have the table she sat on properly wiped for her family. Apparently her mask selling raked in the dough. She wanted the world to see that. I was flabbergasted. This was the same girl who I suffered being blacklisted by the manager. All it took was a few hundred dollars extra of disposable income to show her true colours. Sad to say her face mask endeavour started to wane as the market became flooded with people like her trying to get in on the game. It eventually came to a halt as Government issued that face mask wearing no longer be mandatory, thus killing the market. A year has passed and I haven't seen her since. She apparently moved from the apartment but with whereabouts unknown. I could only hope that some sort of miracle saved her or that she has at least learnt a lesson in life. But her story is practically the stereotypical tragic story of the many women employed in fast food. We all would like to help them and we all should…..but a lot of them really need to first to learn how it is to make the proper decisions to help themselves.

Question: How many people do you know that hooked up in high school, got married, and have been together ever since?
Answer: I had an acquaintance named Avinash in high school. He was a year older than the rest of us in class and by the time I was starting to develop my little ratty strains of moustache he already had a full moustache, beard and sideburns combo. He was tall, athletic and good looking; the typical jock/team captain persona. He was quite laid-back and would laugh at anything good natured. Amelia was another acquaintance of mine. She was attractive in a girl next-door sense, with lightbrown eyes and a charming smile. She had a very homely feel about her and she always gave that wife vibe to all our fellow classmates. I wasn't all that interested in her but after a string of rejections from some of the girls in school I told myself why not and approached Amelia in a flirtatious manner. As I vainly expected, Amelia responded subtly encouragingly. I bemoaned that a good looking guy like me is supposed to have a girlfriend by now (I wasn't the most mature teenager in class) and that she and I would make a great match because we're both poor. I asked her why was she so interested in him and she replied the typical teenaged excuse for such prying, ‘I know someone who likes him.’ After that encounter I had a class with Avinash, whom I sat next to and I began to tell him of my success in scoring with Amelia. He grabbed me by the shoulder with his large hands and shook me in congratulations. I proceeded to recap the conversation I had with her. He thanked me voraciously. After school was over I went to find Amelia so she could leave the compound with me and my buddies. Just treat her good for me.’ Amelia giggled and Avinash gave me an appreciative smile. Nineteen years and two kids later, they're both still together and so in love that you'd swear that they're still a pair of teenaged sweethearts. I'd like to think I had a part to play in this inspiring love story but I think they'd would've hooked up regardless of my interaction. Great souls always find one another. Question: What is the most offensive thing you've been told while out on a date?
Answer: A decade ago, I went on a date with someone I met on a dating website. I considered myself witty back then and a good few of my jokes had a sarcastic element to them. I met someone on the dating site who seemed to greatly appreciate deadpan quirkiness and sarcasm. She seemed to appreciate it a bit too much than is healthy for the average human. We arranged to meet at the mall. When we saw each other her eyes flitted away from mine and she stared at my shoes. 'That's the shoes you came to see me in?’ She then gave a soft yet caustic 'huh huh huh’ laugh to herself and began what would be a series of rolling eyes at everything that was said. I didn't understand what she meant. The shoes were almost new and were my best pair of sneakers. In fact, compared to her I was overdressed as she wore a rather unflattering suspender-skirt combo and an old pair of sandals. Minus the afro she looked a lot like the photo below but far more unkempt. I decided to ignore the comment. I asked her if she wanted to see a movie and she immediately made this whistling noise and started to go off about mindless dribble that Hollywood dishes out. I sort of agreed with her but at the same time her anti-Hollywood rant came across a bit on the pretentious side. We basically walked around the mall, her making random sarcastic comments about anything in her field of vision and me trying to agree with what she said and keep the conversation flowing. When we parted ways and I went homewards I did a quick mental audit of the date and my conclusion was that she definitely was not my cup of tea. However I told myself that maybe she probably suffers from some sort of anxiety and that's why she behaved so strangely. Maybe I ought to give her a chance. I called to tell her that I enjoyed our time and to find out if she was back home safe. 'Calling to see if I'm home safe?’ she replied, 'Bro. That's so corny. That's like men from the 50s.’ I could hear her faint 'huh huh huh’ laugh and could envision her rolling her eyes. I couldn't help but notice a strong pang of irritation develop within me. I put that aside and we spoke for a bit and ended up agreeing to meet her after she finished her classes the following day (she did a Degree in Computer Science). I told myself that with a little patience she would drop that caustic quirkiness of hers and start showing more warmth . I bought a rose for her and travelled to her school. I told myself what girl wouldn't love a man greeting her outside her class, well dressed and holding a rose for all her peers to see. Being that her class was due to over in a few minutes I basically ran up the street. When I arrived at the school, I called her phone to no avail. I told myself that her class was probably still in session. Then I saw a bunch of students filing out and I knew that she had to be among them. I saw her at the back, looking particular slovenly staring at me with her usual vacant stare. 'Oh my God.’ I saw her mouth the words as I moved towards her with the rose. However she mouthed it in distaste as though I were brandishing a slimy toad. As I reached within earshot she said the single most offensive thing I've ever heard someone mutter to me during a date. 'I was hoping you didn't come.’ This was followed by her 'huh huh huh’ laugh and rolling eyes. The irritation from the day before changed to anger. I tried to put aside the statement as another of her offbeat quirkiness and told her passionately about my hasty journey to get to her and how I ran up the street so as not to have her waiting. 'Dude,' she replied, 'That's psycho talk. Shut up.’ I paused and looked at her for a long while. Her supposed sense of humour was truly starting to rub me the wrong way. It sounded like a joke but came across like a vent fashioned into a rude and unfunny joke. She then talked about how she saw phone calls but intentionally disregarded them in the hopes that I would go away. She then mentioned that she saw me running up the street like a madman with a rose in my hand and felt so embarrassed. I remained silent. It was now a code red. Either I give her a piece of my mind or bow gracefully and leave. I opted for the latter and waited for a good civil moment to depart. 'You look like the type who doesn't go anywhere,' she continued, 'Seeing how you just ran through the streets just to see me from class you probably don't go out much. My ex boyfriend was a DJ. I used to get in to all the parties for free. He wasnt much to look at but a little sex now and again and I got into all the exclusive parties…..even aboard yachts. You know what a yacht is right?’ I remained silent. 'Dunno why I'm telling you all this………Look at you.You look like you want knock my head off don't you. Huh huh huh.’ It then dawned upon me that this girl was a twisted individual. This wasnt some quirky sense of humour. This was someone who got their kicks off of provoking others. Whatever hurt she experienced from those she loved in the past, she clearly wanted to exact that hurt on innocent people around her. When she arrived at her taxi stand I stood and waited in silence until she got into one. 'Well look at you,' she said in a last desperate attempt for a reaction from me, 'My knight in shining armour... You should maybe think about buying a car……it's kinda lame that…' The taxi driver sped off without waiting for her to finish what she was saying, probably cognizant that she was someone full of shit. I went home proud of myself that I didn't give her the reaction she desired. I deleted my account on the dating site. After that encounter I became far more conservative towards the use of sarcasm in humour and communication. I've been attracting much more likable and attractive females ever since that minor adjustment. So everything truly is a learning experience.
