Question: Why do the rich become richer and the poor poorer?
Answer: Consider the above drawing. The mountain represents varying degrees of wealth. Poverty, represented by the area at the red P is the most steep area at the slope. Any wrong move, any poor investment, bad financial decision, heck even non action itself would lead to the climber slipping off the slope and down to rock bottom. People born into poverty have to climb that steep slope. There are no second chances. Once you fall you are either dead, crippled or lucky enough to just simply lose the motivation to try climbing again. Stability represented by the blue S is the area where the mountain becomes less steep. You can relax a bit. It is no longer a fight for survival. Most people aspire for stability; a decent job, a nice house and car and loving family. If you make a bad move you are on such stable grounds that you can simply pick yourself back up but too many mistakes and you slip right back into poverty. Wealth represented by the green W is the area where, with just a little additional effort during Stability, you can make it near the top of the mountain. Though you can slip and fall back into poverty it's very unlikely. Any further effort and you will land yourself at the top of the mountain, the super wealthy, the select few at the very top. Here's why the poor get poorer and the rich get richer: The slope representing poverty is steep and long whilst the slope from stability into wealth is steep but not nearly as long. What does this mean? It's harder and takes much longer for poor people to get out of poverty than it is for well-off people to get more rich.

Question: What show / movie had no right to be as good as it was?
Answer: Back in 1999 my brother and I was spending some summer vacation time at our cousin's place in Tobago. It wasn't the greatest of vacations because our cousin and her boyfriend were having these vicious fights over money (they weren't in the best place financially and had four daughters below the age of 5). We decided to spend a Saturday afternoon going to the cinema. We didn't care what was on, we just wanted to get away from the endless arguments amidst the chaos of screaming toddlers and mounds of filthy diapers. This was the double feature of the weekend: As a pair of hormone raging, ignorant and slightly sexist teenage boys, you could guess which movie appealed to us more. We were grateful that the 007 movie was showing first so we wouldn't have to stick around to watch Double Jeopardy or as my brother called it The Fugitive….but with a Woman. When The World Was Not Enough ended with its typical 007 sexual innuendo type final scene my brother and I looked at each other and nodded. It was ok. There was a lot of explosions, chase scenes, Denise Richards’ bouncing breasts and shorty shorts but we both knew we were unimpressed. However, in our typical peer influenced macho-vision we pretended that the movie was the real deal. We had the choice of watching Ashley Judd outrun a police car or go home and face adults yelling while half naked toddlers pee themselves in fright. We decided to watch the movie. What a great decisions that was. Double Jeopardy was like a roller coaster ride that got better by the minute. It was far better than The World is Not Enough. It was even better than The Fugitive. When she got her poetic justice in the end my brother and I jumped from our seats and wanted to hug each other in tears. We could give a fart about our macho ideals, Ashley Judd was our sister and she finally been done right. It was that good of a movie! We left the cinema thoroughly satisfied and entertained in so much that the choas that awaited us home didn't seem to matter anymore. I recently rewatched it with the idea that maybe it wasn't that great and maybe because we were dumb teenagers it had made an impression. I was blown away even moreso a thirty something year old dad than as a thirteen year old boy. The movie abandons every cliche there is about on-the-run and fugitive type action thrillers. The lead role is no superhero, there is no stupid forced comic relief character making racist jokes, there is no romantic subplot. Straight up escape and revenge served on a hot plate with Tommy Lee Jones in his best performance ever imho. I sincerely recommend it.

Question: What is an example of an album that, in your opinion, was ruined by the producer and/or the production?
Answer: It always blows my mind why no one mentions how awfully inconsistent the sound is in Jimi Hendrix's legendary Are You Experienced album. Not saying that it's a bad album, it's one of the greatest albums on Earth. However I can't help but shudder when I hear sound inconsistencies and downright amateurish recording. It's so sad that someone like Hendrix who was possibly the greatest guitarist of the 20th century had his masterpiece recorded in mono. His complex arrangements condescended to just a flat block of sound. Worse yet, because of financial burden, Chas Chandler, the producer and member of The Animals, had the album recorded in 16 different sessions at 3 different locations. When you go from track to track you can hear the chaos behind the production. Songs like Manic Depression, Stone Free and May This Be Love sound hollow as though recorded in someone's basement whilst Fire, Purple Haze and Hey Joe are treated with tender loving care. Love or Confusion sounds as though Chandler was tripping acid while recording and simply toying with the mix as within a few seconds the volume suddenly increases in itself erratically and from then on it's a brawl between guitar, bass and drums. In many instances the Hendrix's voice and guitar overwhelms Mitch Mitchell's drums and Noel Reddings bass. As much as I love Hendrix and his guitar prowess, he wasn't the greatest of vocalists and some tracks could of benefitted with greater accentuation of his talented bandmates. All in all, the chaotic production behind Are You Experienced makes it feel more like a collection of B sides (exceptional B sides) rather than a work of art. Each track takes me to a different place, but not in a good way. I'm sure this wasn't the ‘Experience’ Hendrix wanted the world to have, but say what, it's still an excellent album.

Question: What's the worst experience you've had with telling someone you had feelings for them?
Answer: While at University I observed that any course that had the word 'Management’ within its name was bound to be laden with beautiful women. When I did Management Accounting I was introduced by Lorna, a good female friend of mine, to this tall, shapely and somewhat quirky young lady with thick black curls, full lips and a shapely body. The only flaw that I observed was she had a slight paunch. Her name was Gabrielle or Gabby as she preferred to be called. She had an outspoken yet aloof disposition whereby she could say the most unfiltered thing and it would never come across offensive, well to me at least. I recall while walking with her and Lorna, Gabby randomly blurted out that my fantasy would be for her and Lorna to carry me to some secret location for a lapdance and ménage à trois. Lorna went red, either in anger, embarassment or a combination of the two. I soon discovered that Gabby's sister attended the school where I worked. I was never able to procure Gabby's phone number as I never got another chance encounter (she was very delinquent in class attendance) and Lorna didn't have it either. I then came up with what I considered a fool proof idea. I would write an old fashioned love letter, explaining my feelings for her and sealed with a kiss I would carry it to her sister to have it delivered to Gabby. All my feelings just flowed out of me as I wrote that long letter. I put a sticker of a rose and then neatly folded it into a red envelope. When I came upon the sister (12 years old at the time) I explained to her my feelings for Gabby and my intention for her to deliver this letter of love to her. I was expecting the sister to gush and swoon (as girls her age are prone to do regarding such romance) but instead she gave me an odd look of confusion and disbelief. 'Are you sure?’ Was all she could reply. 'Yeah,' I said flatly, 'Your sister made such an impression on me. I can't stop thinking of her.’ 'Why don't you just tell her yourself?’ the sister replied in that off-putting, emotionless tone quite strange for a girl her age. 'I don't have her phone number,' I replied and after a brief silence where I'm sure the sister sized me up and decided not to give me Gabby's number, she acquiesced to delivering the letter. The following day, I went up to the sister anxious to hear of what was Gabby's response or better yet collect a letter of my own. 'Did you give her the letter? I asked excitedly. The sister avoided my glances. 'Yeah.' I waited for her response. 'And what happened?’ I said, detecting a faint feeling that this wasn't going to work out well. 'She just looked at it and asked who it was from.’ Another silence. 'And what happened after?’ I said with an underlying sense of dread. 'She asked me what it was you wanted. I told her that you liked her…..she looked at the letter and then put it on her dresser.’ I felt my stomach tighten. 'Didnt she read the letter?’ 'No,' the sister flatly replied, 'She still hasn't opened it.’ There was an awkward silence and the sister then uttered, 'Sir I have to go.’ I felt like the world's biggest clown. I half imagined the sister running to tell a her classmates what a loser Mr. Williamson was and then describing the story. Fast forward four months later and I'm shopping around for car insurance. I head into this big building and none other than Gabby is sitting at the reception office, heavily pregnant. She engages me in delightful quirky conversation as normal almost as though the whole love letter incident was a figment of my imagination. I bid her adieu and immediately called Lorna to tell her what happened to her friend. 'My friend!’ Lorna said shocked, 'She wasn't my friend. She's just a girl from my class. I thought she was your friend! Didn't you realize she was pregnant?’ I replied no and then explained my prior feelings for Gabby and the whole love letter fiasco. 'You sent Gabby a love letter!’ Lorna cried in great shock, 'But she's pregnant….and she's engaged. Didn't you see the ring on her finger?’ Suddenly I just felt like a massive brick landed on my head. Soon the pieces started to fit together.

Question: I got an invitation to a high school reunion where I was bullied. I am successful in my career. I want the satisfaction that I’m doing better than my bullies, but I don’t want to demean myself on that level. Should I go?
Answer: The fact that you are basing a decision solely on the hurt you felt by underdeveloped humans many years (or decades) ago makes me question the level of your ‘success’ if that is your state of mind. The most successful people I know from high school are the ones who haven't allowed the hurt they've experienced deter them from being decent human beings. They don't let it affect making simple decisions that require just an hour or two of their time, a little small talk here, a little empathy there and would cost less than taking the family to see a movie. This is my class back in '99. If you're trying to spot me I'm the awkward nerd on the far right trying to fit in with the group (I had to invite myself over to the shoot). I had a decent amount of friends but I would honestly say that I didn't really get along with the majority of my classmates. A lot of them were obsessed with MTV lifestyle, being relevant and popular. A lot of them were quite mean to me because I was poor and didn't hide it or attempt to fit into their mould. Also, I had my fair share of encounters with physical and mental bullies. This guy here taking the absolute cake. But I wasn't perfect myself. I could be quite obnoxious, aloof and frivolous and I did act randomly mean to some of my own friends who looked up to me. No child in in the history of high school could be considered a model citizen. High school reunions are not just made up of bullies and assholes. There might also be some of the nice former classmates. Even better, you may meet one or two who were awful back in the day but now matured into caring and sensitive adults. Even better, some of your former bullies might even have the burning desire to apologize to you for all the years of hurt. To go to a high school reunion solely flaunt success to your former bullies reeks of immaturity and borderline narcissism. If the above question is a valid question in your mind then you definitely should not ‘demean yourself’ by going. Just as a final sidenote, I was invited to the above class' high school reunion but chose not to go. Not because of personal dislike but because a special, self appointed committee had formed amongst some the more well-off classmates and they decided to pick and choose who was worthy of being invited to the reunion (my best friends were not invited). No thanks. In a case like that. You definitely ought not to demean yourself by going to such a class reunion.

Question: Can you describe the smelliest person you have met?
Answer: Some months ago I was on the bus headed homewards. One of my pleasures in life is being able to read leisurely without any disturbance whilst on the typically quiet journey home on such bus. But alas, on that very day, such was not in the cards for me. Not by a longshot. The biggest chatterbox I know in existence happened to come into the bus and sat directly opposite me prodding me on the shoulder while I sat with headphones on attempting to read. I groaned but extended courtesy towards listening and engaging in some small talk about her workplace gossip, family gossip, how great her husband is, how she feels about bla bla bla. Nothing is wrong with all this except that she is one of those rare individuals who doesn't allow the talk to falter and prods you with a barrage of inane questions as though to ensure she has your complete attention. While trying to evade some rather nosy and trifling questions I got a whiff of of a scent that can only be described as startlingly ominous. I grimaced a bit and stared suspiciously at my acquaintance and nervously took a moderate whiff to determine if she was the culprit. Thankfully she wasn't. I was wondering if was just a fluke scent that drafted temporarily from the netherregion of some coarse individual who had left the bus but the scent happened to linger on for some seconds longer. I told myself the scent was gone. But alas, like a slap in the face the scent struck me again. It was even more powerful this time. Even through my facemask I could smell the scent, a scent that could only be described as something so offensive that it was beyond bestial. It smelt as though someone rubbed a sweaty, boozy armpit against my nose and then held my face upon the taint of some scoundrel who refused to bathe for weeks. 'Are you smelling that?’ I asked Madame Chatterbox and she stared at me with a rather dumb smile and replied, 'Smelling what?’ There was a pause and she continued with her monologue interspersed with trivial questionings. I began to get a headache. Someone in the back stank the high hell but I couldn't determine who was the culprit. There was a security officer, a middle aged woman and a sleeping old man in the back. None of them looked like the kind of person whose power of stench could bring the dead back to life. The scent came in waves; faintly menacing at its best, repugnant at its worst. So as not to retch I had to practice breathing through my mouth, but I felt nauseous knowing that I was sucking in that toxic air through my mouth and into my lungs. Madame Chatterbox continued on, despite the natural disaster that occured right in front of her nose. 'I'm so tired. I could just drop on my bed and sleep until next Monday. But I have to cook for my husband. You know how hard it is to cook every evening? You cook? I'm sure you probably go out and buy food every day. Lucky you.’ I didn't know what was worse. Having to endure that scent or having to endure Chatterbox's prying and passive aggressive vents disguised as small talk. Whatever poison was worse, the combination of the two was like a hellish torture. I was hoping at some bus stop, whomsoever was the culprit would hop off the bus. Hardly anyone ever went as far as the final stop. It would usually be just me and (unfortunately) Madame Chatterbox. At mid point the middle aged lady left the bus. At three quarter point the security guard hopped off. The only person left was the sleeping old man. Funny thing was, he didn't look like someone who would smell like a modern day torture instrument. He was relatively well dressed and ordinary looking. Another funny thing was I never saw him in the bus nor in the village before. He was a complete stranger. He lay snoring unwares as to the destruction that lay manifest under his arms and amidst his much unattended nether regions. I felt such a rage at his stink at some point I wanted to grab him by the collar, drag him to the front by the driver and demand that the driver smell him and agree to kick him out the bus. But alas such would not be the case. Mr. Smelly stayed with us the entire journey and Madame Chatterbox squawked the entire trip until I was rendered temporarily disabled by a pounding headache. When Mr. Smelly awoke and saw the final stop he bolted upright and shouted to the driver that he was on the wrong bus. He ran to the driver and begged that he remain on the bus to head back where it came from. The driver, finally getting a whiff of the scent, roared for the man to exit the bus immediately. While we exited the bus I could hear Mr. Smelly drunkenly complain that someone could have woken him up and told him he was on the wrong bus. He would've stoppped off much earlier and head back to the bus station. Hearing him say that and acknowledging the fact that all the torture was unnecessary, made me want to walk up to him and murder him. But alas such was not to happen.

Question: How many people can't stand their neighbors?
Answer: I live in a lower-middle class — middle class neighbourhood. Most people on my street know each other, not so much by name but by face or quirks. If I take a walk out the street there's a 50% chance some good Samaritan would stop to give me a ride. All in all I live in a nice neighborhood. My next door neighbours on the other hand aren't exactly good Samaritans to say the least: They DON'T socialize with anyone. No one even knows their names. They have one of the biggest houses in the street and they stick up in that house as though the minute they set foot on the road, like vicious cannibals the rest of the street would tear them to pieces. The never give anyone a ride. They've never invited anyone over for a beer or even glass of water. They don't hire anyone from the area for odd jobs. They've fenced a lot to the left of them, behind them and was attempting to grab a lot facing my direction (until my stepfather and I called them out on it), as evidenced in the photo below. Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. A phrase that I've followed all my life but for these people it's something I have to work really hard towards. Towards their credit I would admit that they don't disturb the peace, aren't nosy or confrontational and they are for the most part law abiding and non-polluting citizens. But honestly I don't know if a loud, trashy and obnoxious neighbor is worse than a quiet, selfish and sneaky one. It's a question I always sit and ponder.

Question: Who was the rudest person you’ve ever encountered? And what was your response?
Answer: Some years ago I was working the late shift at my part time job doing pizza delivery. I was taking phone calls when a smug, off-putting voice was suddenly heard on the other end of the line. 'Are you hearing me? This is Michael Griffith. G-r-i-f-f-i-t-h.’ There was a second of silence as I registered that that the person didn't even bother to say 'Good Evening.’ I acknowledged that I could hear him and subtly mentioned that I could spell. I then proceeded to ask him for more information. 'I have been a regular customer to this restaurant for over 15 years. I like my pizzas done a special way. Are you listening……what is your name?’ 'Elijah sir.’ 'I want a veggie pizza. Listen to how I want it……Are you hearing me?……..I want the dough baked with the pizza sauce and cheese, nothing else added………are you writing this down?…….Then I want the raw veggies added after the pizza has been cooked. DO NOT COOK MY VEGGIES. I REPEAT. DO NOT COOK THE VEGGIES ON MY PIZZA.’ I tried my best to separate this man's condescending tone and my feelings towards him and mentally process exactly what it was he requested. We always got customers who felt entitled to have their pizza done in some special way. Either they wanted their pizza baked separate from all other pizzas or their dough must be of a certain grade or the pineapples must be cut from fresh fruit and not from our canned stock. Most of the time we ignored them and just gave them what they (and everyone else) were paying for. Most of the time they just wanted to feel bourgeois. This guy however was adamant that I make his pizza with raw veggies. What this guy didn't seem to realize was that these veggies were never freshly cut veggies. These were precut veggies sitting overnight in a plastic tub in a chiller, probably swarming with bacterial matter. Cooking these veggies in the oven was his only defense against E-coli. If he were to get sick from eating his beloved raw veggie pizza, he could hold us accountable and sue and I would be the one to get the blame. I diplomatically expressed to him that we couldn't make his pizza in such a manner, that it was a risk to his health and against the company's policy. In anger he asked for my name a second time. 'Listen to me young man. I am arriving in 15 minutes and if I do not see my veggie pizza prepared the way I want it, I am going to deal with you.’ He then hung up the phone. I explained what just happened to the cashier and she agreed with me that the guy was an idiot and that we couldn't give him a raw veggie pizza. I processed the pizza order as a regular veggie pizza and continued taking calls. Fifteen minutes later I'm in the back, about to head out on a delivery when I heard a smug but familiar voice bellowing out at front counter, 'WHERE'S THAT STUPID BOY NIGEL?’ I looked in front to see Mr. E-coli in the flesh. He looked exactly like how I imagined he would look; large, big-bellied and bespectacled. He was middle aged and greying, with a thick bottom lip that projected outwards in perpetual disgust at the world in front of him. I kid you not he looked like the human version of the obnoxious character Bubble Bass from SpongeBob. Immediately my entire physique and mental structure took to the offense. I literally wanted to clobber this idiot. However, I marched to the front counter to confront him and use all my powers of vocabulary to diplomatically explain to him that he was an idiot and that he was not getting a raw veggie pizza from this branch. As if to make himself as repulsive as ever, with him was a preteen girl (either his niece or daughter) with whom he tried to exaggerate how tough he was, by yelling and berating, mostly female minimum wage paid fast food workers. 'Listen to me,' he shouted at the cashier, 'Remove this pizza and get me what I ordered. I want to see that boy who took my order.’ He then spread a creepy smile over his face, turned to the little girl and cooed, 'You’re gonna taste the real way to eat pizza.’ The poor little girl looked like she wished she could disappear at the moment. Everything about the guy was just so off-putting in an incongruent sense. He was like a living, breathing 'Can you find all the things wrong in this picture’ cartoon brought to life. 'I'm the one who took your order sir,’ I said with seething rage as he glanced me, ‘And you can't get a raw veggie pizza.’ I saw him turn red. This was no longer about the pizza. This was about him proving himself to that little girl. 'You telling me what I can or can't get?’ he bellowed, 'You want me to knock you out?’ I stood there waiting for the tub of lard to attack when the manager flew out her office and came between us. In her best prepared monologue she explained she was sorry for his inconvenience. The manager told me to go to the back. In anger I listened as she explained the danger of consuming such a pizza but acquiesced to his demand. After I cooled down some minutes later I grabbed a delivery and en route to my motorcycle out front I spotted him shovelling away his bacteria ridden pizza in his mouth and commanding the little girl to do the same. He gave me a nervous sideglance as I passed, then continued goading her to finish her slice. I asked God to protect that little girl from getting sick and pleaded that He not allow more idiots like that man to multiply on this Earth.

Question: What movies do you like but everybody hates, and why?
Answer: When The Matrix came out, every nerdy boy over 12 sang its praises. Every nerdy boy except me. I liked it (kinda) but I just couldn’t see the big deal about it. The action was good and everyone raved about the whole bullet time camera innovation. The soundtrack was phenomenal and the story and the main characters were intriguing. But I just couldn’t see the big deal. I just thought it was too silly for the movie to try to be deep and philosophical with its sociological commentary and high-brow sci-fi concepts, while at the same time engage in low-brow kung-fu action, psudo-BDSM rave culture, dystopian cyberpunk futurism, all the while having villains that looked like constipated insurance salesmen. I felt like the movie tried to be several things at once and took itself too seriously. I also felt that the movie would’ve been more enjoyable if it accepted how silly its concept was and focus more on its action scenes rather than having practically ever character besides Neo drifting off into some rambling philosophical stoner rant. Whenever I shared these criticisms with my nerd friends, they would turn red as though I demonstrated the most shocking of blasphemies. ‘You don’t get it. The Matrix is too deep for you to understand. Go watch your cartoons.’ That would be their usual response, but years would pass and my assessment would remain the same. THEN CAME THE MATRIX RELOADED I sat and watched it on TV long after its cinema premier. I wasn’t expecting much; some more philosophical sci-fi mumbo jumbo and a few over-rehearsed fight scenes. However, thirty minutes within the film I was finding myself thoroughly entertained. The movie went in the exact direction I wanted the first one to go. From the beginning to end the movie was a feast of God-like explosive superpowers, vast weaponry utilized in slow motion, explosions and swords slicing through speeding vehicles that contain time and space altering kung-fu fighting white rastas who can’t die, even in explosions. The movie relished in its stupidity and made no attempt to continue with the existential brouhaha of the original film. As an acne-riddled 18yo I ate it up like hot chicken soup but practically everyone I knew who worshipped the original, hated Reloaded with a passion. However, as admittedly dumb as it is, I consider it the superior movie. I haven't seen Resurrections yet but seeing that practically everyone loathes it I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out to be the best of the four.

Question: What advice changed your life financially?
Answer: Observing people’s lives rather than listening to their advice is what inspired my spending habits. So many people who draw some sort of salary have advice about spending that money. Spending advice is at every corner I turn. Here are some examples of such advice I encountered : I get that sort of advice practically everywhere, whether it be my co-workers, acquaintances and within my family, everybody is willing to guide me on how to save a couple bucks here and there with their helpful hints. But one thing that I can never discuss with them is this one taboo question, 'Are you satisfied with the direction of your life?’ Such a question would be considered condescending so such conversation is avoided. I look at the person giving me advice and ask myself does he/she lead the kind of life I want. Do I really want to be that guy stuck in a unfulfilling job to ensure that I pay off my car loan, coming home to an apartment to eat a can of Goya beans every evening? I've met so many people who base their lives around simple analogies: ‘You’re only young once.’ ‘Life is short.’ ‘You can’t eat money.’ ‘Treat yourself.’ ‘Work hard, play hard.’ Regardless of their responsibilities and obligations in life these are their core beliefs and they believe they have the wisdom to offer advice to all listening ears based on their beloved ambiguous three word quotes. In my view this is just a convenient mindset in which one can deny accountability for one self. ‘Honey I'm sorry but I can't pay rent this month. I was hanging out with the boys and one thing leads to another. Life is short. Can you borrow some more money from your parents?’ ‘No I'm not selling my car. This is a limited edition. I'll pay you back what I borrowed before the year is over. Life is short and you can't eat money.’ Sad to say these are the same kind if individuals who are most vocal when it comes to giving advice, personal and financial. If someone's personal lifestyle does not agree with you then do not follow their financial advice. One always goes with the other. In a nutshell I would advise that you stop listening to financial advice from those who place more value on emotional satisfaction. Just my 2¢. A donkey can bray as loud and as often as it feels to but it can never convince anyone that it is a horse.

Question: What movies with interesting concepts were poorly executed?
Answer: Looper (2012) ***Spoilers ahead*** Looper has the distinction of one of those rare movies. In the beginning it reminds me of why I love Hollywood and in the end it reminds me of why I hate Hollywood. Big budget Hollywood has mastered the art of dishing out movies that build imaginative concepts and develops intriguing characters and then by the halfway mark s**ts all over it with mindless action, tepid romance, explosions and low brow sci-fi for the sake of attracting all the Beavises and Buttheads out there. The story deals with bounty hunters who kill without discretion, victims sent from an agency in the future. The very same bounty hunters have an expiry date whereby when they reach a certain age they themselves are sent back to the past to be exterminated to 'close the loop.' Many times their own past selves are the ones who do such an extermination. Fascinating concept, and it gets even more fascinating when Bruce Willis' character escapes extermination from his younger self (Joseph Gordon Levitt) and then seeks to exterminate the guy who started this whole time travel assassination agency (The Rainmaker) while avoiding being killed by himself and several other 'loopers.’ Yeah rock on. Then somehow the movie takes us to a farm with some annoying kid and his mom, some soul searching and romance is flung into the mix, throw in a bunch of boring exposition, random telekinesis and super powers and the suddenly the movie turns into The Terminator meets Akira fanfiction. By the time the movie drew to a close (Joseph Gordon Levitt kills himself to eliminate his older self….big surprise) I yearn for the day time travel could be an actual possibility, so I could undo the precious time I wasted on this overrated movie.

Question: What is the most pointless crime you've witnessed?
Answer: I worked for a short stint as an usher in a multiplex cinema franchise. One of the perks of working in the cinema was that you get to watch as much movies as you want for free on your day off. You could also bring one partner with you. One of our newer teenaged employees didn't fully understand the perk and believed it to be 'one movie, one guest.’ My friends and I recognized this to be his understanding because he would always come with his little brother and after watching his one movie, we would spot him in the corner of our eyes making a lame attempt to sneak into another room with his little baby brother in tow. It was such a cute sight to behold that I informed the rest of the staff about his little crime and many of us would come out to see him snooping about after his movie, pretending to hold conversation with concessions staff or feigning interest in the posters and then the minute our back was turned would run into another showing. He was just so terrible at the 'crime’ that it was almost heartwarming to witness our two freeloaders scurrying about like mice whenever we pretended to turn our backs. It's only when the manager confronted him as to why he acted so strange did the pieces finally fall into place for him. We all rubbed it in how much we enjoyed his lame attempts at petty crime.

Question: Which kind of news do you like to access? Why?
Answer: Anything that is relevant to my way of life and personal interests. It sounds selfish but it's the truth. In the school where I work I teach children the art of how to read the newspaper. Random citizen over 40: 'How to read the newspaper?!’ What?! Children must get in the habit of reading the entire newspaper……every day……front to back…..all the time. Otherwise they will be ignorant.’ To that idealistic but naive person I would reply no. The paradox of modern life is that the more time we spend viewing the news, the more uncritical we allow ourselves get henceforth the more dumb we get. If I lived my life according to the news today I'd think that: Growing up in Trinidad we are taught to listen to the news, not follow it. Because of our colonial past as a tiny island with a large grapevine network, we have had defiance and skepticism over the higher order injected into our bloodstream. ‘Massa say it against the law to trespass into his hunting ground…’ ‘Massa say all trespassers will be shot…' ‘Pahgo say that Massa gone with he family to live in Scotland. Don't even care about hunting ground....does come back to estate only once a year…' ‘I going into the hunting ground…’ Regardless of the critical thinking aspect, I tell students the worst thing to do a newspaper is read it from the front page to the back. It's just such a waste of time to read the newspaper/listen to the news programs in its entirety. The average Trinidadian newspaper usually has 100 pages more or less. 50% is usually advertisements. 20% is usually feature sections of mild interest i.e. How Edward overcame his disability to become a firefighter etc etc. 5% is sport 10% is specialized news: business, technology, health etc 5% is opinions and editorials 10% is relevant news that can be related to the average person. Of that 10% relevant Average Joe news only the first paragraph is of interest and more likely than not political slants are applied, data is exaggerated/underrepresented, status quo agendas and biases are applied to such and such. I tell students to spend more time skimming and skipping articles than actually reading the paper. Trinidad is a small country and we have the benefit of getting together in small units and discussing what we heard/saw on the news and filtering what may be truth from what is bulls**t based on our own common sense, trusted sources, scuttlebutt and that beautiful grapevine that we have that has never failed us for centuries. And the beauty of our grapevine style of news is that it doesn't cost a dime in subscription. Just go out into your world and be friendly. You'd pick up on some news relavent to your existence in less than an hour. Just be sure to verify your information with various trusted sources. All hail scuttlebutt. All hail the grapevine.

Question: What is the worst thing you have seen a teacher do?
Answer: In Trinidad we have problems pronouncing our ‘th’s. If you are an English teacher it makes sense to speak the Queen's English eloquently or at least make an effort to pronounce your 'th’ in front of your class. That's not the case for Ms. Bentham. Or as she likes to call herself Ms. Bend-Tom. Ms. Bentham was recently informed that she had to present a video session of how she conducts her class. This was for credit towards her Diploma in Education or Dip-Ed as teachers like to call it here. Only with her Dip-Ed could she be promoted to a Teacher II. As such, Ms. Bentham was very high strung about recording the perfect classroom session. She stayed up all night creating a beautiful PowerPoint presentation full of animations, sound clips and videos. She got some excellent speakers borrowed to capture crisp sound and had another English teacher friend bring a video camera on a tripod to film her. She even went as far as giving the class 10% towards their final grade to simply 'behave themselves’ and ask/answer questions. She was very particular about the event the day filming was to begin. She wore her best wig and her polka dotted dress that revealed her shapely figure. She had a team of teacher friends guarding the door of the classroom to ensure no mischievous child outside sabotages her film by yelling inside or switching off the lights and running. Everything went according to plan. The PowerPoint was well done, the students were well behaved, the video was filmed without a hitch. All went to plan, all except for one thing: Ms. Bentham herself. She forgot that the whole point of English class is for students to speak and comprehend proper English. Something Ms. Bentham never practiced herself in her job and personal life. This was most prevalent in her Slothy the Sloth story, which she read in front the class to demonstrate descriptive writing. Here's how she told it: 'Slutty was a fat, tree hanging slut that lived in Brazil. Like most sluts she had long claws that looked like nails, a round head, long limbs and was covered in fur. She was laziest slut of all the sluts in South America. In fact the reason the word slut is synonymous with idleness is because of…’ Ms. Bentham stopped because some of the students were giggling. She looked up to see her English teacher friends staring at her in comic disbelief. However she didn't understand what was the problem. She barked at the students to keep quiet. One of the teachers gestured and mouthed softly, 'Say SLOTH… SLOTH’ Ms. Bentham thought that was the cue to go ahead. ‘……is because of the renowned laziness of Slutty the slut. Some would say that she had a wide stupid, smile and barely moved so that other animals would wonder if she were dead, but that's how most sluts behave… There was an uproar of laughter and Ms. Bentham again became confused, until finally the best student in her class rose and explained to her, 'Miss, they're laughing because you're pronouncing it wrong. It's SLOTH not SLUT. A sloth is an animal, a slut is a woman who has a lot of promiscuous sex.’ Ms. Bentham then had the crippling realization of the sheer embarrassment of her faux pas. Not only did she use the word ‘slut’ repeatedly in her presentation but she was corrected by her own student, and on film to boot. She felt humiliated and her anger was suddenly directed to the student whom she felt was purposely trying to embarass her. 'Candice, please pick up your belongings and go to the Principal's Office. I will not have you using such obscene language in my class.’ The students and even some of the teachers broke out in laughter. My all time vote for the worse thing I've ever seen a teacher do.

Question: Have you ever applauded an act of vigilante justice?
Answer: In our capital of Port of Spain we have a major homeless problem and it is advised that you don't give them any money. This story is an example of why. Some years ago there was a homeless man that would come in front of the bank pictured above and sit on the sidewalk. Question: What red flag did you have right before a job offer that you wish you had heeded?
Answer: 'You’re really taking the job at that branch. I heard Ms. Khan is gonna be the manager there!’ There was a frenzied murmur among all the fellow workers of the branch of Mario's pizzeria that I worked in 2020. Ms. Khan was the name that could evoke the strongest emotions of fear, disgust and anger among most frontline staff. Back in 2020 I was strapped for cash and needed an extra source of income to complete my home after COVID had put a hold on everything for an entire year. I worked six years doing pizza delivery prior to this and for the most part it was not the most pleasant experience, especially when it's your evening job and you work 14 hrs a days, 7 days a week. On my little rickety old motorcycle I had been knocked down by drunken motorists, drenched up to my underwear with rain, cursed and threatened by irate customers, robbed at gunpoint and escaped near death collisions more times than I can count on one hand. I left the profession in 2019 with no intention of returning. However that wonderful virus called COVID had me putting on that old red shirt and dusting the old helmet, feeling akin to George Foreman when he took another stab at boxing in his middle ages to pay off his debts. The only redeeming factor was a branch was going to be opened practically next door to where I lived. I wouldn't be stranded late at nights trying to get a taxi home like was the case before. Fast forward to my first day at work at the new branch next to my home. I'm introduced to the dreaded Ms. Khan. I see this lady with a soft, lusty voice, enigmatic brown eyes and huge boobs shake my hands. She looked only a few years older than me (34 at the time) and being a hot blooded, average Joe male I told myself she couldn't be all that bad. I couldn't be more wrong. I never saw someone conduct a meeting whereby they refused to hear any concerns staff had. She simply discussed what she wanted staff to do/not do and made obvious allusions as to who f**ked up for the month. I whispered to my fellow delivery driver that this wasn't a meeting, this was a briefing. With her eerily accentuated sense of hearing Ms. Khan heard me murmuring and angrily asked if I had any problems. I mentioned that I never saw a meeting conducted where staff wasn't allowed to express their concerns and I saw those enigmatic brown eyes stare at me as though I were the spawn of Satan. She ignored me and continued her meeting (briefing). From that moment on my relationship with Ms. Khan became tense to say the least. I observed that she had not the slightest concern to Industrial Law and the basic rights of workers and took advantage of the more naive workers to an almost sickening degree. I witnessed her telling a cashier who was about to finish shift that she couldn't leave because the other cashier couldn't make it. The cashier protested and said she had her two kids home with a babysitter who was leaving in a few minutes. Ms. Khan told her that if she leaved, consider her job gone. After Ms. Khan left I explained to that cashier that she could not be forced to work a double shift and Ms. Khan did not have the authority to fire and the company would dare not do as such under such conditions otherwise the company could have an ugly lawsuit on their hands. The cashier was grateful for my advice and left. Ms. Khan was the forced to take up her role as cashier for that evening. Ms. Khan got wind that I had advised the cashier her rights. From that moment on it became a cold war between Ms. Khan and myself. She became obsessed with my roster and if I came two minutes lates she etched bold red letters in the time book of my 'constant and unapologetic tardiness. ‘ She sent me home if my trousers had a spot of dirt on it, despite it being well known that motorcycle delivery riders always get their trousers dirty due to the nature of the job. Other drivers would perform their duty in filthy and worn trousers but none of that angered Ms. Khan than a tiny ink stain on my trousers. Ms. Khan was obsessed with sales targets. Sales targets gave her cash bonuses and everyone began to witness she had a tendency to employ dirty tactics to get customers to spend more money. These tactics employed fraud and dishonesty and several customers grew wise to it. Some of them began complaining to me about being cheated. Whenever I approached Ms. Khan about these complaints she dismissed me and accused me being the Devil's Advocate. However one fateful day one of these customers sent an angry email to the head office about the scheme and Ms. Khan's name was called. She flew into a fit of paranoia and began to accuse me trying to 'get the customers against’ her.’ She started gathering a bunch of her manager friends from other branches and (according to my fellow deliver drivers) she spread the rumour that I was a pompous chauvinist that didn't like to see women in charge. I got wind that she held meetings while I was at my day job, telling the (mostly female) staff that I was a dangerous defiant, possibly a spy for Pizza Hut and that I was racist, sexist (all the ‘ists in the dictionary) and didn't care if the women employed here lost their jobs. Sounds ridiculous but sadly when you have an organization of which 80% of the frontline staff barely have elementary education and are fearful of losing their bread and butter, such scare tactics actually do work. I was watched upon with suspicion as a dishonest rabble rouser who wanted the company to fail and who stood to lose nothing because I already had a day job. Suddenly everything I said was reported to the manager and every disagreement I had with fellow workers was blown out of proportion. Every time I gave basic legal advice to a stressed out single mother being taken advantage of, someone was in the background reporting my 'insubordination’ to Ms. Khan. Many times I was called to the head office to defend myself and remind them of my great work ethic and relationship with the customers, while Ms. Khan repeated 'insubordination’ and 'I feel uncomfortable with him ’ like an dull parrot. The atmosphere became so tense that when my contract came to an end and I was informed by the head office that it would not be renewed. I grew angry and wanted to take the matter up legally but then I realized it was a gift from God. My home was near finished. Working in that branch was making me constantly angry, shocked and disappointed at how easily people get themselves taken advantaged of and how people like Ms. Khan take advantage of others with no remorse. Nothings screams the decline of an organisation more than when taking advantage of customers become the norm and something only becomes illegal/unethical if you are caught. It's been over a year since I stopped working there and I've never been happier. I advise anyone going through similar problems in their workplace to make that great effort to get out of there. A toxic work environment WILL make you a toxic person. If you are able to make that effort to leave, do it right now. Believe me. It's not the end of the world and it's worth it.

Question: What was the first thing you saw, heard or discovered that made you feel old?
Answer: I was working as a delivery rider for Pizza Hut back in 2015. I was at a rather difficult stage in my life, strapped for cash, domestic problems and an admitted depleted sense of self worth. However I always prided myself on my youthful exuberance. I believed I could’ve pass for 23 even though I was a few months shy of 30. I stopped to deliver at a small grocery. It was late at night and I was fatigued having had to work a double shift. After I gave the guy the pizza he went to the back to get some change. I took a look around. A strange guy stood near me staring deeply into my eyes. He was a middle aged guy, looking rather bedraggled and underfed, dressed in an over-worn raincoat and a threadbare cap. There was a wry smile on his aloof face and I couldn’t help envision him a kindhearted simpleton who probably had a burgeoning drinking problem and a wife who bullied him at home, routinely dragging him out of the pub by his ear. There was nothing youthful about him. He looked to be in his early to mid 40s and looked like the kind of guy with a lot of regrets in life. Then I heard the voice of the customer returning. I saw that someone dressed and looking eerily similar to the customer was near the simpleton while the customer himself was in front of me at the exact same time. It then dawned upon me that I was looking at a mirror the whole time. It then dawned upon me that elder, kindhearted simpleton was me.

Question: What happened to your school bully?
Answer: He had a wonderful transformation. He did a complete 360 from being a LITTLE piece of s**t to a BIG piece of s**t. Back in school there was none more despised than Akeem. He was (still is) quite short (probably 5′6 at most) and dare I say, not one of the better looking boys in class. He deeply desired friends/attention and being that he was neither funny nor pleasant he realized that he could only make a name for himself by instilling fear. Being short, skinny and devoid of athleticism, he knew that he couldn’t cause physical damage to anyone. Instead, he developed a remarkable talent in calling classmates out on anything remotely embarrassing or hurtful about their lives. If you wore hand-me-down clothing… If your father had mental problems and periods of homelessness… If your mother had a gap in her teeth… If your family was on welfare… If you couldn’t afford to buy food in the cafeteria and relied on school feeding programs… If you depended on the free bus service to get home… you had to be sure to NEVER let Akeem get wind of that information because it would be guaranteed that he would make a public announcement of it. ‘Darcelle, you smell like that cheap Him n’ Her unisex deodorant. You don’t feel ashamed to be a female wearing cheap deodorant? How about everybody put up money to get Darcelle some decent deodorant for her birthday?’ ‘Look Elijah’s wearing the same shirt his brother wore to school yesterday.’ ‘Hey Benny. Maybe the principal could pick up your father at the gas station for the Parent-Teacher meeting. Isn’t that where he begs?’ That was his shtick. He would sit all day in class and pick a random person to taunt and reveal something dreadfully sad or embarrassing about their life that he carefully and methodically deduced or discovered through prying. Of course there were kids that he would dare not provoke, the ones who would knock out his teeth if he attempted rip on them. The rest of the class, practically had to avoid eye contact with him during a free period in fear that he say something nasty about their home, mother, father, siblings etc. This attitude of his continued for the duration of his school tenure. Fast forward twenty years later and I see that I’m being followed on Instagram by someone with whom I have a lot of mutual friends. Upon closer inspection I observe that it’s Akeem. I tell myself that maybe he’s trying to reach out to old classmates and show how much he’s changed into a better individual. I couldn't be more wrong. No. Akeem was more interested in showboating bling and lifestyle. He was simply networking, with a little showing off on the side. I looked for any photo that didn't scream 'Bet you never drove/been on/wore/visited this,’ a photo that demonstrated a more subtle side to him, and the most I could find was a photo of him sticking his tongue on his wife's face. But say what, everyone is responsible for his own destiny. According to his Instagram he rents luxury vehicles so lemme be the bigger man and plug his Instagram business/personal link for your enjoyment. You will see for yourself what a wonderful guy he grew up to be.

Question: How old are you and how do you feel about your age, aging, your future?
Answer: In a few months I’ll be 36. I already think of myself as someone who is 40. As with most people who answer this question life was a probably a bittersweet roller coaster ride. I think this is the age where you owe it yourself to exercise moderation in just about everything. I did nothing but work and study for my entire 20s. From age 30 till 35 I worked two jobs 7 days a week, mostly 14 hr work days. Because of this, my 20s and half of my 30s are mostly a blur. Now I’m at the age where I want to take it down a single notch and actually enjoy life. I’ve had my home built (partially, but livable) and my daughter is provided for even though the relationship with her mother has ended. But if you ask me about how I feel about this age at this particular stage in my life. I feel great. I feel relaxed. I feel accomplished. I'm definitely in a better place than I was in my 20s. If I could just put in wee bit of advice to 20-somethings out there: ‘Ask questions……many, many questions. Observe the answers. Test them. Observe what is reality/truth and what is just lip service/deceit.’ You’re on a question-asking platform so you’re already on the right track.

Question: What are the things no one tells you about living alone?
Answer: That it gradually transforms you into someone who WANTS to be alone. If you are like me and have just a drop of introvert blood in you, living alone becomes like an introvert blood transfusion. Or, as I like to call it, an introversion. When you're accustomed hanging out with groups of diverse friends, hearing about the different lifestyles , perceptions and life choices of others, not only does empathy and understanding come naturally but also a desire to empathize and understand people around you grows. If you don't do this regularly, you feel awkward and incomplete. It becomes a subconscious necessity the same way people who have a gym routine tend to always have to be at the gym otherwise they'll be in an awful mood. When you live with someone your mind gravitates towards the study and understanding of the person/persons living with you. Whether it be your spouse, children, sibling, in-law, friend, roommate etc, you naturally become preoccupied studying such an individual and the gears of human nature are in motion in that you become naturally interested in people as a whole. When you live alone, your mind becomes preoccupied with itself and your own interests, likes and dislikes, theories and experiences. Your ability to empathize lessens greatly and you find yourself easily irritated and avoiding people who do not share the same mindset as yours (practically the rest of the world). You've become so used to expending energy inwards that it becomes a Herculean effort to try and get to know others. You'd rather not pretend to be glad about Megan's new boyfriend (who sounds like a piece of s**t) or grudgingly compliment Billy on his decision to take his kids to Disneyland rather than pay off his arrears for the car or be pressured into attending the church cake sale when you're secretly an atheist. Living alone makes you that person who just doesn't want to make that effort to get to know the people around you. Getting to know people seems about as difficult and exhausting as someone with physique of Gandhi trying to do the workout of a prime Arnold Schwarzenegger. Unless you are a natural recluse, living alone is not a good idea for the reasons stated above. But hey that's just my two cents.

Question: What is the weirdest thing you've ever witnessed a parent do?
Answer: Neil was a troubled student in a school I worked in. Ms. Harris was his mom. In Trinidad we joke about the stereotypical ‘oppressed’ single mom who never sees wrong in her kids. The ones trying their best to raise their kids in a Government project, running out of the house delirious and screaming with curlers in their hair, desperately prostrating to the neighborhood to stop the awful policemen from arresting their innocent son who happened 'in the wrong place at the wrong time' during a robbery/breaking and entering. Ms.Harris was the textbook definition of such a mom; loyal to her children to the point of fanaticism and delusion. However, what set her apart from moms like her in the neighborhood was her gift for theatre. Ms. Harris could dish out so much pathos and could reach to the deep place inside her soul, channelling genuine emotions like the flick of a light switch. Those who didn't know any better would get easily influenced by her performances. She used this talent especially to bail Neil out of trouble. Once, Neil and a group of friends were to be expelled for selling marijuana on school premises. Before this was officiated, Ms. Harris came and gave an impromptu performance in the school staff room. ‘ ……go right ahead and tear the heart away from this poor, black woman. I have nothing. Neil has nothing. Only the love of struggling mother at wits end; a poor, black woman with no avenue in this world. Take my son and blind him so he cannot see the pain in his mother's face as we accept the fate of this cruel world; the fate of all poor, black women. As silly as her rhetoric was, she ended up getting her way and Neil and his friends had the matter covered up by the Principal and the police who witnessed this poor, black woman prostrating desperately towards them. One of the Literature teachers was so impressed that she approached Ms. Harris and told her that she belonged to a group that were looking for talent for the upcoming National 'Best Village’ competition sponsored by the Ministry of Culture. It was basically like a talent show with a focus on cultural dance, poetry, drama and spoken word. There were great prizes to be won and even if she didn't win, it would allow for great opportunities for her in local theatre. Ms. Harris agreed and immediately went and submitted an application for the audition. The event was scheduled the following month. Ms. Harris was dead set on giving the performance of a lifetime. She wanted the Minister of Culture to give her a standing ovation. She forgot all about Neil's problems at school to focus on her upcoming performance. She wrote an epic play that revolved around an oppressed woman who makes the journey to the motherland. There was to be a spoken word segment, a short play and end in a song and dance finale, complete with drums, dancers in exquisite costumes and professional lighting. However Ms. Harris bit off far too much than she could chew. Her obessesion with perfecting her vision of the performance led to many disputes with the dancers, sound effects, music and lighting personnel and nearing the date of the competition most of the crew quit and she was hard-pressed to find people to replace them. The day of the audition arrived and almost the entire neighborhood flocked to the Community Center to see Ms. Harris’ performance of a lifetime. Unbeknownst to Ms. Harris, the Minister of Culture was not going to be there, rather just a sole talent scout. There was no need for the amount of spectacle that Ms. Harris had in mind. When her moment came, she was nowhere to be found. Several people tried to contact her on her cell phone but she was not answering. Thirty minutes passed and the talent scout became furious as he had other locations to visit. Ms. Harris then materialized looking out of breath. En route to leaving she stopped the scout in his tracks to tell him that she was ready to perform but if only he could give herself and her dancers ten minutes to get their costumes ready and another ten minutes for the sound and lighting guys to arrive. The talent scout told her to perform now or she would be eliminated from the competition. Ms. Harris then began to prostrate in front of him saying: ‘How can you be so cold? How can you look at a poor, black woman and tell her that you are going to eliminate her? What has the world come to when a poor, black woman has a door shut in her face by a rich, black man? How can you? How can you?’ Needless to say the talent scout was not impressed by Ms. Harris' impromptu performance and had her eliminated. She learned the first lesson in Theatre 101 that day; don't overdo it

Question: What is the biggest lie society has taught you to believe?
Answer: The 'strategy’ that worked for your parents will work for you. In Trinidad we have two different generations with two different mindsets. For ease of understanding I will label them: Any colonial Trinidadian will tell you that the older generation was far different from the modern non colonial, many will argue that, in terms of morals, norms and values, the Colonial mindset was better. The Colonials were greatly influenced by British standards. The path to one's success was deemed to be how closely he/she can emulate an upper class English person. Great emphasis was placed on education, speech (or the ability to speak the Queen's tongue without the influence of corruptive local dialect) and there was manic obsession of gaining recognition by ruling agents of our English masters through social acceptance (a combination of race and etiquette played a big role), scholarship, sport (mainly cricket) and if all else fails, kissing your parents goodbye and hopping aboard the HMT Windrush to the seek opportunity in the land of the Queen. Colonial parents were obsessed with their children's grades. Education was seen as the only means of upward mobility for those who had no other means of gaining English recognition. All of life seemed to be based around this rigid structure of class. The non-Colonials had little to no influence from the British. Those born after 1962 were privy to witness a near chaotic transition to self Government. Speaking proper English and demonstrating a level 'class’ now bore little to no impact on social mobility. Education and good grades provided some measure of success in life but was far less impactful than under British rule. Success was a combination of personal capitalistic drive and being 'in the know’ of certain opportunities the Government provided or exploits to be exploited. The US rather than the UK was now the chief model of success. Most of the laws the British provided were still in place but everyone from the the beggar on the street to the highest titled Government official approached them in 'read between the lines’ or 'you're only guilty if you're caught manner.’ The system is less rigid, less Draconian from the past, allowing, for better measures of opportunity for all levels of society but at the same time it operates within an opportunitistic, 'do as the Romans do,’ style bordering on controlled anarchy. As a boy I was drilled into believing that the path to success is getting good grades, speaking good English, maintaining a proper image, obeying the law and respecting elders. Now if I were to impart such wisdom to an average boy of this generation I would be scoffed at, not just by the boy, but also by his parents.

Question: What corporate buzzword are you most tired of?
Answer: 'Moving forward…' If someone comes and blurts this meaningless phrase to me, my knuckles automatically begin to clench. I worked in a public office that was attempting to transition to 'meet the needs of the changing public’ (another buzzword that irks me). A new Director was appointed, younger, fresher and with a more hands-on (another stupid buzzword) approach to Joe Public (another). She went about various branches with her assistants (who were large and looked like bodyguards) and would give these windy orations that demanded a lot of clapping, high-fiving, with the general theme of moving forward being inserted every few minutes. She did not elaborate what she meant by moving forward but everyone was supposed to act as though they understood. When someone like myself or other confused workers brought up pressing issues, she would speak in parables and end with a hand gesture and utterance of moving forward. Stalled salary negotiations……moving forward. Misappropriated funding…..moving foward. Nepotism/promotion of others without experience and qualification……moving forward. Maintenance issues/workplace hazards…..moving forward. ‘Anymore questions?……..So let's move forward. If we remember our company vision, not necessarily our mission…'’ Only after a few months of working with her did I understand the significance of her constant utterance of moving forward: Reasons as such are why I hate such corporate buzzwords. They usually end up being a smarmy way to get majority approval for your wrong doing and benefit from not being held accountable due to ambiguity. When you mask your intentions with buzzwords like moving forward, how are you any different from the people who used buzzwords like 'The Final Solution’ and 'Year Zero'?

Question: What was your cringiest moment with a boss?
Answer: Ms. B was a former supervisor of mine in a Government building I worked. She was a lady in her early 50’s. She was a nice person but was an eccentric and an introvert to the core. When things were slow she would stay isolated in her office, playing chess online or taking a nap. When she came out of her office her only conversation would usually be short, irritable grumbles about random stuff that annoyed her about the job and the typical ‘can’t wait for the weekend/payday’ talk. Then she would return to her idle privacy. Mary, a co-worker of mine, observing that our supervisor had so much free time on her hands, decided to enroll in an online course. Mary thought it fair she perform her duties during the morning and after lunch work on her online studies. Ms. B began observing this and one day, while stepping out to grab lunch, made a snide comment towards Mary’s direction: ‘Lunch break is just an hour. I don’t want to report people who like to come to work and do their own thing.’ Ms. B’s grumble was directed towards Mary but in a most blunt and condescending manner. Mary, being a woman of passion, could not take such a hypocritical statement without taking some kind of action. For days, she plotted on how she would give Ms. B a piece of her mind; how dare she? Ms. B who does practically nothing, making accusations of others doing as such. They say it’s only thieves who are always paranoid that everyone wants to steal from them. Such and such was the rantings of Mary for that evening. The day Mary decided she was going to confront Ms. B about the statement, something strange happened. Ms. B, in a seemingly good mood, had come out of her office and was helping visitors and getting involved in the day to day operations of junior staff like myself and Mary. Then Mary observed something that made a Cheshire grin spread across her face. ‘Elijah,’ she said, ‘Look at Ms. B’s pants.’ I looked. Ms. B was wearing a beige colored work-pants. Nothing seemed out of the ordinary until I observed that there was a wet, red spot observable from the back, around the crotch area. I stared aghast. Ms. B didn’t seem to notice her period came down on her and clearly had no protection against such an event. She must’ve assumed that her menopause came to an end and periods were now a thing of the past for her. Some of the people she was dealing with seemed to have observed her predicament also but looked as though they felt too awkward to say anything about it. I looked at Mary and said, ‘We should tell her about it.’ ‘No,’ Mary replied, ‘Not right now.’ Mary waited until the very last visitor left the building and the usual evening lull began. Ms. B went into her office and closed the door. I watched as Mary went up to the door, knocked and entered. ~~~~~~~~~~~ Ten minutes later Ms. B, with all her belongings on her, sped past me while uttering, ‘I have to deal with a matter.’ She hastily left the building. Mary told me that when she explained the situation to Ms. B, the look that came upon Ms. B’s face was nothing short of the deepest dread and horror. That for a second she wore the facial expression of a convict at the gallows. I could not help but empathize with the level of cringe Ms. B must've felt on her way back home. Mary got her poetic justice. If she were really mean she could’ve spread the word about the incident through the entire building but the slight torture was enough. Mary and Ms. B began to develop a meaningful relationship after the incident. In other words they started to scratch each other’s back. Maybe it was some sort of neurotic subconscious agreement they both made, as in reminding each other ‘You got me covered right?’ Maybe the situation gave Ms. B a slice of humble pie? I don’t know. What I do know is that to this day I don’t understand women.

Question: If you could choose only one font which one would it be and why?
Answer: Without a doubt Gill Sans. Something about these World War II era fonts stirs up romantic and escapist feelings within my subconscious. From these ugly times came this beautiful, almost flawless font. I’m no anglophile but the British (specifically Eric Gill employed at the prestigious Monotone company) knew a thing or two about subtlety, graceful curvature and ‘breathing space’ when it came to eye-catching typefaces. Symmetry is the essence of being and Gill Sans makes every effort to be symmetrical yet bold and demanding. It is referred to as a ‘humanist’ font, in that it is easily legible in text and display to the extent that lines do not overlap or meld into each other. Intricate focus is put on the roundness of its letters, most notably, having a perfect circle for the ‘O’ Gill Sans, to me, conjures up images of RAF fighter planes heading eastwards in formation, Orwell interviewing coal miners at their last breath due to tuberculosis, children in rags catching colored butterflies amidst the rubble of buildings blown to pieces in Dresden and the decay of British Raj. Terrible times indeed but captured in various newspapers, flyers and magazines with this pleasant font which made many nations feel hope for better times to come.

Question: What is the best album with the worst album cover?
Answer: There are so many great albums out there with terrible album covers that I can’t commit to just listing one. Sorry. If you want to seem like an intellectual hipster who is aware of global issues, look no further than Manic Street Preachers - Everything Must Go. A stunning album that perfect encapsulates that mid-late 90’s arena rock vibe. The album is epic in its scope and profound in its heavy subject matter: loneliness, international crises, suicide, class struggle etc. It was such an underwhelming experience to see the cover as nothing more than three passport photos pasted on a design that looked like a Microsoft Paint project. MGMT - Congratulations (2010) What a great album. MGMT’s music takes you back to the heights of psychedelic pop and prog-rock of the late 60s and 70s. Siberian Breaks is a 12 minute modern day masterpiece. This is one of the generic and unpleasant album covers I’ve ever come across in recent history. The band members are weird and their music videos are beyond bizarre but this artwork looks like some cut and paste crap done by a stoner wannabe with no talent. What is it about the late 80s and early 90s that excessively loud and garish was the aesthetic for everything. Of these three funk metal bands I’d go with Faith No More - The Real Thing by a long shot. But what is that on the album cover? A fire-breathing clam? An oil baron’s mind after taking LSD? God alone knows. Jeff Buckley - Grace If there’s one thing that prevents me from buying/listening to an album, it’s when the album shows the artist’s pretty face trying to look all deep. I would’ve passed this album straight in a record store and assume it’s another one of Josh Groban’s senior-citizen friendly collection of soul covers. I would’ve never guessed the album to be the greatest debut album in the history of rock music. But what’s wrong with this album cover? Black Sabbath’s debut actually has a really good album cover, if not one of the greatest. I put it there to compare with Black Sabbath’s second album’s cover. Both albums were made in 1970. However Paranoid was recorded four months after Black Sabbath to capitalize on the growing popularity. The cover speaks for itself in all honesty. AND THE AWARD FOR THE GREATEST BAND WITH THE WORST ALBUM COVERS GOES TO . . . . . It’s a tie between Pantera and The Grateful Dead Garish, corny, ugly, sleazy are just a few of the adjectives I can think of whenever I see an album from either critically acclaimed bands. Pantera’s covers opt to be as stupidly macho as possible (on a budget) whilst Grateful Dead seem to look for the cheesiest of cheese. But never judge a book (or album) by it’s cover. All the above albums are worth a listen.

Question: What do you think of as “cool”? What makes somebody “cool” to you?
Answer: If someone excels in certain personality traits that I lack in, that person seems extremely cool to me. Persistence, confidence, courage, grace, style are all common traits that people unanimously consider ‘cool.’ However many people simply attribute being cool to just having a certain look or image. There are ‘cool’ factors that appeal to the greater population but not necessarily to me. Modern fashion sense, meticulous grooming, tattoos etc looks cool on the surface to most people, it does to me also, but that does not make a person cool to me. A guy like this (James Arthur) would make a lot of quality women swoon, several men also. He would be seen as the beacon of ‘cool’ to a lot of people around him. But when I see someone walking the streets like that, the last thing I think is, ‘Wow. That guy is so cool. I wanna be like that guy.’ What I think is, ‘Wow. That guy probably has to pay a mortgage just to keep up daily appearances’ or ‘Wow. That guy would probably have a heart attack if pigeon shit lands on his head.’ Guys like that look cool but aren’t so cool to me. Anybody can pay to look good. It’s not impressive, it’s not cool. Instead Take a look at Enrique Iglesias. His balding scalp covered with a baseball cap, ordinary fitted cotton T shirt with a regular denim jeans and a chain securing his wallet. No tattoos (except for D.I.M. aka ‘Do it for Mom' on his wrist), no manicures, no $100 haircuts and clearly healthy and fit. It takes major cojones to impress thousands of adoring fans on stage dressed like a guy going to buy groceries. Enrique is one of the most handsome, revered and wealthy men in the entertainment world yet goes about like an ordinary guy. He has been with the same woman for over twenty years, avoids tabloids and limelight and doesn't try too hard. That to me is extremely cool. Also This is Hugh Hefner. He was flanked by sexy women in almost all his photos. The quintessential playboy obtained the life of many a man’s deepest fantasy; a life of wealth, fame and sex rather than of family. Sex with a physically stunning woman, for him, was easier to source than good tobacco. He is seen as the epitome of 20th century hedonism, spending his remaining years dressed like a clown and vigorously researching effective methods of octogenarian penile erections. Thirsty men and gold diggers around the world would find him the image of cool. Hugh Hefner imho, was not ‘cool.’ Instead Charlton Heston, who could pass for Hefner’s big brother, lived almost the opposite life. He remained married to his wife for 64 years until his death in 2008. While Hefner was paying high school dropouts to be photographed naked, Heston championed Civil Rights and opposed the war in Vietnam. Heston’s confidence, booming voice and commanding figure would capture everyone’s attention. He was not a great looker but Heston had such a charisma of which you would follow him into battle. Hefner had the charisma of a soggy old sock or a deflating balloon when put beside a man of Heston’s stature. All in all, the lesson learned here is ‘coolness’ to me is based on your personality and your actions rather than your ‘look’ and image.

Question: What was the best era of your life?
Answer: I had a happy childhood. My best era had to be the mid 90s to early 00s. My brother and I were introduced to cable television which my mother wisely subscribed to to distract us from the negative influence of the local boys from the Government projects we grew up in. It’s a good thing she did because one of those boys got killed involved in gang related activities while the other two are in jail. Though my brother and I would stare at the tube sometimes sixteen hours a day (during holidays) we were still far more active than today’s generation as we would go bicycling, exploring, kite-flying, football and sometimes cricket. Chasing and catching butterflies was still fashionable. Also catching crickets, grasshoppers and if you were lucky you would catch a praying mantis and put it to fight someone’s champion mantis. The poor creature would be lucky to be alive when is was time for the fight. I mastered grabbing fat toads and launching them into the sky to the delight of the boys around me. I never understood why even the toughest of boys were afraid to do this and was proud of my skill, until I learned why: frog piss. Saturdays were magical because of the deluge of quality cartoons, especially if you had cable. Once a cartoon had karate, missiles, endless shooting, things that transformed, people that kept getting more and more powerful, magic, snot, naked butts, muscles, sexual innuendo, school-related humour or based on a video game you bet your bottom dollar my brother and I watched it. Some of the worst pseudo-macho, dumb-kid cartoons in history were made in the 90s: However there were still lulls of boredom every here and there. This changed with the introduction of the first Playstation. You had to make friends with kids in your school that you didn’t necessarily like so much once word got out he/she had a Playstation because now you could trade games with that person. As the 90s came to an end, puberty came galloping on a horse to demand that I turn off the TV and Playstation and start focusing on the fairer sex. Luckily my cousin David migrated from Scotland to Trinidad and with his cash and my brother’s street smarts, we undertook several missions to get laid through clubbing, playing pool in trendy bars, religiously attending house parties, providing/consuming liquor etc. All of these missions failed miserably but we had fun anyway. Thus our lives revolved around making plans to get laid, failing, dusting our shoulders and enjoying each other’s company watching TV, playing video games, fishing or just plain old hanging out. Then David got his first girlfriend, was stricken with the worst case of ‘whipped’ and that awful scourge of puberty turned us all into taller, deep-voiced, acne riddled young men of differing mindsets and we gradually began to drift away from each other with this awful phenomenon called ‘discovering our identity.’ Now we are three completely different human beings with vastly different goals and perspectives in life. We respect each other, love each other and most of the time enjoy each others’ company but far gone are the days where we were a unit. I do yearn for those days but c’est la vie.
