Question: What is the shadiest industry you've worked in?
Answer: In 2009 right after the whole world was reeling from the AIG insurance scandal, I decided now was a good time to quit my job and and follow the lucrative career of an insurance salesman. What happened was Jason, an old school friend, told me that while attending University, he was selling life insurance policies at his leisure. He told me he made enough money (commissions) in just a couple of months that he was able purchase a car. He also rubbed in the fact that he could afford to purchase decent clothes and go out for a night-life whenever he felt like it. I would be lying if I said I didn’t envy him. The ripple effects of the 2008 recession took a while to impact Trinidad and suddenly our insurance firms were affected, most notably CLICO which had to be bailed out by the Government. ‘You sure selling insurance is a good idea now? With CLICO and all?’ I asked him. ‘Yeah,’ he said. I was convinced. I immediately quit my job and applied to work in the same insurance company and branch that Jason was employed in. Literally, the very same day I started training was the day Jason quit. As I walked in the door he had already collected his belongings and was walking out. ‘Hey bro what’s up?’ I said concernedly, ‘You leaving?’ ‘Just for a little while,’ he replied, ‘I just have a few credits until I graduate. I need to focus on my studies.’ He then left. I was confused. Didn’t he tell me insurance selling was very flexible in regards to his University studies? I tried not to let that bother me and ignore the looming sense of dread that I made a huge mistake quitting my permanent job to go sell insurance on commission in the midst of a global recession and countless insurance scandals. The seasoned insurance salespeople were all warm and friendly. Half of them queried as to whether I had life insurance. A few of them tried (semi-jokingly) to sell me life insurance right then and there. The branch was named after the lead insurance salesman i.e. branch manager, Cecil. He did the training sessions. He was a short, squat middle-aged man with a comical demeanor who loved to include fart jokes in everything he said. He excited us trainees by telling us that if we sold enough policies we could live off the commissions like him. He said he made enough commissions that he didn’t need to sell policies anymore. That all his clients’ premiums (insurance payments) were paying him enough to live comfortably and he was here for fun. I wondered how that was possible. Wasn’t the commissions a one-off thing? It’s not like the insurance salesman gets money every time the insured person pays his premium. ‘Yes!’ the branch manager responded excitedly, ‘You get paid every time your client pays his insurance. A small percentage of each payment goes to us.That’s why I tell my clients when they buy a policy from me, I’m now part of their family……because their payments literally make me part of their family. When daddy goes and pay his premium and buys a new pair of shoes for sonnyboy, Uncle Cecil gets money to buy a new pair of shoes also.’ All the sales agents began to laugh at this. I was then taught the basic tools of selling life insurance policies. And much more. After the training all the newbies were teamed up with a senior agent and left to go find prospects. My coach, Stephen, told me that all insurance agents have their niches. Cecil was good with churchy type families, Lara, the sole female agent was good with police officers and defense force type men and he himself was good with salt of the earth type men i.e. taxi drivers, construction workers, tradesmen etc with security guards being his specialty. He said because his niche weren’t very reliable in regards to being consistent in paying their premiums, that he was one of the lowest performing agents. Stephen’s technique was basically to visit rolling-stone type men who were delinquent with child-support and bully them into ‘at least taking out a policy for the sake of your children.’ After a week I finally got a policy sold. I had the paperwork to file for my first client. Stephen told me to put it in the pile with the others. He directed me to a vacant office where I saw boxes upon boxes of insurances policies pending to be filed and entered into the database. ‘Who’s going to file all those?’ I asked. ‘The girl left the job two months ago,’ he replied, ‘When we get a new girl she has her work cut out for her.’ ‘So my client’s policy…’ I said concernedly, ‘All of these policies aren’t filed yet?’ ‘No,’ he replied. ‘What if something happens to my client like right now? What if she gets in a freak accident today? Her name isn’t even on the database...’ Stephen paused for a minute and then said, ‘There are some things you just shouldn’t worry about in this organization.’ Needless to say my stint in that particular insurance organization ended a few days later.

Question: How do you pretend to be poor even though you are not?
Answer: The poverty culture in Trinidad is different to the rest of the Western world in many aspects but in many aspects it is quite the same. If you are well-off but want to pretend that you are poor in my country (which is actually a good idea) there are several tricks of the trade you MUST adhere to. Learn the subtle art of shutting up. If you are poor you’re not supposed to have the energy to be outspoken about your interests, dreams, ideals etc. Poor people conversation is full of profound silences, minute observations and reflections of good times gone by. Idealism has no place in the conversation among a group of poor, working class Trinidadians. Stifle that urge to discuss art, complex political theory, technology, flora and fauna, science and your Utopian ideals. Deactivate. Never, at any given time, should you utter the following words/phrases while conversing with the average poor person: ethical farming, gourmet foods, non-profit organisations, recycling, 100% cotton, whole grain, organic, fair trade, energy-saving, environmentally friendly, catch and release fishing, walk-in closet, petitioning, neutering, charity of your choice, frequent flyer, volunteering, free range chickens, going green, pet insurance, shoe rack, wine rack, brunch, fuel economy. I'm not stereotyping. Poorer Trinis spend the majority of their days thinking about survival and activities associated with eradicating boredom. The above topics are usually associated with the Trinidadian upper classes. Just a mention of any such word/phrase and your poverty disguise comes into question. Let it be. Poor people quirks are shockingly different from non-poor people quirks. The more shocked and concerned you appear upon discovering quirks of your fellow less fortunate, the less genuine you seem as a poor person. Non-poor person quirk ‘Susan sure is quirky. I invited her over to lunch again. She always repeats her questions and gives a nervous laugh whenever I answer her. Plus she always rinses over my washed dishes for some reason.’ Poor person quirk ‘Jimmy sure is a character. He just killed his rooster because he said it has eyes like Hitler and now he’s out back digging a tunnel for God knows what. I wonder if he could loan me a pack of cigarettes.’ Unless a poor person’s behavior affects his family and neighbours in a negative manner, his peers simply let it be. Do not try to understand the logic in your fellow poor people’s behaviour and actions. Do not try to attempt any psychological evaluation. Do not try to lecture Billy on the dangers of gambling. Do not try to couple counsel Fred and Martha who always have a vicious fight after having sex on Sundays. Don’t try to convince Bruno that World War 3 hasn’t already begun and that it’s not taking place online. Just let it be. Embrace Fridays. There is something about Friday evenings that is almost sanctimonious with poorer working class Trini males. Regardless if there isn’t a cent in his pocket, regardless if the bank or creditors are hunting for his head, he has to ‘live’ and Friday evenings are his time to do it. If binge watching Netflix is your idea of spending your Friday evening in a working class neighborhood, everyone around you will regard you with Cold War level suspicion. Go outside and ‘lime’ (hang out), play a game of All-Fours (cards), drink or simply take a chance at the Lotto (National Lottery). Make sure and wear your best ‘liming’ clothes. You will be accepted in no time. Learn to talk the talk. Get acquainted with all the best working class quotes, parables and quips e.g. ‘It is what is,’ ‘It was his/her time,’ ‘When the cat’s away the mice begin to play.’ Every poor person uses them. Every poor person cherishes them. Learn when to use them. If you keep spewing quotes and parables every time you open your mouth you’ll be looked upon as brain damaged, or trying too hard. Here are some famous Trini working class quotes, quips and parables: ‘Yuh done know.’ (You got it) ‘He not easy.’ (He’s an asshole) ‘Monkey know which tree to climb.’ (Opportunists know who to target) ‘Wha’ yuh go do?’ (Such is life) ‘Don’t be an imps.’ (Stand up for yourself) Learn them well and observe when and how to use them. You’ll be respected and loved in no time. Here are some helpful (but optional) bits of advice to complete the disguise: Have one expensive pair of shoes that you cherish and take great care of. Wear it on Fridays. Do not leave the beach until the sun is completely gone. Never refuse charity or offerings. Even if you don’t need it. Always have that one big regret in your life. Be vocal about it among peers. NEVER buy new tires for your car. NEVER buy brand-name dog-food. Always borrow something from your neighbour and have him/her have to ask you back for it. Always be aware of what numbers played in the lottery. Never throw away clothes. Act as though you know nothing about online shopping, smart devices and ‘the Internet’ in general. Always be able to recognize if a stranger enters the neighbourhood. Memorize the vehicle model and license plate of his vehicle. Be friendly to but wary of that stranger. With all these factors in place your transformation will be complete. WE WELCOME YOU

Question: What’s a typical “masculine” thing you do not want/like to do?
Answer: There are many ‘masculine’ things I don't like or not appreciate as much as other men due to ineptitude. Libations We call this 'a toast to the fallen soldiers’ in Trinidad. This is a macho habit of pouring some of your premium liquor on the floor after you just opened a new bottle in reverence of friends and acquaintances who passed away. I think it's stupid. What if your 'fallen soldiers’ didn't drink? What if alcohol caused their death in the first place? It's not as common here as it used to be but whenever you’re with a group of friends there's always that one salty hermit who proposes that you throw some of your Johnny Walker Blue or Glenlivet 18 yr on the floor in toast of 'his fallen warriors.’ It's funny how the guys who ask for these type toasts are the one who never bring a bottle themselves. A Round of Drinks for Everyone Or 'buying a rounds’ as we call it in Trinidad. When you go to a bar with your friends everyone takes a turn in buying a round of drinks (usually beers) for all members in the group. I'm not cheap it's just that this is one of the worst demonstrations of economic inefficiency and inequity in the world. Firstly, you start of with a small group, usually about five of you. The first guy to buy a round gets off the hook with just having to buy about five beers. Then, before you know it, a friend of a friend comes in, then someone's uncle, then some guy someone knows from way back when, then the cheap, sneaky brown-nose at work and before you know it, you have to buy a round for your friends and all these people you don't know (and in some cases, don’t like). Many of these un-invitees ‘just happen to be passing through’ and never fulfill their duty to buy a round themselves. They drink their free beer and flee, taking advantage of the intoxicated group. It's ridiculous. Another reason buying rounds is a waste is cold beer gets lukewarm in a short space of time. Many times I would be drinking a beer and forced to discard the lukewarm ones because the other beers are coming in so fast. The round of drinks culture needs a modern day revamping. Under the hood chit-chat I'm no mechanic. But even if I were mechanically inclined I'm always dumbfounded to see men gather round staring at their car engines and discussing what modifications they had done, the hell they went through building a bracket to install such and such new engine, V8 versus Rotary, CA18det vs SR20de, NOS vs Turbo, carburetor vs fuel injected etc etc. The amount of time some guys spend on discussing the transformation of their piece o junk Sunnys, Lancers and Familias (their ‘beast’ as they like to call them) is astonishing for me. Even non-gearheads who just got their first vehicle get carried away with under the hood chit-chat even though they have no idea what their peers are talking about. Unless I’m getting good car maintenance/repair advice, under the hood chit-chat bores me. Team/Player/Club Fanaticism (Football) ‘Watch the rest of the World Cup? Are you crazy? Brazil just got massacred. Luiz and Neymar are still (sob) in tears. Go away!’ ‘How the hell can you support both Real Madrid and Barcelona? Bandwagonist!’ ‘I bet you $500 Messi has a bigger penis than Ronaldo.’ ‘Pele is God. Balotelli is Jesus.’ ‘Zidane has the IQ of a caveman. Keep Deschamps.’ And so on. Football fanatics take pride in making such ridiculous statements like a badge of honour. The more outlandish and provocative your statement regarding whatever popular team, player or club, the more psychopathic your obsession is the more warmly fellow football fanatics would accept you as one of theirs. It’s a good idea to befriend them though. Football fanatics are exceedingly loyal and generous to their fellow fanboys. ‘Look at my big bad dog.’ It’s always been a mystery to me why some of my fellow men have an almost cult like worship of possessing the biggest, baddest dog in the neighborhood. Some men are more proud and dedicated to their mean pitbulls, rottweilers, mastiffs and dobermans than they are of their own children. Putting up that ‘Beware of Dog’ sign is almost an orgasmic experience for them. They gather together in groups to discuss unique ways of maltreating these dogs (training they call it) to make them as mean as possible. They almost always do this stupid prank where they approach you with their dog on a leash and tell you that it’s ok to pet it. When you attempt to, their dogs snaps viciously towards your hand and the owners raise their heads in laughter and pride. Many of them end up getting mauled by their own mistreated dogs. And finally My most detested ‘macho’ thing of all time…. ‘Bro’ talk For centuries, being well-spoken, cultured and organized in thoughts and words is seen as weird, effeminate, pompous and pretentious to so-called macho men. In Trinidad, the larger the group of men, the more dumbed down the conversation. Emoting is a no-no. Using words that have more than three syllables is a no-no. Soliloquizing is a big no-no. ‘Macho’ men always repeat ‘you understand, you understand’ but nobody really understands what they’re saying. Think about the youths.’ Or try telling a macho man about your compounding personal problems/crisis: ‘That’s how it is……..it not easy………you understand?’ Or discussing the Machiavellian undertones in the Prime Minister’s new campaign speech. ‘Wha’ da f**k you smoke?’ If there is one thing I definitely wish to see change in the macho ideals is an ideal towards articulation of thoughts and efficient communication. You understand?

Question: What is the most obnoxious type of student for a teacher?
Answer: I'm not a teacher, but my job requires teaching random subjects to the younger students for a single period a day. In my many years of doing this I've always noticed a trend. Let's pretend this is a class clown. He (let's be honest, most of the time it's a boy) has self esteem issues and believes that the only way his peers can recognize his existence is by drawing attention to himself by disrupting the class with jokes, pranks or just acting as stupid as humanly possible. The class clown is NOT the most obnoxious type of student. These are the students who always laugh at and encourage the class clown, regardless of how unfunny/disruptive his performance. These are the fake audience. They are by far the most obnoxious students in a class. In my experience class clowns tend to go through a phase. Most of them grow out of their clownish behaviours as they get older and many of them actually prove themselves to be thoughtful, intelligent and caring. The fake audience (which usually comprises under 5 students) are the one who are real disruptors of the class. They are the ones who are truly inconsiderate and disrespectful. They usually have a consistently bad attitude. They manipulate the class clown to disrupt the class by providing an audience. This allows for them to channel their defiance and disrespect towards you by using a hapless class clown surrogate. When the giggles have ended and the majority of the class have decided to get serious, the fake audience will urge Mr. Clown to continue his antics. Regardless of how unfunny and irritating the clown's later performance is, they hold their bellies in false laughter in a effort to give rise to anarchy and poor Mr. Clown is held fully responsible and gets in serious trouble. The sad fact is the fake audience, in many cases, do not even like the class clown and have nothing to do with him outside of class. My trick for dealing with class clown disruptions is that I totally ignore him. Instead I concentrate on spotting the fake audience members who are egging him on. I then point them out and bring them to the front of the class, letting them know that they are in trouble for disrupting the class and will be taken to the Principal or Safety Officer's office. Like clockwork this action usually follows. The highlighted fake audience becomes enraged and demonstrate overwhelming disrespect, arguing with me that the class clown is the one who disrupted the class and they are innocent. In a short period of time they reveal themselves for who they are by speaking ill against the clown, they start passionately arguing their rights, some go as far as making threats, some walk out of the class and some point the blame at one another. All in all they reveal themselves to the class (and the class clown) what disrespectful, manipulative, conceited and resentful little creatures they are. Works every time. Edit 5.05.22. Click here to see where fate has led him.

Question: Do you sympathize with school teachers?
Answer: When it comes to the teacher with a heart of gold, the teacher who challenges the status quo. The teacher that puts his/her students’ education and development above all else. The teacher that takes pride in his/her work and lives to contribute to our future generation. The teachers that inspired Robin Williams’ characters in Dead Poets Society and Good Will Hunting. When it comes to these teachers (and they do exist) I would say yes. A loud and resounding YES. Unfortunately, in Trinidad many of our teenaged youth may never encounter such a teacher. I have worked in various secondary (high) schools for over ten years and I, and many other like me, would agree that the teaching service has become a swamp over the last twenty years. The work ethic of the modern day teacher is usually corrupt at worst, mediocre at best. Good teachers are stifled and bullied by cliques of bad teachers. Our teachers’ Union has become such a big hairy monster that they wield near absolute political power over the Government. Only in Trinidad teachers can complain that mandating the COVID vaccine for them is against their human rights yet at the same time complain that they are not teaching unless all students are vaccinated. A unionized teacher being fired in Trinidad?…..that’s almost unheard of. A teacher literally has to kill (a student) before he/she is to be considered for termination. We have teachers here who could cite all labour laws relevant to them to a T but have no idea what their new syllabus is about. We have teachers who scream ‘Asbestos’ when a drop of dust touches their shoulder. We have teachers who fall to the ground screaming about violation of COVID social distancing protocols in schools and fight to ensure no students come near them yet such teachers can be found shopping at the nearby crowded public market during lunch hour. We had teachers who argued about getting wage increases during the pandemic and that they had to spend what little money they earned to purchase laptops and tablets to facilitate online teaching. ‘We want compensation. Our salary is too small.’ Meanwhile almost half of the working population was out of a job, while the average teacher earns approximately five figures. To answer the question, honestly, Yes I sympathize with a lot of the hardships teachers encounter on a daily basis but ever since this pandemic, it’s becoming harder and harder to do it. Yeah. I'm pretty sure she is suffering from a lack of groceries.

Question: What is the stupidest assumption you ever made?
Answer: Several years ago I worked as a warehouse attendant for a major distribution company. It was my first job. Every year, usually in September, we had our annual stock-taking exercise. It was bittersweet because though it was hard work (especially for the males who did all the climbing and counting every single product in the warehouse whilst females wrote figures on the notepad) there would usually be a lot of the beautiful Head Office women present and we would be treated to lunch by the Director. We were all randomly assigned one partner. On our notice board they would put the name of our randomly allocated mystery partner. Of course many of the virile and single young men like myself hoped and prayed to be partnered with a stunning beauty from the Head Office. When the list was put up I saw that my partner was ‘Vanessa Milan.’ I jumped high into the air in excitement. VANESSA MILAN What a name! I envisioned a tanned beauty from a Mediterranean island, tall and shapely with arched eyebrows, a sensuous mouth and curly jet, black hair. In other words I imagined a Sophia Loren look-alike. I began bragging to my male friends that Vanessa Milan and I would probably be secretly in each others arms embracing behind a pallet of goods whilst they would be walking on eggshells with their nagging, old-maid partners. Every time I mentioned Vanessa Milan’s name I said it in a low whisper as though she were the Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I drove my co-workers crazy uttering her exotic name every day. ‘Vanessa Milan’ I laughed at some of the names my friends were paired with: ‘Penny Thomas….Ha…..That sounds like a big, fat mama.’ ‘Giselle Aleong….she sounds like a bony psycho.’ And comments to that extent (I was 19 years old). One of my friends Rory advised me that I was a fool. That nothing could be more stupid than guessing what someone is like based on their name. I replied, ‘True, But a name like Vanessa Milan has to be an exotic beauty. Who ever heard a name like Vanessa Milan in this country?’ When the day came for the stock-take, all of us guys stood in the open area of the warehouse and observed a wide array of beauties from the Head Office. The Director gathered us all together for a prayer and then called out the names of the allocated partners for us to team up. Penny Thomas was a straight up knock-out. Giselle Aleong, with a body like that, could’ve graced the cover of Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Edition. I looked stunned as she walked by with my friend Rory (her assigned partner) who had warned me about my assumptions. He looked at me with a faint, mocking smile. When Vanessa Milan’s name was called, (the Director blasphemously screeched her name in her guttural voice) no one answered. All my friends stared at me as they were in great suspense to finally see this exotic mystery woman I boasted about all week. Suddenly, a dumpy, middle-aged lady with bad posture and Coke bottle specs that made her look like someone’s mom from the 60’s came hurriedly into the clearing. ‘I’m here. I’m here,’ she cried in a mournful voice. I was taken aback. Sophia Loren she wasn’t. She looked and acted more like Pat from the It’s Pat SNL sketch. Awkwardly I shook hands with her and stared at the ground. She began to relate a woeful tale of how she wasn’t feeling well that morning and was running late as she sped up the road driving but had forgotten to feed her dog so she had to drive back home and that was why she was late and on and on and on she went relating woeful, semi-depressing tales for me while we were doing our stock checks. ‘One hundred and seventy five cases of Diquez Baby Oil 125ml!’ I shouted down at her from a pallet of goods on the shelf above her, ‘Did you get that?’ ‘Oh sorry,’ she said, ‘I can’t hear you. I have bad hearing in my right ear. Ever since I was…..’ ‘ONE-SEVEN-FIVE CASES……DIQUEZ BABY OIL…….125ML, ‘ I shouted at the top of my lungs. This was the third time in thirty minutes this type of communication problem happened and I was getting frustrated. Part of it was my selfish and immature disappointment at her not being the beauty I imagined but alas she was so whiny and helpless. ‘I can’t hear you.’ she replied woefully, ‘I think we should go ask the Director if the Manager has any walky-talkies around.’ ‘WE DON’T HAVE ANY WALKY-TALKIES IN THE WAREHOUSE,’ I screamed at her but she already left to find the Director while I stood suspended 30 feet above the ground on a shelf waiting on her. In the end I had to count the stock and write in the figures myself as she followed me about apologizing at every turn. After the momentous day passed, for weeks my friends and co-workers would tease me. They would breathlessly whisper her name whenever I passed. ‘Vanessa Milan. Mi amore. Mi amore.’ Thus ended the saga of Vanessa Milan, My Latin Goddess of Forbidden Love.

Question: Have you ever realized that you were wrong about someone?
Answer: I once worked part-time transporting furniture for a small Mom n Pop furniture store. Everyone was wonderful. Mom used to cook us lunch every week. Pop used to carry us out fishing down the islands on weekends in his boat. The boys who did the heavy lifting/labour were very polite and friendly and we would go to each other’s house every Friday evening after having a couple of beers. There was a real camaraderie prevalent in the store that made everyone there feel like a 2nd family, an atmosphere far removed from the resentment and seething suspicion that reigned in my day job at a public office. One day, one of the boys, Chris, was excited because a former worker named Carlton was getting back his position at the store. Chris spoke in volumes about the greatness of Carlton; how Carlton was the funniest, most sharp and charismatic person he ever met. Carlton was also one of the best workers; helpful and diligent. He spoke how he missed Carlton so much, that Carlton was the like the life-essence of the store and such and such. I would be lying if I said that it didn’t make me a tad jealous to hear all this praise about some kid who worked here for a couple months and unceremoniously left, but nevertheless I was mystified by this Carlton persona. When he finally arrived, my expectations were so heightened that in my mind I envisioned the Ultimate Boy Scout entering the store flashing a 1000 Watt smile and making flora and fauna thrive around him with just his illuminating presence. Instead, this scruffy, pot-bellied unshaven man-child wearing the most slovenly and ill-fitting of clothing came into my vision. He was indeed sharp and witty but much like that of a snake-oil salesman or a streetwise con-man. He talked endlessly. It seemed as though his brain never needed a pit stop. He was always in the know or so he liked to make it seem. While sitting around outside waiting for customers, he would point out to me all the hustlers, the liars, high rollers, low riders, all the suckers, the strugglers, the ex-cons, the soon-to-be behind bars, the pipers (bums) and the sprangers (petty thieves), horner-men (men who get involved with married women) and panty-men (men who were beaten by their wives). Carlton knew everyone and everyone knew Carlton. He was loved by the general public and could easily hustle a cigarette or $5 from from practically any random person. Everyone in the store, in the entire street for that matter, was so happy to have him back. Everyone except me, that is. I thought he was nothing more than a glorified scoundrel. He was indeed charismatic and would rule the group conversations. He had a gift for ‘busting balls’ and would send a volley of golden stingers your direction without pause the minute you tried to mock him or make fun of his shabby appearance. However he loved attention, seemed to take everything for a joke and could never shut up. He knew that he irritated me but that didn’t bother him. With his skill and experience as a natural born hustler he never cared for what people thought of him. However it did bother him that I would choose Chris as a loader to go out on deliveries with rather than him. This was a sore point with him because I would share half my transport fee with Chris and it pained him to see Chris alone raking in all that money. However, one day Chris couldn’t make it to work and I had to carry Carlton with me as a loader. Carlton was overjoyed and already started planning what he was gonna do with ‘his half’ of the transport money. I thought it was rather bold of him to assume that because I paid Chris half, I would pay him half. I had specifically told that braggart Chris not to tell anyone how much I paid him so as to avoid situations like this. I immediately got upset. The item was one of our dreaded over sized wardrobes. These were notorious for transport because they were massive and ill-built from the cheapest materials. You had to strap them to your tray with expert precision because the slightest turbulence could make them rock and the cheap pitch pine would crack on itself. They were also very cumbersome to get through the customers’ doors as they were so wide and tall. The last one I transported to a rural area with really bad roads suffered a cracked mirror and a few broken dowels. I had to reimburse the customer for the damage. I groaned knowing that not only did I have to carry one of these monstrosities but I had to go with blabbermouth Carlton and in weather that appeared to be inclement. After hauling the massive wardrobe onto the van, covering it with a tarpaulin and strapping it to the best of our abilities we headed northwards towards the customer location. Carlton, a chain smoker, needed money borrowed to buy cigarettes. I loaned him some money and stopped so he could go and buy a pack at a nearby shop. Several minutes later he returns with but a single cigarette in his mouth. ‘Where’s the pack?’ I asked, wondering if he shafted me. ‘I forget I owe that shop money,’ he replied with a proud smile. I shook my head and sighed as I knew it would be a long evening. As we drove Carlton spoke of his lofty goals and plans. He wanted to open a casino. He wanted to operate a farm. He wanted to be a porn film director. He wanted to start his own political party and so on and so on. He asked to borrow some more money for a cigarette and I told him no. Unfazed he looked out the window for a while and asked me to stop the vehicle for a minute. I did so and watched as he approached a random stranger on the sidewalk and successfully talked his way into getting a cigarette. We then took off but after a few minutes the wind began to blow powerfully and rain started falling in torrents. I could hear the wind making the tarpaulin flap about like a living creature. I asked Carlton to check on the wardrobe for me. To see if it was getting wet anywhere. ‘You crazy,’ he cried, ‘In this rain? I strap down that tarpaulin. No way it getting wet.’ I insisted he go check but he refused on account of the heavy rain. In anger I went out back myself, hopped onto the tray and meticulously checked the wardrobe for any sign of rain infiltrating onto the wardrobe. There was none. Carlton was right. The tarpaulin was indeed strapped well. I returned soaked and watched Carlton as he laughed at me and was in the process of lighting a spliff. I asked him what the hell he thought he was doing. He told me that he found this weed in his backpocket. Today was his lucky day. I told him that I wasn’t going to jail for him and his weed. He laughed and said that we were deep in ‘the bush’ (countryside) and it was raining heavily. What would be the chances of police passing and even if they did, they wouldn’t care. He had a point but I didn’t like the idea of him getting so comfortable in my van. We reached our destination and saw that it was a large apartment complex. We called the customer and she informed us that her apartment was situated at the top floor. That meant that we had to haul this thing up a long flight of stairs and through a narrow balcony area with a low ceiling and then somehow get it through a tiny doorway. ‘Forget about it,’ Carlton said. ‘What?’ I replied. ‘That wardrobe cannot reach there.’ I looked at him as he seemed a bit high. In my mind it seemed he was being lazy. He then began to discuss the length and width of the wardrobe versus the width of the staircase, the corridor and the height of the door-frame. ‘That wardrobe will never get into that apartment. This was a waste-run.’ There was a seriousness in his voice I never heard before. I then began to understand where he was coming from. The thin staircase met the balcony-corridor at right angles, unless one of us could’ve walked on air, there was no way we could’ve gotten the wardrobe around the corner, let alone through the minuscule doorway. On the phone I explained this to the customer and she was beginning to acquiesce. Suddenly her boyfriend took the phone from her and started growling that he was coming to help us carry it inside. He hung up and then we saw this stocky, bald-headed and barechested ignoramus walking out the apartment and downstairs to our direction with a furious expression on his face. Carlton looked at me and said, ‘Boy, forget that man. Let’s just take down this wardrobe and drive off. That wardrobe cannot fit in that apartment. That man is an idiot.’ I felt bewildered. On the one hand I believed Carlton was right but on the other hand I didn’t want this journey to be a waste. Maybe there was some way in which that wardrobe could reach inside… ‘Boy, let’s go.’ Carlton continued, ‘We have to pay for this wardrobe if it falls off that balcony. Don’t study this ass. Let’s go.’ The man came up to the van and began rapping his knuckles against the window. He then gestured with his palms facing forward as if to say, ‘So what the f***?’ ‘Come let us carry this thing upstairs,’ the man demanded, ‘Is money I pay for this thing. Let’s go, let’s go.’ By him saying that I felt it my duty to haul the wardrobe up to his apartment. I had his $300 transport fee in my pocket. I was about to hop out the van and proceed with the haul when Carlton went out of the van and approached the man. Carlton tried to explain to the man the impossibility of getting a wardrobe of such dimensions into the apartment. That he should let us return it the store and choose something smaller. The man got offended by the latter statement and proceeded to verbally abuse us both. I then gathered the courage to tell the man that as transport agents we are not bound to deliver the item inside the home, that we fulfilled our duty by bringing it to the location. The man started getting aggressive and demanded that we take down his property off the van and give him back his $300 transport fee. I politely gave him his money and with Carlton we unstrapped the wardrobe and lay it next to him on the ground. We then watched as the man tried to find some men in the area to help him haul the wardrobe upstairs. ‘Let’s go,’ Carlton said, ‘That wardrobe will fall to pieces off that balcony in a few minutes time from now. Mark my words. Damn jackass…’ We left the man as we saw that he hired two men to help him carry the wardrobe up the stairs. We drove looking at him hand gesturing to his men his great plan on how to maneuver the wardrobe around the bend. While heading back I felt thankful that someone more streetwise, instinctive and assertive was with me, otherwise I would’ve been pushed around by that belligerent idiot and would've probably damaged/destroyed the wardrobe to my expense. Suddenly my phone rang. It was the boss. My heart froze. The boss would only call if we were in trouble. I answered the phone and the boss frantically asked what just happened. He said that the customer just called him and said that the wardrobe fell off the balcony and broke. That he wants to come in the morning to get it replaced for a smaller wardrobe. I explained what happened and to my surprise the boss laughed. ‘So you didn’t attempt to carry the wardrobe upstairs?’ ‘No.’ I replied, 'He hired his own people.’ ‘Thank God,’ he replied with a sigh, ‘You’re not supposed to carry any furniture up any stairs. That’s the customer’s responsibility. I explained that to them when they bought it. They can’t get any refund or exchange.’ I laughed to myself and explained the news to Carlton. Expecting at least a smile I was surprised to see an angry look on his face. He was upset that I gave the man back his $300 transport fee when I could’ve simply called the boss the whole time. Carlton sorely lamented the lost $150 that he was due that could’ve paid for lunch and cigarettes for the rest of the week. But all in all it was a fun and memorable evening and the beginning of a beautiful friendship. Carlton's charm grew on me from then on and I started to grow attached to his manic but quick-witted character. I felt bad that I labelled him as a glorified scoundrel and I’ve since learned never to be so quick to judge. Carlton (left) with a happy customer.

Question: What is a show or movie which was super hyped up but ended up being terrible?
Answer: The Underground (2006) Who doesn't love the Wayans? It seemed like they could do nothing wrong throughout the 80s, 90s and 00s. Keenen Ivory created In Living Color and directed the cult classic I'm Gonna Git You Sucka (1988) as well as the first two Scary Movies and White Chicks (2004). At one point in time he was the highest earning black film director in history. Shawn and Marlon had a large following with The Wayans Brothers television sitcom and a variety of acting credits in the Scary Movie films and In Living Color. Damon on the other hand……..Damon tries. Question: Who was the weirdest kid in your class?
Answer: Ray was the weirdest boy I ever met in my life. To this day I’ve never come across a boy so profoundly odd as this boy Ray who was a classmate of mine. His story is somewhat of a sad one as he was a slow student from a really poor background. Ray had a learning deficiency and was kept down some grades, making him two years older than the rest of us. He had an early growth spurt and at age 11, he could pass for a stocky and pudgy young man. This made him look absolutely ridiculous in our school uniform. Him squeezing into our generic blue shirt/khaki shorts ensemble and with his socks pulled high upon his leg reminded me of those silly yodeling Bavarian men I would see on TV advertisements. To make it worse. Ray would never stop smiling. He had to his credit an indefatigable attitude towards life. No matter how many insults were thrown his way (by both teachers and students), no matter how often he was bullied or was ignored when football/cricket teams were chosen or was screamed at by his teacher, the principal etc, he would simply smile and laugh away the matter. Ray would’ve made a first rate boxer if he had chosen that direction in life. I saw Ray take several punches in play fights and not a single grimace of pain would appear on his face. During a lunch period several boys made it a game to fling stones to shoo a mangy dog that kept coming near the school for food. Ray who, for some unknown reason, was running around the field by himself ran straight into one of those stones as it collided with his head. He stopped and looked about in a confused manner and then continued running around. No one sat near Ray during class. The teachers endorsed this practice to teach him a lesson to buck up on his schoolwork. Once, I had a falling out with my friends and they told me I was banished from the gang. Angrily, I told them I didn’t care and didn’t need them and went and did the unthinkable. I went and sat next to Ray as the entire class looked on in horror. Ray was absolutely delighted to get a new friend. I feigned interest in being his friend to spite my gang. However, in little time, things started to get weird. I knew Ray was weird but spending the week with him made me realize the extent to his weirdness. Firstly, I accidentally spilt some ink on the desk. I was terrified the teacher would see and I frantically looked for some tissue to wipe the mess. In my amazement I watched as Ray scooped up the ink in his palm and rubbed it into his hair. He smiled and told me that ink gives his hair a good shine. Then we began to discuss our personal lives. I told him the bare basics about my family, as to who it composed of and he immediately began to discuss extremely cringe and taboo subjects about his family such as how he has to help his grandmother wipe her butt after she poos and how he hated when there was a water shortage because his sister had a problem with her, let’s just say ‘personal odors.’ Hearing him speak these things so openly and with a huge smile on his face made me recoil. I decided that conversation was the not the best idea for the two of us. During recess I told Ray that I wanted to be alone for the time being and Ray queried as to why. Ray wanted us two to play ‘Catch’ (Tag) but I explained to him that it would be ridiculous for just two boys to play Catch, that we needed a big group. He then gave me a massive shove that sent me on the ground and started giggling ‘Catch me, catch me.’ He had a very effeminate manner of running and the fact that his pants were way too small and tight made him look atrocious as he giggled and ran around, waiting for me to run after him. My friends saw all this and looked at me with pity and shook their heads in dismay. It all came to an end one morning when my best friend came to me and begged that I return to the gang. I said ‘no way.’ He proceeded to tell me that all the girls and even the teachers were starting to speculate that I was gay and Ray was my boyfriend. With that said I immediately returned to my gang and left Ray in the dust. Sad, but that is how the mindset of an impressionable 9 year old boy can be. I look back in regret at how unintentionally mean I was as a kid and if I were to ever encounter Ray again I would formally apologize for my behavior from decades past. I do hope that he found some measure of success and happiness in his life. But he really was quite a weird kid. Edit 02.02.22 I’ve met several fascinating characters in my youth. Ray was one, this ‘child genius’ named Vachel was another. Click here to read about him.

Question: What is a movie you secretly love but would never admit?
Answer: Take the Lead (2006) I could watch this movie 100 times and not get in the least bit fed up of it. Antonio Banderas plays real life dance instructor Pierre Dulaine, as he attempts to help underprivileged city students find inner peace through dance. From the opening to the end credits, almost every inner-city high school movie cliche in existence is used. ‘High school students’ portrayed by actors in their mid 20s - early 30’s - CHECK Rigid, cynical and antagonistic Principal - CHECK Silly, wannabe gangsta white boy - CHECK Virtuous, athletic dude tempted to a life of crime - CHECK Virtuous damsel in distress - CHECK Haughty, soulless and privileged rich kids face off against hungry underdogs with heart in a final showdown - CHECK In the end everyone changes to become a better person - CHECK Despite all this the movie is a fun, little romp that doesn’t take itself too seriously and doesn’t overstay its welcome. The acting is decent enough, the characters, though forgettable, are lovable and interesting and the dancing is cute. The movie sticks rigidly to a generic formula but does it with charm. I really like this movie.

Question: Who is the coolest, Robert Mitchum, Paul Newman, James Dean, or Steve McQueen?
Answer: Steve McQueen was the most ruggedly manly. He was a race car enthusiast, did a lot of his own stunts and was a notorious ladies man. Paul Newman was the most beautifully rugged. When they say someone has a face like a Greek God, Paul Newman's name is usually mentioned. He served in the US Navy and like McQueen was a professional racecar driver. Question: Have you ever had a life-changing experience while working in fast food?
Answer: Right now in Trinidad, there is a growing stigma and stereotype of Venezuelan people. After the massive exodus of Venezuelan migrants following the country’s epic breakdown, Trinidad has had its fair share of migrants. Watching YouTube videos of empty groceries, families eating out of garbage cans, theft, riots etc. Many of our hearts went out to the suffering people and wanted to help as best as we could these poor people going through such tragedy. When the first wave of migrants landed we looked on with bated breath, expecting to scores of people looking like this: and this Instead, what many of saw was mostly this: It was a shock that instead of seeing scared and underfed families grateful for help and a new start in life, many of us instead saw plump, well-dressed, somewhat cocky young men and women parading about the towns, enjoying nightlife, shopping away merrily and just living it up as though the crisis in Venezuela was just a fairy tale. It is not uncommon to see a young Venezuelan couple walking the streets wearing sneakers that are valued more than the average Trini’s monthly salary. On a daily basis one would see men and women who never wore the same outfit twice, pedicured hands, gold watches, necklaces and earrings, Ray-Ban shades and ordering fast food religiously. It was a shock to see many of them indulging in such a costly lifestyle after the economic ruin of their country. It seemed that the people we believed we were saving from starvation were flaunting a high-end lifestyle that many of us wouldn’t dare try to emulate. Were these Venezuelas refugees or tourists? How could they support themselves in the long run with such a lifestyle? Why don't they save their money? This was, of course, not the case for all of the migrants. There were families who adopted humble lifestyles and tried their best to be inconspicuous. Unfortunately these families were rarely seen. The working adults simply went to work and back home while the rest of the family remained indoors, staying out of trouble. What was mostly seen were these young hedonists who paraded their non-existent wealth. Admittedly I began to harbor the same negative stereotype of them. That is until I had a pizza delivery to a certain young Venezuelan woman. On that faithful day I rode my motorcycle into a modest apartment compound. I called her number to inform that I had arrived with her order. Expecting the typical lost-in-translation scenario I was prone to get with Venezuelan customers, I was surprised to hear her speak fluent English when she answered. She came down the stairs and met me in the parking lot. She was quite modestly dressed and didn’t have the cocky flamboyance I was expecting. I couldn’t help but query about her life. She gladly told me that she attended a college in Canada, had a degree in Project Management and held a comfortable job in her home country up until the crisis began. She explained that it was difficult to lose everything and have to start back all over again but she was grateful for life. She shared the tiny apartment with her brother and they both were employed at a popular bakery in the area called Bakery Treatz. We spoke for quite a while until I reminded that her pizza would get cold. She told me to wait for a tip. I said it was not necessary but she insisted. She went upstairs hovered by her door and then returned with a stunned look on her face. I asked what was the matter and she explained that she accidentally locked herself out the apartment. She attempted a sad, self-deprecating laugh and despondently told me not to worry, her brother has a key and he would be back from work soon. I asked what time would he be back. She replied that he finishes work at 5pm. I looked at my watch and saw that it was a little after 1pm. She would be locked out for four hours. I suggested that I ride to the bakery and get her brother’s key. She didn't want me to get in trouble at work but I shushed her and let her use my phone to make a call to her brother. When she started speaking Spanish I was startled: we spoke English for so long that I forgot for a moment that she was a Venezuelan. She told him the situation and that I was coming in a few minutes to collect his key. I then rode to the bakery, met the brother (who was just as pleasant as the sister and spoke great English as well) collected the key and headed back to her. The look of joy on her face when I gave her the key was priceless. She told me to wait. When she dropped off the pizza upstairs, she returned and gave me a $50TT note, a very generous tip. Knowing her financial situation, I told her I couldn’t accept such a high amount. She insisted I take it. I thanked her wished her all the best for herself and her brother and left feeling that I accomplished something small but worthwhile. I felt a warm feeling to know that there were indeed many good people hidden among these migrants and proud to know that despite everything, our country was helping nice people like her and many others who remained out of the spotlight.

Question: What is the most ungrateful way someone reacted when opening up a birthday gift?
Answer: I’m cheating a bit but all my examples are Christmas gifts…..and yes, this would be another ‘ungrateful mother’ answer. Christmas 2001 My aunt gave my brother and I some money to purchase a gift for our mother. My aunt’s relationship with her brother’s ex (my mother) was quite ‘lacking’ to put it diplomatically but to spread the love my aunt insisted that we take the money and buy something nice for her. I was 15 and my brother was 17. We were admittedly not the most thoughtful boys in the world but we put our minds together and decided that we would get something Catholic based as our mother was highly religious. We saw a handcrafted angel that had a decadent, antique look. We both agreed that our mother would love it. It cost almost the entire sum of money we were given. With the remainder we bought a lunch and shared it. When she unwrapped it on Christmas Day she simply stared at it with disapproval. ‘How much this cost?’ We told her the amount. ‘So much money for this?! Where you got the money to buy this?’ We told her how we got the money. ‘Where’s the change?’ We told her we spent the change on buying lunch. Her mouth puckered and she gave the look someone gives when smelling a foul odour. ‘Next time don't buy anything just bring the money for me,’ she said and that was that. Christmas 2009 I’m 23, recently got a new job with a decent salary. My father, whose history of mental illness had him out of our lives for the majority of my childhood has found a solid footing in life as a taxi driver. He has been saving his money and helping my mother financially for the last few years as a sort of reciprocation for his burdens of the past. Though my mother had long moved on and started a new family, my father felt it his duty to be in her life and help her in whatever way he could. My mother,, however, refused to forgive him for the past. I thought he paid his dues twofold, as the majority of the money he earned was directed towards her. My love and appreciation of him was growing but my mother somehow didn’t seem to like that. For Christmas I bought him a small pair of car speakers for his taxi. For my mother I bought a necklace and a purse. My mother’s gift cost far more than my father’s but my father’s gift came in a larger box whilst my mother’s two items fit neatly in a small box. When I presented them with their gifts I could detect the look of disapproval on my mother’s face as she saw that my father’s gift was larger. My father, in his usual excitable manner, showed great joy. My mother decided to go into her bedroom to open her present, away from everyone else. Whilst we were all making merry in the living room; my father, his best friend Henry, my brother, myself and our two half-sisters could hear some mutterings coming out of my mother’s bedroom. Suddenly the mutterings became more audible. My mother was doing what we Trinis call ‘throwing words’ i.e. speaking ill of something/someone to yourself with the intention of that person hearing you. ‘Cheap…cheap and ungrateful,’ we heard her say, ‘I don’t know why they don’t get out of my place.’ I went into the bedroom and as I entered she flung the purse and necklace on the floor towards me. ‘Ummm, I don’t like this,’ she said tartly, ‘I don’t wear cheap things.’ I couldn’t believe my eyes and ears. I protested that her gift cost twice more than my father’s. ‘You raising your voice at me?’ she yelled and she then demanded that we all leave the house, myself, my brother, my father, his friend Henry. She kicked us out her house Christmas Day because she believed I bought her something cheap and wanted to spite her in front of my father. This would be the last Christmas the whole family spent as one. Christmas 2021 I’m 35 and my relationship with my mother has been strained to say the least. She hardly calls to find out about her grand-daughter Adrianna and when she does, she refers to her as ‘your daughter.’ I stumble upon my mother at the bus station and we make an attempt at some kind of reconciliation. I ask if she’d like anything for Christmas and she said she would like an iron (heater). I thought that was a reasonable request as it was a cheap item and I was lacking in funds, but she then decides to ask for a ironing board as well. I told her I may not be able to afford both but I’d try. I wait for her to ask me what she should get for her grand-daughter but I receive no query. Coming close to Christmas Day I encountered several unforeseen expenses so I sent a WhatsApp message to her that I can only afford the iron. She receives the message but doesn’t respond. I call her on Christmas to tell her I wanted to send my father to drop off the present as I didn’t have a vehicle. She replies that she doesn’t want him by her place. After a long time pleading she finally acquiesces. My father takes the gift up to her house and after an hour I get a voice message from her: ‘You didn’t get the ironing board?’

Question: What is the nastiest thing you've done for revenge?

She paid keen attention because my tone of voice was that of a confiding manner. ‘Hey. I’m so happy you said no.’ I then paused to look at her. She didn’t look at me but her body language showed that she was listening. ‘The truth is I really didn’t want to dance with you but your friend begged me to ask you……so yeah, it worked out good for both of us. She stared me in the face and suddenly burst into tears and went into her friend’s car. I thought everyone would’ve come to me with angry questions as to what I said that made her react like that but nobody cared, not even her friend. They all had had enough of her. She played the sympathy card too much and exhausted all of her credit. A heaviness had lifted in the party with her oppressive presence being gone. Was it a nasty thing to do/say? Question: What’s the most unprofessional thing a doctor has said to you?
Answer: Thing? You mean things. If you trust the word of just one doctor here in Trinidad you already have one foot (or in our case, leg) in the grave. My ex and I witnessed the not so great morals and ethics of some of the private health care 'professionals’ in Trinidad after she developed a severe case of cellulitis. This developed after she suffered a cut from a dirty galvanize sheet a neighbor had lying about in the road. This is how it looked after a month of healing. You don’t want to see what it looked like when it was critical. The disrespectful and dishonest negligence of the doctors who treated her was far worse than the actual injury. Left up to them, she could’ve lost her leg or gotten blood poisoning and die. So what did the doctors do/say? Here’s what happened: The cut looked minor so she decided to ignore it. A few days later an infection spreads around it the size of closed fist and it burns her all day. She had the typical Trini mindset that the public hospitals were were no good so I took her to a private doctor her relatives recommended. Said doctor diagnosed the infection as a mild case of cellulitis, gives her a prescription for some weak pills and sends us off. A week later the infection spreads to the size of a man’s foot and it burns even more severely. In panic we visit another private doctor and he tells us something to the extent of: ‘It’s just a minor infection. It’s just running its course.’ He bandages her leg and prescribes her the same medication like the last doctor. He bashes the last doctor for not bandaging her leg. We return to the old doctor to give him a piece of our mind and get our money back. His curmudgeonous, old secretary tells us that the doctor is busy. We show her the extent to which the infection has spread and she replies: ‘So what? It’s not like her leg is rotten.’ Tempted to choke slam the old bitch I take my rage out on the door and in a mad fury I threaten that I would come back to smear s**t all over his office building during the night…..because that what they really were. We place our trust in the second doctor and visit him weekly even though all he does is re-bandage her leg and prescribe the same medicine. He keeps assuring us that cellulitis is common and non-threatening, not to worry. At this point the infection has spread throughout her entire leg. The new doctor is collecting a neat $500 from me for each visit. By the third visit, he unwraps the old bandages and I literally see him gulp in shock as he witnesses the extent of the infection. I’ll never forget the cheap smile on the smug face as he tries to play it off coolly by saying: ‘Ok……it seems to have spread a bit. Maybe if I prescribe a stronger medication?’ That was when I realized the scheme. Some private doctors make their wealth by prolonging the ailment. Took her immediately to our Mt. Hope public hospital where she was confined for several days. The doctor there told her that if we had continued in the manner in which we treated the situation, best case scenario would’ve been an amputated leg. I shuddered when she recalled to me those words. I can only imagine the amount of lives lost due to selfish, negligent doctors looking to profit off of people’s misfortunes. The scar remains on her leg, not as prominent, but as a subtle reminder to a) Do not take any injury for granted, regardless how minor. b) Just because it’s private i.e. non Governmental, doesn’t mean it’s better. Question: Have you ever sabotaged food because someone was stealing it?
Answer: Is it possible to sabotage someone's lunch by accident? Yes it is. I was the saboteur. The idiot saboteur. She was a nice girl but she would often get entangled in workplace drama with other provocative and emotional females likes herself. I collected my lunch in the staff fridge and heated it in the microwave. I joined my friends in the 'mess hall’ where we proceeded to have a very exciting conversation about what crap to do with our money when we got paid. I told my friends I needed to reheat my lunch. Scared to death I would chance upon the true owner coming towards the kitchen, spotting me carrying his/her lunch like a bloody beggar-thief I haphazardly threw the lunch back into the fridge and took out mine. I heated it and returned to my friends like a nervous wreck but eliciting no suspicions. An hour later I'm busy at work when a stern voice comes over the loudspeaker. 'Will all members of staff please report to the kitchen area?’ My heart leaped like stallion in heat. This is it. The s**t has hit the fan. My friends ambled towards me all curious-like saying stuff like 'What the hell is this about?’ and 'Hey, you saw Summer come out from the manager's office in tears? What's her problem now?’ I tried to play it cool but did a terrible job. 'Huh? What da f**k's going on? I got an order to finish. This is bulls**t. Summer is a ho.’ It's a wonder none of them suspected me right then and there. For all staff to be called to a meeting at once meant that this was pretty serious. Somebody's gonna get sent home. My hands started trembling. The warehouse director took center stage and with a wary look on her face explained that Summer had just gone to have her lunch when she observed that it was severely tampered with. She explained that the person tampered with the lunch in such an extreme manner as if to send an insulting, threatening message to her. The director asked that whomsoever did such an act to please reveal him/herself. All the while I stood looking like this: While everyone else around me started to giggle quietly. Summer who stood next to the director stared at me and I immediately looked away. No one came forward. The director gave Summer money to buy lunch. Case dismissed. As we headed back to our respective positions my friends made light banter about the situation. 'We have a food molester at the warehouse. Anyone of us could be the dreaded food molester.’ They then began to laugh. That became a running joke in the warehouse. Twenty minutes later Summer comes towards me and I start to quiver like jelly. 'You see anybody with an orange cover bowl when you were at lunch Elijah?’ I shook my head in the negative. 'Sick f**king people we have working here,’ she continued. 'Yeah.' I said flatly, 'Hmmm.’ 'I mean,’ she continued while raising her voice, 'Interfering with my food? If that person has a problem with me I don't care what they say to my face but to know that some nasty sonofab**ch will go so low…….I mean……. it's just sad…….a sad, sick person.’ 'Yeah.' I replied flatly, 'Boy!……..Hmmm.’ She then stared at me like she did during the meeting. 'Elijah. It was you?’ I feigned a laugh and acted as though it was a joke, 'Yeah. It was me. Who cooked that food girl? Taste real good.’ She smiled and shook her head and went her way. I knew that she suspected the culprit to be a female so I was off the hook. Some years later I am employed elsewhere and I encounter Summer on Facebook. After a brief chat I admitted to her that I was the food molesting culprit. She laughed and said she knew. I asked her how did she know. She said that she found out after the meeting that I had a bowl exactly like hers. She had put 1+1 together. I said, 'So that whole time you spoke to me after the meeting. You knew?’ She said yes. She was playing along with me to judge whether I tampered with her food by accident, as she suspected, or if one of her enemies made me do it……..that my dumb reaction to her comments had said it all. ‘……..It tasted really good though,' was all I could think of saying. Lesson learned: When you tamper with a co-worker's food by accident, it's a good idea to go tell them.

Question: Are straight men ever attracted to very feminine gay guys?
Answer: I saw one of the most beautiful girls I ever saw working behind the counter at a University campus KFC. She had bright hazel eyes that lay upon a soft, small face; an innocently seductive countenance that was accentuated with a small yet stately nose that anchored a teasing mouth. She nonchalantly chewed on gum as she stared at me with a defiant gaze. Her narrow shoulders wanted the protection of a man of resolve, a clever yet ruthless man; a man like me. Her hips swished and swayed as she trotted about in a fitted black trousers that revealed her shapely legs. I felt nervous as she stared at me, eyebrows lifted, awaiting for me to say something. Her breasts……….her breasts were……………..OK she was a bit on the flat side but that face alone was enough to build a Trojan horse for. She looked so cocky. I wanted to show her how cocky I was. I was going to say something like: ‘I order you to give me your number.’ What?? That’s real psycho-rapist stuff. How about: ‘A two piece with you on the side.’ Yeah. That’s class. Ok. Say it………….no. That’s stupid. I’ll just give my order. But I’ll say it seductively. ‘Can I take your order?’ Who said that!? That voice? That tinny, cloying but clearly masculine voice; the voice of an old, curmudgeonous geezer. It felt as though the circuits in my brain sparked and scrambled. It felt as though there was a glitch in the matrix; a tear in the fabric of our universe. It made me shudder and feel paranoid. ‘Sir. Can I take your order please?’ That awful old man voice. It came from the beautiful girl in front of me. I looked at her name tag. ‘Hello. My name is Aaron.’ The most beautiful KFC maiden was a man. An emotion never experienced before; an amalgamation of revulsion, curiosity and betrayed lust made me feel like running away but keeping my eyes on her/him while running. It felt almost similar to the feeling one gets to suddenly detecting that you're being watched and scrutinized by a hidden figure; a feeling of vulnerability. I had to leave the KFC to process what the hell just happened. Did I question my sexuality? Damn right I did. I came to the verdict that I wasn’t gay but by instinct, I was wired to be attracted to feminine features. I learned that, if possible, always read someone’s name tag before you decide to lust after them.

Question: What one thing do you wish you had known about life when you were in your 20s? This question is for those who are older than 20 who would like to share their mistakes and insights with a younger person than themselves.
Answer: I wish I didn’t get caught up in the typical young adult craze of getting a car. When I got my first full time job as a warehouse attendant at age 19, practically every male co-worker around this age would go philosophically deep in the discussion of buying their first car. A car meant everything to us simple minded fools. It signified freedom. It allowed for us to be able to go out wherever we wanted and come back home whenever we wanted. It meant getting premium birds (girls). It meant easier access to sex. It meant getting wasted on beers while bar-hopping and chilling out by the riverside or the beach with our closest pals. It meant blasting our favourite hit songs of the time while cruising through our neighbourhoods and getting attention. There was a certain mystique about getting a car at age 20 and to this day there still is. Now at 35, I can safely say that for the majority of 20 year olds, that mystique is in fact bull***t. There are only two criteria I believe that allows for getting a car at 20 to not be financial suicide. If you are fortunate to belong to either category, upon getting your first car Heaven’s Gate opens up and you have years of wild adventures at your helm that will allow for fond memories. If you don’t belong to either category, Heaven’s Gate opens up for an extremely short while but then suddenly the floor caves in on you and fall into the pits of finance hell that will allow for a bald spot on your head by age 23. Whether new or used, investing in a car at a young age is a recipe for disaster for the average Trinidadian 20 year old. When you’re fresh out of school and you decide to get a car to experience your man-child utopia, you might as well change the name of your bank account to your car’s license plate number. Practically all of your salary belongs to that car. If it’s new or foreign used (as we have in Trinidad) your ass is owned by whichever bank that gave you the loan for your car. You may cry ‘freedom at last’ to your parents but the bank has an even bigger leash around your neck and they don’t love you like mommy and daddy does. When you bite the bullet and save some money to buy a cheap, used car, you may pat yourself on the back for such grit and determination but you are most likely in a worse off position than your friend who has to pay a loan as your ass is owned by the mechanic. It’s almost pathetic to see the typical twenty something year old Trini looking frantic at the side of the road after his car broke down; no money to pay for a wrecking service, desperate for any kind of assistance, his lady-friend abandoning him in shame. Yet I see such a scenario every Friday evening, especially when I pass by the mall. Friends and peers would make the excuse, ‘Once you choose a good car and have a really good mechanic you could buy a used car.’ I fell for this terrible piece of advice and at age 24 bought with cash my first car. It was used and recommended by a trusted mechanic friend. It was one of these: It was a disaster. I had a breakdown the very second day of driving it. I spent more time waiting for the mechanic to fix it than actually driving it. The steering wheel actually came off while driving one fine evening. Going on a date while driving this beauty was more suspenseful than a Hitchcock movie; will it break down on me and roll down the hill? Oh no, what’s that weird noise? When I had to get repairs/service done, sourcing parts for my discontinued model would send me on an Indiana Jones like expedition where I would find myself in some remote scrap-yard miles away from home, climbing up a ghastly stack of aged and abandoned vehicles looking for a model like mine. If I was lucky enough to find my model, the scrap yard owner would gauge how desperate I looked and charged to suit. Forget starting a small business, forget marrying your sweetheart, ignore stock market opportunities, partnerships or simply taking a summer trip to Cancun. My beaten up Ford Laser was my business partner, my lover, my future, my everything. Forget taking out girls to movies and the beach, I might as well carry out my mechanic and try to sweetheart him into cheaper rates. The final straw came when I took out my last bit of money from my account and was siphoning some from my credit card, an epiphany ocurred: At the time, my mechanic informed me that he was unavailable but his son would take over duties for the time being. As I waited at the garage for the son to arrive, I saw a boy, a few years younger than me, ride towards me with his bicycle and park it at the garage. Wondering if the kid was lost or confused, I told him that this was a garage for cars, not bikes. He laughed and said that he was the mechanic. I queried why he didn't have a car, being a mechanic and all. He gave me a knowing glance and said, ‘Can’t afford one.’ ‘But there are so many cheap used cars for sale!?’ I said quite fascinated, ‘And you know how to fix ‘em!?’ He simply smiled and said nothing. He asked me to raise my bonnet. I then realized he probably saw me as a fool. He had already given his answer. Just because he could fix them himself doesn’t mean that they would stop being a bloody expense, a pain in the ass and a sacrifice of all other youthful goals and endeavours. It was time to face the facts, buying a used car, for someone like me, was like buying a dying horse. After the repair I put the car for sale at a great loss and washed my hands of it. Something magical happened after. Like glimmering grass on a summer morning, I could see my money starting to grow. Life suddenly became enjoyable again. Whenever I see a twenty year old posing proudly next to his aged, first car, I shake my head and laugh to myself. The amount of money he is going to spend behind that vehicle could clothe and feed a child. Go ahead and call it your baby.
