Question: What do fast food employees think of customers who come in frequently, say, multiple times a week or even daily?
Answer: Thank you, whomsoever asked this beautiful question. Working as a delivery rider for a popular pizza restaurant it was fascinating how the regular customers seemed to be at polar extremes. There was hardly a middle ground. The regulars were either exceedingly pleasant i.e. the ever smiling, courteous customer who knew you by name, empathized with you, were patient and just radiated warmth and kindness. I would refer to them as the sweethearts. Or there were the ones who saw fast food personnel as a cheap means to vent their personal frustrations, felt entitled (because they believed the company would not survive without them), always tried to 'beat the system,’ always cheap, petty and discourteous and always naturally doing something aggravating to everyone around them e.g. taking up two parking spaces, refusing to sit and wait for the order (standing impatiently by the cashier with folded arms and sullen face) and giving details as to all the operational flaws they've witnessed with the restaurant whilst preaching how they would fix these flaws if they owned the restaurant. I would refer to these as the soul-eaters. Unfortunately I can only distinctly remember the experiences with soul-eaters. Here are three fascinating accounts. The Coffee Boys. Every Saturday night a group of preppy young men, all between the ages of 18 — 20 would come to the restaurant. There were usually five of them and they would occupy an entire table. They would sit at this table for more than an hour regardless if they had long finished their meal, denying that space for other diners. What was the meal they each ordered that merited leasing the table for such an extended period of time: One cup of coffee. That didn't bother any of us. It's not our restaurant, the company has no policy against such an obvious loss-incurring action and we were trained that the customer is always right. What made them unlikable was how they went about ordering their single cup of coffee. The ringleader, the most preppy of them all, would do the ordering. Despite being just some 18yo kid just off of cricket practice, he would speak to you as though he's the son of the owner of the restaurant. 'Things are pretty slow for the hour huh…..Susan?’ 'Patrice…… Are those cookies fresh or are they from the morning batch?’ 'Looks like you need a new shirt huh…… Phillip?’ He would always call out your name from your name tag, not as a show of courtesy, but in an authoritative almost passive-aggressive manner. After a minute or two of his condescending conversation, he would request 5 coffees with cream, literally the cheapest item on the menu. The cashier would pour them out in cups, neatly cover them with lids and place them on a tray. The words 'thank you’ or even subtle gesture of appreciation would never emanate from him as he would eye the cups, lift a cup to his face, remove a lid, sniff at coffee and take a sip in a manner as though he is the ultimate connoisseur of generic fast food coffee. 'Ummm. Maria?’ he would say to the cashier after taking his sip. The cashier would nod and come to him. He would then continue, 'Something is up with this coffee…I think you need to check your coffee machine.’ Then a hullabaloo would ensue with different members of staff tasting the coffee, not finding anything wrong. The manager would come out and taste the coffee and find no fault with it. However coffee-boy is not satisfied until he sees the coffee machine opened up to reveal that there is indeed sufficient powdered coffee and creamer in the machine. The five original cups of coffee are discarded and the cashier has to keep adjusting the machine and pouring out coffee, giving coffee-boy a sample to taste until he finds it is just right. Five fresh cups of coffee are then poured and he goes to his gang to occupy the table for over an hour after having caused over $50 worth of wasted coffee and cups. The Church Group. Once a month, on a Sunday night a large group of people who just finished worshiping at a nearby church would come into the restaurant. Their orders would be large, usually ranging between 4 — 6 family sized pizzas. They were courteous, patient and would attempt to be friendly. However they never failed to infuriate us all whenever they came. Firstly they would always come just a few minutes before closing time to place a big order. Though they could've easily called pick up an hour in advance, they preferred to come when we've already washed up the dishes and mopped the floor, anxiously waiting the closing time. 'I'm sorry but we've closed off dining for the night as we are about to close. You could only have the order as a take-away.’ the cashier would tell them. 'Oh well,' the pastor of the group would say, 'Well then we'll have to forget about the order.’ He's saying this but he knows that we cannot refuse a large order no matter how near it is to closing time. He knew that if the head office got wind of our branch refusing a $500+ order, we would be reprimanded. He knows all this but he is pretending to show humility for his church congregation. The cashier would acquiesce and remind the pastor that in ten minutes time we would be closing. The pastor would smile and assure the cashier that they wouldn’t be long. Staff would have to reheat the ovens, gather all the dough and ingredients that were neatly packed away in the chillers and grudgingly prepare these pizzas, knowing fully well that the order would be finished beyond our closing hour, after which we would have to wait for the church group to finish their meal. The restaurant would close at 10 pm on a Sunday. The church group would get their meal at around that time. Even though we’ve already tucked away the chairs and neatly aligned the tables for the next day, the church group would drag about a couple tables and join them together. Anything that is request-able you bet your bottom the group would request it; more napkins, more cups with ice, more condiments, turn off the air condition please, OK its too warm now, can you turn it back on, mini boxes to carry home leftovers, plastic bags, can this pizza be warmed over? etc, etc. While they are eating, the pastor, though he knows that he promised he will not stay long is encouraging members of the group to share tame, inoffensive church-based jokes and stories. All of us would and listen as Mrs. Nora recounted the time when she sent her grandson to get Communion bread but he didn't remind her that he wasn't a confirmed Catholic yet; how she gave him a good licking that evening when they returned home. The pastor howled with laughter. We would then interrupt their laughter to explain to them that we were ready to lock the building. The pastor would act surprised and apologize for losing track of time. We would wait another 10 minutes as they scrambled to distribute leftovers and gather their belongings. They wouldn’t even bother to help tidy back the area because they are now suddenly concerned about overstaying their time. They all apologized and thanked us for being so patient with them. We would then have to clean up all their spills, stains, used napkins, cups, pizza boxes and trays, re-wipe the tables, re-mop the floor and reposition the tables and chairs. We would lock the restaurant and when we exited the building the church group would be outside hanging about near their vehicles, continuing their conversation. Most of us didn’t have vehicles and would struggle that late hour to get a taxi as the streets would be near-deserted. None of the church group members would even consider offering us a ride as they left the restaurant in their cars. The Pool Guy. Lastly, there was a guy who would come in every day after work to place the same order of a mini pizza with chicken. I can’t remember his name but he would always mention to whomsoever was cashing that he was ‘building his pool.’ That pool must’ve been deeper than the Atlantic Ocean because for years he would always mention that pool that he was building. I can say without the slightest doubt that pool-guy was an asshole. I’m not even going to try to be subtle about it. He was a certified piece of s**t. Of all the scummiest people I’ve met on this Earth, he ranks in the top 5. Pool guy was a short hairy guy in his mid to late 30’s with a head full of graying hair. He always had a disheveled, resentful look as though he just woke up from a sleepless night with a terrible hangover. He was always making threats, harassing or trying to intimidate the mostly female workers to get some sort of preferential treatment i.e. being served before everyone else, getting more toppings on his pizza etc. Such tactics were common on an everyday basis but what set pool guy apart was that he naturally wanted to piss you off and provoke you to the limits of what is legally allowed. Pool guy definitely had some personal problems in his life and saw the restaurant as a means to vent his anger and frustration. Pool guy seemed as though he couldn’t overcome certain obstacles/people in his life so instead he would channel this anger into abusing a bunch of hapless, minimum wage earning women in a fast food restaurant. His tactic was that he would enter the restaurant and with no common courtesy he would gruffly order his mini pizza with chicken. He would remind the cashier at what time he placed his order and would subtly threaten that waiting makes him angry and we really don’t want to see him when he’s angry. He would then stand with arms folded, hearing distance away from the cashier, refusing to take his seat until he got his order. Most of us knew that he didn’t really care about the order. He got his thrill in harassing and psychologically abusing the more timid female staff at the front counter. ‘Go check on my order,’ he would demand every couple of minutes, ‘I’m waiting too long.’ Nothing thrilled him more than when his order took longer than the standard 15 minutes. Now he had an excuse to abuse. ‘Where is my order?’ he would shout. If no one answered him he would use this as an excuse to become vile. ‘ Like there’s only stupid, slow and uneducated people working in here?’ or ‘If I was your ‘child-father’ (baby-daddy) you would’ve moved faster.’ or ‘You could be a disappointment to your family but don’t disappoint me here today.’ The most pathetic thing about pool guy was that he would never dare behave like that in the presence of other customers. He would step away when a queue of customers were around and when they dispersed, like a rat coming out of his hole he would return to provoke and insult. There was never a single moment where he displayed a likable side to him. When he was in a good mood, he wouldn’t threaten and abuse but he would instead rant about his achievements in life. He claimed that he owned a fleet of trucks and his family were of great wealth and status that they practically owned the entire North coast of Trinidad. He would talk about how he traded in his cars every five years, that he spent over 5 million on his house in the past three years and how he was thinking of widening the pool that he had under construction and choosing a different set of tiles than what he originally intended I never met another delivery rider who didn’t feel like punching pool guy’s face in after being forced to listen to one of these boastful and selfish conversations. Funny enough, we got word that his niece was to be employed at the restaurant. The day she arrived at the restaurant pool guy mysteriously stopped coming. His niece explained to us that he was the most detested member of the family. He did not own a fleet of trucks but rather worked loading goods on and off a truck for a major cosmetics retailer. Also, he lived, not in a $5 million dollar+ house but in a tiny annex at his parents’ house which was next to her parents. By no means did the family own any property at the North coast let alone the entire North Coast. We asked if he had a pool and to our surprise she said yes, his family did indeed have a pool. However it was nothing like he described. It looked more like this: Edit 08.01.22: I am honoured that so many of you enjoyed this really long answer. Thank you. Please let me exploit your hospitality by plugging another answer in this vein. It's about the hardest day I've ever had at this restaurant. I'm still reeling. Click here.

Question: What food goes from delicious to revolting when you eat large amounts?
Answer: Many moons ago…. I was hanging out with some friends after work in a bar, shooting some pool, enjoying a few rounds of drinks. It was customary (and proper etiquette) that the person who didn't buy any rounds go out and get some food for everyone. I would always volunteer to be the guy to get food. This is a bit embarrassing for me to admit but I secretly calculated that it was far cheaper to buy the food than a round of drinks for 7 — 10 people ( especially when ladies, requested premium stuff like mud slides and screwdrivers). A donut franchise had recently opened and it was just a few buildings away. A large box of donuts would've cost me almost half of what I usually paid for food. Plus there was less hassle, everything together in one neat box that weighed less than my arms. I ordered two dozen random donuts and returned to the bar, my beer waiting for me. Everyone cheered my idea for donuts. Beer and donuts….like Homer Simpson. We were gonna have a good time. No we weren't. After the first donut a few of us started feeling a bit queasy. We blamed it on the alcohol. It's when we attempted to eat the second donut was when disaster struck. As scrumptious and fresh as they were, they became absolutely revolting the second time around. I have a weakness for Long Johns but after wolfing one down, the second one I had my eye on looked like an instrument of torture. The donuts seemed to have brought in a premature hangover for the majority of us. One of the girls had to go to the toilet and was missing for a half hour. One of the fellas had to go throw up. There were still more than a dozen donuts remaining but I would've loved nothing more than to fling them into a dumpster. Only one guy had a hardcore stomach and survived the ordeal, consuming 3 while casually sipping on his beer. He offered to take the donuts home. Suddenly I became unpopular. They let me know that they were all aware that I chose to get food because it was cheaper for me. They really drilled it into me for taking my cheapness too far. Nothing feels worse than to be publicly humiliated by friends while suffering a sickly sweet, beer-donut hangover. I learned two lessons that day.

Question: Why is reading so important?
Answer: Imagine this. You are with some friends on a fishing excursion in the Mediterranean sea. Miles away from the nearest harbor your yacht begins to sink. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) Another scenario. You are in a cabin in the Swiss Alps. An avalanche occurs and buries your cabin under twenty feet of snow. Your phone has enough juice to make one call. Who do you call? A) B) Final scenario. You have been drugged unconscious and abducted by traffickers who want to harvest your organs. Your kidnappers are taking you to a foreign land in which you cannot decipher the language, pinpoint the culture or recognize the terrain. Who would you rather get help from? A) B) If you chose ‘B’ for all the scenarios, congratulations, you are alive. If you chose ‘A’ for any scenario, you are most likely dead. The characters pictured under 'A’ are men who are extremely well-read. Ken Jennings — Record holder for the longest winning streak on Jeopardy. Karl Marx — Founding father of Marxism, a proponent of communism. Bill Nye — A mechanical engineer and popular television presenter, comedian and educator. The characters pictured under ‘B’ are men who are extremely well-read but also have a lot of worldly experience. Joseph Conrad — Polish born English author, explorer and ship captain. Jack London — American author, sailor, journalist and former Klondike prospector. Richard Francis Burton — English explorer, translator, linguist, historian and writer. This is not slight against the achievements of the characters under 'A’ it's just that the fellows under 'B’ have allowed for the knowledge they've amassed through reading to inspire them towards physical action which in turn develops experience and skill. Ken Jennings and Bill Nye might be able to tell you what is the distance of each planet in the Solar system from the sun in less than a minute but that doesn't mean NASA would aggressively pursue them. Marx, if he were alive, could write a 1000 page book on why he thinks 20th century communism failed but do you think Maduro or Castro would’ve employed him as an advisor? Group A are individuals of impressive intelligence but any logical thinking individual would recognize that Group B is superior in regards to worldly applicability. So to answer the question, reading is important to gain knowledge. Reading is very important, but not as important as the ACTION that it stimulates.

Question: What is the most shocking thing you have seen your mother do?
Answer: Around age 7 or 8 my mother sent me off to school with a brand new pencil case full of sparkling new stationery. Coming from a school full of children of limited means, having brand new stuff was a big deal, especially at the middle of the school term. Classmates would gather round and gaze in awe at your virgin erasers that smelt almost delicious, sharperners with shiny, sharp blades, clear plastic rulers so new you could look through them and make your classmates look taller or shorter according to the angle etc, etc. However the most prided item in my pencil case was my pencil. It was painted a glossy, emerald green and crafted of premium quality wood that gave a musky fragrance. For a class of post-toddlers this never before seen pencil was exceedingly impressive. Everyone ooh-ed and ahh-ed at my 2B Excalibur. I was King for a day…or at least for a few hours. Apparently the meanest, most scoundrel-iest boy in class, Stefan, didn’t like the fact that I was getting so much attention. Stefan came from a troubled background. He had an extensive vocabulary of all forms of obscene language and was extremely disrespectful to the point that he would perversely hold conversations discussing what the genitalia of our female teachers was like. Because of his shocking nature none of the other boys would ever challenge him as we had the juvenile belief that the more filthy the mouth, the more dangerous the boy. Coming back to class after lunch I found Stefan perusing through my bag without my permission. I asked him what he was doing and saw that he had my precious pencil in his hands. ‘I need your pencil borrow,’ he said with great pathos, ‘I didn't do the homework last night and I have no pencil. Miss (the teacher) will beat me if she find out.’ Although I found it strange that Stefan was suddenly interested in his homework and I knew for a fact that our teacher didn't care what Stefan did with his homework book as long as he kept his filthy mouth shut during class, I allowed him use of my pencil. With a heavy heart I watched as a smug smile developed on his face and he proceeded to eye the glossy green paint and sniff at the shaven wood. Some minutes afterwards, while class was in process, Stefan, who was seated directly behind me, could be heard making a weird crunching noise. I looked behind me and recoiled in horror at the most devastating sight my innocent eyes ever beheld. My precious pencil was in Stefan's mouth. Not only that, it was broken in half and he had split one of the halves down the centre with his teeth and was in the process of doing the same with the other half. Although fully aware of the futility of the matter, like a kneejerk I grabbed at my pencil pieces but Stefan evaded my attempt. I could see a cruel Chesire grin spread on on his mouth. He spat out the pieces and said while laughing, ‘The pencil point broke……I needed to get the lead inside.` The teacher demanded for us to explain why we were joking around in class and in tears I ran to her and explained the entire story, how Stefan was caught prying inside my bag, took my pencil without permission, lied and now broke it into pieces. ‘Return to your seat Elijah,’ the teacher said angrily, ‘It's just a pencil. Stop crying like a little girl.’ Stefan and the rest of the class burst out into laughter. I returned to my seat full of anger and remorse. I struggled to fight the tears from flowing. I couldnt speak to anyone for the rest of the day. When I went home I immediately went to my mother and released all those pent up tears and explained the story in great detail. My mother didn’t say anything except ask for the name of the culprit and the name of my teacher. The following day I returned to school in a morose mood. Stefan saw me enter class and began to tease me about crying over a pencil like a little girl. Two hours later, the Principal entered our class and whispered to our teacher and left. The teacher had a stunned look on her face and angrily told Stefan to follow her out the classrom. Ten minutes later Stefan resumed his place looking as though he had just been handed a life sentence. The teacher returned and proceeded to give a speech in which she stated that anyone caught going into another student's belongings would be sent to the Principal and possibly suspended. She mentioned the incident with Stefan and me and explained that Stefan's mother was contacted and had promised to replace the pencil that Stefan stole and destroyed. The following day I recieved a generic replacement pencil from Stefan. He looked me in the eyes and said in a serious but pleading tone, ‘Don't ever call your mother for me again Elijah.’ I told him I didnt know what he was talking about. He told me that yesterday he came into the staff room with the teacher to see this little lady, my mother, acting crazy and talking about going to the police about something. He said that my mother had told the staff room that my grandmother had put $100 in my book bag for me to carry home to her to buy groceries and it was missing. My mother demanded to know why teachers were allowing stealing to happen in front of their eyes. ‘Elijah. Tell your mother I never touched your money.’ Stefan passionately interjected as he told the story, ‘I only take the pencil and that's all.’ He continued the story. ‘No student here stole any money from your son Miss,’ the Principal had said stoically, ‘We do not tolerate theft here.’ ‘If a student didn’t steal the money,’ my mother had replied, ‘Somebody had to have stolen it.’ This of course subtly alleging that my teacher had stolen the money. There was a rabble amongst the teachers and the matter ended with the Principal taking $50 from his wallet and urging other teachers to contribute to make up for the ‘lost’ $100. In the end, $80 was donated from the teachers to my mother, who said thanks but still was upset over the theft. I thought about all that I heard and couldnt make sense of it. Grandma had died years ago. ‘I didn't know I had $100 in my bag!’ I said defensively to Stefan. ‘I don't care,’ Stefan cried, ‘Just keep your mother away from me.’ He was genuinely terrified of my little mother. When I went home that evening I was pleasantly surprised to see my precious 2B Excalibur was waiting for me. My mother had bought another to replace the one Stefan broke and a little toy car and she managed to cook my favorite meal of spaghetti and meatballs that day. Aware of our financial position I asked how she managed to buy all this. She told me it was courtesy of the school. I then told her about the story Stefan gave me about the missing $100 in my bag. She explained that no one in the school would've taken her seriously if she quarrelled about a pencil, regardless if it was a pencil as nice as mine. ‘Then you lied to the teachers and the Principal.’ I said rather shocked. ‘I didn’t lie,’ she said, ‘I exaggerated. Stefan did go into your bag without permission. Stefan did take your pencil without permission. Stefan did lie about using your pencil for homework. The teacher didn't repimand Stefan for his actions. The teacher did mock you and cause emotional damage. If there was $100 in your bag, a boy like Stefan would've definitely stolen it. I embellished the truth so that they could see the seriousness of the matter. Now justice is served.’ I had no idea what she was talking about. She was a big fan of Matlock back then and was talking lawyer talk. In my mind I was shocked that my mother lied to coerce my school into giving us money but as I grew into a teenager I understood better what she did. People sue for far more petty matters, tell much more sensational exagerrations and get rewarded fortunes. That is how the law works. As for Stefan, never heard a peep from him again. The event made him so notorious that he was placed to sit in the back of the class away from me or any other susceptible victims. It's unfair to him, I know, but his mother should've watched Matlock also.

Question: What was the most disgusting thing you have seen at an auto mechanic shop?
Answer: This may be cheating a bit but it actually occurred at an auto-electrician's garage. The guys who ran this garage were really nice. And I'm not just saying that as a form of courtesy. They were eerily pleasant to the point that I wondered if they were on some sort of drug or followers of some type of underground Eastern philiosphy/religion. They would never get impatient or irritated with you. There was a calming resonance in their voice that made you feel everything was going to be OK and they would listen to you with the utmost sympathy and understanding. Sometimes I would find myself wanting to visit them even though I had no electrical issues with my vehicle, just to bask in their warmth and friendliness. They were experts at their job too. As one would expect they were quite popular in the area. You would line up for hours to get a spot inside but it was worth it. Absolutely no one who was familiar with them would haggle, speak condescendingly towards or show any form of bad face towards them. That would be like sacrilege. However one guy had to be the one to disrupt the positive energy coming from our beloved hippie electrical-garage commune. In Trinidad we have this phenomenon called ‘wetman.’ A wetman is usually a vain but ignorant young man who thrives on attention. His life revolves around impressing easy women with a show of careless spending, flashy clothes and the official wetman badge of honour, his Nissan Tiida vehicle. For some inexplicable reason this vehicle is coveted by wetmen throughout the country, most likely due to the fact that it is one of the cheapest (foreign used) sedans available. Wetmen are also known to be notoriously cheap, uncouth and many of them live such a flagrantly hedonistic lifestyle, they are forced to secretly live in their Nissan Tiidas. In other words, a wetman is a scoundrel. One faithful day, a wetman joined the queue that we would form by parking outside the garage on a little road alongside the garage. In typical wetman fashion he had his gangsta music blasting at full volume the entire time he was parked. One of the apprentices would habitually pass to check on each person lined up outside to ask what was their problem. Doing this, they would find out who had simple problems that could be fixed at an instant, so he/she could be dealt with immediately and speeden the process. The apprentice went to the wetman who was blasting his music. The wetman only slightly lowered the volume to communicate with the apprentice. The apprentice had to tell the wetman to lower the music some more so he could hear him, which irritated the wetman. ‘My car giving trouble,’ Wetman said, ‘Everytime I switch off I have to ask someone for a jump start to start it back.’ The apprentice pulled out his multimeter and said, ‘Switch off the vehicle and lift the bonnet.’ The wetman scowled and in a venemous tone replied, ‘Brother. Like you not listening to what I saying? Switch off? You expect me to push this car all the way inside your garage?’ I was behind the wetman in the queue I was aghast at how stupid he was. Didn't he realize he was speaking to an actual electrician? Didn't he realize that the apprentice would find a way to get it started again? Wisely, the apprentice decided it was not worth it explaining all that to him and told him to wait until he gets a space inside the garage and the boss would personally deal with his vehicle. Wetman then resumed blasting his music much to the displeasure of myself and the apprentice who was now trying to ask me as to what was the issue I had. The apprentice had to go back over to the wetman and tell him again to lower the volume. ‘What da f**k boy,’ the wetman cried, ‘You all taking so damn long here and I can't listen to my tunes.’ He kept threatening to leave and I was hoping for him to make good on his threat but to my disappointment he remained. A half hour later we are both inside the garage. Realizing that the wetman was trouble, the apprentice wisely went to fetch the boss to deal with him. The boss arrived and Wetman stood outside his vehicle with arms folded. The engine was still running but the bonnet was lifted. Wetman squinted at the engine as though looking for some creature hiding somewhere that was causing his electrical problem. The boss approached and asked him what was the matter. Wetman scowled and replied, ‘I done tell yuh secretary what is the problem. Like you all dumb inside here?’ At that moment everyone's head turned towards Wetman's direction. Someone had blasphemed our precious garage! Everyone waited to see how the boss would handle it. No one ever witnessed any of the electricians lose their cool, especially the boss who was the kindest and most calm of them all. ‘Yes,’ the boss replied without any change of tone ‘Mike told me that you're getting ignition problems. I was just hoping to get some more information so I could know the best way to approach the problem.’ ‘The car not starting,’ Wetman uttered irritatedly, ‘What else you need to know? You is the electrician, not me. A whole hour I waiting outside, I going to lose out on a job I was getting.’ He then did what we Trinis call ‘steups’ which is the noise poorly raised people make to show disgust by sucking spit through your teeth. ‘Switch off the ignition let me run the tester through.’ Again Wetman's face scowled and he got defensive, ‘Brother,’ he growled, ‘I not switching off my engine. Last man I went by make me switch off the engine. He couldn’t fix my problem and I had to push my car out the road and ask someone for a jumpstart. That is failure. You have to fix my problem with the engine running!’ The boss stared at the apprentice and then glanced at the Wetman, who was clearly of a legendary level of stupidity as he stood there defiant and folding his arms. How is the boss going to deal with this one? Everyone was probably thinking the latter question. ‘I understand,’ said the boss calmly, ‘However if we operate on your vehicle while it's running we could destroy your circuits. The danger…’ The boss then paused for second and said, ‘Next Monday is the best day for you to come. We're getting a device that can work on vehicles while the engine is running without damaging anything. It's being shipped from China so give me a call Sunday evening to confirm when you're coming.’ Like magic, the little white lie worked and wetman accepted and left in a hurry to see about his hired job. Everyone breathed a sigh of relief when the ignoramus left. The next time I came, I enquired about the I individual and they happily informed me that someone must've solved Wetman's problem because he never did call or show up again. Or maybe he was offered a starring role in the movie below.

Question: What local delicacy in your country would horrify most foreigners?
Answer: Iguana Eggs I'm open minded to strange foods but when a co-worker offered me a taste of her iguana egg lunch, I had to reject her offer with more diplomacy than a politician. Iguanas in Trinidad are a common delicacy in rural areas. Curried iguana is the most frequent way of preparing it. I would guess that the meal became popular because iguanas are not the brightest animals in the reptile kingdom. They always get stuck in fences and love to take the path that makes contact with human civilization. Someday I'll venture to consume an iguana egg but for now if one of the critters get caught in my fence I'll be the odd guy who frees it.

Question: What is the hardest you've ever worked at in your entire life?
Answer: A branch of Mario's Pizza had only recently opened in my home town just last year. They were looking for motorcycle delivery riders and though I promised myself to never do motorcycle delivery for them again (it's actually very risky, and you always get soaked in rain) I really needed the money. I reapplied and during the orientation I got a head's up from old friends that one of the most hated branch managers Ms. K, was to be the appointed manager of my branch. The scuttlebutt was that she was a brown-nosed elitist, looking to do anything that it takes to get an area manager position i.e. she was the current area manager's pet. I heard awful stories that some of the best, most dedicated workers either resigned or were transferred to an unfortunate location after having disputes with Ms. K. This made me groan inwardly because I had various encounters with branch managers like that. All they do is to try to makes sales targets to satisfy their superior and be rewarded cash bonuses. They would literally lie, steal and kill to make these sales targets. The customer means nothing to them unless he/she is some big shot. The staff beneath them are nothing more than names on a roster sheet. Once I slipped and fell violently on a poorly mopped floor and such a manager ran out her office, not to help me up, but to demonstrate to everyone that I was wearing the wrong type of shoes hence the restaurant had no legal responsibility for my incident. I sighed but convinced myself with the idea that Ms. K couldn't be all that bad. The opening weekend of the branch was made into a spectacle. There were live artists, our mascot (a stereotypical moustachioed Italian but with a huge head), a bouncy castle, a buy one get one free offer and prizes being handed out to random customers. I arrived for the evening shift. When I arrived there were so much people I had to squeeze through the crowd just to enter the building. This was right after the COVID lockdown of 2020 and though the store was supposed to have a maximum of 20 people indoors at any given time, I counted about 50 indoors and over 100 outside fighting to get in. It was like being thrown into a battlefield. There was no introduction to anyone. No one had anticipated that the restaurant would’ve been flooded with customers to such an extent. I came all smiling and social but everyone wore frowns and all the customers looked furious. 'Hey delivery man,' a man called out angrily, 'Check on order 607 for me…….2 hours now I waiting.’ Suddenly a barrage of people started to hail me out to check on their orders, the men scowling angrily, the women giving me sad, puppy-dog faces. I had to run away from them all. The poor cashier had to stand there and take verbal abuse while angry customers shoved receipts into her face. 'If this order not ready I want my money back.’ 'I want to talk to the manager.’ 'Excuse me! Can I get your name? This service is terrible.’ The poor cashier was just a dwarfish 22yr old single mother who only recently got the job. I wanted to help her but I knew it would be to no avail as I saw that there was a mountain of deliveries on the warmer. Firstly I had to hand my assumption letter to the manager. I spoke to a supervisor who was frantically trying to answer calls that were ringing off the hook. I could barely hear her because the live music was so loud that it was a shouting match between us. 'CHECK INSIDE THE OFFICE.’ 'WHAT?’ 'THE OFFICE' She pointed to a little room ahead where the door was closed. I watched as several workers moved to and fro in a daze getting dough and toppings out of the chiller. There was a stock pile of finished pizzas of unknown destination that lay on the cutting table practically cold. Two workers were frantically sorting through a pile of crumpled bills trying to determine which pizza belonged to whom. Apparently the store invested in some cheaper bill management software that was glitchy and froze when overworked so a lot of old orders resurrected on the screen and pushed out the new orders hence the chaos of customers not getting their orders. I tried to assist in sorting out the orders and finding the right pizzas when I felt a hand on my shoulder. It was another delivery rider I was acquainted with. 'You just reached?’ he asked concernedly. 'No. About an hour now.’ I replied. 'Go talk to the manager.’ he said with a hint of caution. He then said as though reading my mind, 'Boy is madness up in this restaurant.’ He then proceeded to laugh his manical laugh which he did whenever he was under pressure or had something on his mind. I knocked on the manager's door and heard a voice say to come in. Inside I saw a lady in her 30s who I assumed to be the branch manager. Next to her was a lady in her 40s/early 50s who I assumed was her boss, the area manager. They were both watching baby photos on the area manager's phone. The manager Ms.K looked quite attractive with light brown eyes, a svelte figure and huge boobs. I told myself that she couldn't be all that bad. Then she spoke. 'You're an hour late……and this is your first day.’ Her voice was cold and pedantic. She and the area manager then stared at me critically. Ms. K. then adjusted her mask to reveal a rather ugly mouth. The charm was dispelled immediately. I explained to them that I was on time and I was just trying to help because there was a lot of chaos outside. 'Chaos?’ the area manager cried as though offended, 'What chaos is he talking about?’ 'I don't know what he's talking about,' Ms. K replied, 'Staff outside not following orders and want to bawl chaos every 5 seconds.’ She gave me a book to sign in my time. A landline phone that was next to them was ringing off the hook the entire time. It was a customer line. They both proceeded to exit the room and bawl 'Answer the phone! Answer the phone!’ to the frantic staff. I felt uneasy being amongst them and went to do some deliveries. Every customer I reached to had a severe tongue lashing ready for me. 'Tell me why I should pay for this. Three hours now I waiting.’ I had to put on my most pathetic and mournful face and give my most eloquent excuses just to get paid without hassle by almost every customer. ''I'll never order from you all again. What's your name?’ I must've heard that statement 50 times in just an hour. Meanwhile, inside the restaurant, things just never seemed to quell, only intensify. The phone kept ringing incessantly and 9 out of 10 times it was an angry customer yelling obscenities about waiting 5 hours for his/her order. 'Answer the phone. Answer the phone.’ yelled the manager and her master from inside the office. Suddenly the air conditioner malfunctioned. Now we had to contend with the chaos and blistering heat of a massive pizza oven in a closed in building. A fight broke out amongst two customers. Security was dragged into it. A customer used that opportunity to threaten to jump across the counter if he didn't get his order now. Thankfully police came to disperse some of the crowd and warn the restaurant about not following COVID protocols. 'Answer the phone. Answer the phone.’ yelled the managers. I looked at one of the supervisors who was glued to the phone from the minute she arrived. She was an old acquaintance and I liked her. Sadly she was overweight and suffered from high blood pressure. She was trying to answer the phone to the best of her abilities and take orders\deal with irate customers. She had two pages full of orders she scribbled that were to be entered on the database. Everytime she tried to enter them the phone kept ringing, preventing her from doing so. In the end she decided to ignore the calls to focus on entering the orders. The area manager was passing by and observed this. 'Sharon,' the area manager said stoically, 'Why aren't you answering the phone? Do we have to have a chat in the office?’ I felt an overwhelming rage hearing that comment that wasn't even directed to me. I watched Sharon as she gave a look similar to swallowing a frog, wiped the sweat off her face and replied calmly, 'Ms. A, I have almost two pages full of orders still to enter into the system from since an hour ago. I'm trying.’ The area manager looked confused and then glanced at Sharon's list. 'Somebody else answer the phone,’ she yelled, 'Somebody answer the phone!’ She then looked at her watch. 'Oh I have to pick up my daughter,' she said to Ms. K. They exchanged some pleasantries and the area manager left to return in a few hours. Ms. K. returned to her office and closed the door. The chaos continued as the heat intensified. At one point I felt I was going to have a mental breakdown. There was absolutely no order or plan and everyone basically just tried to stay afloat in their little corner amidst a towering pile of tossed aside pizzas; wrong and cancelled orders. Out front was an army of angry customers who looked ready to riot kept shouting to get some kind of attention. The phone kept ringing and ringing and ringing. The two workers who were sorting out orders condescended to just handing out random pizzas and hoping for the best. Whenever I answered the phone and an angry delivery customer demanded for his/her order placed 5 hours ago, I was forced to lie and say that the order was on its way, despite the fact that it was never entered on the database. I was relieved to go on deliveries, anything to take me out of that madhouse. After returning from a severely disgruntled customer of whom I had to give an exceptional performance of sorrow and misery, begging her to pay for the order, I returned to the restaurant, parked the motorcycle and was thinking to abandon the job. I was seriously considering just leaving without a word. I did not want to face more chaos and madness and 'Answer the phone’ anymore. However I realized that that would make me a coward. I entered the restaurant and to my relief, as the sun set, the crowd died down and things were starting to get manageable. I started helping customers source their orders when I observed Ms. K. arrive in her car and exited the vehicle holding a large cake. I assumed that this was a token of appreciation for the staff and the hellish day that they had. I thought that was quite nice of her. She took the cake into her office. A few minutes later the area manager returned and went into the office. Ms. K then announced for all the supervisors to come into the office and whilst the rest of staff toiled in the unbearable heat we could hear strains of 'Happy Birthday to you’ emanating from the room. The cake was not for us. It was the area manager's birthday. The area manager took the cake and thanked Ms. K. Without a word to the rest of staff she left with her cake in one whole piece while the rest of us stood there in disbelief and disgust. Thus ended the opening day of the restaurant. The next day, Sunday, I got word that three employees had quit, including Sharon the supervisor who had almost a decade of service with the company. I told myself that the storm was over and today would be much more pleasant. Boy was I wrong.

Question: What is something Supernatural that you Witnessed, that you know no one would believe you about?
Answer: My aunt and uncle left me alone in their house a night as they went to have their anniversary dinner. I was around 13 years old and felt like a King for that brief moment. After helping myself to many of their premium snacks my stomach churned and I needed to go use the toilet. While I was sitting there a strange phenomenon occured. Directly ahead of me a single ceiling tile lifted upwards, then the one in front of it, then another and another. In a straight line they lifted, with half second intervals. Outside of the bathroom and along the hallway I could hear the procession of lifted ceiling tiles. There was no wind outside. Even if there was, several tiles would've been lifted and rattled all at once in a brief flurry. I could think of no plausible explanation that could make ceiling tiles lift upwards in a singular straight line procession with half second intervals. No animal could cause tiles to be lifted in that manner unless they crawled/walked about with suction shoes of sorts. When it finally stopped I was numb with fear. The event had allowed for my bowels to unintentionally finish its duty much faster than usual. After, I ran out the bathroom and waited in the kitchen where the entrance door was located. When my Aunt and Uncle returned I frantically explained to them the entire story sparing no detail. In shock I watched as they began to laugh at my story and nonchalantly pour themselves a nightcap as they readied themselves to retire to bed. They didn't seem to take it serious at all. My aunt eyed me looking solemn and appeared to have considered my story for a few seconds. 'Did you flush the toilet Elijah?’ Did I? Everything happened in a blur. I ran to the bathroom and saw that in fact I didn't. I felt humiliated as I flushed. It felt like my experience was flushed also. Such is the sad reality of 13 yr old boys like myself trying to convey supernatural experiences to their dismissive relatives.

Question: What is the creepiest thing that happened to you and you never forgot?
Answer: (image altered for legal reasons) For a few hours, a grown ass man like myself experienced exactly how a female feels to be manipulated by someone you place your trust and sexually harassed. I was 22 and out of a job. I became so desperate I went to my old Secondary (High) School to ask for a job recommendation letter from a teacher. Unfortunately I arrived at the school too late as most of the teachers had left. There was this large, hulking man with a shiny bald head, dressed professionally and with a calm, collective manner about himself. I never saw him before. He introduced himself to me as Mr. O.J, a new substitute teacher. He was somewhere around 6 feet tall, looked well over 200 pounds of muscle and could be somewhere in his late 20’s to mid 30’s. I took a shot in the dark and asked him if he could write a recommendation for me. He diplomatically replied that it would be dishonest of him seeing that I was never his student. I respected his honesty and was about to bid him adieu when he stopped me and asked if I was interested in becoming a teacher. ‘Yeah,’ I replied. I told him how I tried to apply with the Ministry of Education but they kept turning me away. He then explained to me that he knows a secret method to get into the teaching service. That this method got him his job the day after he applied. I asked if this ‘secret’ was basically him having some connection with some big shot in the Ministry of Education. He said no. He explained that it was much more complicated and that he couldn’t discuss it here because he could get himself into trouble. I inquired as to whether he was going to use this method to get me into the service. He replied that he would help me. He said to leave my number and he will make the necessary calls and arrangements and he would get back to me when I’m successful. I gave him my number, thanked him and left. As I exited the compound I thought it was kind of strange that he found it dishonest to write a simple letter of recommendation, yet he would take a leap of faith and expose his ‘secret’ to secure me a job as a teacher. I simply told myself that he was just a nice, helpful guy. That very evening I got a call from him. There was a rather playful tone in his voice, much different to his professional manner earlier. He explained to me that I was in luck, his acquaintance in the Ministry said that there were positions for substitute teachers and if I wanted I could get a post in my old school. That was great news. I loved my old Secondary school and was missing it very much since I graduated 3 years earlier. He asked if I was interested. I told him very much so. He told me he would have to meet me somewhere so that I can sign the application form. I agreed to meet him Saturday. I was an Evening student at the University of the West Indies (UWI) and so was he, so we agreed to meet there as we both had classes that day. After the arrangement was confirmed I was hoping to end the call on a brisk, business-like note. Mr. O.J. however, became rather frivolous and began to ask me questions about my life while upkeeping silly, irrelevant banter. He kept referring to how I ‘looked like a player’ and that I probably had a bunch of girlfriends while I attended school. I felt awkward and slightly uncomfortable talking girly talk with a large, grown ass bald headed man. Thankfully this lasted but a few minutes as he took the hint that I didn’t like the direction of the conversation. He reminded me of the arrangement on Saturday and wished me a good night. I told myself he was probably lonely and lacking in the friends department. That could make anybody socially awkward. Despite the weirdness, everything seemed legit. I had not the slightest suspicion of any agenda. We were meeting in a crowded area at a respected institution. I knew his name and his place of work, so clearly any scheme from him could only put himself at risk career-wise. Or so I thought. We met at the University on a sunny Saturday morning. I was dressed casually in a pair of cargo shorts and a T-shirt. Mr. O.J. came eerily dressed in office wear even though it was the weekend and he was off duty. I was expecting him to come with a folder full of documents to sign but all he carried on him was a beaten up, old Netbook. I wished him good morning and he stared me deep in the eyes and smiled, replying good morning softly. It was then I realized that he had a habit of unflinchingly staring at me. I waited for him to explain what the hell was supposed to happen from here when he mentioned that he was hungry to the point of starving. He hinted whether I could see about getting the food while he find a spot where he could get a good WiFi signal. I thought this was a rather thoughtless and inconsiderate thing to suggest: I was unemployed with little funds to go about, he had a salary and was asking me to get him food. I couldn’t protest because I needed his help to get this job. The cheapest thing that I could get was some doubles (fried bread with chickpeas). I bought him two but couldn’t afford any for myself. I found him at some benches outside the gymnasium. Due to it being the weekend, the population was but a handful of students. Question: Which extremely surreal film would you consider to be worth watching?
Answer: The most fascinating surreal film I have ever seen has to be Fellini Satyricon (1969). Did I say most fascinating, surreal movie? I think I could go on a limb and say the most fascinating movie I’ve ever seen is Fellini Satyricon (1969). The movie should’ve been called Fellini Paradox or Fellini Irony . The movie makes absolutely no sense……yet it is understandable. The movie is stunningly gorgeous yet repulsive. It celebrates love and camaraderie yet blanketed in lust, hatred, envy and deception. It can be as richly interwoven as 1001 Arabian Nights, as profound as Shakespeare yet vulgar enough to make the Marquis de Sade proud. Encolpius and Ascyltus are strikingly handsome students in Ancient Rome. They both vie for the affection of Giton, an androgynous, underage male concubine of sorts. Their pursuit of Giton’s affections leads them to a dream-like odyssey involving pirates, hedonists, blood thirsty mercenaries, hermaphrodite demi-gods, minotaurs, women with flaming vaginas, sorcerers, impostor Caesars and the like. The story progresses in a somewhat fragmented nature due to the missing texts of the author Petronius. This can be jarring at first view but upon repeated viewing it adds to the enigma. However the most fascinating aspect of the movie is the production design by Danilo Donati. Despite whatever inherent historical inaccuracies, no film comes remotely close to this film in terms of costume, set design and just plain old aesthetics. This is definitely a love it or passionately detest it movie. However no one can deny its power to shock and awe.

Question: What are the best episodes of the original Twilight Zone TV series?
Answer: I think it's impossible to choose the best episodes of The Twilight Zone, however I can describe one of the most severely underrated. The Incredible World of Horace Ford No it's not scary. It's not spooky. It's barely even eerie. It's a profound reflection of changes of the past, childhood nostalgia and the how our ego manipulates many of us to believe 'things were so much better back then.’ *Spoiler Alert* Horace Ford is a gifted toy designer employed by a commercial toymaker. His talents stem from his ability to delve into the mind of a child and understand what appeals to them. However he's been having a midlife crisis of which, rather than brooding on the acceptance of incoming old age, he instead has mentally reverted back to that of a nine year old. He becomes silly and frivolous, neglects his job and throws tantrums whenever his employer and wife calmly try to reason with him. When he does open up about his problem he feverishly reminisces about the past, his old pals and how much simpler and better life was back then. His wife and boss try to explain to him that he is possibly fatigued and that he just needs to rest so he could get over this silly phase. Angered by their indifference he walks off his job and is magically transported back to his childhood. At first he is thrilled but gradually he is horrified to discover that his childhood was but a collection of poverty, overcrowded and dirty streets and his 'pals’ were mostly thuggish street urchins who bullied him. He is then transported back to the present where he confides to his wife what he saw and she reminds him that his childhood was actually traumatic but his ego manipulated him into believing it was great as a form of coping. He accepts the present and resumes his job, happy to find some closure in his life. Why I think it's great. Everyday we all hear a comment, whether online or in person of how much better things were in whatsoever decade. And so on and so on. Some of these comments are justified but many of them are coping mechanisms in regards to personal failures i.e. 'It's not that my life is a disappoinment. Life for everyone now is a disappoinment and here's the reasons why (refer to list above).’ I myself was guilty at some point of thinking like Horace Ford. That is until I chanced upon some old photos of me during childhood and it suddenly dawned on me things were better in a few aspects, but worse in many others. But no matter how bad things were, for many the ego would always try to romanticize the past and make it seem superior to the present. Baby boomers always talk about how great the 60s were despite the obvious issues of the period and their parents would speak highly of the 30s and 40s despite World War 2. This episode gives so much food for thought towards the question, 'Were things really all that great back then?’

Question: What is the smallest scam you have ever seen?
Answer: Back in 2003 I was a bit of a wacky, teenaged schoolboy. Heading home, I chanced upon a short, scruffy looking man selling a sad collection of pirated DVDs in front of the bank. I say sad because he didnt even have a proper DVD stand nor did he have those neat colored computer printed DVD jackets. No. He held in his hand a collection of cheap, brandless DVD-R discs upon which he scribbled in his unpleasant handwriting, random movie titles such as Love Don't Cost A Thing and National Security. I paid him no heed but then I heard him call to me, ‘Yo, yo check out what I got youth-man.’ I shook my head in refusal and continued past him until he spoke again. ‘Bank Girls Gone Wild my youth,’ he whispered loudly, ‘…local Trini girls.’ My ears pricked up. I went straight up to him. ‘You mean local girls naked?’ I whispered, ‘Naked? That is joke. These girls not just naked my youth……real rudeness.` ‘Bank girls? Even the girls from this bank?’ I said pointing at the bank behind him. At this point I was really excited. Such things were unheard of in our mostly conservative society. Also I was really attracted to one particular young woman who worked at the very bank he stood in front of. ‘Yeah’ he replied and showed me a DVD with no writing on it, ‘This here is bank girls from up north and central. You will see your girl on this DVD. I have bank girls from down south too.’ I was already sold at that point but something made me suspicious. ‘How come you didn't label this DVD? You sure it’s the right one you giving me?’ He was silent for a second then he replied, ‘You want me to get locked up? I can't go around showing everybody I selling Bank Girls Gone Wild…This is real black market business my youth.. So what you say? It's $25 for the DVD, over 3hrs of footage. I`ll give you this one together with the Bank Girls: Down South Edition for $40.’ I was expecting him to sell such a rare item for at least $100. It was a steal of a deal. I told him I just wanted the North-Central Girls DVD. I paid him his money and went home excitedly. No one was home so I immediately stuck the DVD in the player and waited. As the reader would've probably guessed by now, the DVD was a blank. I was scammed. I paid $25 for a generic blank DVD worth $7 max at retail value. I thought the guy would've been smart enough to take his scam to a different location but a few days afterwards I spotted him in front of the bank again, with his same DVD shtick. I went up to him. ‘Mister,’ I said angrily, ‘Gimme back my money or I'm going to the police.’ ‘Whoa youth man,’ he said in a surprisingly calm voice, ‘What is it with the bad vibes?` ‘You sell me a blank DVD. I want back my $25.’ ‘You sure it blank? You sure is not your DVD player not working?` He spoke so calmly and was so unintimidated with his confused and guiltless manner. I started to wonder if maybe I was wrong. Being a horny teenager who really wanted to see these nude bank girls didnt help my situation either. ‘Hear what,’ he continued, ‘I probably gave you the wrong DVD. I probably gave you a blank by mistake.’ He then pulled out a DVD that bore a B&W jacket showing a topless woman captioned Bank Girls Gone Wild: Director's Cut. If I had a tail like a dog, it would've been wagging. I was incredibly excited. ‘Take this copy and when you get chance, bring back my blank DVD for me.’ ‘Thank you,’ I cried while shaking his grubby hands excitedly. I went home and waited until late in the night while my family slept. I stuck in the DVD with more nervous anticipation than a defenseless goalkeeper seeing a star forward thundering towards him. BLANK DVD He did it go me again. However I couldnt help but laugh. He plotted his petty scam better than a Magnus Carlsen endgame. I had to be the biggest idiot on Earth, but it served me right. I never saw that guy again. He was smart enough to carry his scam to a different location. Edit 21.01.22. Ever had someone 'molest’ your food. Question: What was your mechanic scam that you caught that they never expected you to find?
Answer: Some mechanics will charge you based on how you look/dress. Not a scam but rather a form of stereotyping. For a period in my life I worked two jobs. During the day I had an office job in a Ministry in the Government and during the evening I worked pizza delivery. I drove a beat-up, old pickup that was over twenty years old and looked it. At some point in time I was badly overdue in terms of an oil change. I had a decent mechanic, Doc, who would not only change my oil but also my air, fuel and oil filters AND fix any minor issues that needed attention. For all this he would charge $150 TT ($21 US). This was an exceptionally good rate compared to the price and quality of service I got from all the other mechanics. Sadly, Doc began having health problems and I was forced to look for a new mechanic. I was informed of a father-son mechanic team who were known for great service and affordable rates. I took some time off my office job and headed towards their location probably looking a lot like this: I was in some of my best threads, sporting a new haircut and pair of glasses, full of confidence and dare I say, looking quite dashing. I did not intend to impress the mechanics, I was not even aware of how I looked. I was simply having a good fashion day. I introduced myself to the mechanics and explained my situation. I gave it my all to be as friendly, polite and sociable as I could and even offered to help bring over tools for them as they worked on my vehicle. During all this time I couldn't help but notice they were being rigidly formal and courteous with me, constantly referring to me as ‘sir,’ avoiding idle chatter and not showing any particular interest in me or my background. When they were finished, I went to the father mechanic and queried the cost. I was expecting $200 at most, maybe even as high as $250 seeing that they finished my job so speedily. However when I heard him nonchalantly mutter $500, my jaw dropped. ‘Five Hundred?!’ I cried, ‘How come so much?’ ‘We changed your oil, the air, fuel and oil filters,’ he explained lifelessly, ‘Aired your tires and eh…changed your gearbox and differential oil……that’s full service.’ ‘I didn’t want full service,’ I cried, ‘I just wanted my oil and filters changed.’ ‘Oil and filters changed?’ he replied almost stupidly, ‘That’s full service. Full service is $500. Isn’t that right Jason?’ He directed that question to his son who was in the process of jacking up someone’s car. ‘Yup,’ Jason replied monotonously without glancing, ‘Ask anybody here.’ There was a silence. I realized there was nothing I could do. I should’ve queried the cost before I allowed them to work on my pickup. I paid them their money and left, feeling thoroughly cheated and irritated, telling myself I would never do business with them again. Some weeks later I’m off to start my shift doing pizza delivery on a busy Friday evening. I’m nowhere near looking my best as I’m sporting a washed out and stained ‘Mario’s Pizza’ shirt, a beaten up red cap, a baggy and threadbare trousers and I’m in dire need of a haircut. My appearance was similar to the photo below but far more scruffy. I pressed on the clutch pedal, only to find that it was slow to rise up from the floor. Clearly my clutch had a bad fluid leak. If my vehicle broke down I would have to pay a fortune to hire a wrecker and quite possibly miss my shift. I saw that I wasn’t far from the father and son garage so I slowly guided the pickup into their compound. They saw me looking frantic and disheveled in my old pizza delivery clothes and immediately came to my assistance. I cut the pleasantries short and informed them of the clutch problem and how my manager would ‘have my ass if I took a day off on a Friday.’ They told me to calm down, that it wasn’t a serious matter. They began to jokingly tease me that they wouldn’t work on my pickup unless I brought a free pizza for them. They then proceeded to engage in idle chatter regarding fast food vs home cooked meals as they jacked up the pickup and put it on stands. I then realized that they didn’t recognize me with this shoddy uniform. They looked so much at ease and were so much friendlier than when I last visited them. Then the son got into his car, drove off and returned with a clutch slave cylinder and fluid and in two-twos they had my pickup back in order. I was quite impressed and grateful for the speedy service. However I cringed knowing that I would probably be slapped another $500 fee. I queried to the father mechanic as to how much my bill was and he said to his son, ‘How much you pay for that stuff Jason?’ ‘About two hundred,’ Jason replied. ‘Give us $250 pizza man. It’s your lucky day. Just make sure and bring us a pizza when you get the chance.’ ‘Of course!’ I lied. They barely charged for the labor. In fact they were much more fond of me as a salt-of-the-Earth, minimum wage earning, slave to the customer, regular Joe, plying his trade to make a living. They saw me as one of their own and extended a helping hand to someone who they believed roughed it out in life. Had they known that this was actually my second job and I had a comfortable office job in a Government Ministry, I would’ve seen a much different outcome. So I learned a decent hack in life when dealing with mechanics and various other tradesmen. I don’t work pizza delivery anymore but whenever I go to see those mechanics or go to meet plumbers, electricians, builders etc, I wear that old Mario’s Pizza uniform to counteract against their built in stereotypes. Doing this I find myself getting good rates, great service and making new friends much better than if I were wearing office wear and a fancy tie. C’est la vie! Edit 10.01.22. Those mechanics tend to scheme but you can find a way around them. They pale in comparison to the illegal scams some of our fast food restaurants attempt on a daily basis. Question: The Good, the Bad & the Ugly is an amazing movie but I never understood the scene involving Tuco and his monk brother. As much as it was an emotional scene, it did not advance the movie plot at all. Did Leone ever explain why he added the scene?
Answer: Yeah. Quite true. But then again, remember, throughout the movie, how often Tuco does this: Everytime he kills or someone is killed through his double crossing, he makes a sign of the Cross. Clearly he has a conflicted relationship with God. It paves the way for the reveal that he comes from a very religious background i.e. the scene with his disapproving monk brother. Admittedly, that scene sticks out like a sore thumb. I guess it was to give an emotional depth to Tuco`s character. It was meant to show that Tuco had a sympathetic, human side to him. Blondie had an emotional side as evident by the short scene where he shared his cigarette with the young, dying soldier. That scene was perfection. However Tuco`s emotional scene didn't play out so well. It tried a tad too hard. Tuco was well characterized and even without this scene one could sense that though he was bad, he wasn't evil. Tuco kept odd standards of decency, unlike Angel Eyes who was a psychopath. Before the monk scene, the movie had established a macho aesthetic of manly indifference. These guys were looking for gold, not for emotional closure. Then this overwrought scene comes in and goes on too long and is a bit unlike Tuco`s persona. He was too hardened from years of crime and debauchery to care about the opinion of his monk brother who he considered a fool or even his recently deceased father who he obviously didn't have a good relationship with. If I were Leone I would write the scene as Tuco`s brother (who is not a monk) informing him that he is headed towards their father`s funeral and grudgingly invites Tuco to pay his final respect. Tuco, feeling a bit remorseful and embarrassed considers the offer but reflects upon the possibility of Blondie escaping and the lost chance of getting gold, makes an excuse and declines. It would be less than 2 minutes long. But it isn’t too off putting and that is why to this day it's still my favorite movie of all time.

Question: What is the most obnoxious thing you have seen someone do at the grocery store?
Answer: Our local version of Costco is called PriceSmart. Isn't that a clever name? A lady in front of me, at the queue to cash, decided she was cleverer than me and all the fine people employed at PriceSmart. To shop at PriceSmart you have to be a member. You do this by purchasing a membership subscription card which allows you a year of membership. For the average Joe it's a tad costly ($265 TT) but the savings you get shopping at PriceSmart, more than makes up for it. I'm a very economical shopper and I tend to purchase only the bare necessities and would treat myself to something nice only once in a blue moon. This lady in front of me had a cart piled with groceries and also several treats ranging from frozen salmon burgers, Lindt, Toblerone and Mars chocolates, smoked almonds and ribs. Clearly she was not a poor lady. When we neared the cashier she suddenly turned around to stare me in the eyes. This is the conversation that followed. Lady: You don't mind if I use your card right? Me: For what? Lady: To cash. Me: You don't have a card? Lady: No. Can't afford it. I then stared at her pile of groceries tethering at the edge of her trolley. Her bottle of Grey Goose Vodka was almost $300TT but she ‘couldn't afford' a $200TT (at that time) membership. Me: It's only $200 for the membership and it takes just a minute. I saw her face suddenly transform into a look of complete irritation. It was as if I was asking her for the favour. Lady: I don't have the money right now. I just told you. People need to help each other. Me: Well I can't lend you my card. Lady: Why? Me: Because I don't know you. Lady: You need to know me to help me? At that point I remained silent. I didn't want to call her out for attempting to use random strangers for her financial convenience. I didn't want to argue that I spent my hard earned money on this membership and she ought to make that sacrifice also rather than gorge on her four rotisserie chickens as it was not my place to say. Instead she went to the man in front of her, giving him a sad story of how she just lost her card and this stuff is for her mother. The guy took the bait and lent her his card. She then stared at me as if to say, 'Got anything to say now?’ Clearly this wasn't the first time she did this and it definitely wasn't going to be the last. Some people may not see the big deal of what happened there but to me she is trash: a selfish and cheap opportunist. She is a leech on PriceSmart (who generates a profit from membership fees) and on the good people around her who make the necessary sacrifices for the greater good. Edit 24.11.21 Whoa. 5K upvotes. Question: What is the most condescending advice you received from someone who assumed you were poorer or less educated than them?
Answer: Well I definitely was poorer and chances are I was ‘less educated’ than him, but I could bet my last dollar I was much more intelligent. It was the year 2006 and Club ZEN in Port of Spain was the place to be for under 25s. This was to be my first trip to the famous club which was highest on the hierarchy of nightclubs. It was known to be a nest for the more privileged citizens of the country. I can’t remember the cost of the ticket but I remember after having paid for it plus my outfit for the night, half of my monthly salary was gone. But say what, I was young and without a care in the world. My blue collared friends from work and I arrived in a beaten up old, hired maxi (taxi-van). We had all pitched in to pay for this transport and to buy some Tequila of which we downed many shots before we arrived on the compound. When we arrived at the entrance there was a long queue. A few of us were wasted and must have made quite a raucous scene in our excitement. We were in great spirits despite the fact that we just hopped out of a beaten up old maxi and were clearly country bumpkins among these privileged youths, who lived up in the Hills and had their Range Rovers and Benzs waiting on them in the car park. There were two queues; one for general admission and one for VIP. We didn’t seem to notice the glaring looks some of the patrons gave us as we joined the VIP queue accidentally. Petra, the most countrified of us all, was quite drunk and became a bit paranoid. ‘Hey,’ she squawked, ‘I think we in de wrong line. Are we in the wrong line?’ She started looking about at the people around us who avoided her glances when this tall, silken shirt, cocky alpha-male behind us muttered, in proper Queen’s English, for us to hear. ‘Yeah, I really think YOU guys are in the wrong queue.’ He then proceeded to snigger with with his friends. All of them well over 6 feet tall, and dressed exquisitely in black with the top buttons of their shirts opened up to reveal their shaved chests. He then stopped sniggering and looked at us solemnly and said, with condescending, presumptuousness , ‘That’s General Admission across there.’ He pointed to a long line with many average Joes like us. We silently headed to the general admission line as Cocky Alpha Male and his buddies smirked and shook their heads at our embarrassment. The Bouncer then let in Cocky Alpha Male, his buddies and the rest of the VIP crowd. They went through the doors and upstairs to the balcony. We were let in afterwards with the rest of general admission as we remained on the first floor. What Cocky Alpha Male and his buddies didn’t realize was that VIP was used mostly by couples who wanted to snuggle and be comfortably away from the crowd. VIP was simply a long balcony overlooking general with a tiny. half-assed bar and a bunch of older couples making out in every nook and cranny……not exactly the experience Cocky Alpha Male and his buddies were hoping for. Meanwhile, ourselves in general admission were having a blast on the ground floor. General admission composed of younger individuals who wanted to party and socialize. Rich and poor, blue collar and white collar all mingled and got drunk and wined (Trinidad dance) up on each other. My buddies and I quickly forgot the encounter as we scored more drinks and partied like no tomorrow as strobe lights, fog and music encapsulated us in a euphoria. Suddenly in a moment of sobering clarity I saw that Cocky Alpha Male and his buddies were now swaggering around in the general section, obviously hunting for chicks. I went straight up to him and, as the music was loud, I gestured that I had something to tell him. He was drunk. He bent his ears downward for me to yell the message in his ear. I yelled, ‘Looks like YOU were in the wrong queue too!’ Edit 21.01.22 No. I'm not a wiseguy. I have my fair share of moments where I did/said some stupid or cringe things or got taken advantage of.
