Question: What was your scariest "something's not right" moment?
Answer: This is the Port of Scarborough of our sister island Tobago. Pay attention to the second floor of the building. It is quite customary for Trinidadians take their kids to Tobago for the Easter Holidays or for the summer vacation. Back in ’97 my mother carried us for the summer holidays. A week later, on a quiet Sunday night, we are at the above Port of Scarborough waiting for the late boat to take us back to Trinidad. It was around 9:00 pm and my family and I sat in the departure lounge awaiting the MF Panorama which was late as usual. The passenger population was quite small, rounding up to around 20–30 working class people like us. These were the days when WiFi internet was but a dream so the only entertainment for the passengers was a little, beaten up 32″ CRT television that, showed mostly static. Most of the passengers began to doze off, including my mother, older brother and younger sister. The only passengers that remained awake were a handful of old men playing cards, myself and a middle aged cotton candy (sales) man who had his colourful assembly of wares with him. I was age 10 and a rather naive and impressionable boy. The man, seeing me staring at his cotton candy beckoned me over and asked what was my favorite colour. ‘Yellow,’ I replied and to my surprise he plucked a yellow cotton candy from his arrangement and handed it to me. I told him I was going to wake my mother to get some money but he quickly informed me that it was for free. In my mind I recalled my teachers of years ago warning us kids, ‘Don’t take anything from strangers,’ but then again, my mother sat just a few feet away so there was no threat. I began to eat from the cotton candy and the man began speaking. ‘ [The] place really boring eh?’ I was amazed. He sounded just like my friends from class the way he phrased and uttered that sentence. It was rare that I heard adults speaking like kids. ‘Yeah,’ I replied happy to find a brilliant thinker like myself, ‘Why can’t they have a bigger TV here…..with cable?’ He then mentioned that he knew my father. ‘Really?’ I replied in awe. ‘Yeah,’ he continued, ‘Tall, red [mixed race] man…..what’s his name again?’ ‘Trevor.’ I replied. ‘That’s it,’ he said excitedly, ‘Trevor is my boy. Kinda loud sometimes.’ ‘Yeah!’ I cried, won over by such a description. ‘That’s my father!’ He asked how Trevor was going and I gave a long account as to my father’s history and personal problems, how him and my mother separated a long time ago. Then I spoke of school and my friends. He kept interjecting about my father and how sad it was that I didn’t have a father figure. It irritated me a bit but I continued nonchalantly chatting away to my new friend about every random thing that came to my mind. ‘Wanna see the ship sailing in?’ he said all of a sudden. ‘How?’ I replied. ‘Upstairs.’ he uttered quietly, ‘There is a nice view and you could see the whole ocean.’ ‘The whole ocean?’ I cried, ‘Can you see Trinidad from up there?’ ‘Yeah, of course,’ Cotton Candyman replied. We went up the stairs together to the 2nd floor lounge which was practically devoid of life except for one lady who stood at the rails staring at the ship that was a hundred yards away. Cotton Candyman took me to the furthest side of the room and we stared at the sea where he began pointing at made-up locations of where Brazil, China, India etc would be. The lady then left and suddenly I felt old Cotton’s arm drape across my shoulders. ‘I don’t have a son,’ he said in a suddenly more mature tone, ‘Only daughters…’ ‘Alright?’ I replied confusedly. ‘This feels good huh?’ I didn’t answer him. It didn’t feel good. It felt weird. He then tried to return to his child-like voice, ‘Ever want to travel the world?’ I thought he would’ve removed his arm by now but instead he gripped me tighter. Something definitely wasn’t right about this and to make it worse, we were completely alone. Suddenly a voice rang out from downstairs. ‘ELIJAH! Where the hell you gone? ELI-JAH? You gone upstairs with some man?! ELIJAH! ELIJAH!’ It was my mother’s voice. Apparently she had woken up and seen me missing. The old men playing cards informed her where I went and who I went with and she wasted no time in sounding the alarm. I was grateful for her intervention. I went away from Cotton and down the stairs where almost the entire population of passengers stood at the base of the stairs, eager to see who was Elijah, the would-be victim. My older brother stood swollen eyed and irritated from being startled awake. As I reached my family he mumbled something to the extent of, ‘Going upstairs with man Elijah? You gay or something?’ Rather than feel safe to be with my family and out of Cotton’s eerie grasp, I felt a world of embarrassment. My mother continued her big scene. She held nothing back, referring to the man as a rapist and sicko. A man ventured upstairs to get Cotton Candy but came downstairs saying the floor was completely empty. Cotton Candy had found some way to escape my mother and the concerned citizens below. I was rather angry at my mother for embarrassing me like that but as I grew older I became grateful for her quick witted reaction, saving me from being kidnapped or worse. Edit 20.1.22. Question: What did your boss ever say in the office that caused you to resign?
Answer: I once worked as a cinema usher and a projectionist for one of our local multiplex cinema franchises. I was quite young. I already had a full time day job in a warehouse, however I needed cash to do some driving classes as I prepared to get my license so I worked every night at the cinema. In general, that cinema tends to hire heavily during the summer holidays which is the peak season for moviegoers. Most of the staff hired would be college freshmen on holiday or teenagers just out of school. They would mostly be temporary workers and a lot of them had little work experience or knowledge of their rights and labour laws. As such, the management would usually take advantage of them. The first advantage they took was in terms of a fair salary. As I mentioned above I was an usher and a projectionist. I was trained to run the films upstairs and trained to deal with patrons downstairs. Management had the right to change my duty at will according to the situation. Many times, while ushering, if a projectionist did not show up to work for the evening shift or would be late, I was told to go and replace him at once. If you guessed that such an important role would allow for a higher salary than the regular ushers well then you guessed wrong. I had extra responsibilities for the same salary. To add insult to injury, Herold, the finicky supervisor would constantly come up into the projection room to throw a tantrum about how poorly spliced in the advertisements in the film roll were. He had a fetish for sneakily penciling in on the roster board a new lunch time for a random person and then afterwards yelling to that person, 'For the last time. You need to pay attention to your god-damned lunch roster. You have 10 minutes to get your lunch!’ As anyone could tell, Herold had no friends. Secondly the cinema didn't see the need to hire security. If Bin Laden came to see a movie, management wouldn’t bat an eyelash. This made it extremely difficult when dealing with mentally unhinged patrons. I remember collecting/tearing tickets and a large smelly man with mustard smeared all over his shirt walked past me without his ticket. I yelled at him to come right back and show his ticket and he started doing an insidious belly chuckle while telling me that he already gave it to me. I told him he would have to leave and he came up to me and threatened that there would be some problems in here if I continued to harass him. I ran to Martha, the manager, and explained to her that there's a madman without a ticket threatening me. She started laughing to my displeasure and then nonchalantly said that I just met Bo, the nickname for an aggressive, mentally challenged man who comes into the cinema once every summer. She advised that I leave him alone because he gave the last guy who tried to force him out a black eye. Thirdly and the final straw was how unconcerned and unsympathetic the management were towards their staff. I developed an eye infection during the time the film The Dark Knight was having its weekend premier. This was the summer blockbuster of 2008 and management were like headless chickens ensuring they squeeze every ounce of cash from the long lines of patrons who came to see the movie. They pressured the ushers to clean the cinemas as quickly and efficiently as possible. They gave us two minutes (average time was usually 10 minutes) to have the cinema spotless before they let a new batch of patrons inside. They pressured the concessions staff to have the ice bins kept full and for the nachos and hotdogs to be made at lightning speed. Projectionists were cutting and splicing in advertisements into the film roll like mad. Rather than the usual 10 - 15 minutes, there was a solid 30 minutes of advertising before the trailers began. The day before I had gone into the office and explained to Martha my eye condition. My eyes were all red and somehow exceedingly sensitive to light. I felt searing pain and could barely open them, even in the dimly lit cinema. I asked to wear a pair of sunglasses until my eyes cleared up. Martha was busy looking at schedules and distractedly muttered 'Ok yeah.’ The Saturday premier was like a nightmare. Two ushers and a projectionist waited for that day to quit the job in a show of spite. The lines to see the movie stretched far out of the cinema and throughout the outside food court. All of us short-staffed ushers had to get our hands dirty sweeping the floor, cleaning popcorn kernels and nacho cheese off the seats and ripping tickets of eight separate cinemas before the next huge crowd was ushered in. Martha was in a devilish mood and while passing me she glanced at me wearing my sunglasses. She assumed I was trying to look like James Dean and bawled up at me in front of the line of patrons to take off my stupid shades otherwise I would be fired. My friend Alex was there with me (he was a friend from my day job at the warehouse who decided to come make some extra income also) and we looked at each other. I did not take off my sunglasses but we both took off our silly bowties and jackets and handed them to her. We told her that we were quitting effective immediately. 'Quit? Who say you could quit? YOU CANT QUIT!’ The manager shouted but we simply walked off and towards the exit. We had had enough. I asked Alex what he wanted to do now and he said he was hungry. There was a KFC right outside and it offered a good view of the interior of the cinema through the glass walls. We got some chicken and sat to watch the fireworks as Martha and Herold ran around like maniacs trying to deal with hundreds of angry movie goers and run the film at the same time. It was better than any movie I ever saw. Edit 10.01.22. Did you like this? Find out why I always rejected an invitation to one of my former workplaces Christmas party. The nerve of some people. Question: Have you ever gotten into a fight with someone you vastly underestimated? What did you do?
Answer: Approximately a year ago, while working pizza delivery, I was chatting up an attractive, young (and admittedly busty) co-worker named Alia. She came from a tough neighbourhood and would constantly tease me that I was the kind of person, if the restaurant ever got robbed, I would be cowering on the floor in tears or that I looked like the type of guy that was bullied left, right and center at school. As a male, when you work in the fast food industry, spending several hours in close proximity of mostly female co-workers, your sex drive seems to hit the roof. I was no exception. I took her childish taunts to heart (she had a fetish for provocation) and I secretly wanted to impress her with my physique, courage and athleticism (when you work double shifts on a busy Friday at a pizza restaurant, you tend to revert to a more primal version of yourself). We observed the security guard having a tough time with a drunken customer. A hairy little hobgoblin, who looked a bit like comedian Aziz Ansari, was pestering the cashier and the customers. He made a game of jokingly claiming other people's orders and when he was confronted he began cursing the cashier that his order was taking too long and that if he didn't get his order in the next 5 minutes he would take back his money. He did this repeatedly but the third time the guard had had enough and told him to take his money and get the hell out of the restaurant. I observed in slow motion as the little pest struck an ineffectively dandyish slap across the guard's cheek. The guard, waiting for any excuse to get physical, attempted to drag him out by force, but due to advanced age and poor eyesight he recieved a sucker elbow to the belly and found himself in a headlock by the little squirt. Alia gave me the ‘Well, aren't you gonna do something?’ look and I assessed the situation carefully. I figured to myself it would be a piece of cake to grab little Aziz from the back with a solid bear hug. I would apply pressure on his waist while locking his arms thereby freeing his grip of the old security guard. Afterwards, for a bit of show for Alia, I would suspend him off the ground and calmly walk him towards the door and neatly throw him out like garbage. 'Oh it's on!’ I told myself. The idea seemed fool proof, especially since my target was drunk. I sneakily approached him but in that eerie sixth sense that drunk people sometimes possess he felt my presence and cast a glance my direction knowing that I was going to take action. He released the security guard, ready to deflect my attack, but I managed to grab by him the waist. He flailed about like a trapped warthog and I was astonished the amount of resistance he put up as he almost flipped me over like a rag doll. Thankfully I managed to hold on but with massive exertions of energy. Little Aziz had a huge reservoir of stamina, shoving and wiggling as though his life depended on it. Even though he was the one that had a vice like grip across his stomach, I was the one running out of breath and energy. Little Aziz detected this and I felt my heart race as I realized he was freeing himself from my grip and with my overwhelming state of fatigue, he would give me the biggest thrashing in my life. Luckily for me two male customers, construction workers, intervened and gripped Aziz into submission and escorted him off the compound. I held my chest into the air but my stomach and back felt like bursting from overwork. I had to run to the staff washroom to get a ten minute breather. How the hell did that little drunken bastard have so much energy? I thought about it as I sat on the toilet. I then heard Alia's voice outside the door. ‘You alive Elijah?’ In a feeble voice that sounded as though I just crawled the Sahara desert I replied, ‘Yeah…’ I was expecting Alia to make some sort of comment about the fight or query as to my health but instead she said, ‘Well hurry up in there. I want to use the toilet. You taking long.` I came out the toilet groaning inwardly as I felt as though my left kidney was upside down. She hurried in the toilet without a word. She didn’t give a rat's ass about me or the fight. Alia was only concerned with nature's duty at the moment. I was a bit relieved though because anyone with an inkling of fight sense would know that I was a breath away from getting a major whooping from Yosemite Sam. If she had more fight sense she would've had material to taunt me for the rest of the week. As I touched the door handle to exit the washroom I heard her voice again. ‘Short man nearly beat your ass Elijah. You not feeling shame?` *Lessons Learned: 1. Only an idiot would try to impress a girl by fighting. 2. Don't underestimate short people. 3. Unless you're as big and heavy as Tyson Fury, you'll get your ass whooped trying to bear hug someone into submission. Edit 10.01.22 I’m a lover not a fighter…….or maybe I’m neither. Little Aziz was just a drunk pest. I can deal with people like him. I can’t deal with these type of people. Click here to see who I’m talking about.

Question: What is the most enigmatic final scene in a movie?
Answer: When I was much younger I was flipping through the channels late on a Friday night. I came across this movie on TCM showing a larger than life, indefatigable, 1000 watt smile Burt Lancaster as Ned, a charismatic, middle aged man who seems to have it all. He decides to make a mission for himself by swimming through all the neighbouring pools in the affluent Connecticut suburbs where he resides until he reaches his own home. The name of the film is The Swimmer (1968) There was something so odd yet idealistically profound about the film and the protagonist’s childish yet charming personality and mission. Not to mention the sunny weather, gorgeous locale of endless pale blue pools, sprawling, neatly trimmed lawns and quietly impressive Westport houses of which the protagonist encounters several friendly, laid back and sometimes eccentric friends and acquaintances. *Warning. Spoilers and Summary Ahead* The films has a surreal quality as the barechested Ned gallops from house to house diving into everyone's pools and having friendly chats with neighbors and friends. Ned seems to live an idyllic life. He speaks of his loving wife and two daughters, takes pride in his physical prowess and stamina and is apparently financially successful. He encounters a beautiful young woman, Julie, who was his daughters' babysitter in the past and passionately persuades her to come along on his odyssey. It is evident that Julie is naive from the conversations she has with Ned. While laying on a grassy nook, she admits that she had a crush on him when she was younger. It is then that we begin to see a darker side of him as he uses his power of charisma and passion to try to seduce her. Despite her protests Ned attempts to groom her into believing he can protect her, all the while touching her inappropriately and advancing upon her. Julie runs off frantically. From this moment it is clear that Ned is far from the superhuman image he tries to present. He continues his journey but the farther along he goes the less warmly he is received. He invites himself to a pool party taking place along the way. His passion and charisma of wooing women to come with him on his swimming mission is seen by women to be a cheap hook-up scheme. He is shoved to the ground after an argument with a man and is forced to shamefully depart. It is now clear that the effervescent Ned may be, in reality, a loser. He intrudes upon the home of a former mistress of years past and attempts to seduce her only to be aggressively rejected. He goes to his last stop, a crowded, public swimming pool. He is harassed by several shopkeepers for outstanding bills and insulting allegations are made of his wife and his daughters. We see Ned's optimism and charisma disintegrate as he runs off from them up a rocky hill towards his home. We see the sunny weather make way for a thunderstorm just as the 1000 watt smile is replaced by a look of utter dispair as Ned collapses at his doorstep. He is locked out of an abandoned house with broken windows. It is now certain that the Ned we witnessed at the very beginning is but a charlatan, a shell of himself in a desperate attempt for acceptance from a world that he was once a part of. Everything that led to this moment now becomes an enigma.

Question: What best-selling book was just not for you?
Answer: By a looooooooooooooong shot The Beach by Alex Garland is the worst bestseller I’ve ever read. The funny thing is, I love the film version starring Leo DiCaprio and directed by acclaimed director Danny Boyle. This may be an unpopular opinion but Alex Garland to me is a terrible writer. He is gifted with imagination but awful at expressing his imagination. The book reads like if a 15 year old was trying to impress his teacher that he can write a book all by himself. Examples: [it was like] looking at the universe (describing the protagonist viewing plankton underwater) it smelt of death (describing the smell of the tent of a shark bite victim) ‘Uh-huh’ (actual dialogue used several times by different characters) The dialogue is so bad, I can’t tell who is speaking at times because everyone speaks in a sarcastic, non-committal manner. The pacing is all over the place that at times it veered towards adventure, then drama, then suspense, then surrealism, then back to adventure. But most of all: The protagonist is the most irritating protagonist I’ve ever had the misfortune to read. For anyone who found Leo DiCaprio a bit too high strung and irritating as the lead in the film, believe me, he made magic happen considering the asshat the protagonist Richard was in the book. In the novel he’s this moody and irresponsible narcissist who’s supposed to be in his mid-twenties but acts like a 13 yr old, a spoilt and privileged 13 yr old at that. He loves attention. He is envious, spiteful and is easily manipulated. He clearly has an inferiority complex that even the author himself doesn’t seem to acknowledge. Worst of all, he’s written in the first person. You are stuck in his detestable brain while reading this novel. However Garland writes him as though we’re supposed to root for this ass that it begins to feels like swallowing migraine inducing tablets the more you read. I tried my best but had to quit at 85% completion as it got worst as the story progressed. I read the summary of the last chapters……. without spoilers, all I could say is that Danny Boyle’s film turned vinegar into wine with that wannabe Stephen King-on-acid ending Garland wrote in his novel. Question: What are some of the most stunning yet most terrifying images?
Answer: When I was but a preteen, I came across a book of the supernatural and under 'The Flying Dutchman’ an image of this painting was included. Something about the image haunted me for years to come. Firstly was the strangely breathtaking yet ominous sunset that gave me a eerie 'deathbed’ feeling. This made the fact that the ocean was in the midst of a freak storm incongruous and unearthly. It's as if the appearance of the ghostly ship in the sky had some sort of cosmic power over the Earth. The men, clearly on the verge of being drowned, seem to be in a trance at the surreal beauty of this golden phantasm. I never discovered the name of the artist, in fact I never came across the image for the next 20 years. The image randomly passed through my mind recently and I decided it was time to end the mystery. With a simple Google search I found out that the artist was an eccentric 19th century American artist called Albert Pinkham Ryder (1847 — 1917). His oeuvre is quite fascinating as most of his paintings employ that haunted, moody atmospheric theme. I think his work is quite fascinating and worth checking out. I think he is grossly underrated so please allow me to share a few more images of his works. All photos courtesy Google.

Question: Who’s the most unfunny comedian?
Answer: Eric André Ever had a kid in class who was just desperately unfunny but desperately persistent to get attention. I mean just really, really desperate….faking fart noises desperate. When I see Eric André’s antics I’m reminded of that kid in class. I know comedy is subjective. A Chris Rock fan may not find humour in Zach Galifianakis and vice versa. Despite their different styles, they set about with the goal of entertaining their audience, as best as they can, in a harmless manner. André’s style of so-called shock/cringe comedy is to irritate, harass and disturb unknowing victims to entertain a tiny niche of Adult Swim viewers who find public harassment funny and entertaining. His claim to fame is his public pranks where he puts a group of unknowing people in awkward, uncomfortably bizarre situations such as acting like a mailman reading people’s mail out loud on a train and basically just wearing a random, odd costume and scaring/unsettling people around him. Overall I consider André a slightly unhinged narcissist with a fetish to disturb and unsettle people as much as the limits of the law allows. He is like the modern day version of Otto Muehl, a perverted Austrian hack who created a drug induced, minor grooming cult that would go to extremes (public nudity/sex, defecation etc) to disturb and unsettle the public under the veil of performance art.

Question: Have you ever had a bad church experience?
Answer: Some years ago, I was interested in a girl I met through a friend. Let's just call her Lula. Lula was highly religious and she subtly let me know that she was not dating a man unless he 'walked with Jesus.’ I decided that I should indeed become reacquainted with God as I hadn't been to church in several years. She invited me to her church. She was a member of its Youth Group, SRRCY or the San Raphael Roman Catholic Youth. The church was located in a small town in the countryside called San Raphael. I came there after work on a Tuesday around 6pm. The congregation was quite small. Apart from the Youth Group members, there were only five other people, myself included. The youth members all wore SRRCY labelled polos in green or blue. Before the service began many of them came to me, one by one, to welcome and make idle chatter, each bearing a wide smile. They all asked the same question at some point in time: 'Did you bring anyone with you?’ Each time I replied in the negative they would advise me to bring a friend, family or coworkers next time I came. I saw Lula upfront and sat next to her. I was expecting to see a bright smile and get a warm welcome but instead she gave me a confused look and said, 'You didn't bring anyone with you?’ I explained to her that my family weren't keen to attend church on a Tuesday but she didn't seem to be listening so I became faintly annoyed. The service then began with the priest giving a sermon on redemption. He was likable and spoke in a down-to-earth, informal style and related personal stories rather than Bible verses. He asked if there was anyone new in the congregation. Myself and two other guys raised our hands. We were asked to introduce ourselves. I went first and gave my name Elijah (which they cheered for as it's a Biblical name). I explained that I wanted to get closer with God and that I hadn't been to church in ages. When I sat down Lula glared at me angrily and asked why I didn't let everyone know that she was the one who invited me to the church. I wondered what was the big deal when I noticed the other two guys name-drop their inviters while introducing themselves which made me lose points with Lula. Then things started to take a turn for the surreal. One of the youth members, a thin, sickly looking girl around age 23 who sat on the same pew with us started to shake and convulse. She fell to the ground and started to foam at the mouth while uttering indecipherable gibberish in a vicious tone. Instead of telling everyone to clear the way and give this poor, delirious girl some air while he called the ambulance, the priest told the SRRCY to gather around her and pray for her. They all gathered around her while she twisted and contorted her body while sticking out her tongue at the SRRCY and laughing maniacally while they said their prayers. Honestly, I felt a bit frightened. I watched Lula as she pulled out her rosary, bent down and held the possessed girl by the back of the head and started praying intensely. The possessed girl made some nasty gurgling noises and all of a sudden Lula's phone began to ring with the ringtone of Robin Thicke's Blurred Lines. It was quite a macabre yet awkwardly funny sight to behold this possessed girl twisting and squealing while Blurred Lines played in the background. Finally Lula grew angry and paused her prayers to whip out her phone and angrily sent a WhatsApp text to whomever was calling her. After resuming her prayers, the demon was exorcised about two minutes later. ~~~~~~~~ Twenty minutes after the service was ended. The possessed girl had resumed her place on the pew as though having Satan exorcised from her body was as common as recovering from belly cramps. She even had a healthy glow about her. They SRRCY all got together and congratulated each other for another good service and they went around with the priest reminding everyone to bring more people with them next time they arrived. I volunteered to give Lula a ride home. However she and the rest of the SRRCY stood having idle chatter at the entrance of the building for ages. Even the formerly possessed girl, who only a few minutes ago, was on the ground contorting and blaspheming in an unknown demon-language was there chatting in good spirits. Finally they decided to part and Lula hopped in my van. While I drove she asked how I found the experience. I replied that it definitely changed my views on certain churches, priests and church youth groups. I didn't elaborate on what I meant by that because I noticed that she wasn't even paying attention. Her phone was ringing again. Edit 1.11.21 Thank you for all the upvotes. A commenter asked for a link to the parish and in doing so I've managed to glean some photos from their Facebook page. Question: What experience changed your perception on something?
Answer: Vachel was weird. He was a boy who attended my class at primary school. I dont have a photo of him but he had a strong resemblance to the boy above. I attended a somewhat prestigious school for boys and all of us boys found Vachel eerie. We wondered if he was an alien. Why? Vachel never got a single answer wrong in quizzes. Ever. Vachel always scored 100% in the science based subjects. Had it not been for the subjective creative writing essay, he would've had a flawless portfolio. He had a legendary reputation throughout the school and his name was always cited whenever teachers spoke of academic success. As would be expected, he wasn't well liked by many of the boys in class. Because he was somewhat dandy-ish and spoke in a flat, emotionless, baritone voice, the boys in class would secretly refer to him as ultra-nerd, faggot, Spock and all kinds of derogatory labels. He was aware of this but was not the confrontational type of person. He was also seen as an eccentric loner. This was '97. The year of Titanic, who was the hottest Spice Girl, Street Fighter vs Mortal Kombat etc. Vachel would participate in none of these 'ordinary boy’ discussions. We all figured him to be an oddball, only-child, living with wealthy, aged parents in a crumbling estate and his hobbies were listening to opera while playing chess or reenacting Shakespeare to an imaginary audience. Well that was how the cartoons portrayed genius level boys. As it so happened, I was to stay at a relative's house for a week. After school, while about to travel to that location I saw that Vachel was heading the same way and learned that he lived not too far from my relative. We boarded the bus and sat together and for the first time I had a conversation with him. Expecting the conversation to be awkward, I was quite surprised how good of a conversationalist he was. He was quite interested in hearing about my relatives and family. I felt comfortable and basically gave him my whole life story during that time. I didn't even bother to ask him about his family but that didn't bother him. We stopped off at the town of San Juan and he told me he wanted to show me what he liked to do in his spare time. I was a little hesitant, thinking he would carry me in a lab and experiment on my brain but instead he carried me to a book store. I wondered what was the big deal. Neither of us had money and if I did I definitely wouldn't spend it on a book as I had loads home. He took me to a section of the bookstore that had some novelizations of movies. He showed a Ghostbusters 2 novelization, a Return of the Jedi novelization and then he asked me to close my eyes as he had a secret to show me. I did so and when he told me to open my eyes he held a Batman and Robin novelization in front of my face. He was excited because the movie had only premiered a few months ago. I never saw such joy in his face. He then started speaking softly as though he was describing a crime he had committed. He whispered that what he does is that he comes into the bookstore daily. He reads a few pages of these movie-books and would leave before a worker catches him. With pride he said that he had ‘seen’ all the popular movies without paying the price of a single movie ticket, by simply reading a few pages a day of these novelizations. He then hid the Batman book behind some older novels and said that someday, when he has saved the money, he will come back and buy this very book, so he can ‘watch the movie' at his leisure. I was thoroughly confused. The little rascal in me wanted to laugh at him and his 'secret.’ I wanted to ask him, 'Why don't you just watch the movie? Most of these show on cable every day’ when something suddenly caught my eye. In his excitement his shirt became untucked from his pants and I saw that his shirt was much too small for him. Then I realized that his pants had an inkblot on the left leg through which I recalled he always had that same inkblot, every day. This meant that he had but one pair of pants. Then I recognized that his shoes were oversized, almost clownish, they had to be hand-me-downs. It then struck me. Vachel was poor. As in really really poor. This coming from someone from a family of lesser means. As I listened to him going off about how he feels sorry for Mr. Freeze and his dead wife, I felt like crying and giving him a consoling hug. While us boys in class rattled on about shows and movies we saw on cable, trips to the cinema and video games we played on our personal gaming consoles, Vachel was home with none of those luxuries, forced to entertain himself with his school books. His ‘genius’ simply came from the fact that he had nothing else to occupy his time but read whatever books he possessed. He was in fact, a normal boy just like the rest of us. We left the book store and took a taxi together, heading homewards, up a hill. My suspicion was confirmed when he stopped off at a humble wooden house that looked ancient, almost abandoned, inside a dirt track. I saw his plump mother scrubbing at some clothes in a bucket under a tap. There was no sign of electricity available at the house. Vachel went and proudly pointed at me, his new friend, to his mother who cheerily waved. I awkwardly waved back as the taxi reversed out of the track and drove off. It was the first time I got a taste of how alienating and unfair baseless assumptions can be, especially for those who fall under them. Edit 02.02.22 I was a nice child at times. At times I could be naughty. Click here to see this fascinating prank I almost pulled off on my teacher.

Question: What is the scariest moment you have had in your own home?
Answer: This is a roughly 6 feet deep hole that I had dug in my front yard some years ago. It is dug to insert an electrical power pole and concrete and stones are poured to keep it in place. Doesn't it seem like a fun idea to play Rambo and jump in such a hole, cover it with dead leaves and braches and jump out to scare anyone who visits you? That's just the movies and no I did not do anything so silly. But in reality, you could possibly die by jumping into a narrow 6 feet deep hole. I say this because it almost happened to me: Here in the Tropics we have the dry season and the rainy season. I don't think I need to explain the difference. However in the rainy season we tend to get what is called the Hurricane season which is a period that characterizes long and heavy rain, thunderstorms and the occasional flash flood. My area is prone to flooding. This a view of my front yard and the road during an average Hurricane Season flood. (The pole at the center-right is where the hole was located.) My hole was dug during the dry season. However the not-too-wholesome electrician I hired who was to put in the pole delayed the job for months upon months until hurricane season reached. One day, I heard a faint squeaking noise coming from the hole. I looked in to see a cute little mouse fighting to survive in the 8 inches of water that remained in the hole due to rain. I couldn't help but feel sorry for the little bugger so I grabbed a piece of wood and stretched it towards it, thinking the mouse would gladly hop onto the wood and allow me to save him. It turns out the mouse would rather take its chances drowning. I had half the mind to leave the stupid creature to drown but my heart got the better of me and I decided to jump in and fetch the mouse by hand. I got in, carefully avoiding stepping on the creature. It was quite muddy at the base and hard to move because it was mostly clay. I picked up the little mouse and carefully extended my hand out of the hole and dropped him lightly on the surface where I would assume he scuttled off in great appreciation of me. I then tried hoisting myself out. However the entire area was slippery due to last night's showers. I couldn't get a good grip on anything due to the slipperiness, the lack of room to maneuver and because my feet kept getting stuck deep in the mud where I stood. I tried for several times but to no avail. I had no idea that this little hole would be such a challenge. Mind you I'm only 5’ 10 and don't have the wingspan of Michael Phelps. Regardless if I did, everywhere I gripped my hand slid on the clay mud. After several attempts my energy was depleted. Suddenly thunder boomed and a heavy rain started. My heart began to pulse. I realized that I could quite possibly drown here; if not from the rain filling this hole up then the possible flood afterwards. I yelled for help a few times but to no luck, the sound of heavy rain was competing with my yells. The only chance of anyone hearing me was if someone happened to be walking the road nearby. What are the chances of someone casually walking the road during a thunderstorm? I had to get out of this simple hole or drown like my mouse friend almost did. What a dumb way to die I might add. The water level in the hole was beginning to rise towards my knees. In a frenzied fit of desperation I found some reserve of energy and my brain started to click. I undid my mud soaked shoes which was causing additional heaviness, threw them out and like a cat on steroids I simply grabbed and flailed at the four walls with my hands, feet and back until I somehow managed to get a grip and lift myself out. Some fingers and parts of my back were bleeding from contact with sharp stones. I looked as though I just survived D-Day Normandy when all I did was come out of a small, muddy hole; an idiot who almost died saving a mouse. So take it from me if you want to live a long fulfilling life. Don't jump into muddy 6 feet deep holes, especially during Hurricane season. Edit: Wow I'm actually getting upvotes for this. You all care about my life. That's sweet. Here is another mouse (or could very well be the same one) I befriended during a flood a few weeks later. Edit 2: Many commenters are suggesting that I should've simply allowed the water in the hole to rise and simply float/paddle my way to the surface. Please. By all means, if this bizarre situation ever happens to you do not wait for that possibility. This wasn't a tiled pool but a muddy hole more narrow than a coffin. You can drown trying to free your feet from the thick, viscous clay mud that envelops your feet and the fact that your arms and legs have limited motion. Scream for help as best as you can and if that fails get your arse out of that hole by whatever means but do not wait for the water to rise on you. You might as well be buried there the following day.

Question: What's the best "tourist trap" you've ever fallen into?
Answer: Personally I've never fallen into this scheme but whenever I visit our tiny sister island of Tobago I roll my eyes seeing the amount of tourists who get caught in this trap. Imagine this… You’re on vacation with your family in the Caribbean island of Tobago, known for its stunning blue beaches and laid-back, bohemian lifestyle. As many tourists do, seeing that it's the closest beach to the airport, they spend their first day on Store Bay, the most commercially popular beach in Tobago. As you arrive down the steps, past all the numerous souvenirs, handicraft and food stalls, you look for a nice shady area on the sand to lay your beach towel and make camp. Unfortunately all the good spots are taken so you whip out that suntan lotion and decide to take in some Vitamin D because you'll be taking a dip in the water anyhow. Suddenly a sinewy barechested young man looking like this: Comes with a beach umbrella, and while taking puffs of his marijuana spliff, he stabs the umbrella into the sand amongst you, which provides much appreciated shade from the enhanced Vitamin D plus sunrays that are making you sweat. You think, 'Wow, what nice thoughtful people these Tobagonians are.’ You thank him but he doesn't seem to hear you. He leaves and you assume that the umbrella is complimentary of whatever tourism board is running the country as you notice practically everyone has an umbrella like yours. The man returns with a couple of beach chairs. You jump up ready to assist this helpful man. His mind seems distant as he stares towards the sea horizon as though expecting something. You say thanks again but he leaves without a word. You enjoy yourself in the sun and sea, taking a few splashes in the azure waters. Discussing plans for the evening with your spouse, watching the kids frolic on the sand. An old boat adorned in bright colours arrive on shore blasting music from its speakers. You see a bunch of people get up and head towards the boat. It's apparently a glass bottomed boat that tours the nearby beaches. The man magically appears behind you. ‘Yuh wah go on de glass bottom boat?’ he says. You take some time to translate his sentence and you quickly say yeah. He whips out a card of tickets and a pencil and writes a note under some tickets. He then leads you and your family to the boat and assists you all in helping climb onto it. What great hospitality! What great people! What a nice country! They really do go above and beyond for the tourists. These are the thoughts you think whilst enjoying the tour, staring at the beautiful sights while the children look at fishes and coral through the glass bottom. The tour lasts about two hours and when you return you decide that you will stay on the beach for the sunset. When the sun sets most people are leaving and you see your man along with others like him collecting their vacated beach chairs and umbrellas. You watch the sunset and fall in love with the country. Your man is somewhere behind you smoking another spliff and enjoying the sunset with you. However he seems to be scowling. You tell yourself that maybe that's just his countenance. Never judge a book by its cover. You decide to wrap things up and as you and your family assist in dusting off the beach chairs and folding and the umbrella, your man comes over with a few shirtless friends and takes over that duty. He is staring at you and you don't know what to say. 'Thank you for everything,' you say awkwardly, 'You've been so kind…..What's your name?’ 'Yuh have $1200 (TT) dollars for us sir.’ he says in a gruff, solemn tone while staring you in the eyes. His friends are poised nearby smirking at the scene. 'You didn't tell me you were charging me all this time! You didn't tell me the cost?’ You look at him and his men who look agitated and upset and you look nervously at the near deserted beach. You know that quarreling over money with a bunch of unknown, sinewy shirtless locals would not be a good idea given the circumstances. 'Brudda, if yuh don't mind’ said one of his friends, 'We real busy. Y’all went overtime. Jus pay we for our services nuh.’ He is saying this more as a growling threat than a request. You do your calculations. $200 US should cover the fee and give you back a little more than $100 TT change. You grudgingly give him the money. He looks at it, pockets it and he and his men leave without a word, laughing at something they were discussing, not even considering your change. You've just been schemed my good friend. Lesson #1 in coming to Tobago as a tourist. Absolutely nothing is free. Edit: Did not expect this little gem of advice to take off so quickly. But please be aware that these sort of schemes and unwholesome attitudes are mostly prevalent at Store Bay. The rest of Tobago is very easy going and trustworthy. The Government is doing its best to curb these type of characters from tainting our image. This is just a lesson to be on the alert if you do decide to visit our marvelous country. Edit 9.01.22: Those guys who try to scheme you with their beach chairs and boat rides in Tobago are nothing compared to the ‘trailer trash' of Trinidad. Click here to read all about it.

Question: What is the creepiest tree species in the world?
Answer: Ceiba pentandra or better known in Trinidad and Tobago The Silk Cotton Tree Behold the horror. Local legend has it that a West African witch called Gang-gang Sarah attempted to fly back to her homeland after freedom. She climbed the tallest of these beauties and, in a failed attempt to fly, fell to her death, forever cursing the tree which assimilated her corpse. As can be observed, the tree is very limby and sparse of leaves. Many of these trees, such as the example above, if you squint your eyes it looks like several human figures sprawled about in agonized positions. Legend also has it that it is home to supernatural creatures who reside among it or within its massive trunks. Our grandparents would tell us tales of hearing voices or strange noises when approaching these ominous beings in deep forests. Some would claim encountering douens (lost, unchristened demon-children) Or duppies (malevolent spirits) Or even Papa Bois (Father of the woods) himself whilst within range of these trees in the twilight hour. Besides being unsightly these trees can cause great infrastructural damage to roads and house foundations with their massive roots. In the past, only the most brave soul would dear cut down a silk cotton tree for fear of awaking the wrath of the supernatural. Nowadays, our more modern society sees these trees as giant grotesque headaches that need instant removal. Wouldn’t be surprised if they become endangered in the next 50 years. Sad but true. Question: What movie would you recommend every teenage boy sees before he turns 20?
Answer: Obviously these movies would be coming of age type movies. Hollywood, in my honest opinion, usually does a terrible job at capturing men as they blossom into young adults. Only two films have I ever seen that really struck a chord with that awkward period of life that a boy goes through before becoming a man. Dead Poets Society (1989) Dazed and Confused (1993) I know the question asked for one movie but I think it's very hard to limit the complexities of entering manhood with just one film. Dead Poets Society explores the pursuit of dreams, goals and aspirations. It focuses on coming of age as an individual with themes of listening to your heart, being yourself and thinking outside of the box with its famous 'Seize the Day’ catch phrase. Dazed and Confused is on the other end of the spectrum. It focuses on coming of age as a group as it celebrates camaraderie, taking time to enjoy life and the friends around you and passing the torch. These two movies have become modern classics because the presentation of the characters and the situations they undergo are accurate and relatable. In Dead Poets there are no stereotypical cliques and hardly any social hierarchy because they are all boys attending a prestigious boarding school. The only pressure the students undergo is not peer pressure but rather parental expectations and sexual frustrations. In Dazed there are cliques but they are not rigid and they integrate amongst each other. Nerds hang out with stoners who get high with jocks who tolerate bullies who look up to bad boys etc etc. In the end, the cliched good-natured geek doesn't knock out the cliched mean bully in a surprising 'didnt know my own strength’ moment but rather the pretentious intellectual gets beaten up for sucker punching an uncouth greaser. All in all I've seen no other movies captures the complexities of coming of age for boys than these two movies.

Question: What is the sneakiest thing you did in school?

Prior to this announcement we were sharing a modest apartment and no matter how much I tightened my belt I couldn't overcome experiencing great financial difficulties. Besides my day job I also got an income doing transport and lawn maintenance. Soon my vehicle started giving me no end of troubles and I could no longer spend money fixing it so I left it to rot. My credit card was maxed out and I was owing money to some of my friends. After paying rent I could barely afford groceries. My financial woes caused me to lose contact with my friends so when she and I argued (which was every week) and she stormed out, I was left destitute and lonely in a shabby apartment complex, no one and nowhere to turn. During one of these episodes, like an awful aftertaste, a notion came into my mind. You've made a big mistake. You're going to f**k this child's life up . I tried to laugh away the notion but it buzzed around my mind like some sort of devilish fairy. You’re just another deadbeat father who can't get it right. I started pacing around trying to get this notion out of my mind. My heart raced and my nerves were on edge. My head felt light and heavy at the same time. You've made such a big mistake. What the hell were you thinking? I took deep breaths and attempted to think positive thoughts. Then as though a floodgate was released, it came: panic attacks. I felt these strange sensations in my skin, these popping, spasmic sensations similar to the plastic bubbles that wrap your delivery that you pop unconsciously with your fingers. It was completely overwhelming. I sat down to try and breathe it away, mind-over-matter as I used to preach but it simply gave way to what I can only describe as the feeling of a heavy, stifling bog taking residence in my brain. It was depression. My back hunched over as my mind felt clogged and lifeless. I couldn't stop thinking of my problems and asking myself interrogative questions. I sat down in defeat, fearful for anyone to see me like this, fearful for the phone to ring. The worst thing about depression is that it tricks you into believing that your life was always a series of tragedy and sorrow, that this is how things are and has always been. It was as though my positive emotions and memories were locked away in a cellar, unrecognizable in an iron mask. I felt like a burden and a drain on other people's happiness. When I saw other people happy and proactive it only reminded me of how unhappy and useless I was. These sensations would usually happen during sunsets for some strange reason. My appetite was all but gone so was my passions and interests. At its peak I became emaciated, 30–40 pounds lighter than my usual self. This feeling came on a daily basis, first with a dose of panic attacks then sinking into that low, rotting, depressed feeling where my face literally looked like Eeyore from Winnie the Pooh. I would record my suicidal feelings on a rating from 1 to 10 and on many days I would record myself as high as 9. After my daughter was born I was terrified of getting the male version of post partum depression. Thankfully, I was lucky, the depression wasn't chronic and it waned to a point where only once a week I got those horrid familiar feelings but of a lesser intensity. After a year I was healthy enough to take up a second job, clear my debts and provide for my daughter whilst my mental demons were held at bay. Today, I am in a much better place mentally and financially. Not going to brag but I think I've accomplished a bit since depression first reared its ugly head seven years ago. However, it's comes back every now and again. Like a unwanted vagabond it shows up at my doorstep, bedraggled and defeated, but not yet dead and it stops me in my tracks to give me a taste of those familiar feelings of the past, (usually during sunsets). Depression is no joke. If you know someone who demonstrates any symptoms/behaviours such as I had/did, try your best to assist that person, without overwhelming them with pity and making a huge fuss. Be patient with such a person without coming across as though they are helpless. Just play it cool. Edit 21.01.22. Depression and other mental illnesses play a great role in relationships and with families. It is very difficult to be in a relationship with a spouse who suffers from mental illness. It can cause severe problems for future generations. Click here to read how it.

Question: What is the most recent underrated movie?

It’s quite sad the movie went somewhat unnoticed during it’s run, its biggest criticism being that it ignored the author’s Christian faith as one of his biggest inspirations. Question: What are the wrong depictions of the US in Hollywood movies?
Answer: When I think of a Hollywood movie that is far removed from any possible spectrum of realism, this movie always comes to my mind. You can tell by just watching the poster that this is going to be another formulaic family movie; the white background which signifies that this movie will have no content, dialogue or subplot other than this generic couple and their darned dog, the smiling figures staring at you almost sinisterly, the tepid humour of a puppy leading the couple by leash. “A dog leading its masters by leash?…….. that's so clever and ironic!” Sarcasms and cynicisms aside, here are the reasons why this movie is not just a wrong depiction of US life but an offense to ordinary people who tighten their belt and blue collar while slaving it on the 9 to 5. 1. Raising a dog = good practice for raising children, according to this movie. The above image perfectly captures how stupid that notion is. No one would watch a photo like this and and say that this is evidence of good parental skills. Besides feeding and caring there is nothing remotely similar to raising dogs as compared to children. This is a notion you tend to see solely in Hollywood movies where raising children can be condescended to the same level as keeping a litter of puppies. Raising good children, especially for poorer parents, is practically a lifelong sacrifice and the ultimate moral contract. Giving up your youth, freedom and finances and being willing to shield your child from incoming physical harm or even death is not the same as a bowl of Kibbles n Bits and a scratch on the tummy. 2. Every middle class American lives in a mansion on a sprawling well-kept spread of land. Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston's characters are ordinary reporters with two kids. She becomes a stay at home mom which makes him the breadwinner. His highest paying position is at The Philadelphia Inquirer which, according to online research, currently has an average annual salary of $60,000. This would mean that his monthly salary would've been around $5000 give or take. This 16 acre five bedroom Pennsylvania farmhouse had a selling price of $1.25 million in 2011. Using a mortgage calculator based on local interest rates at the time his payment for the house would’ve been roughly $5800 per month based on a 30 year loan repayment. So in other words, for the family to have realistically lived such a lifestyle, Jennifer Aniston's character had to have employed some means of soliciting tax-free money at night. 3. Let's all shed tears……. A dog has died of old age. This was the moment that was the straw that broke the camel's back. We ejected the DVD in sheer annoyance and frustration at this point. The dog died……a natural death. Cue sad music and flashbacks. How entitled can your country be if the natural death of a dog can elicit tears from an audience? A pet dog in Trinidad is lucky to live past 8 years, even in the best of care. My own backyard where I grew up contains the remains of over a dozen unfortunate cats and canines who died prematurely due to illness, speeding cars and just plain bad luck. We had not a single pet that died of natural causes i.e. old age. If we did, we would have celebrated its life and the fact that it led a full life. This supposed tearjerking scene was just another alienating Hollywoodism that highlights how out of touch the film industry is. What an awful movie full of delusional perceptions of the average American life. Don't watch it.

Question: What are the cleverest scams you have come across?
Answer: Take a breath, grab a coffee if you may, and allow me to explain to you why we are called 'Tricky-dadians’ by the rest of the Caribbean. Band Ladies Around 2016 — 2018 a phenomenon occurred where sightings of these cultish ladies in heavy clothing similar to that of traditional Amish females were found throughout Trinidad. They were typically spotted at commercial areas such as malls and PriceSmarts (Costco) mostly at the parking lot. They were renowned for asking for your assistance with the rebuilding of their church. They claimed to do this with the purchase of their cheap rubber hand bands of which they would charge anything upwards of $20TT. If you refused to buy their generic, overpriced bands they would then initiate Phase 2 of their scheme which would be to overwhelm the victim with guilt with a pathos laden statement of 'Or maybe you could contribute just a small donation. Anything?’ They employed great acting skills and for many, seeing these harmless women in humble, old fashioned garb being constantly refused and rejected for their worthy cause tugged a few heartstrings. However, as with most scams, they got too greedy too fast. Their monthly appearances soon turned to weekly and then daily. Rather than target one location for the day and wrap up afterwards, it soon became clear that they began employing routes. A typical Band Lady route would be PriceSmart Chaguanas till 2pm, Trincity Mall until 6pm and PriceSmart Mausica until 9pm. They were noticed and mentioned by some of the populace but being that they were always pleasant and took 'no’ graciously, no one bothered to think twice about their scheme. However, the last straw was a rather desperate appearance at a CPL T20 cricket match (above photograph). Trinidad is very tolerant of beggars and we throw a blind eye towards scammers for the most part but for the Band Ladies, plying their scheme in the middle of a regional cricket match where national pride was at a peak, created an online outcry. Everyone suddenly posted a story, photo or recording of a dubious encounter with one of these Band Ladies and from that moment on they were no longer seen in public. Warning *Foul language*

Question: What is an unpopular opinion you hold?
Answer: Self-Help Books Can Actually Ruin Your Life Especially if you come from a developing country. Have you ever sat and pondered as to the staggering amount of self-help authors there are out there? It seems every week someone is recommending to you some brand new, groundbreaking, best selling title that eschews a whole new perspective on how to view the world and live your life. The problem with 99% of the authors: Are they really living their dreams? Or are they making a living selling dreams? Moulding a life of success, solely based on easily digestible tips, hints and formulae is like solving advanced level algebra, whilst riding a roller coaster, using only your knowledge of multiplication tables. The knowledge can help….you probably might get the most simple problems correct……but it would be ridiculous to think that you would be able to solve all your problems in that manner, under those unique circumstances. These are people living in dire poverty in India. What can I do to help them out of this financial rut?….. I know! Think and Grow Rich by Napoleon Hill A lonely, mentally unhinged taxi driver… That's easy. The Road Less Travelled and How to Win Friends and Influence People. A wealthy but socially and emotionally void and suicidal philanthropist. Hmm. That's a tough one….The Alchemist by Paolo Coelho and you can throw in The Prophet by Gibran as well. Nothing cures rich-man depression more than obscure but romanticised Eastern parables and fables. Ok, so it's foolish to try and live according to a self help book, but how can I ruin my life simply by seeking advice? In every job that I've worked, every year there's always that one newly employed guy who is all jacked up from reading a lifetime's supply of self help books. He is always brimming with confidence and eager to pin his obstacles against the ropes and send failure scattering with his 2000 watt grin. He hates to hear no and scorns to see people second guessing themselves. He wants to take on all life's challenges and has a Napoleon Hill or Robert Kiyosaki quote ready for every situation. Then something inexplicable happens. Something gradually builds up, registers in his subconscious and overflows upon his ego. It usually takes the form of this mental conversation. 'Wait a minute. I've done everything the book advised me to. I've followed the instructions to the hilt…….yet I'm not seeing the results.’ He hasn't been promoted by his supervisor, rather his supervisor has been taking credit for his own efforts and is getting the promotion instead. Despite constantly showing support and empathy, his wife is even more nagging and helpless than when he first met her. His dedication to go above and beyond with the customer now has him doing the workload of all the lazy and incompetent coworkers around him, who still draw the same salary. He gets the lion's share of verbal abuse from disgruntled customers who rather voice their issues with him rather than the incompetent coworkers. His small business as a landscaper is suffering because his fair price is being exploited whilst mediocre landscapers are charging abominably overpriced rates and are getting more work than him. What the hell is happening here? He followed some great and timeless advice. He just forget to put in one small factor in his equation. His personal environment. His ever changing, ever complex, personal environment. The variable that if included onto his scientific calculator would produce the answer E or 'Error.’ In developing countries likes Trinidad, using US or English or German translated or Dutch translated or any developed country self help books can cause ruin your life because the environment is so different. In developing countries: These are all factors that contradict with what he read in his books and come only through experience. Had he been all the wiser he would've known that not every bit of advice in his self help books could be applied to his unique situation and environment. To make matters worse nowadays, everybody is a self help author and rather than have synchronized, compatible, time tested advice, we have polarising, wishy-washy, one-size-fits-all concoctions and psudo-psychological, parabolic gibberish. Basically, self help authors write anecdotes that's easy to understand, easy to apply and appealing to the majority. Below is a list of a few popular modern self help authors and their most famous philosophy: Robert Kiyosaki: If you have to lose, lose spectacularly. Malcolm Gladwell: You have within you an instinct to know when something 'feels’ like a rip-off. Jay Shetty: Think like a monk. Deepak Chopak: Thinking is like brain chemistry. Steve Harvey: Act like a lady, think like a man Paolo Coelho: The universe…

Question: Why does the Caribbean island of Dominica get so few tourists?
Answer: This may be pretty assumptive but Dominica is like an archaic little town on a little island, surrounded by mountains, surrounded by banana trees and surrounded by real, 100% indigenous Carib tribe Amerindians (Native Americans). Indigenous (Carib) teenaged girls selling souvenirs. (I was told they were superstitious against having their pictures taken, but managed to sneak this one behind them.) The first thing one would notice once they arrive at the capital Roseau is that they are transported back into the early 19th century. All the buildings of colonial days are there and still intact. One can see the architectural styles of the Spanish, French, English and even Irish in the building facades. There are some quite interesting architectural innovations to discover when you go to more rural locations. The people that I met were very friendly and laid back. I may get some flak for this but to me the Dominican accent can be best described as a Nigerian trying to sound French or Haitian trying to speak English. Go to the market at Roseau early on a Sunday morning and you will hear the Dominican brogue in all its glory. The group I went with unanimously found their accent and sing song very charming albeit amusing. The locals in turn found my accent strange and asked if I came from India. If you look at this basic map you would notice that Dominica is populated mostly at the coasts. If England is known for its fields Dominica should definitely be known for its mountains. The stocky mountains there stretch as far as the eye can see. It gives one a surreal feeling when driving towards higher altitudes. The hotel we stayed in was called La Flamboyant. When I heard the name I just figured it was just another generic, pseudo-exotic hotel name. However when we got there, the sensation of nails on a chalkboard was felt in my eyes. Yes. Somebody thought it was a good idea to paint a very dreary, blocky building in the most garish and loud colours of the kaleidoscope. If the question is why Dominica lacks tourists, maybe it's because they saw La Flamboyant while looking for hotels online. Funny Story As a very amateur fisherman, I spent a day fishing with a primitive caster and using beef liver as bait. The local fisherman laughed at me and subtly complained in their barely discernable patois that I was stinking up the place and attracting flies with my bloody beef liver. The problem was I didn't come with enough EC dollars to buy proper bait and beef liver was cheapest meat I could buy that would hold well on a hook. After an hour of no success I felt my line pull and the fishermen watched in amazement as I pulled up the most hideous sea creature I ever witnessed in my life. I am so sorry I didn't have the nerve to take a proper video to capture this creature in all its sheer horror. The fishermen around me ran off in fear as the creature looked like it would chase after them on its legs. I myself was severely tempted to throw it back in the water with caster hook and line. Hell, even throw my remaining beef liver behind it to appease its wrath. I flung it back in the water and severed the line with my knife. The creature, now uglier sporting an emo-style lip piercing, swam away in a very unsettling, human like manner. I learned later that this was called a Batfish. When the fishermen returned, I showed them the photos and they chastised me for not getting a bucket and keeping it. They said they would’ve used it as a tourist attraction. Hence, reason #2 Dominica has scarce tourists: I didn't get a bucket to keep the Batfish. On a sidenote, Dominica specializes in two resources: Bananas and souvenirs. Every nook and cranny you will see either a banana tree or someone selling souvenirs under a tent/umbrella. Try to buy from the ones who do not have conveniently located stalls as we noticed that amongst the several dozens of souvenir stalls in Roseau, only a handful actually get significant sales. Also, be aware that most of the souvenirs are not handcrafted by local artisans as they tend to claim. Nearly all of them seem to be imported from China. (The Caribs are masters of pretending to be the artisans of their wares). They put a big Dominica sticker to cover the 'Made in China’ engraving. So to answer the question seriously, why Dominica lacks tourism. The answer is simple. They aren't Westernized enough to attract the typical tourist. Don't expect to see a KFC next to a McDonald's or a big sprawling Ibiza style nightclub next to a Holiday Inn. They are an ecotourism style country and attract tourists who appreciate the purity and serenity of a land lost in time.

Question: What should I absolutely not do when visiting your country?
Answer: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO Avoid hiring 'local tour guides.’ Stick to official touring groups from your hotel or large hiking groups. You’ve come to Trinidad on a vacation but you don't want to be so 'touristy.’ You don't want to sign up for the generic cross country tour the hotel is offering. You don't want to be crammed in a bus with a bunch of khaki short wearing, middle aged couples who want to stop the bus every 10 minutes saying. 'Hey driver, look there's a natural spring there. I want to fill my water bottle.’ Or 'Ooh driver stop the bus. I want to get a picture of those local Trinidadian cows.’ And you definitely don't want to go on the same well beaten hiking track where ten buses like yours are parked so more tourists like yourself could commence on a 5 minute hike, past dozens of souvenir stalls, to see a dormant mud volcano which, if you're lucky, might belch out a nauseating scent of rotten eggs. It sounds awful but believe me the other option is far worse. You'd meet someone who'd tell you, 'I know a guy who does private tours. He'll take you to the real hidden sites that the tour groups don't go and he's very knowledgeable of history and professional. You don't have to stick with the dull tourist tours.’ You want to make the extra effort and discover the hidden Trinidad (or Tobago) and this guy sounds like the real deal. Here are the problems with that offer: Discovering a makeshift stone axe . My Scottish cousins realized this too late when they hired some guy who was a friend of a friend of friend who did private tours. He was taking them to Turure Water Steps which was indeed a beautiful place with four amazing waterfalls, each bigger than the last. When I heard he was charging $1000 TT (roughly 150 US) to take them there I protested and told them that they were being ripped off. Anyone could take them there for free. They argued that he was a professional and had deep knowledge of the history of places. I went along with them for the trip. Some hours later, returning home, they agreed that they were ripped off. In summary the lesson learned here is that there are several people like that so-called tour guide who wants to rip off hapless tourists. Either you stick with your hotel tour or if you want to go off the beaten track, join a professional hiking/tour group or go with a large group of friendly, trustworthy locals. Doing otherwise could have you ripped off or even worse. Edit 31.08.21 Had no idea this little tidbit of info would've garnered so many upvotes. Thank you all for the support. Question: What "poverty food" is actually really delicious?
Answer: Trinidad has many types of delicious poverty meals that stem from colonialism, slavery and East Indian indentureship. Some are despondently looked upon with embarassment while others are now expensive delicacies that tourists pay, 'ah pound and ah crown’ for. Poor poverty meals These are the meals that really represent someone going through hard times. These are the delicacies prepared from the remnants of the pantry and hunger induced experimentation. Rice and butter As the name suggests, boiled rice grains soaked in butter. Actually it's not butter but margarine, as real butter here is more expensive than most meats. Exceedingly unhealthy but much more delicious than you would imagine. Just imagine the taste of mashed potatoes except it's rice. Flour porridge Heat some white flour on a skillet and just before it's about to burn throw in some condensed milk and water. This is a Haitian recipe but used by many older Trinis who want to feel full but can't afford to buy groceries. According to how well you garnish this concoction, it can be a hidden delight. Plain egg rice When you have one egg and a bag of rice and you need to feed an entire family, this is the meal of choice. Basically you heat up some boiled rice and throw in a well beaten egg. You will be astonished at how far one egg can stretch. Green fig (banana) with ‘butter’ and salt A family with a couple of banana trees in the yard could be saved from starvation with this simple, delicious meal. Boil a couple full but unripe bananas (with or without skin) and serve with margarine and salt. A fully developed green fig well soaked in margarine with a dash of salt can beat meals in most 5 star restaurants. Banana fritters Instead of throwing away your near rotted bananas, mash them to a pulp, knead in some flour and deep fry in oil. Even when eaten cold these fritters are a treat. Rich Poverty Meals These were meals made from ingredients the upper class and colonial masters would discard such as chickens’ neck and pig's tail. Now they are culinary delights that tourists flock towards and are quite expensive to make/purchase. Chicken Foot souse Don't run away just yet. This flavor will knock your socks off. This is basically boiled chicken's feet soaked in a zesty broth. You'd be surprised the amount of meat a chicken's foot can give. Geera neck Dont throw away those chicken necks! Season them with cumin roast them on a skillet for a spicy snack. These are popular 'cutters’ or bar foods, made to sober up drunkards. This can be made with chicken gizzards also. Fried chicken livers My mother would carry us to this seedy looking bakery on a Sunday where they served fried chicken livers, mostly to satisfy the patrons of the bar that was situated next to them. You'll spit out its overly pungent flavor at first try but it gets tastier after each bite. Pig tail Pig tail meals are now synonymous with special events such as birthday parties and wedding receptions. Pig tail pelau, as shown above, is made from rice and pig tails cooked in caramelized sugar (stewed) with peas and whatever garnishes desired. There is also pig tail soup. A pig's tail is incredibly meaty, tender and juicy that so much that many people find themselves sucking at the bone upon finishing. Black pudding Thanks to our English rulers of yesteryear who brought this excrement looking sausage, made entirely of pig's blood, to the Caribbean. Our version includes a lot more spices and this dish is quite popular served in bread as a street food. It looks and sounds horrid but it is quite creamy textured and rich in taste. and lastly Cow heel soup Who would've known that a cow's heel would be so gelatinous, meaty and soak up flavour so well. Along with fish broth and corn soup, this is the definitive soup of Trinidad.

Question: What are some dirty tactics used by fast food restaurants?
Answer: I worked delivery for a popular local pizzeria in Trinidad for some years and left somewhat dishonorably discharged after having arguments with management over a growing reliance on a dirty, illegal tactic that they employed with no discretion. I can best describe it by means of a short skit. Customer: Hi. Good day. Do you have any specials today? Newly Employed Cashier: Good day. Our Monday special is two large pizzas for only $100. Customer: That's great. That's like two for the price of one. I'll have it. Newly Employed Cashier: Yes. We have a different specials everyday. You can check them online or simply ask us. Question: What did you learn too late in life?
Answer: This is Ernie and Bert. Riggs and Murtaugh Thelma and Louise Agents K and J Oscar and Felix As you are already aware, these are all famous 'buddies’ from television and movies. In every example both buddies are almost polar opposites of the other, yet they get along well. One is usually compulsive, an extrovert, carefree and full of wit and charisma. The other is usually more reserved, wary, introverted and high strung. Together, their contrasting personalities allow them to solve each other's problems. This type of buddy pairing in film and television has become iconic and timeless. Why? Because it applies to us all. We all have that buddy or best friend who is either personality A or personality B. What some of us don't realize is that we actually do function better in life with them. Regardless of how successful you become in your personal or financial life, that buddy represents what it is you lack and could never achieve on your own. You both come together and resolve issues the other is having by offering a differing mindset. As a young adult, I was the extroverted type buddy. I was always looking for adventure, heart on my sleeves, witty and somewhat charismatic. I had my buddy but I didn't look at him in terms of a mutually beneficial friendship. I considered myself the leader and him my mere follower. He enjoyed the fact that I brought him out in the social spheres and would make situations light and fun but he would shake his head and sigh watching me consistently crashing and burning and stubbornly ignoring his advice. Many major personal disappointments I experienced because I didn't respect or value my buddy's wisdom. My advice is to take a stock check of your friends and associates and determine who is your buddy. Are you treating him/her with proper consideration? Sometimes your buddy is not even your friend per se but a mutual acquaintance or work associate. Shut up for a second and listen to what he/she has to say. You won't find another like him/her again.
